Thus, O Rama, O lotus-eyed one, (the Raksasas) had innumerable warriors beaten down and their foremost leaders slain.

अशक्नुवन्तस्ते विष्णुं प्रतियोद्धुं भयार्दिताः
त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः

aśaknuvantaste viṣṇuṁ pratiyoddhuṁ bhayārditāḥ
tyaktvā laṅkāṁ gatā vastuṁ pātālaṁ sahapatnayaḥ
And albeit inflated with pride, they, incapable of coping with Visnu, leaving Lanka, went to the nether regions with their wives dwelling there.

सुमालिनं समासाद्य राक्षसं रघुनन्दन
स्थिताः प्रख्यातवीर्यास्ते वंशे सालकटङ्कटे

sumālinaṁ samāsādya rākṣasaṁ raghunandana
sthitāḥ prakhyātavīryāste vaṁśe sālakaṭaṅkaṭe
O best of the Raghus, these Raksasa of celebrated prowess, related to the race of Salakatankata, remained under the leadership of the Raksasa Sumali.

ये त्वया निहतास्ते वै पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः
सुमाली माल्यवान्माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः
सर्व एते महाभाग रावणाद्बलवत्तराः

ye tvayā nihatāste vai paulastyā nāma rākṣasāḥ
sumālī mālyavānmālī ye ca teṣāṁ puraḥsarāḥ
sarva ete mahābhāga rāvaṇādbalavattarāḥ
All those exalted Raksasas going under the name of Pulastya that had been headed by Sumali, Malyavan and Mali, were stronger than Ravana.

न चान्यो रक्षसां हन्ता सुरेष्वपि पुरंजय
ऋते नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम्

na cānyo rakṣasāṁ hantā sureṣvapi puraṁjaya
ṛte nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ śaṅkhacakragadādharam
No other than the god Narayana, holding the conch, the discus and the mace, could slay those Raksasa-foes to the celestials and thorns in the side of the deties.

भवान्नारायणो देवश्चतुर्बाहुः सनातनः
राक्षसान्हन्तुमुत्पन्नो अजेयः प्रभुरव्ययः

bhavānnārāyaṇo devaścaturbāhuḥ sanātanaḥ
rākṣasānhantumutpanno ajeyaḥ prabhuravyayaḥ
And you are that eternal god the four armed Narayana, the lord, undeteriorating and unconquerable, sprung to exterminate Raksasas.

तं दृष्ट्वामरसंकाशं गच्छन्तं पावकोपमम्
अथाब्रवीत्सुतां रक्षः कैकसीं नाम नामतः

taṁ dṛṣṭvāmarasaṁkāśaṁ gacchantaṁ pāvakopamam
athābravītsutāṁ rakṣaḥ kaikasīṁ nāma nāmataḥ
And that great-minded lord of Raksasas, resembling dark clouds, decked in burnished earrings of gold, then began to reflect. And then the Raksasa addressed his daughter, named Kaikasi.

पुत्रि प्रदानकालोऽयं यौवनं तेऽतिवर्तते
त्वत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः

putri pradānakālo'yaṁ yauvanaṁ te'tivartate
tvatkṛte ca vayaṁ sarve yantritā dharmabuddhayaḥ
But desirous of acquiring religious merit, we are striving our best in your interests. My daughter, you are finished with every perfection like to Sri herself.

त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः सपद्मेव पुत्रिके
प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः प्रतिगृह्यसे

tvaṁ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sapadmeva putrike
pratyākhyānācca bhītaistvaṁ na varaiḥ pratigṛhyase
O daughter, the time has come when I should give you away. Your youth is about to be passed. (Kept back) by the fear of refusal, no suiter has sought you (up to his time).

कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम्
न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति पुत्रिके

kanyāpitṛtvaṁ duḥkhaṁ hi sarveṣāṁ mānakāṅkṣiṇām
na jñāyate ca kaḥ kanyāṁ varayediti putrike
The being father to a daughter is misery to every one that seekes honour. O daughter, one does not know who shall ask for one's daughter.

मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव प्रदीयते
कुलत्रयं सदा कन्या संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति

mātuḥ kulaṁ pitṛkulaṁ yatra caiva pradīyate
kulatrayaṁ sadā kanyā saṁśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati
Whenever may a daughter be conferred, a daughter stayes, placing in uncertainly the three races* to which she is related. *The races respectively of her father, mother and husband.

सा त्वं मुनिवरश्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम्
गच्छ विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम्

sā tvaṁ munivaraśreṣṭhaṁ prajāpatikulodbhavam
gaccha viśravasaṁ putri paulastyaṁ varaya svayam
Do you, my daughter, seek for your husband that best and foremost of ascetics sprung in the line of Prajapati Pulastya's son, Visrava, and of yourself accept him (for your lord).

ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः
तेजसा भास्करसमा यादृशोऽयं धनेश्वरः

īdṛśāste bhaviṣyanti putrāḥ putri na saṁśayaḥ
tejasā bhāskarasamā yādṛśo'yaṁ dhaneśvaraḥ
Then, O daughter, even as this lord of riches, so you will, without doubt, have sons resembling the Sun himself in energy.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम पुलस्त्यतनयो द्विजः
अग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठच्चतुर्थ इव पावकः

etasminnantare rāma pulastyatanayo dvijaḥ
agnihotramupātiṣṭhaccaturtha iva pāvakaḥ
In the meanwhile, O Rama, that twice-born one-Pulastya's was performing the Agnihotra, like the fourth Fire itself.

सा तु तां दारुणां वेलामचिन्त्य पितृगौरवात्
उपसृत्याग्रतस्तस्य चरणाधोमुखी स्थिता

sā tu tāṁ dāruṇāṁ velāmacintya pitṛgauravāt
upasṛtyāgratastasya caraṇādhomukhī sthitā

And without minding that terrific time, (Kaikasi), having regard to the dignity of her sire, coming up before him, stood (there) son hanging her head down towards his feet and throwing up the earth with her great foe.

भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता
किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने

bhadre kasyāsi duhitā kuto vā tvamihāgatā
kiṁ kāryaṁ kasya vā hetostattvato brūhi śobhane

Seeing that one of the shapely hips, having a face fair as the full Moon, (that exceedingly high-minded ascetic) flaming in energy accosted her thus. O gentle one, whose daughter are you? And when do you come hither? And what is your errand? And for whom (do you come)? O beauteous (damsel), truly tell me this.

किं तु विद्धि हि मां ब्रह्मञ्शासनात्पितुरागताम्
कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि

kiṁ tu viddhi hi māṁ brahmañśāsanātpiturāgatām
kaikasī nāma nāmnāhaṁ śeṣaṁ tvaṁ jñātumarhasi

Thus addressed, the girl, with joined hands, said, 'O ascetic, you are competent to get at my intent by virtue of your own power. Yet, O Brahmarsi, know me as having come here at the mandate of my sire. My name is Kaikasi. The rest do you read yourself.

सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रणिपत्याब्रवीद्वचः
भगवन्नेदृशाः पुत्रास्त्वत्तोऽर्हा ब्रह्मयोनितः

sā tu tadvacanaṁ śrutvā praṇipatyābravīdvacaḥ
bhagavannedṛśāḥ putrāstvatto'rhā brahmayonitaḥ
Hearing his speech, she, bowing down, said, 'O reverend (ascetic), such sons of terrific ways seek I not from you that follow the Veda. Therefore it behoves you to favour me.'

अथाब्रवीन्मुनिस्तत्र पश्चिमो यस्तवात्मजः
मम वंशानुरूपश्च धर्मात्मा च भविष्यति

athābravīnmunistatra paścimo yastavātmajaḥ
mama vaṁśānurūpaśca dharmātmā ca bhaviṣyati
O fair-faced one, the son that you bring forth last, shall be like to my line, he shall, without doubt-be righteous-souled.

एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या राम कालेन केनचित्
जनयामास बीभत्सं रक्षोरूपं सुदारुणम्

evamuktā tu sā kanyā rāma kālena kenacit
janayāmāsa bībhatsaṁ rakṣorūpaṁ sudāruṇam

Having been thus accosted, the girl, O Rama, after a length of time brought forth a very terrible and hideous offspring having the form of a Raksasa, having ten necks, furnished with large teeth, and resembling a heap of collyrium, with coppery lips, twenty arms, huge faces, and flaming hair.

जातमात्रे ततस्तस्मिन्सज्वालकवलाः शिवाः
क्रव्यादाश्चापसव्यानि मण्डलानि प्रचक्रिरे

jātamātre tatastasminsajvālakavalāḥ śivāḥ
kravyādāścāpasavyāni maṇḍalāni pracakrire
On his having been born, jacka.s with flaming mouths and other ferocious beasts began to gyrate on the left.

ववर्ष रुधिरं देवो मेघाश्च खरनिस्वनाः
प्रबभौ न च खे सूर्यो महोल्काश्चापतन्भुवि

vavarṣa rudhiraṁ devo meghāśca kharanisvanāḥ
prababhau na ca khe sūryo maholkāścāpatanbhuvi

That god showered down blood; and the clouds uttered forth harsh sounds. And the sun was deprived of his splendour; and meteors began to dart to the earth. And the earth shook; and the wind swept away violently. And that lord of streams-the ocean, which was calm before, became agitated.

अथ नामाकरोत्तस्य पितामहसमः पिता
दशशीर्षः प्रसूतोऽयं दशग्रीवो भविष्यति

atha nāmākarottasya pitāmahasamaḥ pitā
daśaśīrṣaḥ prasūto'yaṁ daśagrīvo bhaviṣyati
And his sire resembling his grand-father named him, (saying), 'As this one has been born with ten necks, he shall be called Ten-necked.'

तस्य त्वनन्तरं जातः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
प्रमाणाद्यस्य विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते

tasya tvanantaraṁ jātaḥ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
pramāṇādyasya vipulaṁ pramāṇaṁ neha vidyate
After him was born Kumbhakarna endowed with prodigious strength, than whose proportions there are none other's on earth.

ततः शूर्पणखा नाम संजज्ञे विकृतानना
विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा कैकस्याः पश्चिमः सुतः

tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā nāma saṁjajñe vikṛtānanā
vibhīṣaṇaśca dharmātmā kaikasyāḥ paścimaḥ sutaḥ
Then was born she that, having a frightful visage, goes under the name of Surpanakha; the righteous Vibhisana is the youngest son of Kaikasi.

ते तु तत्र महारण्ये ववृधुः सुमहौजसः
तेषां क्रूरो दशग्रीवो लोकोद्वेगकरोऽभवत्

te tu tatra mahāraṇye vavṛdhuḥ sumahaujasaḥ
teṣāṁ krūro daśagrīvo lokodvegakaro'bhavat
'Excellent!' And in that extensive forest those exceedingly energetic ones, Kumbhakarna and the Ten-necked one grew up, and became the sources of anxiety to the people.

कुम्भकर्णः प्रमत्तस्तु महर्षीन्धर्मसंश्रितान्
त्रैलोक्यं त्रासयन्दुष्टो भक्षयन्विचचार ह

kumbhakarṇaḥ pramattastu maharṣīndharmasaṁśritān
trailokyaṁ trāsayanduṣṭo bhakṣayanvicacāra ha
Kumbhakarma, maddened to the height, devouring mighty-saints devoted to religion, constantly ranged the triune world in a dissatisfied spirit.

विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपथे स्थितः
स्वाध्यायनियताहार उवास नियतेन्द्रियः

vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā nityaṁ dharmapathe sthitaḥ
svādhyāyaniyatāhāra uvāsa niyatendriyaḥ
But the righteous Vibhisana, ever intent on piety, dwelt there studying the Veda, restraining his fare, and controlling his senses.

अथ वित्तेश्वरो देवस्तत्र कालेन केनचित्
आगच्छत्पितरं द्रष्टुं पुष्पकेण महौजसं

atha vitteśvaro devastatra kālena kenacit
āgacchatpitaraṁ draṣṭuṁ puṣpakeṇa mahaujasaṁ
It came to pass that after a length of time the god, Vaisravana-lord of riches-came to see his sire, mounted on Puspaka.

तं दृष्ट्वा कैकसी तत्र ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा
आस्थाय राक्षसीं बुद्धिं दशग्रीवमुवाच ह

taṁ dṛṣṭvā kaikasī tatra jvalantamiva tejasā
āsthāya rākṣasīṁ buddhiṁ daśagrīvamuvāca ha
Seeing him, the Raksasi-Kaikasi-flaming up in energy, coming to the Ten-necked one, represented to him.

पुत्र वैश्रवणं पश्य भ्रातरं तेजसा वृतम्
भ्रातृभावे समे चापि पश्यात्मानं त्वमीदृशम्

putra vaiśravaṇaṁ paśya bhrātaraṁ tejasā vṛtam
bhrātṛbhāve same cāpi paśyātmānaṁ tvamīdṛśam
O son, behold your brother, Vaisravana, enfolded in effulgence; and, albeit of equal fraternity, behold you in this plight!

दशग्रीव तथा यत्नं कुरुष्वामितविक्रम
यथा भवसि मे पुत्र शीघ्रं वैश्वरणोपमः

daśagrīva tathā yatnaṁ kuruṣvāmitavikrama
yathā bhavasi me putra śīghraṁ vaiśvaraṇopamaḥ
Therefore, O Ten-necked one, O you of measureless prowess, do you so strive that you also, my son, may be like Vaisravana himself.

मातुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्
अमर्षमतुलं लेभे प्रतिज्ञां चाकरोत्तदा

mātustadvacanaṁ śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān
amarṣamatulaṁ lebhe pratijñāṁ cākarottadā
Hearing that speech of his mother, the powerful Ten-necked one was wrought up with exceeding great ill-will, and he vowed then.

सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि तुल्यो भ्रात्राधिकोऽपि वा
भविष्याम्यचिरान्मातः संतापं त्यज हृद्गतम्

satyaṁ te pratijānāmi tulyo bhrātrādhiko'pi vā
bhaviṣyāmyacirānmātaḥ saṁtāpaṁ tyaja hṛdgatam
I truly promise to you that I will be equal to my brother (in energy), or excel him in it. Therefore do you cast off this sorrow in your heart.

ततः क्रोधेन तेनैव दशग्रीवः सहानुजः
प्राप्स्यामि तपसा काममिति कृत्वाध्यवस्य च
आगच्छदात्मसिद्ध्यर्थं गोकर्णस्याश्रमं शुभम्

tataḥ krodhena tenaiva daśagrīvaḥ sahānujaḥ
prāpsyāmi tapasā kāmamiti kṛtvādhyavasya ca
āgacchadātmasiddhyarthaṁ gokarṇasyāśramaṁ śubham

And influenced by that passion, the tennecked one with his younger brother began to perform rigid acts, with his mind fixed on asceticism. 'I must through austerities have my wish,' thus fixed and resolved, he compassing his end, came to the sacred asylum of Gokarna.

अथाब्रवीद्द्विजं रामः कथं ते भ्रातरो वने
कीदृशं तु तदा ब्रह्मंस्तपश्चेरुर्महाव्रताः

athābravīddvijaṁ rāmaḥ kathaṁ te bhrātaro vane
kīdṛśaṁ tu tadā brahmaṁstapaścerurmahāvratāḥ
Then Rama spoke to the ascetic, O Brahmana, how did those exceedingly mighty brothers carry on austerities in that forest; and what kind of penances was theirs?

अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र रामं प्रयत मानसं
तांस्तान्धर्मविधींस्तत्र भ्रातरस्ते समाविशन्

agastyastvabravīttatra rāmaṁ prayata mānasaṁ
tāṁstāndharmavidhīṁstatra bhrātaraste samāviśan
Thereat there Agastya said to Rama of a complacent mind, “The brothers severally observed the morality proper to each.”

एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तस्यातिचक्रमुः
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य सत्पथे निष्ठितस्य च

evaṁ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa tasyāticakramuḥ
dharme prayatamānasya satpathe niṣṭhitasya ca
Thus passed away ten thousand of that one putting forth exertions in behalf of religion, and established in the path of honesty.

विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपरः शुचिः
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि पादेनैकेन तस्थिवान्

vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā nityaṁ dharmaparaḥ śuciḥ
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi pādenaikena tasthivān
The virtuous Vibhisana, ever intent on virtue and pure of spirit, remained standing on one leg for five thousand years.

समाप्ते नियमे तस्य ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः
पपात पुष्पवर्षं च क्षुभिताश्चापि देवताः

samāpte niyame tasya nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ
papāta puṣpavarṣaṁ ca kṣubhitāścāpi devatāḥ
When he had completed (his term of restriction), swarms of apsaras danced, and blossoms showered, and the deities hymned (him).

पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यं चैवान्ववर्तत
तस्थौ चोर्ध्वशिरोबाहुः स्वाध्यायधृतमानसः

pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi sūryaṁ caivānvavartata
tasthau cordhvaśirobāhuḥ svādhyāyadhṛtamānasaḥ
And for five thousand years, he adored the Sun, and with his mind concentrated in the study of the Veda, remained with his head and hands raised up.

एवं विभीषणस्यापि गतानि नियतात्मनः
दशवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गस्थस्येव नन्दने

evaṁ vibhīṣaṇasyāpi gatāni niyatātmanaḥ
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi svargasthasyeva nandane
In this wise Vibhisana like a deity in Nandana passed away ten thousand years, observing restrictions.

दशवर्षसहस्रं तु निराहारो दशाननः
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्चाग्नौ जुहाव सः

daśavarṣasahasraṁ tu nirāhāro daśānanaḥ
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śiraścāgnau juhāva saḥ
The ten-necked passed ten thousand years without fare. On a thousand years being complete, he offered his own head as a sacrifice to Fire.

एवं वर्षसहस्राणि नव तस्यातिचक्रमुः
शिरांसि नव चाप्यस्य प्रविष्टानि हुताशनम्

evaṁ varṣasahasrāṇi nava tasyāticakramuḥ
śirāṁsi nava cāpyasya praviṣṭāni hutāśanam
In this way, he passed away nine thousand years, and nine of his heads entered into Fire.

अथ वर्षसहस्रे तु दशमे दशमं शिरः
छेत्तुकामः स धर्मात्मा प्राप्तश्चात्र पितामहः

atha varṣasahasre tu daśame daśamaṁ śiraḥ
chettukāmaḥ sa dharmātmā prāptaścātra pitāmahaḥ
And as in the tenth year he intended to strike off his tenth head, the Great-father (Brahma) presented himself at that place.

पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतः सार्धं देवैरुपस्थितः
वत्स वत्स दशग्रीव प्रीतोऽस्मीत्यभ्यभाषत

pitāmahastu suprītaḥ sārdhaṁ devairupasthitaḥ
vatsa vatsa daśagrīva prīto'smītyabhyabhāṣata
Well-pleased, the Pitamaha Brahma came there along with the celestials. 'O Ten-necked one,' said (the Great-father), 'I am well-pleased with you.

शीघ्रं वरय धर्मज्ञ वरो यस्तेऽभिकाङ्क्षितः
किं ते कामं करोम्यद्य न वृथा ते परिश्रमः

śīghraṁ varaya dharmajña varo yaste'bhikāṅkṣitaḥ
kiṁ te kāmaṁ karomyadya na vṛthā te pariśramaḥ
Do you, O cognisant of righteousness, at once ask for the boon that you wish to have. What wish of your shall I realise? Your toil must not go for nothing.

ततोऽब्रवीद्दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा

tato'bravīddaśagrīvaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
praṇamya śirasā devaṁ harṣagadgadayā girā
Thereat, the Ten-necked one, bowing down his head to the deity, said with a delighted heart, his words faltering with ecstasy.

भगवन्प्राणिनां नित्यं नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्
नास्ति मृत्युसमः शत्रुरमरत्वमतो वृणे

bhagavanprāṇināṁ nityaṁ nānyatra maraṇādbhayam
nāsti mṛtyusamaḥ śatruramaratvamato vṛṇe
O reverend one, creatures have no other fear than (that of) death; and enemy there is none that is like to death. Therefore immortality is even what I crave for.

सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम्
अवध्यः स्यां प्रजाध्यक्ष देवतानां च शाश्वतम्

suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṁ daityadānavarakṣasām
avadhyaḥ syāṁ prajādhyakṣa devatānāṁ ca śāśvatam

O lord of creatures, I would, O external one, he incapable of being slain by birds and serpents, Yaksas, Daityas, Danavas and Raksasas, and the deities; for, O you that are worshipped by the immortals, anxiety I have none from any other beings. Indeed, I deem as straw creatures such as men etc.

एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा
उवाच वचनं राम सह देवैः पितामहः

evamuktastu dharmātmā daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā
uvāca vacanaṁ rāma saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ
Thus accosted by the Raksasa the Ten-necked one-that righteous-souled one, the great-father, along with the celestials, said.

हुतानि यानि शीर्षाणि पूर्वमग्नौ त्वयानघ
पुनस्तानि भविष्यन्ति तथैव तव राक्षस

hutāni yāni śīrṣāṇi pūrvamagnau tvayānagha
punastāni bhaviṣyanti tathaiva tava rākṣasa

I, having been gratified, will confer on you a fresh boon. O Raksasa, O sinless one, those heads of your which have been offered as sacrifices and which have sunk, into the fire, shall again be your. And, a placid one, I shall also confer on you another boon difficult of being obtained, The form that you shall wish to wear, shall instantly be yours.

एवं पितामहोक्तस्य दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः
अग्नौ हुतानि शीर्षाणि यानि तान्युत्थितानि वै

evaṁ pitāmahoktasya daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ
agnau hutāni śīrṣāṇi yāni tānyutthitāni vai
As soon as the Ten-necked Raksasa had spoken, thus, the heads that had been offered as sacrifices into the fire, rose up again.

एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं प्रजापतिः
विभीषणमथोवाच वाक्यं लोकपितामहः

evamuktvā tu taṁ rāma daśagrīvaṁ prajāpatiḥ
vibhīṣaṇamathovāca vākyaṁ lokapitāmahaḥ
Having said this to the Ten-necked one, the. great sire of all creatures addressed Vibhisana, saying.

विभीषण त्वया वत्स धर्मसंहितबुद्धिना
परितुष्टोऽस्मि धर्मज्ञ वरं वरय सुव्रत

vibhīṣaṇa tvayā vatsa dharmasaṁhitabuddhinā
parituṣṭo'smi dharmajña varaṁ varaya suvrata

O Vibhisana, gratified have I been by you, whose intelligence is established in righteousness. Therefore, my child, O righteoussouled one, O you of excellent vows, ask for the boon that you would have.

विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा वचनं प्राह साञ्जलिः
वृतः सर्वगुणैर्नित्यं चन्द्रमा इव रश्मिभिः

vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā vacanaṁ prāha sāñjaliḥ
vṛtaḥ sarvaguṇairnityaṁ candramā iva raśmibhiḥ

Thereat the virtuous Vibhisana spoke with joined hands, 'O reverend one, since the spiritual preceptor of all creatures himself (is pleased) with me, I (deem myself) as furnished with every perfection, even as the Moon is envisioned with rays. If you will bestow on me a boon with pleasure, then, O you of excellent vows, hear of the boon that I would have.

या या मे जायते बुद्धिर्येषु येष्वाश्रमेष्विह
सा सा भवतु धर्मिष्ठा तं तं धर्मं च पालये

yā yā me jāyate buddhiryeṣu yeṣvāśrameṣviha
sā sā bhavatu dharmiṣṭhā taṁ taṁ dharmaṁ ca pālaye

And inay every sense of mine sprung during the observance of particular modes of life, be in unison with righteousness, so that I may practice the form of religion (in harmony with any particular mode of life!) O exceedingly noble one, this best of boons, is even what is sought for by me, for nothing in this world is incapable of being attained by those attached to righteousness.' Then the lord of creatures, being again delighted, spoke to Vibhisana.

यस्माद्राक्षसयोनौ ते जातस्यामित्रकर्षण
नाधर्मे जायते बुद्धिरमरत्वं ददामि ते

yasmādrākṣasayonau te jātasyāmitrakarṣaṇa
nādharme jāyate buddhiramaratvaṁ dadāmi te

As you are virtuous, so all this shall come to pass on your behalf. And inasmuch as in spite of your having been born in the Raksasa race, your thoughts, ( destroyer of enemies, do not originate in sin, I confer on the immortality. Having said this, he intended to grant boons to Kumbhakarna.

न तावत्कुम्भकर्णाय प्रदातव्यो वरस्त्वया
जानीषे हि यथा लोकांस्त्रासयत्येष दुर्मतिः

na tāvatkumbhakarṇāya pradātavyo varastvayā
jānīṣe hi yathā lokāṁstrāsayatyeṣa durmatiḥ

Thereat the celestials in a body represented to the lord of creatures with joined hands. 'On Kumbhakarna you should confer no boons, since you know in what manner does this wickedminded one frighten people.

नन्दनेऽप्सरसः सप्त महेन्द्रानुचरा दश
अनेन भक्षिता ब्रह्मन्नृषयो मानुषास्तथा

nandane'psarasaḥ sapta mahendrānucarā daśa
anena bhakṣitā brahmannṛṣayo mānuṣāstathā
And, O Brahmana, even Apsaras in Nandana, ten attendants of Mahendra, as well as sages and human beings, have been devoured by this one.

वरव्याजेन मोहोऽस्मै दीयताममितप्रभ
लोकानां स्वस्ति चैव स्याद्भवेदस्य च संनतिः

varavyājena moho'smai dīyatāmamitaprabha
lokānāṁ svasti caiva syādbhavedasya ca saṁnatiḥ

Do you then, o lord having immeasurable prowess, pretending to give him a boon, give stupefaction (instead). Thereby the welfare of the people would be secured, and the honour of this one too shall be maintained.

एवमुक्तः सुरैर्ब्रह्माचिन्तयत्पद्मसंभवः
चिन्तिता चोपतस्थेऽस्य पार्श्वं देवी सरस्वती

evamuktaḥ surairbrahmācintayatpadmasaṁbhavaḥ
cintitā copatasthe'sya pārśvaṁ devī sarasvatī
Thus addressed by the celestials, Brahma, the Lotus-sprung one, pondered. The goddess, Sarasvati, who was by his side was also agitated by anxiety.

प्राञ्जलिः सा तु पर्श्वस्था प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वती
इयमस्म्यागता देव किं कार्यं करवाण्यहम्

prāñjaliḥ sā tu parśvasthā prāha vākyaṁ sarasvatī
iyamasmyāgatā deva kiṁ kāryaṁ karavāṇyaham
And remaining by him, Sarasvati with joined hands observed, 'O god, I have come here. What work shall I accomplish?'

प्रजापतिस्तु तां प्राप्तां प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वतीम्
वाणि त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भव या देवतेप्सिता

prajāpatistu tāṁ prāptāṁ prāha vākyaṁ sarasvatīm
vāṇi tvaṁ rākṣasendrasya bhava yā devatepsitā

And the lord of creatures, on having her, spoke to Sarasvati,' O Vani!' be you the goddess of speech of this foremost of Raksasas, favourable to the deities. 1. Lit. word, a designation of Saraswati. 2. i.e. preside over Kumbhakarna's speech while asking for the boon, and let him, through your power, ask for such a gift as may turn our profitable to the gods.

तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत्
कुम्भकर्ण महाबाहो वरं वरय यो मतः

tathetyuktvā praviṣṭā sā prajāpatirathābravīt
kumbhakarṇa mahābāho varaṁ varaya yo mataḥ
Having said, 'So be it,' she entered (within Kumbhakarna's throat); and Prajapati said,' O Kumbhakarma, O mighty-armed one, do you ask for the boon that you would have.

एवं लब्धवराः सर्वे भ्रातरो दीप्ततेजसः
श्लेष्मातकवनं गत्वा तत्र ते न्यवसन्सुखम्

evaṁ labdhavarāḥ sarve bhrātaro dīptatejasaḥ
śleṣmātakavanaṁ gatvā tatra te nyavasansukham
Having thus obtained the boons, the brothers endowed with flaming energy, going to the Slesmataka wood, began to dwell there peacefully.

सुमाली वरलब्धांस्तु ज्ञात्वा तान्वै निशाचरान्
उदतिष्ठद्भयं त्यक्त्वा सानुगः स रसातलात्

sumālī varalabdhāṁstu jñātvā tānvai niśācarān
udatiṣṭhadbhayaṁ tyaktvā sānugaḥ sa rasātalāt
Learning that these night-rangers had obtained boons, Sumali with his followers, casting off fear, rose up from the nether regions.

मारीचश्च प्रहस्तश्च विरूपाक्षो महोदरः
उदतिष्ठन्सुसंरब्धाः सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः

mārīcaśca prahastaśca virūpākṣo mahodaraḥ
udatiṣṭhansusaṁrabdhāḥ sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ
And wrought up with exceeding great wrath, the counsellors of that Raksasas-Marica and Prahasta and Virupaksa and Mahodara-also rose up.

सुमाली चैव तैः सर्वैर्वृतो राक्षसपुंगवैः
अभिगम्य दशग्रीवं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्

sumālī caiva taiḥ sarvairvṛto rākṣasapuṁgavaiḥ
abhigamya daśagrīvaṁ pariṣvajyedamabravīt
Accompanied by his counsellors-foremost of Raksasas-Sumali presenting himself before the Ten-necked one and embracing him, addressed him, saying.

दिष्ट्या ते पुत्र संप्राप्तश्चिन्तितोऽयं मनोरथः
यस्त्वं त्रिभुवणश्रेष्ठाल्लब्धवान्वरमीदृशम्

diṣṭyā te putra saṁprāptaścintito'yaṁ manorathaḥ
yastvaṁ tribhuvaṇaśreṣṭhāllabdhavānvaramīdṛśam
By good fortune it is, O child, that through you we have had the wish that was in our heart, inasmuch as you have received the best of boons from him that is the foremost of all these three worlds.

यत्कृते च वयं लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा याता रसातलम्
तद्गतं नो महाबाहो महद्विष्णुकृतं भयम्

yatkṛte ca vayaṁ laṅkāṁ tyaktvā yātā rasātalam
tadgataṁ no mahābāho mahadviṣṇukṛtaṁ bhayam
O mighty-armed one, that great fear arising from Visnu, from which leaving Larka, we had gone to the nethermost abysses, has been removed.

असकृत्तेन भग्ना हि परित्यज्य स्वमालयम्
विद्रुताः सहिताः सर्वे प्रविष्टाः स्म रसातलम्

asakṛttena bhagnā hi parityajya svamālayam
vidrutāḥ sahitāḥ sarve praviṣṭāḥ sma rasātalam
Full many a time, brought down by that fear, we, on being pursued (by our enemies), forsaking our homes, had gone to the nether regions along with all those (related to us).

अस्मदीया च लङ्केयं नगरी राक्षसोषिता
निवेशिता तव भ्रात्रा धनाध्यक्षेण धीमता

asmadīyā ca laṅkeyaṁ nagarī rākṣasoṣitā
niveśitā tava bhrātrā dhanādhyakṣeṇa dhīmatā
This Lanka was our city, inhabited by Raksasas. (Now) it is inhabited by the brotherthe intelligent lord of riches.

यदि नामात्र शक्यं स्यात्साम्ना दानेन वानघ
तरसा वा महाबाहो प्रत्यानेतुं कृतं भवेत्

yadi nāmātra śakyaṁ syātsāmnā dānena vānagha
tarasā vā mahābāho pratyānetuṁ kṛtaṁ bhavet

O mighty-armed one, if you can through selfcontrol or charity or by a sudden display of prowess, repossesses yourself of the same, a (great) thing shall have been achieved; and then, O child, you should, without doubt, be the lord of Lanka; and this Raksasa race, which has sunk, shall have been raised up by you.

अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवो मातामहमुपस्थितम्
वित्तेशो गुरुरस्माकं नार्हस्येवं प्रभाषितुम्

athābravīddaśagrīvo mātāmahamupasthitam
vitteśo gururasmākaṁ nārhasyevaṁ prabhāṣitum
O you endowed with prodigious strength, you shall be the lord of all. Then the Ten-necked one addressed his maternal grand-father, who was present.

दशग्रीव महाबाहो नार्हस्त्वं वक्तुमीदृशम्
सौभ्रात्रं नास्ति शूराणां शृणु चेदं वचो मम

daśagrīva mahābāho nārhastvaṁ vaktumīdṛśam
saubhrātraṁ nāsti śūrāṇāṁ śṛṇu cedaṁ vaco mama
O Ten-necked one, O long-armed (hero), it does not behove you to speak thus. Faternal feeling there is none among heroes. Listen to these words of mine!

अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव भगिन्यौ सहिते किल
भार्ये परमरूपिण्यौ कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः

aditiśca ditiścaiva bhaginyau sahite kila
bhārye paramarūpiṇyau kaśyapasya prajāpateḥ
There two sisters-Aditi and Diti, mutually attached to each other, those (damsels) endowed with surpassing beauty, became the wives of that lord of creatures-Kasyapa.

अदितिर्जनयामास देवांस्त्रिभुवणेश्वरान्
दितिस्त्वजनयद्दैत्यान्कश्यपस्यात्मसंभवान्

aditirjanayāmāsa devāṁstribhuvaṇeśvarān
ditistvajanayaddaityānkaśyapasyātmasaṁbhavān
Aditi brought forth the gods, who are the lords of three worlds. And Diti gave birth to the Daityas, offspring of Kasyapa.

निहत्य तांस्तु समरे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
देवानां वशमानीतं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम्

nihatya tāṁstu samare viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
devānāṁ vaśamānītaṁ trailokyamidamavyayam

O you cognisant of righteousness, formerly this earth, O hero, having the ocean for her garment, and furnished with mountains, belonged to the Daityas; and (gradually) they grew very powerful. And then this undeteriorating triune world was brought under the dominion of the celestials.

नैतदेको भवानेव करिष्यति विपर्ययम्
सुरैराचरितं पूर्वं कुरुष्वैतद्वचो मम

naitadeko bhavāneva kariṣyati viparyayam
surairācaritaṁ pūrvaṁ kuruṣvaitadvaco mama

So that you are not the only one that would act inimically (to your brother); but this course had formerly been pursued by both the celestials and the Asuras. Therefore do you act in conformity with my word.

एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहस्तेन दुरात्मना
चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं वै बाढमित्येव सोऽब्रवीत्

evamukto daśagrīvaḥ prahastena durātmanā
cintayitvā muhūrtaṁ vai bāḍhamityeva so'bravīt

Thus exhorted, the Ten-necked one, with a delighted heart, reflecting for a moment, said, 'Very well.' And wrought up with delight, the Ten-necked one endowed with prowess the very same day went to the forest, accompanied by the night-rangers.

त्रिकूटस्थः स तु तदा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः
प्रेषयामास दौत्येन प्रहस्तं वाक्यकोविदम्

trikūṭasthaḥ sa tu tadā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
preṣayāmāsa dautyena prahastaṁ vākyakovidam
Arriving at Trikuta, that one skilled in speechthe night-ranger, Ravana-sent Prahasta in the ca vacity of an ambassador:

प्रहस्त शीघ्रं गत्वा त्वं ब्रूहि नैरृतपुंगवम्
वचनान्मम वित्तेशं सामपूर्वमिदं वचः

prahasta śīghraṁ gatvā tvaṁ brūhi nairṛtapuṁgavam
vacanānmama vitteśaṁ sāmapūrvamidaṁ vacaḥ
O Prahasta, hie you; and tell the foremost of Naistas-the lord of riches-in my words informed with mildness.

इयं लङ्का पुरी राजन्राक्षसानां महात्मनाम्
त्वया निवेशिता सौम्य नैतद्युक्तं तवानघ

iyaṁ laṅkā purī rājanrākṣasānāṁ mahātmanām
tvayā niveśitā saumya naitadyuktaṁ tavānagha
This city of Lanka, O king, belongs to the high-souled Raksasas; but you have established yourself in her. This, O sinless one, is not proper for you.

तद्भवान्यदि साम्नैतां दद्यादतुलविक्रम
कृता भवेन्मम प्रीतिर्धर्मश्चैवानुपालितः

tadbhavānyadi sāmnaitāṁ dadyādatulavikrama
kṛtā bhavenmama prītirdharmaścaivānupālitaḥ
Therefore, O you of unrivalled prowess, if you should render the same (back), I shall be highly gratified; and righteousness also you will maintain.

प्रहस्तादपि संश्रुत्य देवो वैश्रवणो वचः
प्रत्युवाच प्रहस्तं तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः

prahastādapi saṁśrutya devo vaiśravaṇo vacaḥ
pratyuvāca prahastaṁ taṁ vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ
Hearing these words from Prahasta, the god Vaisravana, best of those skilled in speech, answered the former.

ब्रूहि गच्छ दशग्रीवं पुरी राज्यं च यन्मम
तवाप्येतन्महाबाहो भुङ्क्ष्वैतद्धतकण्टकम्

brūhi gaccha daśagrīvaṁ purī rājyaṁ ca yanmama
tavāpyetanmahābāho bhuṅkṣvaitaddhatakaṇṭakam
Go and tell the Ten-necked one, as this city and this kingdom are mine, so they are your, O mighty-armed one. Do you enjoy this kingdom without a foe.

एष तात दशग्रीवो दूतं प्रेषितवान्मम
दीयतां नगरी लङ्का पूर्वं रक्षोगणोषिता
मयात्र यदनुष्ठेयं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रत

eṣa tāta daśagrīvo dūtaṁ preṣitavānmama
dīyatāṁ nagarī laṅkā pūrvaṁ rakṣogaṇoṣitā
mayātra yadanuṣṭheyaṁ tanmamācakṣva suvrata

May my kingdom and wealth never undergo division when you are present! 'Having said this, the lord of riches sought the side of his sire, and, paying him reverence, he communicated Ravana's wish to him:' My father, this Tennecked one had sent a messenger to me, saying, Give (back) the city Lanka, which had before been inhabited by hosts of Raksasa. Now, O you of excellent vows, do you tell me what I should do.

ब्रह्मर्षिस्त्वेवमुक्तोऽसौ विश्रवा मुनिपुंगवः
उवाच धनदं वाक्यं शृणु पुत्र वचो मम

brahmarṣistvevamukto'sau viśravā munipuṁgavaḥ
uvāca dhanadaṁ vākyaṁ śṛṇu putra vaco mama
Thus accosted, that foremost of ascetics, the Brahmarsi Visrava spoke to the lord of riches (standing) with joined hands, 'O son, listen to my words.

दशग्रीवो महाबाहुरुक्तवान्मम संनिधौ
मया निर्भर्त्सितश्चासीद्बहुधोक्तः सुदुर्मतिः

daśagrīvo mahābāhuruktavānmama saṁnidhau
mayā nirbhartsitaścāsīdbahudhoktaḥ sudurmatiḥ

The mighty-armed Ten-necked one had (once); spoken in my presence (to that effect). Thereat I greatly rebuked that wicked-minded one; and I said again and again in anger, You disregard (your religion and honour).

वरप्रदानसंमूढो मान्यामान्यं सुदुर्मतिः
न वेत्ति मम शापाच्च प्रकृतिं दारुणां गतः

varapradānasaṁmūḍho mānyāmānyaṁ sudurmatiḥ
na vetti mama śāpācca prakṛtiṁ dāruṇāṁ gataḥ

Do you listen to my words fraught with religion and profit. Of a wicked heart, you, with your understanding spoilt in consequence of the granting of the boon, can not distinguish between those deserving honour and those not; and, further, through my curse, you have come by fierce nature.

तस्माद्गच्छ महाबाहो कैलासं धरणीधरम्
निवेशय निवासार्थं त्यज लङ्कां सहानुगः

tasmādgaccha mahābāho kailāsaṁ dharaṇīdharam
niveśaya nivāsārthaṁ tyaja laṅkāṁ sahānugaḥ
Therefore, O mighty-armed one, go to the mountain, Kailasa. Do you, along with your retainers, for the purpose of dwelling there, take up your quarters (there).

तत्र मन्दाकिनी रम्या नदीनां प्रवरा नदी
काञ्चनैः सूर्यसंकाशैः पङ्कजैः संवृतोदका

tatra mandākinī ramyā nadīnāṁ pravarā nadī
kāñcanaiḥ sūryasaṁkāśaiḥ paṅkajaiḥ saṁvṛtodakā
There flowes the Mandakini best of streams, with her water covered with golden lotuses resembling suns, as also with lilies and blue lotuses and various other fragment flowers.

न हि क्षमं त्वया तेन वैरं धनद रक्षसा
जानीषे हि यथानेन लब्धः परमको वरः

na hi kṣamaṁ tvayā tena vairaṁ dhanada rakṣasā
jānīṣe hi yathānena labdhaḥ paramako varaḥ

And coming there frequently, celestials with Gandharvas and Apsaras and serpents and Kinnaras, ever sport there. O lord of riches, you ought not to enter into hostilities with that Raksasa. You know how he has obtained a great boon.

एवमुक्तो गृहीत्वा तु तद्वचः पितृगौरवात्
सदारपौरः सामात्यः सवाहनधनो गतः

evamukto gṛhītvā tu tadvacaḥ pitṛgauravāt
sadārapauraḥ sāmātyaḥ savāhanadhano gataḥ
Thus addressed, Vaisravana, for the sake of his father's dignity, with his wives and sons, with his counsellors and his vehicles and wealth went (to Kailasa).

प्रहस्तस्तु दशग्रीवं गत्वा सर्वं न्यवेदयत्
शून्या सा नगरी लङ्का त्रिंशद्योजनमायता
प्रविश्य तां सहास्माभिः स्वधर्मं तत्र पालय

prahastastu daśagrīvaṁ gatvā sarvaṁ nyavedayat
śūnyā sā nagarī laṅkā triṁśadyojanamāyatā
praviśya tāṁ sahāsmābhiḥ svadharmaṁ tatra pālaya
The city of Lanka is (now) empty. Renouncing her, the bestower of riches has gone out of her. (Now) entering into her, along with us, do you there maintain your own religion.

स चाभिषिक्तः क्षणदाचरैस्तदा; निवेशयामास पुरीं दशाननः
निकामपूर्णा च बभूव सा पुरी; निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः

sa cābhiṣiktaḥ kṣaṇadācaraistadā; niveśayāmāsa purīṁ daśānanaḥ
nikāmapūrṇā ca babhūva sā purī; niśācarairnīlabalāhakopamaiḥ
Having been installed, that night-ranger the Ten-faced one dwelt in that city; and that city teemed with night-rangers resembling dark clouds.

धनेश्वरस्त्वथ पितृवाक्यगौरवा;न्न्यवेशयच्छशिविमले गिरौ पुरीम्
स्वलंकृतैर्भवनवरैर्विभूषितां; पुरंदरस्येव तदामरावतीम्

dhaneśvarastvatha pitṛvākyagauravā;nnyaveśayacchaśivimale girau purīm
svalaṁkṛtairbhavanavarairvibhūṣitāṁ; puraṁdarasyeva tadāmarāvatīm
The lord of riches, for the sake of his father's dignity, dwelt in a palace situated on the hill bright as moon-light, graced with ornamented superb piles; even as Purandara dwells in Amaravati.

राक्षसेन्द्रोऽभिषिक्तस्तु भ्रातृभ्यां सहितस्तदा
ततः प्रदानं राक्षस्या भगिन्याः समचिन्तयत्

rākṣasendro'bhiṣiktastu bhrātṛbhyāṁ sahitastadā
tataḥ pradānaṁ rākṣasyā bhaginyāḥ samacintayat
The lord of Raksasas was installed along with his brothers. And then he thought of the giving away in marriage of his Raksasi sister.

ददौ तां कालकेयाय दानवेन्द्राय राक्षसीम्
स्वसां शूर्पणखां नाम विद्युज्जिह्वाय नामतः

dadau tāṁ kālakeyāya dānavendrāya rākṣasīm
svasāṁ śūrpaṇakhāṁ nāma vidyujjihvāya nāmataḥ
Then that Raksasa bestowed his sister, the Raksasi Surpanakha, on that lord of the Danavas and king of the Kalakesa Vidyujjihva.

कन्यासहायं तं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः
अपृच्छत्को भवानेको निर्मनुष्य मृगे वने

kanyāsahāyaṁ taṁ dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
apṛcchatko bhavāneko nirmanuṣya mṛge vane

Having given her away, the Raksasa was wandering about for the purpose of hunting, when, o Rama, he happened to see Diti's son, named Maya. And seeing him accompanied by his daughter, that night-ranger the Ten-necked one asked him, saying, 'Who are you that (wanderest) alone in this first devoid of men as well as deer? And are you accompanied by this one having the eyes of a young deer?' Thereat Maya, O Rama, answered that nightranger, when he had asked this.

तत्राहमरतिं विन्दंस्तया हीनः सुदुःखितः
तस्मात्पुराद्दुहितरं गृहीत्वा वनमागतः

tatrāhamaratiṁ vindaṁstayā hīnaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ
tasmātpurādduhitaraṁ gṛhītvā vanamāgataḥ
From then, taking my daughter, I have come to this wood. This, O king, is my daughter, grown in her womb.

कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि नराणां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम्
कन्या हि द्वे कुले नित्यं संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति

kanyāpitṛtvaṁ duḥkhaṁ hi narāṇāṁ mānakāṅkṣiṇām
kanyā hi dve kule nityaṁ saṁśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati

I have come hither with her, seeing of her husband. Verily being father to a daughter is misery to everyone that seekes one's honour. A daughter, forsooth, stayes, ever placing the two lines* in uncertainity. *The lines, namely, of her father and mother. The line of a mother as distinct from that of a father would be impossible under the present economy of Hindu society inasmuch as, as soon as a girl is married, she by that ceremony leaves her father's line and becomes incorporated with that of her husband. But this seems to have been otherwise in ancient times, This opens up an interesting social problem for the research of orientalists.

द्वौ सुतौ तु मम त्वस्यां भार्यायां संबभूवतुः
मायावी प्रथमस्तात दुन्दुभिस्तदनन्तरम्

dvau sutau tu mama tvasyāṁ bhāryāyāṁ saṁbabhūvatuḥ
māyāvī prathamastāta dundubhistadanantaram
On this wife of mine I have also beget two sons. The first is Mayavi and the next Dundubhi.

एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः
त्वामिदानीं कथं तात जानीयां को भवानिति

etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ
tvāmidānīṁ kathaṁ tāta jānīyāṁ ko bhavāniti
Thus have I truly related to everything to you that had asked for it. But, my child, how can I know you now? Who are you?

एवमुक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रो विनीतमिदमब्रवीत्
अहं पौलस्त्यतनयो दशग्रीवश्च नामतः

evamukto rākṣasendro vinītamidamabravīt
ahaṁ paulastyatanayo daśagrīvaśca nāmataḥ
Thus addressed, the Raksasas humbly said, 'Ten-necked by name, I am the son of ascetic, Paulastya, who was born as the third son of Brahma.

ब्रह्मर्षेस्तं सुतं ज्ञात्वा मयो हर्षमुपागतः
दातुं दुहितरं तस्य रोचयामास तत्र वै

brahmarṣestaṁ sutaṁ jñātvā mayo harṣamupāgataḥ
dātuṁ duhitaraṁ tasya rocayāmāsa tatra vai

Thus accosted, O Rama, by that lord of Raks asas, that Danava and foremost of Danavas, Maya; learning that he was the son of Maharsi, Paulastya, there desired in his heart to give away his daughter to him.

प्रहसन्प्राह दैत्येन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रमिदं वचः
इयं ममात्मजा राजन्हेमयाप्सरसा धृता
कन्या मन्दोदरी नाम पत्न्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्

prahasanprāha daityendro rākṣasendramidaṁ vacaḥ
iyaṁ mamātmajā rājanhemayāpsarasā dhṛtā
kanyā mandodarī nāma patnyarthaṁ pratigṛhyatām
This daughter of mine, O king, O king, borne by the Apsara, Hema, this my daughter named Mandodari do you accept as my wife.

बाढमित्येव तं राम दशग्रीवोऽभ्यभाषत
प्रज्वाल्य तत्र चैवाग्निमकरोत्पाणिसंग्रहम्

bāḍhamityeva taṁ rāma daśagrīvo'bhyabhāṣata
prajvālya tatra caivāgnimakarotpāṇisaṁgraham
'Well' thereupon the Ten-necked answered him, O Rama. And lighting a fire, he took her hand.

न हि तस्य मयो राम शापाभिज्ञस्तपोधनात्
विदित्वा तेन सा दत्ता तस्य पैतामहं कुलम्

na hi tasya mayo rāma śāpābhijñastapodhanāt
viditvā tena sā dattā tasya paitāmahaṁ kulam

O Rama, Maya knew the curse of the sage touching him.* Knowing this, he gave away his daughter, having regard to the race of Ravana's paternal grand-father; and he also conferred on him an exceedingly wonderful dart acquired through the most rigid austerities, by which he wounded Laksmana. *Respecting his birth.

एवं स कृतदारो वै लङ्कायामीश्वरः प्रभुः
गत्वा तु नगरं भार्ये भ्रातृभ्यां समुदावहत्

evaṁ sa kṛtadāro vai laṅkāyāmīśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
gatvā tu nagaraṁ bhārye bhrātṛbhyāṁ samudāvahat
Having thus wedded, that master-Lanka's lord-going (back) to that city, married his brothers.

गन्धर्वराजस्य सुतां शैलूषस्य महात्मनः
सरमां नाम धर्मज्ञो लेभे भार्यां विभीषणः

gandharvarājasya sutāṁ śailūṣasya mahātmanaḥ
saramāṁ nāma dharmajño lebhe bhāryāṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ

Ravana married the grand-daughter of Virocana (on the maternal side) named Vajrajvala, to Kumbhakarna. And Vibhisana obtained for his wife the righteous (damsel) named Sarama-daughter to the high-souled Sailusa-sovereign of the Gandharvas.

मात्रा तु तस्याः कन्यायाः स्नेहेनाक्रन्दितं वचः
सरो मा वर्धतेत्युक्तं ततः सा सरमाभवत्

mātrā tu tasyāḥ kanyāyāḥ snehenākranditaṁ vacaḥ
saro mā vardhatetyuktaṁ tataḥ sā saramābhavat

Sarama was born on the shores of the lake, Manasa, was swollen with water on the arrival of the rains, her mother, hearing her cries, affectionately said, Saro ma varddhata 'O lake, do not swell,' and from this circumstance, her name became Sarama.

एवं ते कृतदारा वै रेमिरे तत्र राक्षसाः
स्वां स्वां भार्यामुपादाय गन्धर्वा इव नन्दने

evaṁ te kṛtadārā vai remire tatra rākṣasāḥ
svāṁ svāṁ bhāryāmupādāya gandharvā iva nandane
Having thus wedded, those Raksasas, taking each his wife, set about sporting there, like to Gandharvas sporting in Nandana. And then was born Mandodari's son-Meghanada. Him you call Indarjit.

जातमात्रेण हि पुरा तेन राक्षससूनुना
रुदता सुमहान्मुक्तो नादो जलधरोपमः

jātamātreṇa hi purā tena rākṣasasūnunā
rudatā sumahānmukto nādo jaladharopamaḥ
As soon as he was born, Ravana's son, formerly crying, emitted a tremendous roar resembling the rumbling of clouds.

जडीकृतायां लङ्कायां तेन नादेन तस्य वै
पिता तस्याकरोन्नाम मेघनाद इति स्वयम्

jaḍīkṛtāyāṁ laṅkāyāṁ tena nādena tasya vai
pitā tasyākaronnāma meghanāda iti svayam
O Raghava, Lanka was petrified at his voice: and (accordingly) his sire himself kept his name, Meghanada.

सोऽवर्धत तदा राम रावणान्तःपुरे शुभे
रक्ष्यमाणो वरस्त्रीभिश्छन्नः काष्ठैरिवानलः

so'vardhata tadā rāma rāvaṇāntaḥpure śubhe
rakṣyamāṇo varastrībhiśchannaḥ kāṣṭhairivānalaḥ
O Rama, remaining hidden like a fire by fuel, Ravana's son, rejoicing (the bosoms of) his father and mother, grew up in Ravana's elegant inner apartments.

अथ लोकेश्वरोत्सृष्टा तत्र कालेन केनचित्
निद्रा समभवत्तीव्रा कुम्भकर्णस्य रूपिणी

atha lokeśvarotsṛṣṭā tatra kālena kenacit
nidrā samabhavattīvrā kumbhakarṇasya rūpiṇī
Once upon a time in came to pass that, despatched by the lord of creatures, Steep in her (native) form powerfully overpowered Kumbhakarna.

ततो भ्रातरमासीनं कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः
निद्रा मां बाधते राजन्कारयस्व ममालयम्

tato bhrātaramāsīnaṁ kumbhakarṇo'bravīdvacaḥ
nidrā māṁ bādhate rājankārayasva mamālayam
Then Kumbhakarna spoke to his brother, who was seated, 'O king, Sleep obstructs me. Do you, therefore, have my mansion made.

तत्र निद्रां समाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो निशाचरः
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि शयानो नावबुध्यते

tatra nidrāṁ samāviṣṭaḥ kumbhakarṇo niśācaraḥ
bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi śayāno nāvabudhyate
There, overcome with slumber, the wondrous strong Kumbhakarna, lying down for many thousand years, did not wake up.

उद्यानानि विचित्राणि नन्दनादीनि यानि च
तानि गत्वा सुसंक्रुद्धो भिनत्ति स्म दशाननः

udyānāni vicitrāṇi nandanādīni yāni ca
tāni gatvā susaṁkruddho bhinatti sma daśānanaḥ

While Kumbhakarna was overpowered by sleep, Dasanana* without let began to destroy Devarsis, Yaksas and Gandharvas, and going to graceful gardens, Nandana, etc., he devastated them (ruthlessly). *Henceforth we shall use this significant surname of Ravana, meaning Ten-faced.

नदीं गज इव क्रीडन्वृक्षान्वायुरिव क्षिपन्
नगान्वज्र इव सृष्टो विध्वंसयति नित्यशः

nadīṁ gaja iva krīḍanvṛkṣānvāyuriva kṣipan
nagānvajra iva sṛṣṭo vidhvaṁsayati nityaśaḥ
That Raksasa spread destruction, even as an elephant sporting agitates a river, as the wind bring down trees, or as the thunder-bolt rive mountain-peaks.

सौभ्रात्रदर्शनार्थं तु दूतं वैश्वरणस्तदा
लङ्कां संप्रेषयामास दशग्रीवस्य वै हितम्

saubhrātradarśanārthaṁ tu dūtaṁ vaiśvaraṇastadā
laṅkāṁ saṁpreṣayāmāsa daśagrīvasya vai hitam

Hearing of the doings of Dasagriva,* and remembering his conduct chiming in with his race, the righteous lord of riches Vaisravanashowing his fraternal affection, despatched a messenger to Lanka, seeking the welfare of Dasagriva. *Ten-necked.

स गत्वा नगरीं लङ्कामाससाद विभीषणम्
मानितस्तेन धर्मेण पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति

sa gatvā nagarīṁ laṅkāmāsasāda vibhīṣaṇam
mānitastena dharmeṇa pṛṣṭaścāgamanaṁ prati
Going to the city of Lanka, he presented himself before Vibhisana. And having received him with honour, he asked him as to the cause of his visit.

पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राज्ञो ज्ञातीनपि च बान्धवान्
सभायां दर्शयामास तमासीनं दशाननम्

pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṁ rājño jñātīnapi ca bāndhavān
sabhāyāṁ darśayāmāsa tamāsīnaṁ daśānanam
Having enquired after the welfare of the king as well as his kindred, Vibhisana, showed him to Dasanana seated in his court.

स दृष्ट्वा तत्र राजानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा
जयेन चाभिसंपूज्य तूष्णीमासीन्मुहूर्तकम्

sa dṛṣṭvā tatra rājānaṁ dīpyamānaṁ svatejasā
jayena cābhisaṁpūjya tūṣṇīmāsīnmuhūrtakam
Seeing the king there flaming in his own energy, he (the messenger), saluting him (Ravana) with the word Jaya* stood silent. *Jaya may mean (1) victory and (2) all the deities of the Hindu pantheon.

तस्योपनीते पर्यङ्के वरास्तरणसंवृते
उपविश्य दशग्रीवं दूतो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्

tasyopanīte paryaṅke varāstaraṇasaṁvṛte
upaviśya daśagrīvaṁ dūto vākyamathābravīt
The envoy addressed Dasagriva, seated on a superb couch, graced with a costly coverlet.

साधु पर्याप्तमेतावत्कृतश्चारित्रसंग्रहः
साधु धर्मे व्यवस्थानं क्रियतां यदि शक्यते

sādhu paryāptametāvatkṛtaścāritrasaṁgrahaḥ
sādhu dharme vyavasthānaṁ kriyatāṁ yadi śakyate

O king, I shall tell you all that your brother has said, worthy of both the character and race of your father and mother, Enough of wrong doing. Now you should mend your ways. If you can, stay in righteousness. I have seen Nandana ravaged; and I have heard of the sages slain, and Oking, of the preparations the deities are making against you.

निराकृतश्च बहुशस्त्वयाहं राक्षसाधिप
अपराद्धा हि बाल्याच्च रक्षणीयाः स्वबान्धवाः

nirākṛtaśca bahuśastvayāhaṁ rākṣasādhipa
aparāddhā hi bālyācca rakṣaṇīyāḥ svabāndhavāḥ
I have been utterly disregarded by you; but even if a boy should transgress, he should, for all that be protected by his family members.

अहं तु हिमवत्पृष्ठं गतो धर्ममुपासितुम्
रौद्रं व्रतं समास्थाय नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः

ahaṁ tu himavatpṛṣṭhaṁ gato dharmamupāsitum
raudraṁ vrataṁ samāsthāya niyato niyatendriyaḥ
Self-restrained and controlling my senses, I, adopting a terrific vow, had gone to the breast to the Himavan for practising righteousness.

तत्र देवो मया दृष्टः सह देव्योमया प्रभुः
सव्यं चक्षुर्मया चैव तत्र देव्यां निपातितम्

tatra devo mayā dṛṣṭaḥ saha devyomayā prabhuḥ
savyaṁ cakṣurmayā caiva tatra devyāṁ nipātitam

There I saw that lord of the gods in company with Uma. There I happened to cast my left eye on the goddess, for ‘knowing, O mighty king, who she was, and not for any other reason. Rudrani was staying then, wearing a surpassing form.

ततो देव्याः प्रभावेन दग्धं सव्यं ममेक्षणम्
रेणुध्वस्तमिव ज्योतिः पिङ्गलत्वमुपागतम्

tato devyāḥ prabhāvena dagdhaṁ savyaṁ mamekṣaṇam
reṇudhvastamiva jyotiḥ piṅgalatvamupāgatam
Thereupon through the divine energy of the goddess my left eye was burnt and seemed to be covered with dust, and its lustre became tawny.

ततोऽहमन्यद्विस्तीर्णं गत्वा तस्य गिरेस्तटम्
पूर्णं वर्षशतान्यष्टौ समवाप महाव्रतम्

tato'hamanyadvistīrṇaṁ gatvā tasya girestaṭam
pūrṇaṁ varṣaśatānyaṣṭau samavāpa mahāvratam
Then I, going to another spacious peak of the inountain, became engaged in silently observing a mighty vow.

समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिंस्तत्र देवो महेश्वरः
प्रीतः प्रीतेन मनसा प्राह वाक्यमिदं प्रभुः

samāpte niyame tasmiṁstatra devo maheśvaraḥ
prītaḥ prītena manasā prāha vākyamidaṁ prabhuḥ
On my term of restraint having been complete, that lord of the gods Mahesvara with a gratified heart addressed me, saying.

प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ तपसानेन सुव्रत
मया चैतद्व्रतं चीर्णं त्वया चैव धनाधिप

prīto'smi tava dharmajña tapasānena suvrata
mayā caitadvrataṁ cīrṇaṁ tvayā caiva dhanādhipa
O righteous one, you of fair vows, I am wellpleased with this asceticism of your. I also had observed this vow; and you also, O lord of riches, have done the same.

तृतीयः पुरुषो नास्ति यश्चरेद्व्रतमीदृशम्
व्रतं सुदुश्चरं ह्येतन्मयैवोत्पादितं पुरा

tṛtīyaḥ puruṣo nāsti yaścaredvratamīdṛśam
vrataṁ suduścaraṁ hyetanmayaivotpāditaṁ purā
A third person there is none that practise such a vow. This vow is hard to perform, and formerly it was I that introduced it.

तत्सखित्वं मया सार्धं रोचयस्व धनेश्वर
तपसा निर्जितत्वाद्धि सखा भव ममानघ

tatsakhitvaṁ mayā sārdhaṁ rocayasva dhaneśvara
tapasā nirjitatvāddhi sakhā bhava mamānagha
Therefore, O mild one, O lord of riches, do you contract friendship with me. And you have conquered me by your penances. Therefore, O be you my friend.

देव्या दग्धं प्रभावेन यच्च साव्यं तवेक्षणम्
एकाक्षि पिङ्गलेत्येव नाम स्थास्यति शाश्वतम्

devyā dagdhaṁ prabhāvena yacca sāvyaṁ tavekṣaṇam
ekākṣi piṅgaletyeva nāma sthāsyati śāśvatam

This your left eye has been burnt through the energy of the goddess, and has turned tawny in consequence of having seen the grace of the goddess; your shall be Ekaksipingala. Then at Saikara's command I sinless one, SO name ever have obtained the privilege of companionship (with him). Having come here I have heard of your evil designs.

तदधर्मिष्ठसंयोगान्निवर्त कुलदूषण
चिन्त्यते हि वधोपायः सर्षिसंघैः सुरैस्तव

tadadharmiṣṭhasaṁyogānnivarta kuladūṣaṇa
cintyate hi vadhopāyaḥ sarṣisaṁghaiḥ suraistava
Do you then desist from this impious course, tending to sully your line. The celestials along with the sages are pondering over the means of compassing your death.

एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः क्रुद्धः संरक्तलोचनः
हस्तान्दन्तांश संपीड्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह

evamukto daśagrīvaḥ kruddhaḥ saṁraktalocanaḥ
hastāndantāṁśa saṁpīḍya vākyametaduvāca ha
Thus addressed, the Ten necked one, with his eyes reddened in wrath, rubbing his hands and knashing his teeth, said.

विज्ञातं ते मया दूत वाक्यं यत्त्वं प्रभाषसे
नैव त्वमसि नैवासौ भ्रात्रा येनासि प्रेषितः

vijñātaṁ te mayā dūta vākyaṁ yattvaṁ prabhāṣase
naiva tvamasi naivāsau bhrātrā yenāsi preṣitaḥ

O messenger, I have learnt what you have uttered. Neither you nor this brother of mine by whom you have been despatched, (shall live); nor does the keeper of riches say what is for my good. And the fool makes me hear the circumstance of his having made friends with Mahesvara.

न हन्तव्यो गुरुर्ज्येष्ठो ममायमिति मन्यते
तस्य त्विदानीं श्रुत्वा मे वाक्यमेषा कृता मतिः

na hantavyo gururjyeṣṭho mamāyamiti manyate
tasya tvidānīṁ śrutvā me vākyameṣā kṛtā matiḥ
But now hearing his (utterances), even this is my resolve. Depending upon the might of my arms, I shall conquer the three worlds.

त्रीँल्लोकानपि जेष्यामि बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः
एतन्मुहूर्तमेषोऽहं तस्यैकस्य कृते च वै
चतुरो लोकपालांस्तान्नयिष्यामि यमक्षयम्

trī̐llokānapi jeṣyāmi bāhuvīryamupāśritaḥ
etanmuhūrtameṣo'haṁ tasyaikasya kṛte ca vai
caturo lokapālāṁstānnayiṣyāmi yamakṣayam
On his account solely I shall on the instant despatch the four Lokapalas to the abode of Death.

एवमुक्त्वा तु लङ्केशो दूतं खड्गेन जघ्निवान्
ददौ भक्षयितुं ह्येनं राक्षसानां दुरात्मनाम्

evamuktvā tu laṅkeśo dūtaṁ khaḍgena jaghnivān
dadau bhakṣayituṁ hyenaṁ rākṣasānāṁ durātmanām
Having said this, Lanka's lord killed the emissary with his sword and made him over to the wicked Raksasas for being eaten.

ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययनो रथमारुह्य रावणः
त्रैलोक्यविजयाकाङ्क्षी ययौ तत्र धनेश्वरः

tataḥ kṛtasvastyayano rathamāruhya rāvaṇaḥ
trailokyavijayākāṅkṣī yayau tatra dhaneśvaraḥ
Then, having performed Svastyayana, Ravana, ascending his car, went to where the lord of riches was, bent on conquering the three worlds.

धूम्राक्षेण च वीरेण नित्यं समरगृध्नुना
वृतः संप्रययौ श्रीमान्क्रोधाल्लोकान्दहन्निव

dhūmrākṣeṇa ca vīreṇa nityaṁ samaragṛdhnunā
vṛtaḥ saṁprayayau śrīmānkrodhāllokāndahanniva

Accompanied by his six counsellor Mohodara and Prahasta, Marica, Suka and Sarana, and the heroic Dhumraksa eager for encounter the graceful Ravana, elated with his strength sallied out, as if consuming all creatures with his wrath.

पुराणि स नदीः शैलान्वनान्युपवनानि च
अतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तेन कैलासं गिरिमाविशत्

purāṇi sa nadīḥ śailānvanānyupavanāni ca
atikramya muhūrtena kailāsaṁ girimāviśat
Leaving behind cities and steams and hills and woods and groves, he in a moment came to the mountain Kailasa.

तं निविष्टं गिरौ तस्मिन्राक्षसेन्द्रं निशम्य तु
राज्ञो भ्रातायमित्युक्त्वा गता यत्र धनेश्वरः

taṁ niviṣṭaṁ girau tasminrākṣasendraṁ niśamya tu
rājño bhrātāyamityuktvā gatā yatra dhaneśvaraḥ

And hearing that wicked-minded lord of Raks asas, breathing high spirits, had arrived at the mount in company with his counsellors, the Yaksas could not stay before that Raksasa, and knowing this one is the king's brother,' went to where the lord of riches was.

गत्वा तु सर्वमाचख्युर्भ्रातुस्तस्य विनिश्चयम्
अनुज्ञाता ययुश्चैव युद्धाय धनदेन ते

gatvā tu sarvamācakhyurbhrātustasya viniścayam
anujñātā yayuścaiva yuddhāya dhanadena te
Going to him they in full related all about the doings of his brother. And on being permitted by the bestower of treasures, they went out for battle.

ततो बलस्य संक्षोभः सागरस्येव वर्धतः
अभून्नैरृतराजस्य गिरिं संचालयन्निव

tato balasya saṁkṣobhaḥ sāgarasyeva vardhataḥ
abhūnnairṛtarājasya giriṁ saṁcālayanniva
And then, like to the agitation of the ocean, there took place a mighty ferment of the forces of the Naista king, as if making the mountain tremble.

ततो युद्धं समभवद्यक्षराक्षससंकुलम्
व्यथिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः

tato yuddhaṁ samabhavadyakṣarākṣasasaṁkulam
vyathitāścābhavaṁstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ
And then there took place an encounter between the Yaksas and the Raksasa were smitten fiercely.

तं दृष्ट्वा तादृशं सैन्यं दशग्रीवो निशाचरः
हर्षान्नादं ततः कृत्वा रोषात्समभिवर्तत

taṁ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṁ sainyaṁ daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
harṣānnādaṁ tataḥ kṛtvā roṣātsamabhivartata
And finding his forces in that plight, Dasagriva set up full many a cheerful shout and in wrath began to speak.

ये तु ते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सचिवा घोरविक्रमः
ते सहस्रं सहस्राणामेकैकं समयोधयन्

ye tu te rākṣasendrasya sacivā ghoravikramaḥ
te sahasraṁ sahasrāṇāmekaikaṁ samayodhayan
Each of the terrific and mightiest councillors of the Raksasa-chief, coped with a thousand Yaksas.

स दुरात्मा समुद्यम्य कालदण्डोपमां गदाम्
प्रविवेश ततः सैन्यं नयन्यक्षान्यमक्षयम्

sa durātmā samudyamya kāladaṇḍopamāṁ gadām
praviveśa tataḥ sainyaṁ nayanyakṣānyamakṣayam
And that high-souled one, raising up his mace resembling the rod itself of Time, entered into that army, despatching Yaksas to the abode of Yama.

स कक्षमिव विस्तीर्णं शुष्केन्धनसमाकुलम्
वातेनाग्निरिवायत्तोऽदहत्सैन्यं सुदारुणम्

sa kakṣamiva vistīrṇaṁ śuṣkendhanasamākulam
vātenāgnirivāyatto'dahatsainyaṁ sudāruṇam
And as a flaming fire burn up an extensive sward of grass stocked with dry fire-wood, he began to consume that Yaksa army.

तैस्तु तस्य मृधेऽमात्यैर्महोदरशुकादिभिः
अल्पावशिष्टास्ते यक्षाः कृता वातैरिवाम्बुदाः

taistu tasya mṛdhe'mātyairmahodaraśukādibhiḥ
alpāvaśiṣṭāste yakṣāḥ kṛtā vātairivāmbudāḥ
And as the wind scatter clouds, the small remnant of Yaksa army was scattered by the redoubtable councillors (of Ravana) Mahodara, Suka, etc.

हतानां स्वर्गसंस्थानां युध्यतां पृथिवीतले
प्रेक्षतामृषिसंघानां न बभूवान्तरं दिवि

hatānāṁ svargasaṁsthānāṁ yudhyatāṁ pṛthivītale
prekṣatāmṛṣisaṁghānāṁ na babhūvāntaraṁ divi

And no room was left (in the sky) in consequence of its being thronged by hosts of sages; and warriors, wounded and rushing for conflict, and (finally) ascending heaven.* *The idea of the author is: "The welkin was thronged with sages as well as warriors, who swelled the ranks of the sages stationed in the sky, by ascending heaven after having fallen in fight.”

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः
अगमत्सुमहान्यक्षो नाम्ना संयोधकण्टकः

etasminnantare rāma vistīrṇabalavāhanaḥ
agamatsumahānyakṣo nāmnā saṁyodhakaṇṭakaḥ
In the meantime, o Rama, a Yaksa named Sanyodhakantaka, accompanied by an extensive force and a large number of vehicles, on being despatched, rushed (on the foe).

तेन यक्षेण मारीचो विष्णुनेव समाहतः
पतितः पृथिवीं भेजे क्षीणपुण्य इवाम्बरात्

tena yakṣeṇa mārīco viṣṇuneva samāhataḥ
patitaḥ pṛthivīṁ bheje kṣīṇapuṇya ivāmbarāt
And wounded in the conflict (by Sanyodhakantaka) with his discus, as if by Visnu himself, Marica toppled down to the ground from the mountain, like to a planet whose merit has waned.

प्राप्तसंज्ञो मुहूर्तेन विश्रम्य च निशाचरः
तं यक्षं योधयामास स च भग्नः प्रदुद्रुवे

prāptasaṁjño muhūrtena viśramya ca niśācaraḥ
taṁ yakṣaṁ yodhayāmāsa sa ca bhagnaḥ pradudruve
And in a moment regaining his consciousness and resting (for a while), that night-ranger fought with the Yaksa; and thereat, on being defeated, he* fled. *The Yaksa, that is.)

ततो राम दशग्रीवं प्रविशन्तं निशाचरम्
सूर्यभानुरिति ख्यातो द्वारपालो न्यवारयत्

tato rāma daśagrīvaṁ praviśantaṁ niśācaram
sūryabhānuriti khyāto dvārapālo nyavārayat

Then (Ravana) entered within the gate-way (of the place), garnished with gold, and decked with lapises and silver, And thereat, o king, the warder named Suryabhanu prevented the nightranger Dasagriva as he was entering.

स तु तेनैव तं यक्षं तोरणेन समाहनत्
नादृश्यत तदा यक्षो भस्म तेन कृतस्तु सः

sa tu tenaiva taṁ yakṣaṁ toraṇena samāhanat
nādṛśyata tadā yakṣo bhasma tena kṛtastu saḥ
And on being struck by the same gate-way, the Yaksa ceased to be seen, his body having then been consumed to ashes.

ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे यक्षा दृष्ट्वा पराक्रमम्
ततो नदीर्गुहाश्चैव विविशुर्भयपीडिताः

tataḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve yakṣā dṛṣṭvā parākramam
tato nadīrguhāścaiva viviśurbhayapīḍitāḥ
And witnessing the prowess of the Raksasa, all began to flee; and then they afflicted with affright, fatigued, and with pale faces entered into rivers and caves, leaving their arms behind.

तत्र माणिचारो नाम यक्षः परमदुर्जयः
वृतो यक्षसहस्रैः स चतुर्भिः समयोधयत्

tatra māṇicāro nāma yakṣaḥ paramadurjayaḥ
vṛto yakṣasahasraiḥ sa caturbhiḥ samayodhayat
Thus addressed, the mighty-armed and invincible Manibhadra, surrounded by four thousand Yaksas began the fight.

ते गदामुसलप्रासशक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः
अभिघ्नन्तो रणे यक्षा राक्षसानभिदुद्रुवुः

te gadāmusalaprāsaśaktitomaramudgaraiḥ
abhighnanto raṇe yakṣā rākṣasānabhidudruvuḥ
And attacking the Raksasas with maces and clubs and bearded darts, and with darts tomoras and bludgeons, the Yaksas rushed at (their adversaries).

ततः प्रहस्तेन तदा सहस्रं निहतं रणे
महोदरेण गदया सहस्रमपरं हतम्

tataḥ prahastena tadā sahasraṁ nihataṁ raṇe
mahodareṇa gadayā sahasramaparaṁ hatam
And a thousand of the Yaksas were slain by Prasasta in the conflict; and another thousand of capable warriors were slain by Mahodara.

क्रुद्धेन च तदा राम मारीचेन दुरात्मना
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण द्वे सहस्रे निपातिते

kruddhena ca tadā rāma mārīcena durātmanā
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa dve sahasre nipātite
O king, in the twinkling of an eye Marica, waxing wroth and eager for encounter brought down two thousand (of enemy's soldiers).

धूम्राक्षेण समागम्य माणिभद्रो महारणे
मुसलेनोरसि क्रोधात्ताडितो न च कम्पितः

dhūmrākṣeṇa samāgamya māṇibhadro mahāraṇe
musalenorasi krodhāttāḍito na ca kampitaḥ
And Dhumraksa, confronting Manibhadra in the mighty conflict hit him as the chest with a bludgeon; but he did not move thereat.

ततो गदां समाविध्य माणिभद्रेण राक्षसः
धूम्राक्षस्ताडितो मूर्ध्नि विह्वलो निपपात ह

tato gadāṁ samāvidhya māṇibhadreṇa rākṣasaḥ
dhūmrākṣastāḍito mūrdhni vihvalo nipapāta ha
Then Manibhadra dealt the Raksasa a blow with his mace; and thereat Dhumraksa smite at the head fell down senseless (on the ground).

धूम्राक्षं ताडितं दृष्ट्वा पतितं शोणितोक्षितम्
अभ्यधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धो माणिभद्रं दशाननः

dhūmrākṣaṁ tāḍitaṁ dṛṣṭvā patitaṁ śoṇitokṣitam
abhyadhāvatsusaṁkruddho māṇibhadraṁ daśānanaḥ
And seeing Dhumraksa wounded and down, bathed in blood, the Ten-necked Ravana rushed at Manibhadra in the encounter.

तं क्रुद्धमभिधावन्तं युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम्
शक्तिभिस्ताडयामास तिसृभिर्यक्षपुंगवः

taṁ kruddhamabhidhāvantaṁ yugāntāgnimivotthitam
śaktibhistāḍayāmāsa tisṛbhiryakṣapuṁgavaḥ
Then that foremost of Yaksas hit Dasanana with three darts as he was rushing in wrath.

ततो राक्षसराजेन ताडितो गदया रणे
तस्य तेन प्रहारेण मुकुटः पार्श्वमागतः
तदा प्रभृति यक्षोऽसौ पार्श्वमौलिरिति स्मृतः

tato rākṣasarājena tāḍito gadayā raṇe
tasya tena prahāreṇa mukuṭaḥ pārśvamāgataḥ
tadā prabhṛti yakṣo'sau pārśvamauliriti smṛtaḥ
And on being thus hit, (Ravana) struck at Manibhadra's head: and at that stroke his crown was depressed at one side.

तस्मिंस्तु विमुखे यक्षे माणिभद्रे महात्मनि
संनादः सुमहान्राम तस्मिञ्शैले व्यवर्धत

tasmiṁstu vimukhe yakṣe māṇibhadre mahātmani
saṁnādaḥ sumahānrāma tasmiñśaile vyavardhata
From that day forth that Yaksa remained with his head hollow on one side. And on the highsouled Manibhadra having been baffled, a great uproar, O king rose in that mountain.

ततो दूरात्प्रददृशे धनाध्यक्षो गदाधरः
शुक्रप्रोष्टःपदाभ्यां च शङ्खपद्मसमावृतः

tato dūrātpradadṛśe dhanādhyakṣo gadādharaḥ
śukraproṣṭaḥpadābhyāṁ ca śaṅkhapadmasamāvṛtaḥ
Then at a distance, the lord of riches, mace in hand, accompanied by Sukra and Praushthapada and Padma and Sanka saw (Ravana) in the field.

स दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं संख्ये शापाद्विभ्रष्टगौरवम्
उवाच वचनं धीमान्युक्तं पैतामहे कुले

sa dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṁ saṁkhye śāpādvibhraṣṭagauravam
uvāca vacanaṁ dhīmānyuktaṁ paitāmahe kule
Seeing his brother in the encounter with his glory obscured through the curse (he had ere this come by), the intelligent (Lord of Yaksas) spoke in words worthy of the line of his grand-father.

मया त्वं वार्यमाणोऽपि नावगच्छसि दुर्मते
पश्चादस्य फलं प्राप्य ज्ञास्यसे निरयं गतः

mayā tvaṁ vāryamāṇo'pi nāvagacchasi durmate
paścādasya phalaṁ prāpya jñāsyase nirayaṁ gataḥ
As, O wicked-minded one, you desistest not, albeit forbidden by me, you shall, afterwards attaining the fruit of this, and repairing to hell, know (the fate that follow there).

यो हि मोहाद्विषं पीत्वा नावगच्छति मानवः
परिणामे स वि मूढो जानीते कर्मणः फलम्

yo hi mohādviṣaṁ pītvā nāvagacchati mānavaḥ
pariṇāme sa vi mūḍho jānīte karmaṇaḥ phalam
That perverse one, that through ignorance having drunk poison, neglects to adopt proper measures, know the consequence of his act ultimately.

दैवतानि हि नन्दन्ति धर्मयुक्तेन केनचित्
येन त्वमीदृशं भावं नीतस्तच्च न बुध्यसे

daivatāni hi nandanti dharmayuktena kenacit
yena tvamīdṛśaṁ bhāvaṁ nītastacca na budhyase
The gods have set their face against you on account of a certain misdeed of your; and having for this, been reduced to this condition, you do not understand things.

यो हि मातॄः पितॄन्भ्रातॄनाचर्यांश्चावमन्यते
स पश्यति फलं तस्य प्रेतराजवशं गतः

yo hi mātṝḥ pitṝnbhrātṝnācaryāṁścāvamanyate
sa paśyati phalaṁ tasya pretarājavaśaṁ gataḥ

He that dishonour his father and mother* and spiritual preceptor, reap the fruit of his act on coming under the sway of the sovereign of the dead. *Unless he serve his parents, his heart does not incline to piety.

अध्रुवे हि शरीरे यो न करोति तपोऽर्जनम्
स पश्चात्तप्यते मूढो मृतो दृष्ट्वात्मनो गतिम्

adhruve hi śarīre yo na karoti tapo'rjanam
sa paścāttapyate mūḍho mṛto dṛṣṭvātmano gatim
Having regard that this body is uncertain, that foolish person, that does not acquire asceticism, dying go the way that he deserve.

कस्यचिन्न हि दुर्बुधेश्छन्दतो जायते मतिः
यादृशं कुरुते कर्म तादृशं फलमश्नुते

kasyacinna hi durbudheśchandato jāyate matiḥ
yādṛśaṁ kurute karma tādṛśaṁ phalamaśnute
The mind of a perverse man does not willingly incline towards good; and as he acts, he gets the fruits (he reaps as he sows).

बुद्धिं रूपं बलं वित्तं पुत्रान्माहात्म्यमेव च
प्रप्नुवन्ति नराः सर्वं स्वकृतैः पूर्वकर्मभिः

buddhiṁ rūpaṁ balaṁ vittaṁ putrānmāhātmyameva ca
prapnuvanti narāḥ sarvaṁ svakṛtaiḥ pūrvakarmabhiḥ
In this world people, making their own good fortune and beauty, strength, sons, wealth and valour, gain these by virtue of their pious acts.

एवं निरयगामी त्वं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी
न त्वां समभिभाषिष्ये दुर्वृत्तस्यैष निर्णयः

evaṁ nirayagāmī tvaṁ yasya te matirīdṛśī
na tvāṁ samabhibhāṣiṣye durvṛttasyaiṣa nirṇayaḥ
Being given to such iniquitous acts, you will go to hell; and your designs being such, I will not hold parley with you.

एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तेन तस्यामात्याः समाहताः
मारीचप्रमुखाः सर्वे विमुखा विप्रदुद्रुवुः

evamuktvā tatastena tasyāmātyāḥ samāhatāḥ
mārīcapramukhāḥ sarve vimukhā vipradudruvuḥ
Honest people should act carefully in connection with the wicked.' Thus reprimanded by him, his (Ravana's) councillors, headed by Marica, on being struck, took to their heels.

ततस्तेन दशग्रीवो यक्षेन्द्रेण महात्मना
गदयाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि न च स्थानाद्व्यकम्पत

tatastena daśagrīvo yakṣendreṇa mahātmanā
gadayābhihato mūrdhni na ca sthānādvyakampata
Then Dasagriva on being Struck in the head with the mace by the lord of Yaksas, did not move from his place.

ततस्तौ राम निघ्नन्तावन्योन्यं परमाहवे
न विह्वलौ न च श्रान्तौ बभूवतुरमर्षणैः

tatastau rāma nighnantāvanyonyaṁ paramāhave
na vihvalau na ca śrāntau babhūvaturamarṣaṇaiḥ
And then, O Rama, the Yaksa and Raksasa, smiting each other in mighty encounter, did not get bewildered of experience fatigue.

आग्नेयमस्त्रं स ततो मुमोच धनदो रणे
वारुणेन दशग्रीवस्तदस्त्रं प्रत्यवारयत्

āgneyamastraṁ sa tato mumoca dhanado raṇe
vāruṇena daśagrīvastadastraṁ pratyavārayat
And then the bestower of riches discharged a fiery weapon at him; and thereat the lord of Raks asa resisted it with a Varuna weapon.

एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः
कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः

evaṁ sa tenābhihato vihvalaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ
kṛttamūla ivāśoko nipapāta dhanādhipaḥ
Thus smitten by him, the lord of wealth, baffled, toppled down to the earth covered with blood like an asoka whose roots have been hewn away.

ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स धनाधिपः
नन्दनं वनमानीय धनदो श्वासितस्तदा

tataḥ padmādibhistatra nidhibhiḥ sa dhanādhipaḥ
nandanaṁ vanamānīya dhanado śvāsitastadā
Thereat Padma and other Nidhi deities, surrounding the granter the granter of wealth, raised him up and brought him to the Nandana wood.

स जित्वा भ्रातरं राम धनदं राक्षसाधिपः
महासेनप्रसूतिं तु ययौ शरवणं ततः

sa jitvā bhrātaraṁ rāma dhanadaṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
mahāsenaprasūtiṁ tu yayau śaravaṇaṁ tataḥ
O Rama, having, vanquished his brother, the lord of riches, the king of Raksasas went to the great wood of reeds, where Mahasena was born.

अथापश्यद्दशग्रीवो रौक्मं शरवणं तदा
गभस्तिजालसंवीतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम्

athāpaśyaddaśagrīvo raukmaṁ śaravaṇaṁ tadā
gabhastijālasaṁvītaṁ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram

The Ten-necked Ravana saw the great golden wood of reeds. Furnished with networks of solar rays, and appearing like a second Sun, and ascending the mountain, he was surveying the heart of the forest, when, O Rama, Puspaka was (suddenly) deprived of its motion.

ततः पार्श्वमुपागम्य भवस्यानुचरो बली
नन्दीश्वर उवाचेदं राक्षसेन्द्रमशङ्कितः

tataḥ pārśvamupāgamya bhavasyānucaro balī
nandīśvara uvācedaṁ rākṣasendramaśaṅkitaḥ

As they were speaking thus, that attendant of Bhava, Nandi, terrific, of yellow black hue, dwarfish, frightful, with his head shaven, having short arms, and stout, coming up to them, said (this). And the lordly Nandi, undaunted, addressed the sovereign of the Raksasas, saying.

सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम्
प्राणिनामेव सर्वेषामगम्यः पर्वतः कृतः

suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṁ daityadānavarakṣasām
prāṇināmeva sarveṣāmagamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ
Desist you O Ten-necked one; Sankara sport in the mountain; and (now) He is incapable of being approached by every one, birds, serpents and Yaksas; gods, Gandharvas and Raksasas?

स रोषात्ताम्रनयनः पुष्पकादवरुह्य च
कोऽयं शंकर इत्युक्त्वा शैलमूलमुपागमत्

sa roṣāttāmranayanaḥ puṣpakādavaruhya ca
ko'yaṁ śaṁkara ityuktvā śailamūlamupāgamat

Hearing Nandi's speech, (Ravana), wrought up with wrath, his eyes coppery, and his earrings shaking, leapt down from Puspaka. And saying, 'who is this Sankara? and he came down to the base of the mount. He beheld there Nandi stationed at the side of the deity, supporting himself on his flaming dart, resembling a second Sankara.

स वानरमुखं दृष्ट्वा तमवज्ञाय राक्षसः
प्रहासं मुमुचे मौर्ख्यात्सतोय इव तोयदः

sa vānaramukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā tamavajñāya rākṣasaḥ
prahāsaṁ mumuce maurkhyātsatoya iva toyadaḥ
And seeing that one having the face of a monkey, the Raksasas, deriding him, burst out into laughter, and seemed as if a mass of clouds were sending roars.

संक्रुद्धो भगवान्नन्दी शंकरस्यापरा तनुः
अब्रवीद्राक्षसं तत्र दशग्रीवमुपस्थितम्

saṁkruddho bhagavānnandī śaṁkarasyāparā tanuḥ
abravīdrākṣasaṁ tatra daśagrīvamupasthitam
Thereat, growing enraged, the reverend Nandi Sankara's other body spoke into that Raksasa The Ten-necked one present there.

तस्मान्मद्रूपसंयुक्ता मद्वीर्यसमतेजसः
उत्पत्स्यन्ते वधार्थं हि कुलस्य तव वानराः

tasmānmadrūpasaṁyuktā madvīryasamatejasaḥ
utpatsyante vadhārthaṁ hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ

“As O Dasanana, deriding me for my monkery-form, you have indulged in a laughter resembling the bursting of thunder, do monkeys endowed with prowess, and possessed of my form and energy shall be born for compassing the destruction of your race.

किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं यत्त्वां निशाचर
न हन्तव्यो हतस्त्वं हि पूर्वमेव स्वकर्मभिः

kiṁ tvidānīṁ mayā śakyaṁ kartuṁ yattvāṁ niśācara
na hantavyo hatastvaṁ hi pūrvameva svakarmabhiḥ
But, O night-ranger, I can even now end you quite; yet I must not slay you for you have ere this been slain by your acts.

अचिन्तयित्वा स तदा नन्दिवाक्यं निशाचरः
पर्वतं तं समासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह

acintayitvā sa tadā nandivākyaṁ niśācaraḥ
parvataṁ taṁ samāsādya vākyametaduvāca ha
But without heeding Nandi's speech, that highly powerful one Dasanana coming to the mountain, said.

पुष्पकस्य गतिश्छिन्ना यत्कृते मम गच्छतः
तदेतच्छैलमुन्मूलं करोमि तव गोपते

puṣpakasya gatiśchinnā yatkṛte mama gacchataḥ
tadetacchailamunmūlaṁ karomi tava gopate
'O Gopati, I will even uproot this mountain, for whom Puspaka was deprived of its motion as I was journeying.

केन प्रभावेन भवस्तत्र क्रीडति राजवत्
विज्ञातव्यं न जानीषे भयस्थानमुपस्थितम्

kena prabhāvena bhavastatra krīḍati rājavat
vijñātavyaṁ na jānīṣe bhayasthānamupasthitam
It must be known by what influence Bhavasvara sport here king-like. He does not know that an occasion of fear has presented itself?'

एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्भुजान्प्रक्षिप्य पर्वते
तोलयामास तं शैलं समृगव्यालपादपम्

evamuktvā tato rājanbhujānprakṣipya parvate
tolayāmāsa taṁ śailaṁ samṛgavyālapādapam
Having said this, O Rama, Ravana seizing the mountain with his arms, lifted it up at once; and then the mountain trembled greatly.

ततो राम महादेवः प्रहसन्वीक्ष्य तत्कृतम्
पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया

tato rāma mahādevaḥ prahasanvīkṣya tatkṛtam
pādāṅguṣṭhena taṁ śailaṁ pīḍayāmāsa līlayā
Then, O Rama, Mahadeva foremost of the deities even Hara, as in sport pressed the mount with his great toe.

ततस्ते पीडितास्तस्य शैलस्याधो गता भुजाः
विस्मिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः

tataste pīḍitāstasya śailasyādho gatā bhujāḥ
vismitāścābhavaṁstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ
Thereat his arms, resembling blocks of stone felt the shock and then there the councillors of that Raksasa were struck with amaze.

रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां पीडनात्तथा
मुक्तो विरावः सुमहांस्त्रैलोक्यं येन पूरितम्

rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṁ pīḍanāttathā
mukto virāvaḥ sumahāṁstrailokyaṁ yena pūritam
The Raksasa, from wrath and the pain felt in his arms, set up a shout that shook the entire triune world.

ततः प्रीतो महादेवः शैलाग्रे विष्ठितस्तदा
मुक्त्वा तस्य भुजान्राजन्प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम्

tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāgre viṣṭhitastadā
muktvā tasya bhujānrājanprāha vākyaṁ daśānanam
Thereat that Lord Mahadeva, pleased, set free the hands of Dasanana stationed at the top of the mount, and O Rama, addressed him, saying.

यस्माल्लोकत्रयं त्वेतद्रावितं भयमागतम्
तस्मात्त्वं रावणो नाम नाम्ना तेन भविष्यसि

yasmāllokatrayaṁ tvetadrāvitaṁ bhayamāgatam
tasmāttvaṁ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā tena bhaviṣyasi

O Dasanana, pleased am I with you on account of your hymns. And as in consequence of your arms having been hurt by the mountain, you have uttered a terrific yell, which struck horror into the worlds and put them shaking, therefore, o King, your name shall be Ravana.

देवता मानुषा यक्षा ये चान्ये जगतीतले
एवं त्वामभिधास्यन्ति रावणं लोकरावणम्

devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale
evaṁ tvāmabhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṁ lokarāvaṇam
And deities and men, Yaksas and others living on earth shall call you Ravana terror to creatures,

गच्छ पौलस्त्य विस्रब्धः पथा येन त्वमिच्छसि
मया त्वमभ्यनुज्ञातो राक्षसाधिप गम्यताम्

gaccha paulastya visrabdhaḥ pathā yena tvamicchasi
mayā tvamabhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām
Go, O Paulastya, which way you wish with confidence, and permitted by me, O Lord of Raksasas, go you.

साक्षान्महेश्वरेणैवं कृतनामा स रावणः
अभिवाद्य महादेवं विमानं तत्समारुहत्

sākṣānmaheśvareṇaivaṁ kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ
abhivādya mahādevaṁ vimānaṁ tatsamāruhat
Having thus received his his name from Mahesvara, Ravana, saluting Mahadeva, ascended Puspaka.

ततो महीतले राम परिचक्राम रावणः
क्षत्रियान्सुमहावीर्यान्बाधमानस्ततस्ततः

tato mahītale rāma paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ
kṣatriyānsumahāvīryānbādhamānastatastataḥ

Then, O Rama, Ravana, began to go round the earth. And opposed at places, by the heroic Ksatriyas endowed with energy and irrepressible in fight, fight, who refused submission, he exterminated them along with their retainers.

अथ राजन्महाबाहुर्विचरन्स महीतलम्
हिमवद्वनमासाद्य परिचक्राम रावणः

atha rājanmahābāhurvicaransa mahītalam
himavadvanamāsādya paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ
Then, O King, the mighty-armed Ravana ranging the earth, came to Himavan and began to go round it.

तत्रापश्यत वै कन्यां कृष्टाजिनजटाधराम्
आर्षेण विधिना युक्तां तपन्तीं देवतामिव

tatrāpaśyata vai kanyāṁ kṛṣṭājinajaṭādharām
ārṣeṇa vidhinā yuktāṁ tapantīṁ devatāmiva
It came to pass that there he saw a damsel wearing a dark deer-skin and matted locks, leading the life of a saint, and flaming like a celestial.

स दृष्ट्वा रूपसंपन्नां कन्यां तां सुमहाव्रताम्
काममोहपरीतात्मा पप्रच्छ प्रहसन्निव

sa dṛṣṭvā rūpasaṁpannāṁ kanyāṁ tāṁ sumahāvratām
kāmamohaparītātmā papraccha prahasanniva
Seeing the girl observing high vows, endowed with beauty, he, with his soul overwhelmed with lust asked her, laughing.

किमिदं वर्तसे भद्रे विरुद्धं यौवनस्य ते
न हि युक्ता तवैतस्य रूपस्येयं प्रतिक्रिया

kimidaṁ vartase bhadre viruddhaṁ yauvanasya te
na hi yuktā tavaitasya rūpasyeyaṁ pratikriyā
How is it, o amiable one, that you act thus contrary to your youth? This course of life surely does not befit your beauty.

एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या तेनानार्येण रक्षसा
अब्रवीद्विधिवत्कृत्वा तस्यातिथ्यं तपोधना

evamuktā tu sā kanyā tenānāryeṇa rakṣasā
abravīdvidhivatkṛtvā tasyātithyaṁ tapodhanā
Thus accosted by Ravana, that illustrious girl, having asceticism for wealth, having received him hospitably in due form, said.

कुशध्वजो नाम पिता ब्रह्मर्षिर्मम धार्मिकः
बृहस्पतिसुतः श्रीमान्बुद्ध्या तुल्यो बृहस्पतेः

kuśadhvajo nāma pitā brahmarṣirmama dhārmikaḥ
bṛhaspatisutaḥ śrīmānbuddhyā tulyo bṛhaspateḥ
My sire is named Kusadhvaja a Brahmarsi of immeasurable energy, son to Behaspati, endowed with grace, and like to Bphaspati himself in intelligence.

तस्याहं कुर्वतो नित्यं वेदाभ्यासं महात्मनः
संभूता वान्मयी कन्या नाम्ना वेदवती स्मृता

tasyāhaṁ kurvato nityaṁ vedābhyāsaṁ mahātmanaḥ
saṁbhūtā vānmayī kanyā nāmnā vedavatī smṛtā
And while that high sound one was engaged in the daily study of the Vedas, I was born as his word-impregnated daughter, named Vedavati.

न च मां स पिता तेभ्यो दत्तवान्राक्षसेश्वर
कारणं तद्वदिष्यामि निशामय महाभुज

na ca māṁ sa pitā tebhyo dattavānrākṣaseśvara
kāraṇaṁ tadvadiṣyāmi niśāmaya mahābhuja

When the gods and the Gandharvas and the Yaksas, Raksasas, and Pannagas, coming to my sire asked for me, O foremost of Raksasas, my father did not bestow me on any one of them. And I shall you the reason thereof; listen, O long-armed one.

दातुमिच्छति धर्मात्मा तच्छ्रुत्वा बलदर्पितः
शम्भुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितोऽभवत्
तेन रात्रौ प्रसुप्तो मे पिता पापेन हिंसितः

dātumicchati dharmātmā tacchrutvā baladarpitaḥ
śambhurnāma tato rājā daityānāṁ kupito'bhavat
tena rātrau prasupto me pitā pāpena hiṁsitaḥ

My father's intended son-in-law was even Visnu sovereign of the celestials, and the lord of the triune world; and my father would not bestow me on any other. And hearing this, a certain king of the Daityas, named Sambhu proud, of his prowess was wrought up with wrath, and one night as my sire was on bed, that wicked one slew him. Thereat my forlorn mother, of exalted righteousness embracing my father's body entered into fire.

ततो मनोरथं सत्यं पितुर्नारायणं प्रति
करोमीति ममेच्छा च हृदये साधु विष्ठिता

tato manorathaṁ satyaṁ piturnārāyaṇaṁ prati
karomīti mamecchā ca hṛdaye sādhu viṣṭhitā
Then wishing to realise my father's wish touching Narayana, I have fixed my heart even upon him.

विज्ञातस्त्वं हि मे राजन्गच्छ पौलस्त्यनन्दन
जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते

vijñātastvaṁ hi me rājangaccha paulastyanandana
jānāmi tapasā sarvaṁ trailokye yaddhi vartate
I know you, O king. Go you, O son of Paulastya. By virtue of my asceticism I know all that takes place in these three regions.

सोऽब्रवीद्रावणस्तत्र तां कन्यां सुमहाव्रताम्
अवरुह्य विमानाग्रात्कन्दर्पशरपीडितः

so'bravīdrāvaṇastatra tāṁ kanyāṁ sumahāvratām
avaruhya vimānāgrātkandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ
Thereat descending from the front of his car, Ravana, affected with the shafts of Kandarpa, again addressed that girl, observant of a mighty VOW. a

अवलिप्तासि सुश्रोणि यस्यास्ते मतिरीदृशी
वृद्धानां मृगशावाक्षि भ्राजते धर्मसंचयः

avaliptāsi suśroṇi yasyāste matirīdṛśī
vṛddhānāṁ mṛgaśāvākṣi bhrājate dharmasaṁcayaḥ
O you of sharply hips, in as much as such is your intent, you must be very proud. O you having the eyes of young antelope, accumulation of religious merit suits old people.

त्वं सर्वगुणसंपन्ना नार्हसे कर्तुमीदृशम्
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी भीरु यौवने वार्धकं विधिम्

tvaṁ sarvaguṇasaṁpannā nārhase kartumīdṛśam
trailokyasundarī bhīru yauvane vārdhakaṁ vidhim
You, furnished with every perfection, should not talk thus. You are the paragon in these three worlds,. Your youth wax away.

कश्च तावदसौ यं त्वं विष्णुरित्यभिभाषसे
वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च
न मयासौ समो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसेऽङ्गने

kaśca tāvadasau yaṁ tvaṁ viṣṇurityabhibhāṣase
vīryeṇa tapasā caiva bhogena ca balena ca
na mayāsau samo bhadre yaṁ tvaṁ kāmayase'ṅgane
Who is he whom you call Visnu O mild one, neither in prowess, nor in asceticism, nor in enjoyment, nor in strength, is he my equal, whom, O damsel, you seek.

मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम्
मूर्धजेषु च तां रक्षः कराग्रेण परामृशत्

mā maivamiti sā kanyā tamuvāca niśācaram
mūrdhajeṣu ca tāṁ rakṣaḥ karāgreṇa parāmṛśat
Thus addressed there by Vedavati, the nightranger seized the girl by the hair.

ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान्हस्तेन साच्छिनत्
उवाचाग्निं समाधाय मरणाय कृतत्वरा

tato vedavatī kruddhā keśānhastena sācchinat
uvācāgniṁ samādhāya maraṇāya kṛtatvarā
Thereat Vedavati, wroth, cut off her hair with her hand transformed into a sword.

धर्षितायास्त्वयानार्य नेदानीं मम जीवितम्
रक्षस्तस्मात्प्रवेक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्ते हुताशनम्

dharṣitāyāstvayānārya nedānīṁ mama jīvitam
rakṣastasmātpravekṣyāmi paśyataste hutāśanam
You object, having been outraged by you I wish not to live. Therefore, O Raksasa, I will enter into fire in your very presence.

यस्मात्तु धर्षिता चाहमपापा चाप्यनाथवत्
तस्मात्तव वधार्थं वै समुत्पत्स्याम्यहं पुनः

yasmāttu dharṣitā cāhamapāpā cāpyanāthavat
tasmāttava vadhārthaṁ vai samutpatsyāmyahaṁ punaḥ
As I have in this world been dishonoured by you you are nefarious. I shall again be born to compass your destruction.

न हि शक्यः स्त्रिया पाप हन्तुं त्वं तु विशेषतः
शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत्

na hi śakyaḥ striyā pāpa hantuṁ tvaṁ tu viśeṣataḥ
śāpe tvayi mayotsṛṣṭe tapasaśca vyayo bhavet
It lie not in a female to slay a male intent on sin; and if I utter a curse, it shall cost my asceticism.

यदि त्वस्ति मया किंचित्कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा
तेन ह्ययोनिजा साध्वी भवेयं धर्मिणः सुता

yadi tvasti mayā kiṁcitkṛtaṁ dattaṁ hutaṁ tathā
tena hyayonijā sādhvī bhaveyaṁ dharmiṇaḥ sutā
But if I have done anything, given away any thing, offered oblations to the fire, then I shall be the chaste daughter of some virtuous person, albeit unborn of any female vessel.

एवमुक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा ज्वलन्तं वै हुताशनम्
पपात च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः

evamuktvā praviṣṭā sā jvalantaṁ vai hutāśanam
papāta ca divo divyā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ
Having delivered herself thus, she entered into the flaming fire; and thereat a celestial shower of blossoms rained all around from heaven.

पूर्वं क्रोधहतः शत्रुर्ययासौ निहतस्त्वया
समुपाश्रित्य शैलाभं तव वीर्यममानुषम्

pūrvaṁ krodhahataḥ śatruryayāsau nihatastvayā
samupāśritya śailābhaṁ tava vīryamamānuṣam
The enemy, endowed with the splendour of a hill, formerly that been slain by her, by help of your superhuman prowess.

एवमेषा महाभागा मर्त्येषूत्पद्यते पुनः
क्षेत्रे हलमुखग्रस्ते वेद्यामग्निशिखोपमा

evameṣā mahābhāgā martyeṣūtpadyate punaḥ
kṣetre halamukhagraste vedyāmagniśikhopamā
