tadavasthāṁ ca tāṁ dṛṣṭvā mahātmā nalakūbaraḥ
abravītkimidaṁ bhadre pādayoḥ patitāsi me
Having seen her in that plight the high-souled Nalakubara said-"O fair one, what is this? Why have you placed yourself at my feet?”

सा तु निश्वसमाना च वेपमानाथ साञ्जलिः
तस्मै सर्वं यथातथ्यमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे

sā tu niśvasamānā ca vepamānātha sāñjaliḥ
tasmai sarvaṁ yathātathyamākhyātumupacakrame
Sighing heavily and trembling she with folded palms, related to him everything from the beginning to the end.

आयान्ती तेन दृष्टास्मि त्वत्सकाशमरिंदम
गृहीत्वा तेन पृष्टास्मि कस्य त्वमिति रक्षसा

āyāntī tena dṛṣṭāsmi tvatsakāśamariṁdama
gṛhītvā tena pṛṣṭāsmi kasya tvamiti rakṣasā

O lord, on his way to heaven, Dasagriva has arrived here and has spent the night with his army. While I was coming to you, O slayer of foes, I was seen by him. Then holding me he said-“Where are you going?"

मया तु सर्वं यत्सत्यं तद्धि तस्मै निवेदितम्
काममोहाभिभूतात्मा नाश्रौषीत्तद्वचो मम

mayā tu sarvaṁ yatsatyaṁ taddhi tasmai niveditam
kāmamohābhibhūtātmā nāśrauṣīttadvaco mama
I related to him everything truly. But being possessed by lust he did not pay heed to my, words.

याच्यमानो मया देव स्नुषा तेऽहमिति प्रभो
तत्सर्वं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा बलात्तेनास्मि धर्षिता

yācyamāno mayā deva snuṣā te'hamiti prabho
tatsarvaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā balāttenāsmi dharṣitā
He was again prayed by me, O lord, saying “I am your daughter-in-law." But neglecting that he ravished me.

एवं त्वमपराधं मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि मानद
न हि तुल्यं बलं सौम्य स्त्रियाश्च पुरुषस्य च

evaṁ tvamaparādhaṁ me kṣantumarhasi mānada
na hi tulyaṁ balaṁ saumya striyāśca puruṣasya ca
O you of firm vows, it behove you to forgive me for this folly. O gentle one, a woman's strength can never equal that of a man.

एवं श्रुत्वा तु संक्रुद्धस्तदा वैश्वरणात्मजः
धर्षणां तां परां श्रुत्वा ध्यानं संप्रविवेश ह

evaṁ śrutvā tu saṁkruddhastadā vaiśvaraṇātmajaḥ
dharṣaṇāṁ tāṁ parāṁ śrutvā dhyānaṁ saṁpraviveśa ha
Hearing of this ravishment Vaisravana's son was greatly enraged and entered into meditation.

तस्य तत्कर्म विज्ञाय तदा वैश्रवणात्मजः
मुहूर्ताद्रोषताम्राक्षस्तोयं जग्राह पाणिना

tasya tatkarma vijñāya tadā vaiśravaṇātmajaḥ
muhūrtādroṣatāmrākṣastoyaṁ jagrāha pāṇinā
Having ascertained the truth within a moment Vaisravana's son, with eyes reddened with ire, took water in his palms.

गृहीत्वा सलिलं दिव्यमुपस्पृश्य यथाविधि
उत्ससर्ज तदा शापं राक्षसेन्द्राय दारुणम्

gṛhītvā salilaṁ divyamupaspṛśya yathāvidhi
utsasarja tadā śāpaṁ rākṣasendrāya dāruṇam
Having taken this and rinsed his mouth duly, he imprecated a dreadful curse upon that lord of Raksasas.

अकामा तेन यस्मात्त्वं बलाद्भद्रे प्रधर्षिता
तस्मात्स युवतीमन्यां नाकामामुपयास्यति

akāmā tena yasmāttvaṁ balādbhadre pradharṣitā
tasmātsa yuvatīmanyāṁ nākāmāmupayāsyati
O fair one, since you have been ravished by him despite your unwillingness he shall never be able to get by an unwilling damsel.

तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे ज्वलिताग्निसमप्रभे
देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता

tasminnudāhṛte śāpe jvalitāgnisamaprabhe
devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā

Whenever he shall, stricken by lust, ravish a reluctant damsel, his head shall be sundered into seven pieces. As soon as this curse, like to a burning flame, was uttered, the celestials bugles were sounded and a shower of flowers fell from heavens.

प्रजापतिमुखाश्चापि सर्वे देवाः प्रहर्षिताः
ज्ञात्वा लोकगतिं सर्वां तस्य मृत्युं च रक्षसः

prajāpatimukhāścāpi sarve devāḥ praharṣitāḥ
jñātvā lokagatiṁ sarvāṁ tasya mṛtyuṁ ca rakṣasaḥ
Being apprised of the plight of people (brought about by him) and of the death of that Raksasa the patriarch Brahma and other gods were greatly delighted.

श्रुत्वा तु स दशग्रीवस्तं शापं रोमहर्षणम्
नारीषु मैथुनं भावं नाकामास्वभ्यरोचयत्

śrutvā tu sa daśagrīvastaṁ śāpaṁ romaharṣaṇam
nārīṣu maithunaṁ bhāvaṁ nākāmāsvabhyarocayat

Hearing of that curse capable of making the down erect, Dasagriva abstained from entertaining lust for unwilling females. And hearing of the curse imprecated by Nalakubara all the chaste damsels, that were kept captive, attained to great delight.

कैलासं लङ्घयित्वाथ दशग्रीवः सराक्षसः
आससाद महातेजा इन्द्रलोकं निशाचरः

kailāsaṁ laṅghayitvātha daśagrīvaḥ sarākṣasaḥ
āsasāda mahātejā indralokaṁ niśācaraḥ
Having crossed the mount Kailasa, the highiy powerful Ten-necked demon, with his army, reached the region of Indra.

तस्य राक्षससैन्यस्य समन्तादुपयास्यतः
देवलोकं ययौ शब्दो भिद्यमानार्णवोपमः

tasya rākṣasasainyasya samantādupayāsyataḥ
devalokaṁ yayau śabdo bhidyamānārṇavopamaḥ
There arose in the region of celestials an uproar from the Raksasa army, like to the sound of the agitated deep.

आदित्यान्सवसून्रुद्रान्विश्वान्साध्यान्मरुद्गणान्
सज्जीभवत युद्धार्थं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः

ādityānsavasūnrudrānviśvānsādhyānmarudgaṇān
sajjībhavata yuddhārthaṁ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ

Hearing of the arrival of Ravana, Indra shook on his throne and said to the assembled gods, Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sadhyas and Maruts"Prepare yourselves, for fighting with the vicious-souled Ravana."

एवमुक्तास्तु शक्रेण देवाः शक्रसमा युधि
संनह्यन्त महासत्त्वा युद्धश्रद्धासमन्विताः

evamuktāstu śakreṇa devāḥ śakrasamā yudhi
saṁnahyanta mahāsattvā yuddhaśraddhāsamanvitāḥ
Being thus addressed by Sakra, the celestials, his equals in the encounter and gifted with great prowess, armed themselves for fight. some

स तु दीनः परित्रस्तो महेन्द्रो रावणं प्रति
विष्णोः समीपमागत्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह

sa tu dīnaḥ paritrasto mahendro rāvaṇaṁ prati
viṣṇoḥ samīpamāgatya vākyametaduvāca ha
Mahendra, afraid of Ravana, poorly went to: Visnu and gave vent to the following accents.

विष्णो कथं करिष्यामो महावीर्यपराक्रम
असौ हि बलवान्रक्षो युद्धार्थमभिवर्तते

viṣṇo kathaṁ kariṣyāmo mahāvīryaparākrama
asau hi balavānrakṣo yuddhārthamabhivartate

“How shall I, O Visnu, withstand, the Raks asa Ravana? The highly powerful Raksasa has come here for battle. It is by virtue of the boon that he is powerful, not for any thing else. It is proper to make the words uttered by Brahma, truthful.

तद्यथा नमुचिर्वृत्रो बलिर्नरकशम्बरौ
त्वन्मतं समवष्टभ्य यथा दग्धास्तथा कुरु

tadyathā namucirvṛtro balirnarakaśambarau
tvanmataṁ samavaṣṭabhya yathā dagdhāstathā kuru
As resorting to your prowess I destroyed Namuci, Vrtra, Bali, Naraka and Sambara, so do you make arrangements (for his destruction).

त्वं हि नारायणः श्रीमान्पद्मनाभः सनातनः
त्वयाहं स्थापितश्चैव देवराज्ये सनातने

tvaṁ hi nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmānpadmanābhaḥ sanātanaḥ
tvayāhaṁ sthāpitaścaiva devarājye sanātane

There is no other excellent refuge but you in the three worlds, mobile and immobile, O lord, O gods of gods, O slayer of Madhu. You are the graceful, ever-existing Narayana, having a lotus naval. By you the worlds have been settled and myself and Sakra, the lord of the celestials.

तदाख्याहि यथातत्त्वं देवदेव मम स्वयम्
असिचक्रसहायस्त्वं युध्यसे संयुगे रिपुम्

tadākhyāhi yathātattvaṁ devadeva mama svayam
asicakrasahāyastvaṁ yudhyase saṁyuge ripum
Do you tell me, the truth, O god of gods, that I may myself fight; or do you, with your sword and discus, vanquish Ravana.

एवमुक्तः स शक्रेण देवो नारायणः प्रभुः
अब्रवीन्न परित्रासः कार्यस्ते श्रूयतां च मे

evamuktaḥ sa śakreṇa devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
abravīnna paritrāsaḥ kāryaste śrūyatāṁ ca me

Being thus addressed by Sakra the lord Narayana; said, "Do not fear, hear what I say. He is invincible by virtue of the boon, and that vicious-souled one is incapable of being vanquished even by the celestials and Asuras.

सर्वथा तु महत्कर्म करिष्यति बलोत्कटः
रक्षः पुत्रसहायोऽसौ दृष्टमेतन्निसर्गतः

sarvathā tu mahatkarma kariṣyati balotkaṭaḥ
rakṣaḥ putrasahāyo'sau dṛṣṭametannisargataḥ
Irrepressible by virtue of his prowess, that Raksasa, with his son, shall accomplish a mighty object. It seems to be real.

अनिहत्य रिपुं विष्णुर्न हि प्रतिनिवर्तते
दुर्लभश्चैष कामोऽद्य वरमासाद्य राक्षसे

anihatya ripuṁ viṣṇurna hi pratinivartate
durlabhaścaiṣa kāmo'dya varamāsādya rākṣase
Without slaying the enemies in the encounter, Visnu does never go black, but it is hard to fulfil my desire from Ravana, well protected by the boon.

प्रतिजानामि देवेन्द्र त्वत्समीपं शतक्रतो
राक्षसस्याहमेवास्य भविता मृत्युकारणम्

pratijānāmi devendra tvatsamīpaṁ śatakrato
rākṣasasyāhamevāsya bhavitā mṛtyukāraṇam
However I do promise before you, O lord of the celestials, O performer of hundred sacrifices, I shall, soon become the cause of this Raksasa's death.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे नादः शुश्रुवे रजनीक्षये
तस्य रावणसैन्यस्य प्रयुद्धस्य समन्ततः

etasminnantare nādaḥ śuśruve rajanīkṣaye
tasya rāvaṇasainyasya prayuddhasya samantataḥ
Meanwhile at the latter part of the night there was audible the uproar of Ravana's army fighting on all sides.

अथ युद्धं समभवद्देवराक्षसयोस्तदा
घोरं तुमुलनिर्ह्रादं नानाप्रहरणायुधम्

atha yuddhaṁ samabhavaddevarākṣasayostadā
ghoraṁ tumulanirhrādaṁ nānāpraharaṇāyudham
Thereupon there ensued a conflict, setting up a terrible sound, with various weapons between the Raksasas and gods.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरा राक्षसा घोरदर्शनाः
युद्धार्थमभ्यधावन्त सचिवा रावणाज्ञया

etasminnantare śūrā rākṣasā ghoradarśanāḥ
yuddhārthamabhyadhāvanta sacivā rāvaṇājñayā
In the interval issued out for another encounter the heroic and grim-visaged Raksasas, Ravana's councillors.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरो वसूनामष्टमो वसुः
सावित्र इति विख्यातः प्रविवेश महारणम्

etasminnantare śūro vasūnāmaṣṭamo vasuḥ
sāvitra iti vikhyātaḥ praviveśa mahāraṇam

Being thus distressed by the night-rangers the hoist of the gods fled away into diverse directions like a herd of deer attacked by a lion. In the meantime, entered the battle-field, the heroic and brave Savitra, the eight Vasu, encircled by soldiers and striking terror into the hearts of the enemies.

ततो युद्धं समभवत्सुराणां राक्षसैः सह
क्रुद्धानां रक्षसां कीर्तिं समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्

tato yuddhaṁ samabhavatsurāṇāṁ rākṣasaiḥ saha
kruddhānāṁ rakṣasāṁ kīrtiṁ samareṣvanivartinām
Thereupon there arose with Raksasas a terrible encounter of the celestials unable to bear their fame in battle.

ततस्ते राक्षसाः शूरा देवांस्तान्समरे स्थितान्
नानाप्रहरणैर्घोरैर्जघ्नुः शतसहस्रशः

tataste rākṣasāḥ śūrā devāṁstānsamare sthitān
nānāpraharaṇairghorairjaghnuḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
Then the Raksasas, with thousands of terrible weapons, began to belabour the deities in the encounter.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरः सुमाली नाम राक्षसः
नानाप्रहरणैः क्रुद्धो रणमेवाभ्यवर्तत

etasminnantare śūraḥ sumālī nāma rākṣasaḥ
nānāpraharaṇaiḥ kruddho raṇamevābhyavartata

In the interim, O Rama, a Raksasa, Sumali, by name, getting enraged, and with diverse weapons, ran amok of the soldiery. As the winds scatter clouds, so he, under the influence of rage, with various sharpened weapons, committed a havoc among the celestial soldiers.

ते महाबाणवर्षैश्च शूलैः प्रासैश्च दारुणैः
पीड्यमानाः सुराः सर्वे न व्यतिष्ठन्समाहिताः

te mahābāṇavarṣaiśca śūlaiḥ prāsaiśca dāruṇaiḥ
pīḍyamānāḥ surāḥ sarve na vyatiṣṭhansamāhitāḥ
Thereupon being assailed by a downpour of huge shafts, maces, Prasas and diverse dreadful weapons, the celestials could not keep their ground upon the field of warfare.

संवृतः स्वैरनीकैस्तु प्रहरन्तं निशाचरम्
विक्रमेण महातेजा वारयामास संयुगे

saṁvṛtaḥ svairanīkaistu praharantaṁ niśācaram
vikrameṇa mahātejā vārayāmāsa saṁyuge

The celestials being thus distressed by Sumali the eighth of Vasu, Savitra stood there enraged. And encircled by his own car-warriors that highly powerful one, with his prowess, repulsed the striking night-rangers.

सुमत्तयोस्तयोरासीद्युद्धं लोके सुदारुणम्
सुमालिनो वसोश्चैव समरेष्वनिवर्तिनोः

sumattayostayorāsīdyuddhaṁ loke sudāruṇam
sumālino vasoścaiva samareṣvanivartinoḥ
Thereupon there arose a terrible encounter, capable of making down erect, between Sumalin and the Vasu, who did not retire from the field of battle.

ततस्तस्य महाबाणैर्वसुना सुमहात्मना
महान्स पन्नगरथः क्षणेन विनिपातितः

tatastasya mahābāṇairvasunā sumahātmanā
mahānsa pannagarathaḥ kṣaṇena vinipātitaḥ
His chariot drawn by serpents was pulled down and destroyed by the high-souled Vasu by means of his huge shafts.

हत्वा तु संयुगे तस्य रथं बाणशतैः शितैः
गदां तस्य वधार्थाय वसुर्जग्राह पाणिना

hatvā tu saṁyuge tasya rathaṁ bāṇaśataiḥ śitaiḥ
gadāṁ tasya vadhārthāya vasurjagrāha pāṇinā

Having destroyed his car in the warfare with hundreds of arrows Vasu took up mace in his hands for his destruction. Having taken up that mace having a burning head and resembling the rod of Death Savitra struck Sumalin on his head there with.

तस्य नैवास्थि कायो वा न मांसं ददृशे तदा
गदया भस्मसाद्भूतो रणे तस्मिन्निपातितः

tasya naivāsthi kāyo vā na māṁsaṁ dadṛśe tadā
gadayā bhasmasādbhūto raṇe tasminnipātitaḥ
By the stroke of that mace his person was reduced to ashes and therefore, there was not seen in the battle field either his bone, head or flesh.

तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं संख्ये राक्षसास्ते समन्ततः
दुद्रुवुः सहिताः सर्वे क्रोशमाना महास्वनम्

taṁ dṛṣṭvā nihataṁ saṁkhye rākṣasāste samantataḥ
dudruvuḥ sahitāḥ sarve krośamānā mahāsvanam
Having beheld him slain in the warfare the Raksasas bewailing ran about on all sides and being distressed by Vasu they could not stay in the battle field.

सुमालिनं हतं दृष्ट्वा वसुना भस्मसात्कृतम्
विद्रुतं चापि स्वं सैन्यं लक्षयित्वार्दितं शरैः

sumālinaṁ hataṁ dṛṣṭvā vasunā bhasmasātkṛtam
vidrutaṁ cāpi svaṁ sainyaṁ lakṣayitvārditaṁ śaraiḥ

Beholding Sumali slain and reduced to ashes by Vasu and being assailed by the deities the Raksasa host fled into diverse directions. And collecting all the Raksasas stood there the highly powerful Meghanada, enraged, the son of Ravana.

स रथेनाग्निवर्णेन कामगेन महारथः
अभिदुद्राव सेनां तां वनान्यग्निरिव ज्वलन्

sa rathenāgnivarṇena kāmagena mahārathaḥ
abhidudrāva senāṁ tāṁ vanānyagniriva jvalan
Like to flaming fire approaching towards forest that great car-warrior encountered the enemies in a precious car coursing at will.

ततः प्रविशतस्तस्य विविधायुधधारिणः
विदुद्रुवुर्दिशः सर्वा देवास्तस्य च दर्शनात्

tataḥ praviśatastasya vividhāyudhadhāriṇaḥ
vidudruvurdiśaḥ sarvā devāstasya ca darśanāt
As soon as he, armed with various weapons, entered the field the celestials, at his very sight. And away to all directions.

न भेतव्यं न गन्तव्यं निवर्तध्वं रणं प्रति
एष गच्छति मे पुत्रो युद्धार्थमपराजितः

na bhetavyaṁ na gantavyaṁ nivartadhvaṁ raṇaṁ prati
eṣa gacchati me putro yuddhārthamaparājitaḥ
Be not afraid, O you celestials; do not fly away; come back to the battle; this my son, who has never been vanquished, goes to battle.

ततः शक्रसुतो देवो जयन्त इति विश्रुतः
रथेनाद्भुतकल्पेन संग्राममभिवर्तत

tataḥ śakrasuto devo jayanta iti viśrutaḥ
rathenādbhutakalpena saṁgrāmamabhivartata
Thereupon Sakra's son, known as divine Jayanta, proceeded towards the field of action by a wondrous car.

ततस्ते त्रिदशाः सर्वे परिवार्य शचीसुतम्
रावणस्य सुतं युद्धे समासाद्य व्यवस्थिताः

tataste tridaśāḥ sarve parivārya śacīsutam
rāvaṇasya sutaṁ yuddhe samāsādya vyavasthitāḥ
Having encircled Saci's son and encountered Ravana's son, the deities began to assail him.

तेषां युद्धं महदभूत्सदृशं देवरक्षसाम्
कृते महेन्द्रपुत्रस्य राक्षसेन्द्रसुतस्य च

teṣāṁ yuddhaṁ mahadabhūtsadṛśaṁ devarakṣasām
kṛte mahendraputrasya rākṣasendrasutasya ca
The encounter between Mahendra's son Jayanta and Ravana's son Meghanada was like one between gods and demons.

ततो मातलिपुत्रे तु गोमुखे राक्षसात्मजः
सारथौ पातयामास शरान्काञ्चनभूषणान्

tato mātaliputre tu gomukhe rākṣasātmajaḥ
sārathau pātayāmāsa śarānkāñcanabhūṣaṇān
Thereupon Ravana's son began to assail, with shafts feathered in gold, his (Jayanta's) charioteer Gomukha, Matali's son.

शचीसुतस्त्वपि तथा जयन्तस्तस्य सारथिम्
तं चैव रावणिं क्रुद्धः प्रत्यविध्यद्रणाजिरे

śacīsutastvapi tathā jayantastasya sārathim
taṁ caiva rāvaṇiṁ kruddhaḥ pratyavidhyadraṇājire
Sacis son too, enraged, assailed on all sides, Ravana's son and his charioteer. And the powerful Ravani, stricken with ire and with eyes expanded, covered Sakra's son with arrows.

ततः प्रगृह्य शस्त्राणि सारवन्ति महान्ति च
शतघ्नीस्तोमरान्प्रासान्गदाखड्गपरश्वधान्
सुमहान्त्यद्रिशृङ्गाणि पातयामास रावणिः

tataḥ pragṛhya śastrāṇi sāravanti mahānti ca
śataghnīstomarānprāsāngadākhaḍgaparaśvadhān
sumahāntyadriśṛṅgāṇi pātayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ
Thereupon Ravana's son struck the celestial host with thousands of huge mountain summits, Sataghnis, maces, Prasas, Prasas, clubs, daggers, Parasus and various other sharp pointed weapons.

ततः प्रव्यथिता लोकाः संजज्ञे च तमो महत्
तस्य रावणपुत्रस्य तदा शत्रूनभिघ्नतः

tataḥ pravyathitā lokāḥ saṁjajñe ca tamo mahat
tasya rāvaṇaputrasya tadā śatrūnabhighnataḥ
Ravana's son thus striking Indra's army the quarters were enshrouded with darkness by his illusory power.

ततस्तद्दैवतबलं समन्तात्तं शचीसुतम्
बहुप्रकारमस्वस्थं तत्र तत्र स्म धावति

tatastaddaivatabalaṁ samantāttaṁ śacīsutam
bahuprakāramasvasthaṁ tatra tatra sma dhāvati
Being overpowered with arrows on all sides the celestial army, leaving aside Jayanta, became restless.

नाभ्यजानंस्तदान्योन्यं शत्रून्वा दैवतानि वा
तत्र तत्र विपर्यस्तं समन्तात्परिधावितम्

nābhyajānaṁstadānyonyaṁ śatrūnvā daivatāni vā
tatra tatra viparyastaṁ samantātparidhāvitam
The deities or the Raksasas, they could not recognise one another. And being distressed they ran about on all sides.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरः पुलोमा नाम वीर्यवान्
दैतेयस्तेन संगृह्य शचीपुत्रोऽपवाहितः

etasminnantare śūraḥ pulomā nāma vīryavān
daiteyastena saṁgṛhya śacīputro'pavāhitaḥ
In the interim a heroic and powerful Daityachief, Puloma, be name, taking saci's son disappeared.

प्रणाशं दृश्य तु सुरा जयन्तस्यातिदारुणम्
व्यथिताश्चाप्रहृष्टाश्च समन्ताद्विप्रदुद्रुवुः

praṇāśaṁ dṛśya tu surā jayantasyātidāruṇam
vyathitāścāprahṛṣṭāśca samantādvipradudruvuḥ
Thinking that Jayanta was slain all the deities greatly sorry and distressed fled away on all sides.

रावणिस्त्वथ संहृष्टो बलैः परिवृतः स्वकैः
अभ्यधावत देवांस्तान्मुमोच च महास्वनम्

rāvaṇistvatha saṁhṛṣṭo balaiḥ parivṛtaḥ svakaiḥ
abhyadhāvata devāṁstānmumoca ca mahāsvanam
Thereupon Ravana's son, enraged and encircled by his own powerful followers, pursued the celestials emitting loud cries.

दृष्ट्वा प्रणाशं पुत्रस्य रावणेश्चापि विक्रमम्
मातलिं प्राह देवेन्द्रो रथः समुपनीयताम्

dṛṣṭvā praṇāśaṁ putrasya rāvaṇeścāpi vikramam
mātaliṁ prāha devendro rathaḥ samupanīyatām
Not beholding his son and observing the flight of the deities the king of the celestials said to Matali, “Bring the car."

स तु दिव्यो महाभीमः सज्ज एव महारथः
उपस्थितो मातलिना वाह्यमानो मनोजवः

sa tu divyo mahābhīmaḥ sajja eva mahārathaḥ
upasthito mātalinā vāhyamāno manojavaḥ
By Matali was brought, the celestial, highly dreadful, huge and quick-coursing chariot, that was ready.

ततो मेघा रथे तस्मिंस्तडिद्वन्तो महास्वनाः
अग्रतो वायुचपला गच्छन्तो व्यनदंस्तदा

tato meghā rathe tasmiṁstaḍidvanto mahāsvanāḥ
agrato vāyucapalā gacchanto vyanadaṁstadā
(And he having) ascended the car, the huge clouds, with lightening, being driven by winds, began to emit forth loud mutterings before the chariot.

नानावाद्यानि वाद्यन्त स्तुतयश्च समाहिताः
ननृतुश्चाप्सरःसंघाः प्रयाते वासवे रणम्

nānāvādyāni vādyanta stutayaśca samāhitāḥ
nanṛtuścāpsaraḥsaṁghāḥ prayāte vāsave raṇam
The Gandharvas began to play on various instruments and the Apsaras began to dance.

रुद्रैर्वसुभिरादित्यैः साध्यैश्च समरुद्गणैः
वृतो नानाप्रहरणैर्निर्ययौ त्रिदशाधिपः

rudrairvasubhirādityaiḥ sādhyaiśca samarudgaṇaiḥ
vṛto nānāpraharaṇairniryayau tridaśādhipaḥ
Taking up various weapons, Indra, the king of divinities, set out for the field of action, in the company of Rudras, Vasus, Adityas, the two Asvins and Maruts.

निर्गच्छतस्तु शक्रस्य परुषं पवनो ववौ
भास्करो निष्प्रभश्चासीन्महोल्काश्च प्रपेदिरे

nirgacchatastu śakrasya paruṣaṁ pavano vavau
bhāskaro niṣprabhaścāsīnmaholkāśca prapedire
He, having set out for battle, the winds began to blow high, the sun was divested of its brilliance and the huge fire-brands began to send out flames.

पन्नगैः सुमहाकायैर्वेष्टितं लोमहर्षणैः
येषां निश्वासवातेन प्रदीप्तमिव संयुगम्

pannagaiḥ sumahākāyairveṣṭitaṁ lomaharṣaṇaiḥ
yeṣāṁ niśvāsavātena pradīptamiva saṁyugam

In the interval the heroic and the highly powerful Dasagriva ascended the celestial car, constructed by the Architect of the deities, encircled by the huge-bodied serpents capable of making down erect and by whose breath the battle-field was ablaze.

दैत्यैर्निशाचरैः शूरै रथः संपरिवारितः
समराभिमुखो दिव्यो महेन्द्रमभिवर्तत

daityairniśācaraiḥ śūrai rathaḥ saṁparivāritaḥ
samarābhimukho divyo mahendramabhivartata
Surrounded by demons and night-rangers and with the celestial car he encountered Mahendra in the battle-field.

पुत्रं तं वारयित्वासौ स्वयमेव व्यवस्थितः
सोऽपि युद्धाद्विनिष्क्रम्य रावणिः समुपाविशत्

putraṁ taṁ vārayitvāsau svayameva vyavasthitaḥ
so'pi yuddhādviniṣkramya rāvaṇiḥ samupāviśat
Having desisted his son he himself stood there. And having coming out from the field of action Ravana's son too stood silent.

ततो युद्धं प्रवृत्तं तु सुराणां राक्षसैः सह
शस्त्राभिवर्षणं घोरं मेघानामिव संयुगे

tato yuddhaṁ pravṛttaṁ tu surāṇāṁ rākṣasaiḥ saha
śastrābhivarṣaṇaṁ ghoraṁ meghānāmiva saṁyuge
Thereupon there arose an encounter between the Raksasas and the deities and there began a downpour of weapons in the conflict like clouds.

कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुष्टात्मा नानाप्रहरणोद्यतः
नाज्ञायत तदा युद्धे सह केनाप्ययुध्यत

kumbhakarṇastu duṣṭātmā nānāpraharaṇodyataḥ
nājñāyata tadā yuddhe saha kenāpyayudhyata

The vicious-souled Kumbhakarna armed with various weapons came you, but he did not know,* O king, with whom the conflict was going on. *For he was asleep till then so he was not acquainted with the particulars war-fare. He used to sleep for six months at a time.

दन्तैर्भुजाभ्यां पद्भ्यां च शक्तितोमरसायकैः
येन केनैव संरब्धस्ताडयामास वै सुरान्

dantairbhujābhyāṁ padbhyāṁ ca śaktitomarasāyakaiḥ
yena kenaiva saṁrabdhastāḍayāmāsa vai surān
And by him enraged, the celestials were assailed with his teeth, feet, arms, hands, Saktis, Tomaras and clubs or any weapon whatsoever.

ततो रुद्रैर्महाभागैः सहादित्यैर्निशाचरः
प्रयुद्धस्तैश्च संग्रामे कृत्तः शस्त्रैर्निरन्तरम्

tato rudrairmahābhāgaiḥ sahādityairniśācaraḥ
prayuddhastaiśca saṁgrāme kṛttaḥ śastrairnirantaram
Thereupon the night-ranger engaged with the highly powerful Rudra and was wounded, in the conflict, with incessant strokes of weapons.

ततस्तद्राक्षसं सैन्यं त्रिदशैः समरुद्गणैः
रणे विद्रावितं सर्वं नानाप्रहरणैः शितैः

tatastadrākṣasaṁ sainyaṁ tridaśaiḥ samarudgaṇaiḥ
raṇe vidrāvitaṁ sarvaṁ nānāpraharaṇaiḥ śitaiḥ
Thereupon the Raksasas army began to fight with Maruts and they were overwhelmed in the encounter with the stroke of various weapons.

शोणितोदक निष्यन्दाकङ्कगृध्रसमाकुला
प्रवृत्ता संयुगमुखे शस्त्रग्राहवती नदी

śoṇitodaka niṣyandākaṅkagṛdhrasamākulā
pravṛttā saṁyugamukhe śastragrāhavatī nadī
There issued out in the battle-field a river from weapons, having blood for its silent waters and infested with crows and vultures.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्
निरीक्ष्य तद्बलं सर्वं दैवतैर्विनिपातितम्

etasminnantare kruddho daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān
nirīkṣya tadbalaṁ sarvaṁ daivatairvinipātitam

Having beheld his own army slain by the deities the highly powerful Dasanana, enraged beholding the army slain by gods, entered the ocean of celestial army and slaying the deities in the conflict confronted Sakra.

ततः शक्रो महच्चापं विस्फार्य सुमहास्वनम्
यस्य विस्फारघोषेण स्वनन्ति स्म दिशो दश

tataḥ śakro mahaccāpaṁ visphārya sumahāsvanam
yasya visphāraghoṣeṇa svananti sma diśo daśa
Thereupon Sakra took up his huge bow by the twang where-of the ten quarters were filled.

तद्विकृष्य महच्चापमिन्द्रो रावणमूर्धनि
निपातयामास शरान्पावकादित्यवर्चसः

tadvikṛṣya mahaccāpamindro rāvaṇamūrdhani
nipātayāmāsa śarānpāvakādityavarcasaḥ
Having unstrung his huge bow Indra struck Ravana, on his head, with arrows resembling the flame of fire and the rays of the sun.

तथैव च महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवो व्यवस्थितः
शक्रं कार्मुकविभ्रष्टैः शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्

tathaiva ca mahābāhurdaśagrīvo vyavasthitaḥ
śakraṁ kārmukavibhraṣṭaiḥ śaravarṣairavākirat
And the Raksasa-chief Dasanana, having long arms, also assailed Indra with hundreds of shafts discharged off his bow.

प्रयुध्यतोरथ तयोर्बाणवर्षैः समन्ततः
नाज्ञायत तदा किंचित्सर्वं हि तमसा वृतम्

prayudhyatoratha tayorbāṇavarṣaiḥ samantataḥ
nājñāyata tadā kiṁcitsarvaṁ hi tamasā vṛtam
They having been thus engaged with each other with the downpour of dreadful shafts, all the quarters were filled with darkness and in consequence thereof nothing was visible.

ततस्तमसि संजाते राक्षसा दैवतैः सह
अयुध्यन्त बलोन्मत्ताः सूदयन्तः परस्परम्

tatastamasi saṁjāte rākṣasā daivataiḥ saha
ayudhyanta balonmattāḥ sūdayantaḥ parasparam
Thereupon darkness having set in all the celestials and Raksasas, maddened with their strength, began to fight rushing one another.

इन्द्रश्च रावणश्चैव रावणिश्च महाबलः
तस्मिंस्तमोजालवृते मोहमीयुर्न ते त्रयः

indraśca rāvaṇaścaiva rāvaṇiśca mahābalaḥ
tasmiṁstamojālavṛte mohamīyurna te trayaḥ

And in that darkness-Indra, Ravana and Meghanada— these three were not possessed by the influence of illusion. Beholding his whole army slain in a moment, Ravana, worked up with dreadful ire, sent out terrible roars.

क्रोधात्सूतं च दुर्धर्षः स्यन्दनस्थमुवाच ह
परसैन्यस्य मध्येन यावदन्तं नयस्व माम्

krodhātsūtaṁ ca durdharṣaḥ syandanasthamuvāca ha
parasainyasya madhyena yāvadantaṁ nayasva mām
And in anger, that irrepressible one said to the charioteer, stationed on the car, “Do you take me to the other end of the enemies' host."

अद्यैतांस्त्रिदशान्सर्वान्विक्रमैः समरे स्वयम्
नानाशस्त्रैर्महासारैर्नाशयामि नभस्तलात्

adyaitāṁstridaśānsarvānvikramaiḥ samare svayam
nānāśastrairmahāsārairnāśayāmi nabhastalāt
I shall soon in the field of battle, with the stroke of various weapons despatch all the deities to the abode of Death,

अहमिन्द्रं वधिष्यामि वरुणं धनदं यमम्
त्रिदशान्विनिहत्याशु स्वयं स्थास्याम्यथोपरि

ahamindraṁ vadhiṣyāmi varuṇaṁ dhanadaṁ yamam
tridaśānvinihatyāśu svayaṁ sthāsyāmyathopari
I shall slay Indra, Kubera, Varuna and Yama, what to speak of more, I shall soon destroy all the deities and place myself above them.

विषादो न च कर्तव्यः शीघ्रं वाहय मे रथम्
द्विः खलु त्वां ब्रवीम्यद्य यावदन्तं नयस्व माम्

viṣādo na ca kartavyaḥ śīghraṁ vāhaya me ratham
dviḥ khalu tvāṁ bravīmyadya yāvadantaṁ nayasva mām
Be not sorry; do you soon drive my chariot. To-day I have told you twice to take me to the end of the enemy's army.

अयं स नन्दनोद्देशो यत्र वर्तामहे वयम्
नय मामद्य तत्र त्वमुदयो यत्र पर्वतः

ayaṁ sa nandanoddeśo yatra vartāmahe vayam
naya māmadya tatra tvamudayo yatra parvataḥ
We are now waiting near the Nandana grove, do you take me to the hill when the sun rises.

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा तुरगान्स मनोजवान्
आदिदेशाथ शत्रूणां मध्येनैव च सारथिः

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā turagānsa manojavān
ādideśātha śatrūṇāṁ madhyenaiva ca sārathiḥ
Hearing his words the charioteer drove the steeds, coursing at will through the enemies' host.

तस्य तं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा शक्रो देवेश्वरस्तदा
रथस्थः समरस्थांस्तान्देवान्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्

tasya taṁ niścayaṁ jñātvā śakro deveśvarastadā
rathasthaḥ samarasthāṁstāndevānvākyamathābravīt
Thereupon being apprised of his intention, Sakra, the king of the celestials, stationed on car, said to the deities, in the field of battle.

सुराः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यत्तावन्मम रोचते
जीवन्नेव दशग्रीवः साधु रक्षो निगृह्यताम्

surāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṁ yattāvanmama rocate
jīvanneva daśagrīvaḥ sādhu rakṣo nigṛhyatām
O you deities-bear my words, what appear to me best. This Ten-necked demon must be vanquished by us while alive.

एष ह्यतिबलः सैन्ये रथेन पवनौजसा
गमिष्यति प्रवृद्धोर्मिः समुद्र इव पर्वणि

eṣa hyatibalaḥ sainye rathena pavanaujasā
gamiṣyati pravṛddhormiḥ samudra iva parvaṇi
Ascending his car, gifted with the velocity of the wind, the highly powerful one is proceeding among the army like to the deep with waves rising during Parva.

न ह्येष हन्तुं शक्योऽद्य वरदानात्सुनिर्भयः
तद्ग्रहीष्यामहे रक्षो यत्ता भवत संयुगे

na hyeṣa hantuṁ śakyo'dya varadānātsunirbhayaḥ
tadgrahīṣyāmahe rakṣo yattā bhavata saṁyuge
It is not possible to slay him now, for he shall not meet with death in consequence of the boon. So let us make him captive-and we should all exert to that end.

यथा बलिं निगृह्यैतत्त्रैलोक्यं भुज्यते मया
एवमेतस्य पापस्य निग्रहो मम रोचते

yathā baliṁ nigṛhyaitattrailokyaṁ bhujyate mayā
evametasya pāpasya nigraho mama rocate
Bali being held captive, I am enjoying the three worlds-and I think proper to obstruct the course of this vicious-souled one.

ततोऽन्यं देशमास्थाय शक्रः संत्यज्य रावणम्
अयुध्यत महातेजा राक्षसान्नाशयन्रणे

tato'nyaṁ deśamāsthāya śakraḥ saṁtyajya rāvaṇam
ayudhyata mahātejā rākṣasānnāśayanraṇe
Having said this and left aside Ravana, Sakra went to another side, O King, and fought terrifying the Raksasas in the conflict.

उत्तरेण दशग्रीवः प्रविवेशानिवर्तितः
दक्षिणेन तु पार्श्वेन प्रविवेश शतक्रतुः

uttareṇa daśagrīvaḥ praviveśānivartitaḥ
dakṣiṇena tu pārśvena praviveśa śatakratuḥ
Dasagriva, incapable of being thwarted, entered by the northern route and the performer of hundred sacrifices by the southern.

ततः स योजनशतं प्रविष्टो राक्षसाधिपः
देवतानां बलं कृत्स्नं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्

tataḥ sa yojanaśataṁ praviṣṭo rākṣasādhipaḥ
devatānāṁ balaṁ kṛtsnaṁ śaravarṣairavākirat
Thereupon having entered into the army up to a hundred leagues the lord of Raksasas overpowered the celestial host with a downpour of shafts.

ततः शक्रो निरीक्ष्याथ प्रविष्टं तं बलं स्वकम्
न्यवर्तयदसंभ्रान्तः समावृत्य दशाननम्

tataḥ śakro nirīkṣyātha praviṣṭaṁ taṁ balaṁ svakam
nyavartayadasaṁbhrāntaḥ samāvṛtya daśānanam
Thereupon beholding his own army slain Sakra, returned fearlessly and obstructed the Ten-necked demon.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे नादो मुक्तो दानवराक्षसैः
हा हताः स्मेति तं दृष्ट्वा ग्रस्तं शक्रेण रावणम्

etasminnantare nādo mukto dānavarākṣasaiḥ
hā hatāḥ smeti taṁ dṛṣṭvā grastaṁ śakreṇa rāvaṇam
In the interim beholding Ravana brought under his grasp by Sakra the demons and Raksasas cried aloud, “Alas we are slain."

ततो रथं समारुह्य रावणिः क्रोधमूर्छितः
तत्सैन्यमतिसंक्रुद्धः प्रविवेश सुदारुणम्

tato rathaṁ samāruhya rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
tatsainyamatisaṁkruddhaḥ praviveśa sudāruṇam
Thereupon ascending his car Ravana's son, became senseless by his wrath and beside himself with rage, entered the dreadful flank.

ततः स देवान्संत्यज्य शक्रमेवाभ्ययाद्द्रुतम्
महेन्द्रश्च महातेजा न ददर्श सुतं रिपोः

tataḥ sa devānsaṁtyajya śakramevābhyayāddrutam
mahendraśca mahātejā na dadarśa sutaṁ ripoḥ
Having left behind all other deities he pursued Indra and the highly effulgent Mahendra too espied his enemy's son.

स मातलिं हयांश्चैव ताडयित्वा शरोत्तमैः
महेन्द्रं बाणवर्षेण शीघ्रहस्तो ह्यवाकिरत्

sa mātaliṁ hayāṁścaiva tāḍayitvā śarottamaiḥ
mahendraṁ bāṇavarṣeṇa śīghrahasto hyavākirat
Having overpowered the approaching charioteer Matalt, with many excellent arrows he covered Mahendra with a downpour of shafts.

ततः शक्रो रथं त्यक्त्व विसृज्य च स मातलिम्
ऐरावतं समारुह्य मृगयामास रावणिम्

tataḥ śakro rathaṁ tyaktva visṛjya ca sa mātalim
airāvataṁ samāruhya mṛgayāmāsa rāvaṇim
Thereat having left his car and charioteer Indra mounted his elephant Airavata and ran about in search of Ravana's son.

स तं यदा परिश्रान्तमिन्द्रं मेनेऽथ रावणिः
तदैनं मायया बद्ध्वा स्वसैन्यमभितोऽनयत्

sa taṁ yadā pariśrāntamindraṁ mene'tha rāvaṇiḥ
tadainaṁ māyayā baddhvā svasainyamabhito'nayat
When Ravana's son came to know that Indra was exhausted he, having bound him up by virtue of illusion, proceeded towards his army.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चापि सर्वे सुरगणास्तदा
अभ्यद्रवन्सुसंक्रुद्धा रावणं शस्त्रवृष्टिभिः

etasminnantare cāpi sarve suragaṇāstadā
abhyadravansusaṁkruddhā rāvaṇaṁ śastravṛṣṭibhiḥ
In the meantime, the celestials, all enraged, covered Ravana with a downpour of shafts and belaboured him.

तं तु दृष्ट्वा परिश्रान्तं प्रहारैर्जर्जरच्छविम्
रावणिः पितरं युद्धेऽदर्शनस्थोऽब्रवीदिदम्

taṁ tu dṛṣṭvā pariśrāntaṁ prahārairjarjaracchavim
rāvaṇiḥ pitaraṁ yuddhe'darśanastho'bravīdidam
Beholding his father thus distressed and assailed in warfare with strokes, Ravana's son, although invisible, said.

आगच्छ तात गच्छावो निवृत्तं रणकर्म तत्
जितं ते विदितं भोऽस्तु स्वस्थो भव गतज्वरः

āgaccha tāta gacchāvo nivṛttaṁ raṇakarma tat
jitaṁ te viditaṁ bho'stu svastho bhava gatajvaraḥ
Do you come, O father, our work in the battle field is finished; know, we have achieved victory; be you consoled and divested of agonies.

अयं हि सुरसैन्यस्य त्रैलोक्यस्य च यः प्रभुः
स गृहीतो मया शक्रो भग्नमानाः सुराः कृताः

ayaṁ hi surasainyasya trailokyasya ca yaḥ prabhuḥ
sa gṛhīto mayā śakro bhagnamānāḥ surāḥ kṛtāḥ
By virtue of my illusory powers I have made Mahendra captive the lord of the three worlds and of the celestial host and have crushed down the pride of the deities.

यथेष्टं भुङ्क्ष्व त्रैलोक्यं निगृह्य रिपुमोजसा
वृथा ते किं श्रमं कृत्वा युद्धं हि तव निष्फलम्

yatheṣṭaṁ bhuṅkṣva trailokyaṁ nigṛhya ripumojasā
vṛthā te kiṁ śramaṁ kṛtvā yuddhaṁ hi tava niṣphalam
Having subdued your enemy by virtue of your prowess do you enjoy the three worlds at your pleasure. What is the use of labouring again? And useless it is to fight again.

स दैवतबलात्तस्मान्निवृत्तो रणकर्मणः
तच्छ्रुत्वा रावणेर्वाक्यं स्वस्थचेता दशाननः

sa daivatabalāttasmānnivṛtto raṇakarmaṇaḥ
tacchrutvā rāvaṇervākyaṁ svasthacetā daśānanaḥ
Hearing the words of Ravana's son the deities retired from the battle field, and went away without Sakra.

अतिबलसदृशैः पराक्रमैस्तै;र्मम कुलमानविवर्धनं कृतम्
यदमरसमविक्रम त्वया; त्रिदशपतिस्त्रिदशाश्च निर्जिताः

atibalasadṛśaiḥ parākramaistai;rmama kulamānavivardhanaṁ kṛtam
yadamarasamavikrama tvayā; tridaśapatistridaśāśca nirjitāḥ
You have enhanced the glory of our race displaying the prowess like a highly powerful man. You have vanquished the celestials and their king of unequalled might.

त्वरितमुपनयस्व वासवं; नगरमितो व्रज सैन्यसंवृतः
अहमपि तव गच्छतो द्रुतं; सह सचिवैरनुयामि पृष्ठतः

tvaritamupanayasva vāsavaṁ; nagaramito vraja sainyasaṁvṛtaḥ
ahamapi tava gacchato drutaṁ; saha sacivairanuyāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ
Do you set out hence for the city, taking Indra on your chariot and surrounded by soldiers. I shall, soon, delighted, follow you with my councillors.

अथ स बलवृतः सवाहन;स्त्रिदशपतिं परिगृह्य रावणिः
स्वभवनमुपगम्य राक्षसो; मुदितमना विससर्ज राक्षसान्

atha sa balavṛtaḥ savāhana;stridaśapatiṁ parigṛhya rāvaṇiḥ
svabhavanamupagamya rākṣaso; muditamanā visasarja rākṣasān
Thereupon having returned home with his army and chariots and taking the king of the celestials, the powerful son of Ravana dismissed the victorious warriors.

जिते महेन्द्रेऽतिबले रावणस्य सुतेन वै
प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य गता लङ्कां सुरास्तदा

jite mahendre'tibale rāvaṇasya sutena vai
prajāpatiṁ puraskṛtya gatā laṅkāṁ surāstadā
The highly powerful Mahendra being thus defeated by Ravana's son, all the celestials, taking the patriarch Brahma before them, went to Lanka.

तं रावणं समासाद्य पुत्रभ्रातृभिरावृतम्
अब्रवीद्गगने तिष्ठन्सान्त्वपूर्वं प्रजापतिः

taṁ rāvaṇaṁ samāsādya putrabhrātṛbhirāvṛtam
abravīdgagane tiṣṭhansāntvapūrvaṁ prajāpatiḥ
Having obtained Ravana encircled by his sons and brothers the Patriarch, stationed in the welkin, calmly said.

वत्स रावण तुष्टोऽस्मि तव पुत्रस्य संयुगे
अहोऽस्य विक्रमौदार्यं तव तुल्योऽधिकोऽपि वा

vatsa rāvaṇa tuṣṭo'smi tava putrasya saṁyuge
aho'sya vikramaudāryaṁ tava tulyo'dhiko'pi vā
My son, Ravana, I have been pleased with your son in the conflict. Oh! what wonderful prowess, what strength-equal or greater than your.

जितं हि भवता सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं स्वेन तेजसा
कृता प्रतिज्ञा सफला प्रीतोऽस्मि स्वसुतेन वै

jitaṁ hi bhavatā sarvaṁ trailokyaṁ svena tejasā
kṛtā pratijñā saphalā prīto'smi svasutena vai
You have, by your own prowess, conquered the three worlds — your promise has borne fruits-I have been pleased with you-both the father and son.

अयं च पुत्रोऽतिबलस्तव रावण रावणिः
इन्द्रजित्त्विति विख्यातो जगत्येष भविष्यति

ayaṁ ca putro'tibalastava rāvaṇa rāvaṇiḥ
indrajittviti vikhyāto jagatyeṣa bhaviṣyati
O Ravana, this your son is highly powerful and gifted with great strength and he shall be celebrated in the world under the appellation of 'Indrajit' or the conqueror of Indra.

बलवाञ्शत्रुनिर्जेता भविष्यत्येष राक्षसः
यमाश्रित्य त्वया राजन्स्थापितास्त्रिदशा वशे

balavāñśatrunirjetā bhaviṣyatyeṣa rākṣasaḥ
yamāśritya tvayā rājansthāpitāstridaśā vaśe
The Raksasa shall be powerful and irrepressible, by those help, O King, the celestials have been brought under your subjection.

तन्मुच्यतां महाबाहो महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः
किं चास्य मोक्षणार्थाय प्रयच्छन्ति दिवौकसः

tanmucyatāṁ mahābāho mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ
kiṁ cāsya mokṣaṇārthāya prayacchanti divaukasaḥ
Do you therefore, O you having long arms, release Mahendra, she chastiser of Paka and for setting him free what do you want from the celestials?

अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा इन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः
अमरत्वमहं देव वृणोमीहास्य मोक्षणे

athābravīnmahātejā indrajitsamitiṁjayaḥ
amaratvamahaṁ deva vṛṇomīhāsya mokṣaṇe
Thereupon the highly powerful Indrajit-the subduer of enemies, said: "If do you say so, O god, I pray for immortality."

तस्मिंश्चेदसमाप्ते तु जप्यहोमे विभावसोः
युध्येयं देव संग्रामे तदा मे स्याद्विनाशनम्

tasmiṁścedasamāpte tu japyahome vibhāvasoḥ
yudhyeyaṁ deva saṁgrāme tadā me syādvināśanam
May I meet with destruction, O deity, whenever I shall engage in fight without finishing my offerings to fire.

सर्वो हि तपसा चैव वृणोत्यमरतां पुमान्
विक्रमेण मया त्वेतदमरत्वं प्रवर्तितम्

sarvo hi tapasā caiva vṛṇotyamaratāṁ pumān
vikrameṇa mayā tvetadamaratvaṁ pravartitam
All others, O god, attain to immortality by virtue of devout penances but I shall acquire that by dint of my own prowess.

एवमस्त्विति तं प्राह वाक्यं देवः प्रजापतिः
मुक्तश्चेन्द्रजिता शक्रो गताश्च त्रिदिवं सुराः

evamastviti taṁ prāha vākyaṁ devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
muktaścendrajitā śakro gatāśca tridivaṁ surāḥ
Where to the grand-father replied saying "so be it." Thereupon Meghanada released Indra and the celestials returned to their own abode.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शक्रो दीनो भ्रष्टाम्बरस्रजः
राम चिन्तापरीतात्मा ध्यानतत्परतां गतः

etasminnantare śakro dīno bhraṣṭāmbarasrajaḥ
rāma cintāparītātmā dhyānatatparatāṁ gataḥ
In the interval, O Rama, Indra became poorly, divested of his immortal brilliance, stricken with anxiety and pensive.

तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतं प्राह देवः प्रजापतिः
शतक्रतो किमुत्कण्ठां करोषि स्मर दुष्कृतम्

taṁ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtaṁ prāha devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
śatakrato kimutkaṇṭhāṁ karoṣi smara duṣkṛtam
Beholding him in that plight the grand-father of the deities said:-O performer of hundred sacrifices, why did you formerly perpetrate that mighty iniquity?

अमरेन्द्र मया बह्व्यः प्रजाः सृष्टाः पुरा प्रभो
एकवर्णाः समाभाषा एकरूपाश्च सर्वशः

amarendra mayā bahvyaḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ purā prabho
ekavarṇāḥ samābhāṣā ekarūpāśca sarvaśaḥ
O Chief of the immortals! O lord!, some creatures were all of the same colour, same speech, and same appearance.

तासां नास्ति विशेषो हि दर्शने लक्षणेऽपि वा
ततोऽहमेकाग्रमनास्ताः प्रजाः पर्यचिन्तयम्

tāsāṁ nāsti viśeṣo hi darśane lakṣaṇe'pi vā
tato'hamekāgramanāstāḥ prajāḥ paryacintayam
There was no difference visible in their appearance or marks. Thereupon, with wholeminded-ness, I began to think of these created beings.

सोऽहं तासां विशेषार्थं स्त्रियमेकां विनिर्ममे
यद्यत्प्रजानां प्रत्यङ्गं विशिष्टं तत्तदुद्धृतम्

so'haṁ tāsāṁ viśeṣārthaṁ striyamekāṁ vinirmame
yadyatprajānāṁ pratyaṅgaṁ viśiṣṭaṁ tattaduddhṛtam

And I created a female distinct from them. Collecting all those limbs that were most excellent among the created, I made a female under the name of Ahalya. Hal means uglinessone born from Hal is called Halya. That female was known as Ahalya because she had nothing blameable in her, I gave her that name.

निर्मितायां तु देवेन्द्र तस्यां नार्यां सुरर्षभ
भविष्यतीति कस्यैषा मम चिन्ता ततोऽभवत्

nirmitāyāṁ tu devendra tasyāṁ nāryāṁ surarṣabha
bhaviṣyatīti kasyaiṣā mama cintā tato'bhavat
Having created that female I was thinking, O king of the celestials! O foremost of the deities!, on whom I should confer her.

त्वं तु शक्र तदा नारीं जानीषे मनसा प्रभो
स्थानाधिकतया पत्नी ममैषेति पुरंदर

tvaṁ tu śakra tadā nārīṁ jānīṣe manasā prabho
sthānādhikatayā patnī mamaiṣeti puraṁdara
Being proud of dignity, O Sakra, O lord, O Purandara you did regard her in your mind as your spouse.

सा मया न्यासभूता तु गौतमस्य महात्मनः
न्यस्ता बहूनि वर्षाणि तेन निर्यातिता च सा

sā mayā nyāsabhūtā tu gautamasya mahātmanaḥ
nyastā bahūni varṣāṇi tena niryātitā ca sā
I placed her under the care of the high-souled Gautama and he rendered her back after many long years.

ततस्तस्य परिज्ञाय मया स्थैर्यं महामुनेः
ज्ञात्वा तपसि सिद्धिं च पत्न्यर्थं स्पर्शिता तदा

tatastasya parijñāya mayā sthairyaṁ mahāmuneḥ
jñātvā tapasi siddhiṁ ca patnyarthaṁ sparśitā tadā
Thereupon considering the patience and accomplished asceticism of Gautama I married her with him.

स तया सह धर्मात्मा रमते स्म महामुनिः
आसन्निराशा देवास्तु गौतमे दत्तया तया

sa tayā saha dharmātmā ramate sma mahāmuniḥ
āsannirāśā devāstu gautame dattayā tayā
That virtuous-souled, great ascetic enjoyed her company; and for my thus conferring her upon Gautama alll the celestials disappointed.

त्वं क्रुद्धस्त्विह कामात्मा गत्वा तस्याश्रमं मुनेः
दृष्टवांश्च तदा तां स्त्रीं दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव

tvaṁ kruddhastviha kāmātmā gatvā tasyāśramaṁ muneḥ
dṛṣṭavāṁśca tadā tāṁ strīṁ dīptāmagniśikhāmiva
But being enraged and possessed by lust you did repair to the hermitage of the ascetic and see her resplendent like the flaming fire.

सा त्वया धर्षिता शक्र कामार्तेन समन्युना
दृष्टस्त्वं च तदा तेन आश्रमे परमर्षिणा

sā tvayā dharṣitā śakra kāmārtena samanyunā
dṛṣṭastvaṁ ca tadā tena āśrame paramarṣiṇā
Maddened with lust and ire you did ravish her and you was seen in that hermitage by the great ascetic. were

यस्मान्मे धर्षिता पत्नी त्वया वासव निर्भयम्
तस्मात्त्वं समरे राजञ्शत्रुहस्तं गमिष्यसि

yasmānme dharṣitā patnī tvayā vāsava nirbhayam
tasmāttvaṁ samare rājañśatruhastaṁ gamiṣyasi

You were then imprecated by him, enraged and gifted with great effulgence saying, 'O lord of the celestials, you have attained to a change of circumstances-for which, O Vasava, you have fearlessly ravished my spouse. You shall, therefore, O Sakra, go under the arms of the enemies, in conflict.

अयं तु भावो दुर्बुद्धे यस्त्वयेह प्रवर्तितः
मानुषेष्वपि सर्वेषु भविष्यति न संशयः

ayaṁ tu bhāvo durbuddhe yastvayeha pravartitaḥ
mānuṣeṣvapi sarveṣu bhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ
And this vile desire, O you having a vicious intellect, which you have first created, shall undoubtedly spread in the world of mortals.

यश्च यश्च सुरेन्द्रः स्याद्ध्रुवः स न भविष्यति
एष शापो मया मुक्त इत्यसौ त्वां तदाब्रवीत्

yaśca yaśca surendraḥ syāddhruvaḥ sa na bhaviṣyati
eṣa śāpo mayā mukta ityasau tvāṁ tadābravīt
Whoever shall be the lord of the celestials, shall not have his position secure. This is the curse I give, which I have communicated to you.

तां तु भार्यां विनिर्भर्त्स्य सोऽब्रवीत्सुमहातपाः
दुर्विनीते विनिध्वंस ममाश्रमसमीपतः

tāṁ tu bhāryāṁ vinirbhartsya so'bravītsumahātapāḥ
durvinīte vinidhvaṁsa mamāśramasamīpataḥ

Having remonstrated with his wife that one of devout penances said to her-'O vicious one, let your beauty be spoiled in the vicinity of the hermitage. You are gifted with beauty and youth but your mind is fickle; so you shall not continue as the single beautiful damsel in the world.

रूपं च तत्प्रजाः सर्वा गमिष्यन्ति सुदुर्लभम्
यत्तवेदं समाश्रित्य विभ्रमेऽयमुपस्थितः

rūpaṁ ca tatprajāḥ sarvā gamiṣyanti sudurlabham
yattavedaṁ samāśritya vibhrame'yamupasthitaḥ
All created beings shall participate your beauty; your matchless beauty has brought about this mischief.' Thenceforward all created beings were gifted with beauty.

तदा प्रभृति भूयिष्ठं प्रजा रूपसमन्विताः
शापोत्सर्गाद्धि तस्येदं मुनेः सर्वमुपागतम्

tadā prabhṛti bhūyiṣṭhaṁ prajā rūpasamanvitāḥ
śāpotsargāddhi tasyedaṁ muneḥ sarvamupāgatam
You have met with all this in consequence of the imprecation of that ascetic. Therefore, O you having long arms, do you think of your past iniquity.

शीघ्रं यजस्व यज्ञं त्वं वैष्णवं सुसमाहितः
पावितस्तेन यज्ञेन यास्यसि त्रिदिवं ततः

śīghraṁ yajasva yajñaṁ tvaṁ vaiṣṇavaṁ susamāhitaḥ
pāvitastena yajñena yāsyasi tridivaṁ tataḥ
For that curse and nothing else, O Vasava, you have been brought under the grasp of enemies. Having controlled your senses, do you soon undertake a sacrifice in honour of Visnu.

पुत्रश्च तव देवेन्द्र न विनष्टो महारणे
नीतः संनिहितश्चैव अर्यकेण महोदधौ

putraśca tava devendra na vinaṣṭo mahāraṇe
nītaḥ saṁnihitaścaiva aryakeṇa mahodadhau
You shall be purified by that sacrifice and go to heaven; and your son, O lord of celestials, has not been destroyed in the conflict. He has been taken into the ocean by his grand father.

एतच्छ्रुत्वा महेन्द्रस्तु यज्ञमिष्ट्वा च वैष्णवम्
पुनस्त्रिदिवमाक्रामदन्वशासच्च देवताः

etacchrutvā mahendrastu yajñamiṣṭvā ca vaiṣṇavam
punastridivamākrāmadanvaśāsacca devatāḥ
Hearing this and having celebrated the sacrifice in honour of Visnu he again went to the region of celestials and reigned there as their king.

एतदिन्द्रजितो राम बलं यत्कीर्तितं मया
निर्जितस्तेन देवेन्द्रः प्राणिनोऽन्ये च किं पुनः

etadindrajito rāma balaṁ yatkīrtitaṁ mayā
nirjitastena devendraḥ prāṇino'nye ca kiṁ punaḥ
I have thus described to you the strength of Indrajit-what to speak of others he vanquished even Indra-the king of the celestials.

ततो रामो महातेजा विस्मयात्पुनरेव हि
उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्

tato rāmo mahātejā vismayātpunareva hi
uvāca praṇato vākyamagastyamṛṣisattamam
Thereupon having bowed to Agastya the foremost of ascetics, the highly effulgent Rama again surprisingly said.

भगवन्किं तदा लोकाः शून्या आसन्द्विजोत्तम
धर्षणां यत्र न प्राप्तो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः

bhagavankiṁ tadā lokāḥ śūnyā āsandvijottama
dharṣaṇāṁ yatra na prāpto rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
"O Brahmana, O foremost of twice-born ones, when that cruel Ravana journeyed over the earth, was it void of people? Was there no king, or prince on earth to administer punishment to him?

उताहो हीनवीर्यास्ते बभुवुः पृथिवीक्षितः
बहिष्कृता वरास्त्रैश्च बहवो निर्जिता नृपाः

utāho hīnavīryāste babhuvuḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ
bahiṣkṛtā varāstraiśca bahavo nirjitā nṛpāḥ
Were all the kings then shorn of their strength and prowess? And many kings I (hear) were vanquished an driven out by him with various excellent weapons.

राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा अगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः
उवाच रामं प्रहसन्पितामह इवेश्वरम्

rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā agastyo bhagavānṛṣiḥ
uvāca rāmaṁ prahasanpitāmaha iveśvaram
Hearing the words of Raghava, the ascetic Agastya, having six sorts of wealth, laughing said, like to Brahma, speaking to Rudra

तमेव दिवसं सोऽथ हैहयाधिपतिर्बली
अर्जुनो नर्मदां रन्तुं गतः स्त्रीभिः सहेश्वरः

tameva divasaṁ so'tha haihayādhipatirbalī
arjuno narmadāṁ rantuṁ gataḥ strībhiḥ saheśvaraḥ
One day the highly powerful Arjuna, the king of Haihayas, repaired to the river Narmada, with his wives to sport.

रावणो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तस्यामात्यानपृच्छत
क्वार्जुनो वो नृपः सोऽद्य शीघ्रमाख्यातुमर्हथ

rāvaṇo rākṣasendrastu tasyāmātyānapṛcchata
kvārjuno vo nṛpaḥ so'dya śīghramākhyātumarhatha
At the very same day, Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, arrived there and asked his councillors saying.

इत्येवं रावणेनोक्तास्तेऽमात्याः सुविपश्चितः
अब्रुवन्राक्षसपतिमसाम्निध्यं महीपतेः

ityevaṁ rāvaṇenoktāste'mātyāḥ suvipaścitaḥ
abruvanrākṣasapatimasāmnidhyaṁ mahīpateḥ
Do you, at first, communicate to him the news of my arrival. Being thus addressed by Ravana, the learned ministers informed the lord of Raksasas, of the absence of the king.

श्रुत्वा विश्रवसः पुत्रः पौराणामर्जुनं गतम्
अपसृत्यागतो विन्ध्यं हिमवत्संनिभं गिरिम्

śrutvā viśravasaḥ putraḥ paurāṇāmarjunaṁ gatam
apasṛtyāgato vindhyaṁ himavatsaṁnibhaṁ girim
Hearing of the absence of the king from the citizens Visravasa's son came out of the city and reached the Vindhya mountain resembling the Himalayas.

चक्रवाकैः सकारण्डैः सहंसजलकुक्कुटैः
सारसैश्च सदामत्तैः कोकूजद्भिः समावृताम्

cakravākaiḥ sakāraṇḍaiḥ sahaṁsajalakukkuṭaiḥ
sārasaiśca sadāmattaiḥ kokūjadbhiḥ samāvṛtām
Having covered her, Cakravakas, Karandavas, swans, water-cocks and Sarasas, maddened, were emitting notes.

एष रश्मिसहस्रेण जगत्कृत्वेव काञ्चनम्
तीक्ष्णतापकरः सूर्यो नभसो मध्यमास्थितः
मामासीनं विदित्वेह चन्द्रायाति दिवाकरः

eṣa raśmisahasreṇa jagatkṛtveva kāñcanam
tīkṣṇatāpakaraḥ sūryo nabhaso madhyamāsthitaḥ
māmāsīnaṁ viditveha candrāyāti divākaraḥ

Delighted at her beauty and having spoken highly of Narmada like to Ganga he addressed his ministers Suka and Sarana with gestures, saying:-“Behold, having rendered the earth pale, with his many rays, the sun, emitting parching heat, is in the sky.

नर्मदा जलशीतश्च सुगन्धिः श्रमनाशनः
मद्भयादनिलो ह्येष वात्यसौ सुसमाहितः

narmadā jalaśītaśca sugandhiḥ śramanāśanaḥ
madbhayādanilo hyeṣa vātyasau susamāhitaḥ

But seeing me here seated, his rays have become cool like those of the moon. At my fear, even the wind is blowing carefully, being cold and fragrant by the touch of the waters of the Narmada and removing our toil.

इयं चापि सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा नर्मदा नर्म वर्धिनी
लीनमीनविहंगोर्मिः सभयेवाङ्गना स्थिता

iyaṁ cāpi saricchreṣṭhā narmadā narma vardhinī
līnamīnavihaṁgormiḥ sabhayevāṅganā sthitā
This charming Narmada, abounding in crocodiles, fishes and birds, though a natural stream, is standing still like a terrified damsel.

तद्भवन्तः क्षताः शस्त्रैर्नृपैरिन्द्रसमैर्युधि
चन्दनस्य रसेनेव रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः

tadbhavantaḥ kṣatāḥ śastrairnṛpairindrasamairyudhi
candanasya raseneva rudhireṇa samukṣitāḥ
Being wounded in conflicts with many a king your persons have been pasted with blood.

ते यूयमवगाहध्वं नर्मदां शर्मदां नृणाम्
महापद्ममुखा मत्ता गङ्गामिव महागजाः

te yūyamavagāhadhvaṁ narmadāṁ śarmadāṁ nṛṇām
mahāpadmamukhā mattā gaṅgāmiva mahāgajāḥ
Therefore like to Sarvabhauma and other infuriated elephants going down into the water of the Ganges, do you descend into the water of Narmada conferring auspiciousness and health.

अहमप्यत्र पुलिने शरदिन्दुसमप्रभे
पुष्पोपहरं शनकैः करिष्यामि उमापतेः

ahamapyatra puline śaradindusamaprabhe
puṣpopaharaṁ śanakaiḥ kariṣyāmi umāpateḥ

Bathing in this stream you shall be cleansed from sins. I shall, also on the coast of this river, like the rays of the autumnal moon, reverentially worship with flowers Mahadeva, holding Pinaka in his hands.

रावणेनैवमुक्तास्तु मारीचशुकसारणाः
समहोदरधूम्राक्षा नर्मदामवगाहिरे

rāvaṇenaivamuktāstu mārīcaśukasāraṇāḥ
samahodaradhūmrākṣā narmadāmavagāhire
Hearing the words of Ravana, Prahasta, Suka, Sarana, Mahodara, Dhumraksa and other councillors descended into the waters of Narmada.

राक्षसेन्द्रगजैस्तैस्तु क्षोभ्यते नर्मदा नदी
वामनाञ्जनपद्माद्यैर्गङ्गा इव महागजैः

rākṣasendragajaistaistu kṣobhyate narmadā nadī
vāmanāñjanapadmādyairgaṅgā iva mahāgajaiḥ
She was agitated by those elephant like leading Raksasas like to the Garga by Vamana, Anjana, Padma and other elephants.

ततस्ते राक्षसाः स्नात्वा नर्मदाया वराम्भसि
उत्तीर्य पुष्पाण्याजह्रुर्बल्यर्थं रावणस्य तु

tataste rākṣasāḥ snātvā narmadāyā varāmbhasi
uttīrya puṣpāṇyājahrurbalyarthaṁ rāvaṇasya tu
Thereupon having got up from the waters the highly powerful Raksasas culled flowers for Ravana's offerings.

नर्मदा पुलिने रम्ये शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे
राक्षसेन्द्रैर्मुहूर्तेन कृतः पुष्पमयो गिरिः

narmadā puline ramye śubhrābhrasadṛśaprabhe
rākṣasendrairmuhūrtena kṛtaḥ puṣpamayo giriḥ
In a moment the Raksasas collected heaps of flowers on the picturesque banks of Narmada, resembling the white clouds.

पुष्पेषूपहृतेष्वेव रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
अवतीर्णो नदीं स्नातुं गङ्गामिव महागजः

puṣpeṣūpahṛteṣveva rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
avatīrṇo nadīṁ snātuṁ gaṅgāmiva mahāgajaḥ
Flowers being thus collected, Ravana, the king of Raksasas descended into the Narmada for bathing like a huge elephant into the Ganga. And having bathed he got up, reciting excellent incantations.

रावणं प्राञ्जलिं यान्तमन्वयुः सप्तराक्षसाः
यत्र यत्र स याति स्म रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
जाम्बूनदमयं लिङ्गं तत्र तत्र स्म नीयते

rāvaṇaṁ prāñjaliṁ yāntamanvayuḥ saptarākṣasāḥ
yatra yatra sa yāti sma rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
jāmbūnadamayaṁ liṅgaṁ tatra tatra sma nīyate
Wherever Ravana went the golden Siva Linga was brought.

वालुकवेदिमध्ये तु तल्लिङ्गं स्थाप्य रावणः
अर्चयामास गन्धैश्च पुष्पैश्चामृतगन्धिभिः

vālukavedimadhye tu talliṅgaṁ sthāpya rāvaṇaḥ
arcayāmāsa gandhaiśca puṣpaiścāmṛtagandhibhiḥ
Thereupon Ravana placed that upon a heap of sands and began to worship it with various nectar-smelling flowers and sandal.

ततः सतामार्तिहरं हरं परं; वरप्रदं चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम्
समर्चयित्वा स निशाचरो जगौ; प्रसार्य हस्तान्प्रणनर्त चायतान्

tataḥ satāmārtiharaṁ haraṁ paraṁ; varapradaṁ candramayūkhabhūṣaṇam
samarcayitvā sa niśācaro jagau; prasārya hastānpraṇanarta cāyatān

Having finished the worship of Siva, the foremost of deities, having ww moon on his crown, the conferrer of boons and the remover of miseries, the night-ranger danced with uplifted hands and sang before it.

अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो माहिष्मत्याः पतिः प्रभुः
क्रीडिते सह नारीभिर्नर्मदातोयमाश्रितः

arjuno jayatāṁ śreṣṭho māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ
krīḍite saha nārībhirnarmadātoyamāśritaḥ

At no distance from where on the banks of the river Narmada, that dreadful lord of Raksasas collected the flowers, Arjuna, the King of Mahismati, and the foremost of the victorious, was sporting with his wives in the water.

तासां मध्यगतो राज रराज स ततोऽर्जुनः
करेणूनां सहस्रस्य मध्यस्थ इव कुञ्जरः

tāsāṁ madhyagato rāja rarāja sa tato'rjunaḥ
kareṇūnāṁ sahasrasya madhyastha iva kuñjaraḥ
And being encircled by them the king Arjuna appeared like a leading elephant surrounded by a thousands of she elephants.

जिज्ञासुः स तु बाहूनां सहस्रस्योत्तमं बलम्
रुरोध नर्मदा वेगं बाहुभिः स तदार्जुनः

jijñāsuḥ sa tu bāhūnāṁ sahasrasyottamaṁ balam
rurodha narmadā vegaṁ bāhubhiḥ sa tadārjunaḥ
In order to measure the strength of his thousand arms the King of Haihayas obstructed the course of Narmada.

कार्तवीर्यभुजासेतुं तज्जलं प्राप्य निर्मलम्
कूलापहारं कुर्वाणं प्रतिस्रोतः प्रधावति

kārtavīryabhujāsetuṁ tajjalaṁ prāpya nirmalam
kūlāpahāraṁ kurvāṇaṁ pratisrotaḥ pradhāvati
Being obstructed by the arms of Kartaviryarjuna and having flooded the banks with her pure waters, Narmada flowed in an opposite direction.

समीननक्रमकरः सपुष्पकुशसंस्तरः
स नर्मदाम्भसो वेगः प्रावृट्काल इवाबभौ

samīnanakramakaraḥ sapuṣpakuśasaṁstaraḥ
sa narmadāmbhaso vegaḥ prāvṛṭkāla ivābabhau
The currents of Narmada, rising high as during the rainy season flowed with fishes, and crocodiles.

स वेगः कार्तवीर्येण संप्रेषिट इवाम्भसः
पुष्पोपहारं तत्सर्वं रावणस्य जहार ह

sa vegaḥ kārtavīryeṇa saṁpreṣiṭa ivāmbhasaḥ
puṣpopahāraṁ tatsarvaṁ rāvaṇasya jahāra ha
That stream, as if driven against Ravana by Kartaviryarjuna, carried away his collection of flowers.

सव्येतरकराङ्गुल्या सशब्दं च दशाननः
वेगप्रभवमन्वेष्टुं सोऽदिशच्छुकसारणौ

savyetarakarāṅgulyā saśabdaṁ ca daśānanaḥ
vegaprabhavamanveṣṭuṁ so'diśacchukasāraṇau
Thereupon being anxious to learn the cause of the rise of the river, the Ten-necked demon, with his right finger, hinted Suka and Sarana.

तौ तु रावणसंदिष्टौ भ्रातरौ शुकसारणौ
व्योमान्तरचरौ वीरौ प्रस्थितौ पश्चिमोन्मुखौ

tau tu rāvaṇasaṁdiṣṭau bhrātarau śukasāraṇau
vyomāntaracarau vīrau prasthitau paścimonmukhau
Being commanded by Ravana, the two brothers, the heroic Suka and Sarana proceeded towards the west by the aerial way.

अर्धयोजनमात्रं तु गत्वा तौ तु निशाचरौ
पश्येतां पुरुषं तोये क्रीडन्तं सहयोषितम्

ardhayojanamātraṁ tu gatvā tau tu niśācarau
paśyetāṁ puruṣaṁ toye krīḍantaṁ sahayoṣitam
And going half a league, the two night-rangers espied a man sporting in the waters with some females.

बृहत्सालप्रतीकशं तोयव्याकुलमूर्धजम्
मदरक्तान्तनयनं मदनाकारवर्चसं

bṛhatsālapratīkaśaṁ toyavyākulamūrdhajam
madaraktāntanayanaṁ madanākāravarcasaṁ
He was huge as a Sala tree, his hairs were floating on the water, he was inebriate and his eyes were reddened in consequence thereof.

नदीं बाहुसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमरिमर्दनम्
गिरिं पादसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमिव मेदिनीम्

nadīṁ bāhusahasreṇa rundhantamarimardanam
giriṁ pādasahasreṇa rundhantamiva medinīm
Like to Sumeru holding the earth with his thousand feet he obstructed the current of the river with his thousand arms.

बालानां वरनारीणां सहस्रेणाभिसंवृतम्
समदानां करेणूनां सहस्रेणेव कुञ्जरम्

bālānāṁ varanārīṇāṁ sahasreṇābhisaṁvṛtam
samadānāṁ kareṇūnāṁ sahasreṇeva kuñjaram
He was surrounded by a thousands of beautiful damsels like an elephant by a thousands of she-elephants.

तमद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसौ शुकसारणौ
संनिवृत्तावुपागम्य रावणं तमथोचतुः

tamadbhutatamaṁ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasau śukasāraṇau
saṁnivṛttāvupāgamya rāvaṇaṁ tamathocatuḥ
Beholding that dreadful spectacle, the Raksasas-Suka and Sarana came back and approaching Ravana communicated (all) to him.

बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशः कोऽप्यसौ राक्षसेश्वर
नर्मदां रोधवद्रुद्ध्वा क्रीडापयति योषितः

bṛhatsālapratīkāśaḥ ko'pyasau rākṣaseśvara
narmadāṁ rodhavadruddhvā krīḍāpayati yoṣitaḥ
O lord of Raksasas, an unknown person, huge as a Sala tree, is sporting with females obstructing the course of Narmada like to a dam.

तेन बाहुसहस्रेण संनिरुद्धजला नदी
सागरोद्गारसंकाशानुद्गारान्सृजते मुहुः

tena bāhusahasreṇa saṁniruddhajalā nadī
sāgarodgārasaṁkāśānudgārānsṛjate muhuḥ
Being withheld by the thousand arms of that man the waters of Narmada were continually throwing up high waves.

इत्येवं भाषमाणौ तौ निशम्य शुकसारणौ
रावणोऽर्जुन इत्युक्त्वा उत्तस्थौ युद्धलालसः

ityevaṁ bhāṣamāṇau tau niśamya śukasāraṇau
rāvaṇo'rjuna ityuktvā uttasthau yuddhalālasaḥ
Hearing the words of suka and Sarana, Ravana exclaimed “This is Arjuna' and proceeded to fight with him.

महोदरमहापार्श्वधूम्राक्षशुकसारणैः
संवृतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तत्रागाद्यत्र सोऽर्जुनः

mahodaramahāpārśvadhūmrākṣaśukasāraṇaiḥ
saṁvṛto rākṣasendrastu tatrāgādyatra so'rjunaḥ
The clouds began to mutter with a downpour of rain. And the lord of Raksasas proceeded against Arjuna with Mahodara. Mahaparava, Dhumraksa, Suka and Sarana.

स तत्र स्त्रीपरिवृतं वाशिताभिरिव द्विपम्
नरेन्द्रं पश्यते राजा राक्षसानां तदार्जुनम्

sa tatra strīparivṛtaṁ vāśitābhiriva dvipam
narendraṁ paśyate rājā rākṣasānāṁ tadārjunam
Within a short time the dreadful Raksasa, powerful as the elephant Arjuna, reached the banks of Narmada and espied there Arjuna encircled by females as an elephant surrounded by she-elephants.

स रोषाद्रक्तनयनो राक्षसेन्द्रो बलोद्धतः
इत्येवमर्जुनामात्यानाह गम्भीरया गिरा

sa roṣādraktanayano rākṣasendro baloddhataḥ
ityevamarjunāmātyānāha gambhīrayā girā
At the very sight the eyes of the lord of Raksasas, proud of his prowess, grew red and addressing the councillors of the king Arjuna he said.

अमात्याः क्षिप्रमाख्यात हैहयस्य नृपस्य वै
युद्धार्थं समनुप्राप्तो रावणो नाम नामतः

amātyāḥ kṣipramākhyāta haihayasya nṛpasya vai
yuddhārthaṁ samanuprāpto rāvaṇo nāma nāmataḥ
Do you communicate to the king of Haihayas that Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, has come to fight with him.

रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणोऽथार्जुनस्य ते
उत्तस्थुः सायुधास्तं च रावणं वाक्यमब्रुवन्

rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mantriṇo'thārjunasya te
uttasthuḥ sāyudhāstaṁ ca rāvaṇaṁ vākyamabruvan
Hearing the words of Ravana, the ministers of Arjuna stood up with arms and said.

ततस्ते रावणामात्यैरमात्याः पार्थिवस्य तु
सूदिताश्चापि ते युद्धे भक्षिताश्च बुभुक्षितैः

tataste rāvaṇāmātyairamātyāḥ pārthivasya tu
sūditāścāpi te yuddhe bhakṣitāśca bubhukṣitaiḥ
Thereupon the hungry councillors of Ravana, slew some of the ministers of the king and devoured some.

ततो हलहलाशब्दो नर्मदा तिर आबभौ
अर्जुनस्यानुयात्राणां रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणाम्

tato halahalāśabdo narmadā tira ābabhau
arjunasyānuyātrāṇāṁ rāvaṇasya ca mantriṇām
There arose a dreadful uproar on the banks of Narmada, of the councillors of Ravana and Arjuna.

इषुभिस्तोमरैः शूलैर्वज्रकल्पैः सकर्षणैः
सरावणानर्दयन्तः समन्तात्समभिद्रुताः

iṣubhistomaraiḥ śūlairvajrakalpaiḥ sakarṣaṇaiḥ
sarāvaṇānardayantaḥ samantātsamabhidrutāḥ
The warriors of Arjuna assailed Ravana and his ministers with hundreds of arrows, Prasas, darts, Tomaras, thunder-bolts and Karsanas.

हैहयाधिपयोधानां वेग आसीत्सुदारुणः
सनक्रमीनमकरसमुद्रस्येव निस्वनः

haihayādhipayodhānāṁ vega āsītsudāruṇaḥ
sanakramīnamakarasamudrasyeva nisvanaḥ
The warriors of Arjuna became dreadfully furious and emitted cries like the roaring of the deep infested with crocodiles, fishes and other marine monsters.

रावणस्य तु तेऽमात्याः प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः
कार्तवीर्यबलं क्रुद्धा निर्दहन्त्यग्नितेजसः

rāvaṇasya tu te'mātyāḥ prahastaśukasāraṇāḥ
kārtavīryabalaṁ kruddhā nirdahantyagnitejasaḥ
Thereupon being enraged and displaying their own prowess Suka, Sarana and other ministers of Ravana began to destroy Arjuna's soldiers.

अर्जुनाय तु तत्कर्म रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः
क्रीडमानाय कथितं पुरुषैर्द्वाररक्षिभिः

arjunāya tu tatkarma rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ
krīḍamānāya kathitaṁ puruṣairdvārarakṣibhiḥ
Thereupon the emissaries, stricken with fear, went to the sporting king and communicated to him the proceedings of Ravana and his iministers.

उक्त्वा न भेतव्यमिति स्त्रीजनं स ततोऽर्जुनः
उत्ततार जलात्तस्माद्गङ्गातोयादिवाञ्जनः

uktvā na bhetavyamiti strījanaṁ sa tato'rjunaḥ
uttatāra jalāttasmādgaṅgātoyādivāñjanaḥ
Hearing those words and saying to the females-"Do not fear” he rose up from the waters like an elephante

क्रोधदूषितनेत्रस्तु स ततोऽर्जुन पावकः
प्रजज्वाल महाघोरो युगान्त इव पावकः

krodhadūṣitanetrastu sa tato'rjuna pāvakaḥ
prajajvāla mahāghoro yugānta iva pāvakaḥ
The eyes of that fire-like Arjuna were reddened with ire and he shone dreadfully like the fire of dissolution.

स तूर्णतरमादाय वरहेमाङ्गदो गदाम्
अभिद्रवति रक्षांसि तमांसीव दिवाकरः

sa tūrṇataramādāya varahemāṅgado gadām
abhidravati rakṣāṁsi tamāṁsīva divākaraḥ
And taking up speedily his club, that one, always using golden clubs, pursued the Raksasas like to darkness following the sun.

बाहुविक्षेपकरणां समुद्यम्य महागदाम्
गारुडं वेगमास्थाय आपपातैव सोऽर्जुनः

bāhuvikṣepakaraṇāṁ samudyamya mahāgadām
gāruḍaṁ vegamāsthāya āpapātaiva so'rjunaḥ
Holding up the huge club and hurling it with his arms, Arjuna, resorting to the velocity of Garuda, went on

तस्य मर्गं समावृत्य विन्ध्योऽर्कस्येव पर्वतः
स्थितो विन्ध्य इवाकम्प्यः प्रहस्तो मुसलायुधः

tasya margaṁ samāvṛtya vindhyo'rkasyeva parvataḥ
sthito vindhya ivākampyaḥ prahasto musalāyudhaḥ
Thereupon stood there obstructing his course Raksasa, worked up with anger and with a mace in his hand, like to the Vindhya range standing in the way of the sun.

ततोऽस्य मुसलं घोरं लोहबद्धं मदोद्धतः
प्रहस्तः प्रेषयन्क्रुद्धो ररास च यथाम्बुदः

tato'sya musalaṁ ghoraṁ lohabaddhaṁ madoddhataḥ
prahastaḥ preṣayankruddho rarāsa ca yathāmbudaḥ
And throwing down off his hand the iron mace, he, in anger, began to roar, like Yama.

तस्याग्रे मुसलस्याग्निरशोकापीडसंनिभः
प्रहस्तकरमुक्तस्य बभूव प्रदहन्निव

tasyāgre musalasyāgniraśokāpīḍasaṁnibhaḥ
prahastakaramuktasya babhūva pradahanniva
And the top of the mace freed from the hand of Prahasta, was ablaze like the tips of Asoka flowers.

आधावमानं मुसलं कार्तवीर्यस्तदार्जुनः
निपुणं वञ्चयामास सगदो गजविक्रमः

ādhāvamānaṁ musalaṁ kārtavīryastadārjunaḥ
nipuṇaṁ vañcayāmāsa sagado gajavikramaḥ
Not the least agitated on beholding that mace, the king Arjuna, by his club, baffled its action.

ततस्तमभिदुद्राव प्रहस्तं हैहयाधिपः
भ्रामयाणो गदां गुर्वीं पञ्चबाहुशतोच्छ्रयाम्

tatastamabhidudrāva prahastaṁ haihayādhipaḥ
bhrāmayāṇo gadāṁ gurvīṁ pañcabāhuśatocchrayām
Thereupon uplifting the huge club, five hundred hands long, the king of Haihayas pursued Prahasta.

तेनाहतोऽतिवेगेन प्रहस्तो गदया तदा
निपपात स्थितः शैलो वज्रिवज्रहतो यथा

tenāhato'tivegena prahasto gadayā tadā
nipapāta sthitaḥ śailo vajrivajrahato yathā
And within a short time being struck down by that club gifted with great velocity Prahasta fell down on earth like to the summit of a mountain clapped down by the thunder-bolt of Indra.

प्रहस्तं पतितं दृष्ट्वा मारीचशुकसारणाः
समहोदरधूम्राक्षा अपसृप्ता रणाजिरात्

prahastaṁ patitaṁ dṛṣṭvā mārīcaśukasāraṇāḥ
samahodaradhūmrākṣā apasṛptā raṇājirāt
Beholding Prahasta fallen, Marica, Suka, Sarana, Mahodara and Dhumraksa fled away from the battle-field.

अपक्रान्तेष्वमात्येषु प्रहस्ते च निपातिते
रावणोऽभ्यद्रवत्तूर्णमर्जुनं नृपसत्तमम्

apakrānteṣvamātyeṣu prahaste ca nipātite
rāvaṇo'bhyadravattūrṇamarjunaṁ nṛpasattamam
All the councillors having thus fled away and Prahasta being slain, Ravana speedily proceeded towards Arjuna, the foremost of kings.

सहस्रबाहोस्तद्युद्धं विंशद्बाहोश्च दारुणम्
नृपराक्षसयोस्तत्र आरब्धं लोमहर्षणम्

sahasrabāhostadyuddhaṁ viṁśadbāhośca dāruṇam
nṛparākṣasayostatra ārabdhaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
Thereupon there ensued a terrible encounter capable of making down erect between the thousand-armed Arjuna, the king of men, and the twenty-armed Ravana, the king of Raksasas.

सागराविव संक्षुब्धौ चलमूलाविवाचलौ
तेजोयुक्ताविवादित्यौ प्रदहन्ताविवानलौ

sāgarāviva saṁkṣubdhau calamūlāvivācalau
tejoyuktāvivādityau pradahantāvivānalau

And taking up their clubs Arjuna and Ravana began to fight with one another emitting cries like the mutterings of clouds, like to two huge balls fighting for a cow, two agitated oceans, two moving mountains, two effulgent Adityas, two burning flames, two proud elephants, two proud lions and like the very Rudra and Kala.

वज्रप्रहारानचला यथा घोरान्विषेहिरे
गदाप्रहारांस्तद्वत्तौ सहेते नरराक्षसौ

vajraprahārānacalā yathā ghorānviṣehire
gadāprahārāṁstadvattau sahete nararākṣasau
As the mountains suffer many clappings of thunder-bolts so did they bear many strokes.

यथाशनिरवेभ्यस्तु जायते वै प्रतिश्रुतिः
तथा ताभ्यां गदापातैर्दिशः सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुताः

yathāśaniravebhyastu jāyate vai pratiśrutiḥ
tathā tābhyāṁ gadāpātairdiśaḥ sarvāḥ pratiśrutāḥ
And all the quarters were resounded with the sound proceeding from the stroke of their clubs like to the sound of thunder-bolts.

अर्जुनस्य गदा सा तु पात्यमानाहितोरसि
काञ्चनाभं नभश्चक्रे विद्युत्सौदामनी यथा

arjunasya gadā sā tu pātyamānāhitorasi
kāñcanābhaṁ nabhaścakre vidyutsaudāmanī yathā
Being placed against the breast of Ravana Arjuna's club rendered, for a moment, the welkin look like the burning gold as does the lightning.

तथैव रावणेनापि पात्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः
अर्जुनोरसि निर्भाति गदोल्केव महागिरौ

tathaiva rāvaṇenāpi pātyamānā muhurmuhuḥ
arjunorasi nirbhāti gadolkeva mahāgirau
And striking again and again against Arjuna's breast Ravana's club looked like a huge firebrand.

नार्जुनः खेदमाप्नोति न राक्षसगणेश्वरः
सममासीत्तयोर्युद्धं यथा पूर्वं बलीन्द्रयोः

nārjunaḥ khedamāpnoti na rākṣasagaṇeśvaraḥ
samamāsīttayoryuddhaṁ yathā pūrvaṁ balīndrayoḥ
Neither Arjuna was worn out nor was Ravana. And the conflict went on between them like the encounter between Bali and Vasava in the days of yore.

शृङ्गैर्महर्षभौ यद्वद्दन्ताग्रैरिव कुञ्जरौ
परस्परं विनिघ्नन्तौ नरराक्षससत्तमौ

śṛṅgairmaharṣabhau yadvaddantāgrairiva kuñjarau
parasparaṁ vinighnantau nararākṣasasattamau
The King of men and the King of Raksasas assailed and wounded one another with their clubs like to two bulls striking one another with their horns and two elephants with their tusks.

ततोऽर्जुनेन क्रुद्धेन सर्वप्राणेन सा गदा
स्तनयोरन्तरे मुक्ता रावणस्य महाहवे

tato'rjunena kruddhena sarvaprāṇena sā gadā
stanayorantare muktā rāvaṇasya mahāhave
Thereupon worked up with rage, Arjuna, with his full might, smote Ravana on his breast, with his club.

वरदानकृतत्राणे सा गदा रावणोरसि
दुर्बलेव यथा सेना द्विधाभूतापतत्क्षितौ

varadānakṛtatrāṇe sā gadā rāvaṇorasi
durbaleva yathā senā dvidhābhūtāpatatkṣitau
But Ravana was well protected by the boon of the celestial, so the club fell on earth sundered into two pieces like one hurled by a weak wight.

स त्वर्जुनप्रमुक्तेन गदापातेन रावणः
अपासर्पद्धनुर्मात्रं निषसाद च निष्टनन्

sa tvarjunapramuktena gadāpātena rāvaṇaḥ
apāsarpaddhanurmātraṁ niṣasāda ca niṣṭanan
Still wounded by the mace of Arjuna, Ravana, shedding tears, ran away at a distance of four feet and sat there.

बध्यमाने दशग्रीवे सिद्धचारणदेवताः
साध्वीति वादिनः पुष्पैः किरन्त्यर्जुनमूर्धनि

badhyamāne daśagrīve siddhacāraṇadevatāḥ
sādhvīti vādinaḥ puṣpaiḥ kirantyarjunamūrdhani

Beholding Ravana thus over-whelmed Arjuna sprang up and caught him like Garuda holding a serpent and Visnu binding Bali. Dasagriva being thus bound, the Siddhas, Caranas and the celestials exclaiming "Well done! Well done!!” showered flowers upon Arjuna.

व्याघ्रो मृगमिवादाय सिंहराडिव दन्तिनम्
ररास हैहयो राजा हर्षादम्बुदवन्मुहुः

vyāghro mṛgamivādāya siṁharāḍiva dantinam
rarāsa haihayo rājā harṣādambudavanmuhuḥ
And the king emitted leonine roars again and again as a tiger joyous roars like a cloud, holding a deer under his grasp.

प्रहस्तस्तु समाश्वस्तो दृष्ट्वा बद्धं दशाननम्
सह तै राकसैः क्रुद्ध अभिदुद्राव पार्थिवम्

prahastastu samāśvasto dṛṣṭvā baddhaṁ daśānanam
saha tai rākasaiḥ kruddha abhidudrāva pārthivam
Regaining his sense and beholding Ravana bound, Prahasta, in great anger, pursued, the King of Haihaya.

नक्तंचराणां वेगस्तु तेषामापततां बभौ
उद्धृत आतपापाये समुद्राणामिवाद्भुतः

naktaṁcarāṇāṁ vegastu teṣāmāpatatāṁ babhau
uddhṛta ātapāpāye samudrāṇāmivādbhutaḥ
And the Raksasa force grew tempestuous like to the rising of the ocean during rains.

मुञ्च मुञ्चेति भाषन्तस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चासकृत्
मुसलानि च शूलानि उत्ससर्जुस्तदार्जुने

muñca muñceti bhāṣantastiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cāsakṛt
musalāni ca śūlāni utsasarjustadārjune
Thereupon exclaiming repeatedly “Leave him off! Leave him off Wait! Wait!!" The Raksasa host hurled hundreds of Musalas and darts in the battle-field.

अप्राप्तान्येव तान्याशु असंभ्रान्तस्तदार्जुनः
आयुधान्यमरारीणां जग्राह रिपुसूदनः

aprāptānyeva tānyāśu asaṁbhrāntastadārjunaḥ
āyudhānyamarārīṇāṁ jagrāha ripusūdanaḥ
Not the least moved thereby the king Arjuna, the slayer of enemies, bore those weapons of the enemies of the celestials.

ततस्तैरेव रक्षांसि दुर्धरैः प्रवरायुधैः
भित्त्वा विद्रावयामास वायुरम्बुधरानिव

tatastaireva rakṣāṁsi durdharaiḥ pravarāyudhaiḥ
bhittvā vidrāvayāmāsa vāyurambudharāniva
Thereupon baffling the weapons of the Raksasas by means of many a dreadful and excellent one, Arjuna, the king of Haihayas, drove them away · like winds scattering the clouds.

स कीर्यमाणः कुसुमाक्षतोत्करै;र्द्विजैः सपौरैः पुरुहूतसंनिभः
तदार्जुनः संप्रविवेश तां पुरीं; बलिं निगृह्यैव सहस्रलोचनः

sa kīryamāṇaḥ kusumākṣatotkarai;rdvijaiḥ sapauraiḥ puruhūtasaṁnibhaḥ
tadārjunaḥ saṁpraviveśa tāṁ purīṁ; baliṁ nigṛhyaiva sahasralocanaḥ

Having thus struck terror to the night-rangers, he, encircled by his own kinsmen, repaired to his own city with Ravana, carrying him bound like to Indra carrying Bali bound. Thereupon flowers and fried paddy were showered upon him by the Brahmanas and citizens.

रावणग्रहणं तत्तु वायुग्रहणसंनिभम्
ऋषिः पुलस्त्यः शुश्राव कथितं दिवि दैवतैः

rāvaṇagrahaṇaṁ tattu vāyugrahaṇasaṁnibham
ṛṣiḥ pulastyaḥ śuśrāva kathitaṁ divi daivataiḥ
Thereupor Pulastya heard from the celestials ot the capture of Ravana like to the holding of the.wind.

ततः पुत्रसुतस्नेहात्कम्प्यमानो महाधृतिः
माहिष्मतीपतिं द्रष्टुमाजगाम महानृषिः

tataḥ putrasutasnehātkampyamāno mahādhṛtiḥ
māhiṣmatīpatiṁ draṣṭumājagāma mahānṛṣiḥ
Having seen moved by the love for his son, the highly effulgent, great ascetic, proceeded to see the king of Mahismati.

स वायुमार्गमास्थाय वायुतुल्यगतिर्द्विजः
पुरीं माहिष्मतीं प्राप्तो मनःसंतापविक्रमः

sa vāyumārgamāsthāya vāyutulyagatirdvijaḥ
purīṁ māhiṣmatīṁ prāpto manaḥsaṁtāpavikramaḥ
Proceeding by the aerial way, that twice-born one, gifted with the velocity of wind and the flight of wind, reached the city of Mahismati.

सोऽमरावतिसंकाशां हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम्
प्रविवेश पुरीं ब्रह्मा इन्द्रस्येवामरावतीम्

so'marāvatisaṁkāśāṁ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtām
praviveśa purīṁ brahmā indrasyevāmarāvatīm
Like to Brahma entering Indra's Amaravati, he entered the city resembling the capital of Indr and filled with delighted and plump citizens.

पादचारमिवादित्यं निष्पतन्तं सुदुर्दृशम्
ततस्ते प्रत्यभिज्ञाय अर्जुनाय न्यवेदयन्

pādacāramivādityaṁ niṣpatantaṁ sudurdṛśam
tataste pratyabhijñāya arjunāya nyavedayan
Beholding that dreadful Rsis approach like to Aditya walking on foot, the warders communicated the intelligence to the king Arjuna.

पुलस्त्य इति तं श्रुत्वा वचनं हैहयाधिपः
शिरस्यञ्जलिमुद्धृत्य प्रत्युद्गच्छद्द्विजोत्तमम्

pulastya iti taṁ śrutvā vacanaṁ haihayādhipaḥ
śirasyañjalimuddhṛtya pratyudgacchaddvijottamam
Understanding from their words that Pulastya was coming, the king of Haihayas, placing his folded palms on his crown, proceeded to welcome him.

पुरोहितोऽस्य गृह्यार्घ्यं मधुपर्कं तथैव च
पुरस्तात्प्रययौ राज्ञ इन्द्रस्येव बृहस्पतिः

purohito'sya gṛhyārghyaṁ madhuparkaṁ tathaiva ca
purastātprayayau rājña indrasyeva bṛhaspatiḥ
Like, to Brhaspati preceding Purandara, the royal priests went before him carrying, Madhuparka and water to wash feet.

ततस्तमृषिमायान्तमुद्यन्तमिव भास्करम्
अर्जुनो दृश्य संप्राप्तं ववन्देन्द्र इवेश्वरम्

tatastamṛṣimāyāntamudyantamiva bhāskaram
arjuno dṛśya saṁprāptaṁ vavandendra iveśvaram
And beholding the ascetic resembling the rising sun arrived, the King Arjuna bowed to him reverentially like Indra saluting Mahadeva.

स तस्य मधुपर्कं च पाद्यमर्घ्यं च दापयन्
पुलस्त्यमाह राजेन्द्रो हर्षगद्गदया गिरा

sa tasya madhuparkaṁ ca pādyamarghyaṁ ca dāpayan
pulastyamāha rājendro harṣagadgadayā girā
Thereupon offering him Madhuparka, cow and water to wash feet, the king of Haihayas, in accents obstructed with delight, addressed the ascetic saying

अद्येयममरावत्या तुल्या माहिष्मती कृता
अद्याहं तु द्विजेन्द्रेन्द्र यस्मात्पश्यामि दुर्दृशम्

adyeyamamarāvatyā tulyā māhiṣmatī kṛtā
adyāhaṁ tu dvijendrendra yasmātpaśyāmi durdṛśam
Reverend Sir, your visit, it is hard to obtain. On beholding you my city Mahismati has been turned into Amaravati.

इदं राज्यमिमे पुत्रा इमे दारा इमे वयम्
ब्रह्मन्किं कुर्म किं कार्यमाज्ञापयतु नो भवान्

idaṁ rājyamime putrā ime dārā ime vayam
brahmankiṁ kurma kiṁ kāryamājñāpayatu no bhavān

Today have I obtained all auspiciousness, O lord; today has my religious observance been fruitful; today has my birth proved blessed and today has my devout penance been crowned with success, for I bow to your feet, which have been worshipped by the celestials. This my kingdom, these my sons, this my wife and myself are all at your disposal do you order me, O Brahmana, what I may do for you.

तं धर्मेऽग्निषु भृत्येषु शिवं पृष्ट्वाथ पार्थिवम्
पुलस्त्योवाच राजानं हैहयानां तदार्जुनम्

taṁ dharme'gniṣu bhṛtyeṣu śivaṁ pṛṣṭvātha pārthivam
pulastyovāca rājānaṁ haihayānāṁ tadārjunam
Thereupon having enquired of the king about his piety, offerings and the well-being of his sons, Pulastya said to Arjuna, the king of Haihayas.

राजेन्द्रामलपद्माक्षपूर्णचन्द्रनिभानन
अतुलं ते बलं येन दशग्रीवस्त्वया जितः

rājendrāmalapadmākṣapūrṇacandranibhānana
atulaṁ te balaṁ yena daśagrīvastvayā jitaḥ
O foremost of kings, O you having eyes like lotus-petals! O you having a countenance like the full moon! When you have vanquished Ravana, your prowess is matchless in the triple world.

भयाद्यस्यावतिष्ठेतां निष्पन्दौ सागरानिलौ
सोऽयमद्य त्वया बद्धः पौत्रो मेऽतीवदुर्जयः

bhayādyasyāvatiṣṭhetāṁ niṣpandau sāgarānilau
so'yamadya tvayā baddhaḥ pautro me'tīvadurjayaḥ
You have bound up my invincible son in the conflict at whose fear the wind and the ocean stand still.

तत्पुत्रक यशः स्फीतं नाम विश्रावितं त्वया
मद्वाक्याद्याच्यमानोऽद्य मुञ्च वत्स दशाननम्

tatputraka yaśaḥ sphītaṁ nāma viśrāvitaṁ tvayā
madvākyādyācyamāno'dya muñca vatsa daśānanam
Having drunk up the glories of my son you have announced your own; so I do say, O my son, do you release Dasanana.

पुलस्त्याज्ञां स गृह्याथ अकिंचनवचोऽर्जुनः
मुमोच पार्थिवेन्द्रेन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रं प्रहृष्टवत्

pulastyājñāṁ sa gṛhyātha akiṁcanavaco'rjunaḥ
mumoca pārthivendrendro rākṣasendraṁ prahṛṣṭavat
Hearing this command of Pulastya, the king Arjuna did not utter a single world and set, most delightedly the king of Raksasas, free.

स तं प्रमुक्त्वा त्रिदशारिमर्जुनः; प्रपूज्य दिव्याभरणस्रगम्बरैः
अहिंसाकं सख्यमुपेत्य साग्निकं; प्रणम्य स ब्रह्मसुतं गृहं ययौ

sa taṁ pramuktvā tridaśārimarjunaḥ; prapūjya divyābharaṇasragambaraiḥ
ahiṁsākaṁ sakhyamupetya sāgnikaṁ; praṇamya sa brahmasutaṁ gṛhaṁ yayau

Having released that foe of the celestials, worshipped him with celestials ornaments and garlands and established friendship removing all enmities with Ravana before fire, and bowed to Pulastya, the son of Brahma, he repaired to his own house.

पुलस्त्येनापि संगम्य राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्
परिष्वङ्गकृतातिथ्यो लज्जमानो विसर्जितः

pulastyenāpi saṁgamya rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān
pariṣvaṅgakṛtātithyo lajjamāno visarjitaḥ
And being released by the influence of Pulastya, the highly powerful Dasanana, the king of Raksasas, accepted his hospitality and being embraced by him, returned home ashamed.

पितामहसुतश्चापि पुलस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः
मोचयित्वा दशग्रीवं ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम सः

pitāmahasutaścāpi pulastyo munisattamaḥ
mocayitvā daśagrīvaṁ brahmalokaṁ jagāma saḥ
And having set Dasagriva at liberty Pulastya, the son of Brahma and the foremost of Munis repaired to the celestial region.

एवं स रावणः प्राप्तः कार्तवीर्यात्तु धर्षणात्
पुलस्त्यवचनाच्चापि पुनर्मोक्षमवाप्तवान्

evaṁ sa rāvaṇaḥ prāptaḥ kārtavīryāttu dharṣaṇāt
pulastyavacanāccāpi punarmokṣamavāptavān
O Rama, in this wise, the highly powerful Ravana was defeated by Arjuna and released by Pulastya.

एवं बलिभ्यो बलिनः सन्ति राघवनन्दन
नावज्ञा परतः कार्या य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः

evaṁ balibhyo balinaḥ santi rāghavanandana
nāvajñā parataḥ kāryā ya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ
Observe therefore, O descendant of Raghu, there is a mightier man than the mighty; therefore, one, desirous of his own well-being, should not disregard another.

ततः स राजा पिशिताशनानां; सहस्रबाहोरुपलभ्य मैत्रीम्
पुनर्नराणां कदनं चकार; चचार सर्वां पृथिवीं च दर्पात्

tataḥ sa rājā piśitāśanānāṁ; sahasrabāhorupalabhya maitrīm
punarnarāṇāṁ kadanaṁ cakāra; cacāra sarvāṁ pṛthivīṁ ca darpāt
Having acquired friendship with thousandarmed Arjuna, Dasanana, the king of Raksasas, the world began again to journey over distressing the kings.

अर्जुनेन विमुक्तस्तु रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
चचार पृथिवीं सर्वामनिर्विण्णस्तथा कृतः

arjunena vimuktastu rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
cacāra pṛthivīṁ sarvāmanirviṇṇastathā kṛtaḥ
Released by Arjuna, and yet not conceiving any shame, Ravana, the king of Raksasas again began to transverse the earth.

राक्षसं वा मनुष्यं वा शृणुते यं बलाधिकम्
रावणस्तं समासाद्य युद्धे ह्वयति दर्पितः

rākṣasaṁ vā manuṣyaṁ vā śṛṇute yaṁ balādhikam
rāvaṇastaṁ samāsādya yuddhe hvayati darpitaḥ
Raksasas or men, of whom the proud Ravana heard to be powerful he used to approach and summon them for fight.

ततः कदाचित्किष्किन्धां नगरीं वालिपालिताम्
गत्वाह्वयति युद्धाय वालिनं हेममालिनम्

tataḥ kadācitkiṣkindhāṁ nagarīṁ vālipālitām
gatvāhvayati yuddhāya vālinaṁ hemamālinam
After some time he arrived at the city of Kiskindha reared by Vali and invited him, wearing golden garland, to fight.

ततस्तं वानरामात्यस्तारस्तारापिता प्रभुः
उवाच रावणं वाक्यं युद्धप्रेप्सुमुपागतम्

tatastaṁ vānarāmātyastārastārāpitā prabhuḥ
uvāca rāvaṇaṁ vākyaṁ yuddhaprepsumupāgatam
Thereat, Tara, her father Susena and the Prince Sugriva said to the king of Raksasas.

राक्षसेन्द्र गतो वाली यस्ते प्रतिबलो भवेत्
नान्यः प्रमुखतः स्थातुं तव शक्तः प्लवंगमः

rākṣasendra gato vālī yaste pratibalo bhavet
nānyaḥ pramukhataḥ sthātuṁ tava śaktaḥ plavaṁgamaḥ
O lord of Raksasas, he is not present here, who shall be able to withstand you. What monkey else is capable of standing before you?

चतुर्भ्योऽपि समुद्रेभ्यः संध्यामन्वास्य रावण
इमं मुहूर्तमायाति वाली तिष्ठ मुहूर्तकम्

caturbhyo'pi samudrebhyaḥ saṁdhyāmanvāsya rāvaṇa
imaṁ muhūrtamāyāti vālī tiṣṭha muhūrtakam
However, O Ravana, Vali shall soon return after performing the Sandhya rites at the confluence of the four oceans; therefore wait here for a moment.

एतानस्थिचयान्पश्य य एते शङ्खपाण्डुराः
युद्धार्थिनामिमे राजन्वानराधिपतेजसा

etānasthicayānpaśya ya ete śaṅkhapāṇḍurāḥ
yuddhārthināmime rājanvānarādhipatejasā
Behold, O Dasanana, there lie the bones of all those, like conch, who came ere this to fight with the powerful king of monkeys.

यद्वामृतरसः पीतस्त्वया रावणराक्षस
तथा वालिनमासाद्य तदन्तं तव जीवितम्

yadvāmṛtarasaḥ pītastvayā rāvaṇarākṣasa
tathā vālinamāsādya tadantaṁ tava jīvitam
O Ravana, O Raksasa, ever if you have drunk nectar, you shall at this very moment loose your life, when the encounter with Vali shall take place.

अथ वा त्वरसे मर्तुं गच्छ दक्षिणसागरम्
वालिनं द्रक्ष्यसे तत्र भूमिष्ठमिव भास्करम्

atha vā tvarase martuṁ gaccha dakṣiṇasāgaram
vālinaṁ drakṣyase tatra bhūmiṣṭhamiva bhāskaram
Or if you do wish to meet with death do you speedily repair to the southern ocean and you shall behold there Vali like to fire placed on earth.

तत्र हेमगिरिप्रख्यं तरुणार्कनिभाननम्
रावणो वालिनं दृष्ट्वा संध्योपासनतत्परम्

tatra hemagiriprakhyaṁ taruṇārkanibhānanam
rāvaṇo vālinaṁ dṛṣṭvā saṁdhyopāsanatatparam
