Hearing those words, Ravana, the aggrandiser of the triple world, remonstrated with Tara and ascending his flowery car went to the southern ocean and espied Vali, having red countenance like the rising sun, engaged in Sandhya rites with whole-mindedness.

पुष्पकादवरुह्याथ रावणोऽञ्जनसंनिभः
ग्रहीतुं वालिनं तूर्णं निःशब्दपदमाद्रवत्

puṣpakādavaruhyātha rāvaṇo'ñjanasaṁnibhaḥ
grahītuṁ vālinaṁ tūrṇaṁ niḥśabdapadamādravat
Thereupon having descended from his Puspaka car he with silent approached Vali to bring him under his grasp.

शशमालक्ष्य सिंहो वा पन्नगं गरुडो यथा
न चिन्तयति तं वाली रावणं पापनिश्चयम्

śaśamālakṣya siṁho vā pannagaṁ garuḍo yathā
na cintayati taṁ vālī rāvaṇaṁ pāpaniścayam

Casting his looks at pleasure, Vali saw him. Albeit apprised of his evil intention, he was not the least moved. And he did not care for him as a lion is not moved on beholding a hare and Garuda on beholding a serpent.

जिघृक्षमाणमद्यैनं रावणं पापबुद्धिनम्
कक्षावलम्बिनं कृत्वा गमिष्यामि महार्णवान्

jighṛkṣamāṇamadyainaṁ rāvaṇaṁ pāpabuddhinam
kakṣāvalambinaṁ kṛtvā gamiṣyāmi mahārṇavān
He then thought within himself-“This vicious-souled Ravana is approaching to catch me; holding him under my arm pit I shall journey over the three great oceans.

द्रक्ष्यन्त्यरिं ममाङ्कस्थं स्रंसितोरुकराम्बरम्
लम्बमानं दशग्रीवं गरुडस्येव पन्नगम्

drakṣyantyariṁ mamāṅkasthaṁ sraṁsitorukarāmbaram
lambamānaṁ daśagrīvaṁ garuḍasyeva pannagam
Everyone will behold the enemy Ravana, under my arm pit as a serpent possessed by Garuda, with his thighs, arms and clothes loosened.

इत्येवं मतिमास्थाय वाली कर्णमुपाश्रितः
जपन्वै नैगमान्मन्त्रांस्तस्थौ पर्वतराडिव

ityevaṁ matimāsthāya vālī karṇamupāśritaḥ
japanvai naigamānmantrāṁstasthau parvatarāḍiva
Having thought thus Vali remained silent for sometime and reciting incantations he waited there like a mountain.

तावन्योन्यं जिघृक्षन्तौ हरिराक्षसपार्थिवौ
प्रयत्नवन्तौ तत्कर्म ईहतुर्बलदर्पितौ

tāvanyonyaṁ jighṛkṣantau harirākṣasapārthivau
prayatnavantau tatkarma īhaturbaladarpitau
Thereupon the king of monkeys and the lord of Raksasas, proud of strength, essayed to catch one another.

हस्तग्राह्यं तु तं मत्वा पादशब्देन रावणम्
पराङ्मुखोऽपि जग्राह वाली सर्पमिवाण्डजः

hastagrāhyaṁ tu taṁ matvā pādaśabdena rāvaṇam
parāṅmukho'pi jagrāha vālī sarpamivāṇḍajaḥ

Vali was seated with his back (towards Ravana); still from his footsteps he perceived that he had come within the grasp of Ravana's army and he at once caught hold of him like to Garuda holding a serpent.

ग्रहीतुकामं तं गृह्य रक्षसामीश्वरं हरिः
खमुत्पपात वेगेन कृत्वा कक्षावलम्बिनम्

grahītukāmaṁ taṁ gṛhya rakṣasāmīśvaraṁ hariḥ
khamutpapāta vegena kṛtvā kakṣāvalambinam
Getting hold of Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, desirous of catching him, (Vali) and placing him under his arm-pit Vali vehemently rose high up in the welkin.

स तं पीड्दयमानस्तु वितुदन्तं नखैर्मुहुः
जहार रावणं वाली पवनस्तोयदं यथा

sa taṁ pīḍdayamānastu vitudantaṁ nakhairmuhuḥ
jahāra rāvaṇaṁ vālī pavanastoyadaṁ yathā
And he went away carrying him, scratching him again and again with his snails like to winds scattering clouds.

अथ ते राक्षसामात्या ह्रियमाणे दशानने
मुमोक्षयिषवो घोरा रवमाणा ह्यभिद्रवन्

atha te rākṣasāmātyā hriyamāṇe daśānane
mumokṣayiṣavo ghorā ravamāṇā hyabhidravan
The Ten-necked demon being thus carried away, his councillors, to release him, pursued, exclaiming, Vali, in the welkin.

अन्वीयमानस्तैर्वाली भ्राजतेऽम्बरमध्यगः
अन्वीयमानो मेघौघैरम्बरस्थ इवांशुमान्

anvīyamānastairvālī bhrājate'mbaramadhyagaḥ
anvīyamāno meghaughairambarastha ivāṁśumān
They thus following him, Vali, appeared in the sky like the sun in the midst of clouds.

तेऽशक्नुवन्तः संप्राप्तं वालिनं राक्षसोत्तमाः
तस्य बाहूरुवेगेन परिश्रान्तः पतन्ति च

te'śaknuvantaḥ saṁprāptaṁ vālinaṁ rākṣasottamāḥ
tasya bāhūruvegena pariśrāntaḥ patanti ca
The Raksasas could not catch Vali but were rather exhausted by the stroke of his arms and thighs.
वालिमार्गादपाक्रामन्पर्वतेन्द्रा हि गच्छतः
vālimārgādapākrāmanparvatendrā hi gacchataḥ
What to speak of animals made of flesh and blood anxious for their lives even the mountains make way when Vali goes.

अपक्षिगणसंपातो वानरेन्द्रो महाजवः
क्रमशः सागरान्सर्वान्संध्याकालमवन्दत

apakṣigaṇasaṁpāto vānarendro mahājavaḥ
kramaśaḥ sāgarānsarvānsaṁdhyākālamavandata
Rising high up into the sky where even the birds cannot reach, Vali, the lord of monkeys and gifted with great velocity, by and by finished his Sandhya rites above the oceans.

सभाज्यमानो भूतैस्तु खेचरैः खेचरो हरिः
पश्चिमं सागरं वाली आजगाम सरावणः

sabhājyamāno bhūtaistu khecaraiḥ khecaro hariḥ
paścimaṁ sāgaraṁ vālī ājagāma sarāvaṇaḥ
Being worshipped by the aerials their lord, with Ravana, first proceeded to the western ocean.

तत्र संध्यामुपासित्वा स्नात्वा जप्त्वा च वानरः
उत्तरं सागरं प्रायाद्वहमानो दशाननम्

tatra saṁdhyāmupāsitvā snātvā japtvā ca vānaraḥ
uttaraṁ sāgaraṁ prāyādvahamāno daśānanam
Having finished there Sandhya prayers and recited incantations he, with Dasanana, went to the northern ocean.

उत्तरे सागरे संध्यामुपासित्वा दशाननम्
वहमानोऽगमद्वाली पूर्वमम्बुमहानिधिम्

uttare sāgare saṁdhyāmupāsitvā daśānanam
vahamāno'gamadvālī pūrvamambumahānidhim
And having journeyed over many thousand leagues like the wind and mind, that huge monkey, with his enemy, finished his prayers at the northern ocean and then proceeded to the eastern ocean.

तत्रापि संध्यामन्वास्य वासविः स हरीश्वरः
किष्किन्धाभिमुखो गृह्य रावणं पुनरागमत्

tatrāpi saṁdhyāmanvāsya vāsaviḥ sa harīśvaraḥ
kiṣkindhābhimukho gṛhya rāvaṇaṁ punarāgamat
And having recited his prayers there also, Vali, the son of Indra, and the king of monkeys, carrying Ravana, returned to the city of Kisikindha.

चतुर्ष्वपि समुद्रेषु संध्यामन्वास्य वानरः
रावणोद्वहनश्रान्तः किष्किन्धोपवनेऽपतत्

caturṣvapi samudreṣu saṁdhyāmanvāsya vānaraḥ
rāvaṇodvahanaśrāntaḥ kiṣkindhopavane'patat
Having gone through his Sandhya rites at the four oceans and carrying Ravana, that monkeychief was greatly exhausted and (therefore) descended into the gardens of Kiskindha.

रावणं तु मुमोचाथ स्वकक्षात्कपिसत्तमः
कुतस्त्वमिति चोवाच प्रहसन्रावणं प्रति

rāvaṇaṁ tu mumocātha svakakṣātkapisattamaḥ
kutastvamiti covāca prahasanrāvaṇaṁ prati
Having got out Ravana from his arm-pit, the foremost of monkeys, laughing again and again said:-"Where are you coming?"

विस्मयं तु महद्गत्वा श्रमलोकनिरीक्षणः
राक्षसेशो हरीशं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्

vismayaṁ tu mahadgatvā śramalokanirīkṣaṇaḥ
rākṣaseśo harīśaṁ tamidaṁ vacanamabravīt
Thereupon being surprised greatly, Dasanana, the king of Raksasas, with eyes, shaking with exhaustion, said to the king of monkeys.

वानरेन्द्र महेन्द्राभ राक्षसेन्द्रोऽस्मि रावणः
युद्धेप्सुरहं संप्राप्तः स चाद्यासादितस्त्वया

vānarendra mahendrābha rākṣasendro'smi rāvaṇaḥ
yuddhepsurahaṁ saṁprāptaḥ sa cādyāsāditastvayā
O king of monkeys, resembling Mahendra, I am Ravana, the king of Raksasas; I came here to fight: but I have been defeated by you. Alas!

अहो बलमहो वीर्यमहो गम्भीरता च ते
येनाहं पशुवद्गृह्य भ्रामितश्चतुरोऽर्णवान्

aho balamaho vīryamaho gambhīratā ca te
yenāhaṁ paśuvadgṛhya bhrāmitaścaturo'rṇavān
What strength is your! what prowess! What gravity! Holding me like a beast you have journeyed over the four oceans.

एवमश्रान्तवद्वीर शीघ्रमेव च वानर
मां चैवोद्वहमानस्तु कोऽन्यो वीरः क्रमिष्यति

evamaśrāntavadvīra śīghrameva ca vānara
māṁ caivodvahamānastu ko'nyo vīraḥ kramiṣyati
O hero! What heroic wight is there who is not exhausted by carrying me so vehemently?

त्रयाणामेव भूतानां गतिरेषा प्लवंगम
मनोऽनिलसुपर्णानां तव वा नात्र संशयः

trayāṇāmeva bhūtānāṁ gatireṣā plavaṁgama
mano'nilasuparṇānāṁ tava vā nātra saṁśayaḥ
O monkey, mind, wind and Garuda-these three are gifted with the velocity. Undoubtedly you have got the same velocity.

सोऽहं दृष्टबलस्तुभ्यमिच्छामि हरिपुंगव
त्वया सह चिरं सख्यं सुस्निग्धं पावकाग्रतः

so'haṁ dṛṣṭabalastubhyamicchāmi haripuṁgava
tvayā saha ciraṁ sakhyaṁ susnigdhaṁ pāvakāgrataḥ
Your prowess has been sufficiently displayed. But bow I wish, O king of monkeys, to make friends with you for ever before fire.

दाराः पुत्राः पुरं राष्ट्रं भोगाच्छादनभोजनम्
सर्वमेवाविभक्तं नौ भविष्यति हरीश्वर

dārāḥ putrāḥ puraṁ rāṣṭraṁ bhogācchādanabhojanam
sarvamevāvibhaktaṁ nau bhaviṣyati harīśvara
O king of monkeys, from today, wife sons, city, kingdom, enjoyment, cloth and food shall be our common,

ततः प्रज्वालयित्वाग्निं तावुभौ हरिराक्षसौ
भ्रातृत्वमुपसंपन्नौ परिष्वज्य परस्परम्

tataḥ prajvālayitvāgniṁ tāvubhau harirākṣasau
bhrātṛtvamupasaṁpannau pariṣvajya parasparam
Thereupon having lighted up fire the king of monkeys and the king of Raksasas, embracing each other, became friends.

अन्योन्यं लम्बितकरौ ततस्तौ हरिराक्षसौ
किष्किन्धां विशतुर्हृष्टौ सिंहौ गिरिगुहामिव

anyonyaṁ lambitakarau tatastau harirākṣasau
kiṣkindhāṁ viśaturhṛṣṭau siṁhau giriguhāmiva
Thereupon holding each other by the arms they entered the city of Kiskindha like to two lions, entering delightedly a cave.

स तत्र मासमुषितः सुग्रीव इव रावणः
अमात्यैरागतैर्नीचस्त्रैलोक्योत्सादनार्थिभिः

sa tatra māsamuṣitaḥ sugrīva iva rāvaṇaḥ
amātyairāgatairnīcastrailokyotsādanārthibhiḥ
There like Sugriva Ravana spent a month. Afterwards his councillors, desirous of destroying the triple world, took him away.

एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तं वालिना रावणः प्रभो
धर्षितश्च कृतश्चापि भ्राता पावकसंनिधौ

evametatpurāvṛttaṁ vālinā rāvaṇaḥ prabho
dharṣitaśca kṛtaścāpi bhrātā pāvakasaṁnidhau
O lord Rama, I have thus related to you the previous history. Having thus belaboured Ravana Vali at last made friends with him before fire.

बलमप्रतिमं राम वालिनोऽभवदुत्तमम्
सोऽपि तया विनिर्दग्धः शलभो वह्निना यथा

balamapratimaṁ rāma vālino'bhavaduttamam
so'pi tayā vinirdagdhaḥ śalabho vahninā yathā
O Rama, Vali and unequalled and great strength. Like to fire burning down locusts you did burn down Vali.

अपृच्छत ततो रामो दक्षिणाशालयं मुनिम्
प्राञ्जलिर्विनयोपेत इदमाह वचोऽर्थवत्

apṛcchata tato rāmo dakṣiṇāśālayaṁ munim
prāñjalirvinayopeta idamāha vaco'rthavat
Thereupon Rama, being stricken with curiosity, with folded palms and humbly accosted Agastya, residing in the southern quarter, with pregnant accents, saying.

अतुलं बलमेताभ्यां वालिनो रावणस्य च
न त्वेतौ हनुमद्वीर्यैः समाविति मतिर्मम

atulaṁ balametābhyāṁ vālino rāvaṇasya ca
na tvetau hanumadvīryaiḥ samāviti matirmama
You say that Ravana and Vali had unequalled strength but I think their can not equal that of Hanuman.

शौर्यं दाक्ष्यं बलं धैर्यं प्राज्ञता नयसाधनम्
विक्रमश्च प्रभावश्च हनूमति कृतालयाः

śauryaṁ dākṣyaṁ balaṁ dhairyaṁ prājñatā nayasādhanam
vikramaśca prabhāvaśca hanūmati kṛtālayāḥ
Heroism, liberality, strength, patience, intellect, knowledge of lawn and means, prowess and energy all exist together in Hanuman. on

दृष्ट्वोदधिं विषीदन्तीं तदैष कपिवाहिनीम्
समाश्वास्य कपीन्भूयो योजनानां शतं प्लुतः

dṛṣṭvodadhiṁ viṣīdantīṁ tadaiṣa kapivāhinīm
samāśvāsya kapīnbhūyo yojanānāṁ śataṁ plutaḥ
When the monkey host lost heart beholding the ocean, Hanuman, consoling crossed over the deep extending over a hundred leagues.

धर्षयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कां रावणान्तःपुरं तथा
दृष्ट्वा संभाषिता चापि सीता विश्वासिता तथा

dharṣayitvā purīṁ laṅkāṁ rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṁ tathā
dṛṣṭvā saṁbhāṣitā cāpi sītā viśvāsitā tathā
Having discarded the presiding goddess of Lanka he went to the mansion of Ravana and on beholding Sita there, he consoled her.

सेनाग्रगा मन्त्रिसुताः किंकरा रावणात्मजः
एते हनुमता तत्र एकेन विनिपातिताः

senāgragā mantrisutāḥ kiṁkarā rāvaṇātmajaḥ
ete hanumatā tatra ekena vinipātitāḥ
What to speak of more, Hanuman, singlehanded, slew Ravana's commander-in-chief, the minister's son, his servants and his one son.

भूयो बन्धाद्विमुक्तेन संभाषित्वा दशाननम्
लङ्का भस्मीकृता तेन पावकेनेव मेदिनी

bhūyo bandhādvimuktena saṁbhāṣitvā daśānanam
laṅkā bhasmīkṛtā tena pāvakeneva medinī
Being released from the Brahma weapon Hanuman remonstrated with Ravana, and reduced Larka into ashes like to fire burning down earth.

न कालस्य न शक्रस्य न विष्णोर्वित्तपस्य च
कर्माणि तानि श्रूयन्ते यानि युद्धे हनूमतः

na kālasya na śakrasya na viṣṇorvittapasya ca
karmāṇi tāni śrūyante yāni yuddhe hanūmataḥ
What I have seen myself performed by Hanuman in the conflict is above the power of Kala, Vasava and even the lord of riches.

एतस्य बाहुवीर्येण लङ्का सीता च लक्ष्मणः
प्राप्तो मया जयश्चैव राज्यं मित्राणि बान्धवाः

etasya bāhuvīryeṇa laṅkā sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
prāpto mayā jayaścaiva rājyaṁ mitrāṇi bāndhavāḥ
It is by the strength of the arms of that Windgod's son I ave obtained Lanka, Sita, Laksmana, Victory, kingdom and my friends.

हनूमान्यदि मे न स्याद्वानराधिपतेः सखा
प्रवृत्तमपि को वेत्तुं जानक्याः शक्तिमान्भवेत्

hanūmānyadi me na syādvānarādhipateḥ sakhā
pravṛttamapi ko vettuṁ jānakyāḥ śaktimānbhavet
What more, had not Hanuman, the friend of the king of monkeys-Sugriva, been in my company who could have brought Sita intelligence?

किमर्थं वाली चैतेन सुग्रीवप्रियकाम्यया
तदा वैरे समुत्पन्ने न दग्धो वीरुधो यथा

kimarthaṁ vālī caitena sugrīvapriyakāmyayā
tadā vaire samutpanne na dagdho vīrudho yathā
Why did not Hanuman, although wishing welfare to Sugriva, reduce Vali to ashes like so many creepers on the occasion of his quarrel with Sugriva?

न हि वेदितवान्मन्ये हनूमानात्मनो बलम्
यद्दृष्टवाञ्जीवितेष्टं क्लिश्यन्तं वानराधिपम्

na hi veditavānmanye hanūmānātmano balam
yaddṛṣṭavāñjīviteṣṭaṁ kliśyantaṁ vānarādhipam
Methinks, Hanuman was not cognisant of his own prowess then? And therefore he did stood to witness the miseries of Sugriva— the king of monkeys who was dearer than his life.

एतन्मे भगवन्सर्वं हनूमति महामुने
विस्तरेण यथातत्त्वं कथयामरपूजित

etanme bhagavansarvaṁ hanūmati mahāmune
vistareṇa yathātattvaṁ kathayāmarapūjita
O you worshipped of the immortals, do you truly describe to me in detail this action of Hanuman.

राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुयुक्तमृषिस्ततः
हनूमतः समक्षं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्

rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetuyuktamṛṣistataḥ
hanūmataḥ samakṣaṁ tamidaṁ vacanamabravīt
Hearing those well-meaning words of Raghava, the ascetic Agastya said to him in the presence of Hanuman.

सत्यमेतद्रघुश्रेष्ठ यद्ब्रवीषि हनूमतः
न बले विद्यते तुल्यो न गतौ न मतौ परः

satyametadraghuśreṣṭha yadbravīṣi hanūmataḥ
na bale vidyate tulyo na gatau na matau paraḥ
O foremost of Raghus, what, you have said regarding Hanuman, is all true. As regards, strength, velocity and intellect there is none who can equal Hanuman.

अमोघशापैः शापस्तु दत्तोऽस्य ऋषिभिः पुरा
न वेदिता बलं येन बली सन्नरिमर्दनः

amoghaśāpaiḥ śāpastu datto'sya ṛṣibhiḥ purā
na veditā balaṁ yena balī sannarimardanaḥ
O repressor of enemies, in the days of yore Hanuman was imprecated by the ascetics, whose curses never become fruitless, to the effect that he would never be conscious of his whole strength.

बाल्येऽप्येतेन यत्कर्म कृतं राम महाबल
तन्न वर्णयितुं शक्यमतिबालतयास्य ते

bālye'pyetena yatkarma kṛtaṁ rāma mahābala
tanna varṇayituṁ śakyamatibālatayāsya te
I am not capable of describing to you the wondrous childish feat which Hanuman did perform in his boyhood.

यदि वास्ति त्वभिप्रायस्तच्छ्रोतुं तव राघव
समाधाय मतिं राम निशामय वदाम्यहम्

yadi vāsti tvabhiprāyastacchrotuṁ tava rāghava
samādhāya matiṁ rāma niśāmaya vadāmyaham
But if you are, O Raghava, greatly anxious to hear it, I shall relate do you hear with a quiescent mind.

सूर्यदत्तवरस्वर्णः सुमेरुर्नाम पर्वतः
यत्र राज्यं प्रशास्त्यस्य केसरी नाम वै पिता

sūryadattavarasvarṇaḥ sumerurnāma parvataḥ
yatra rājyaṁ praśāstyasya kesarī nāma vai pitā
Hanuman's father Kesari reigned in the mountain Sumeru which resembles gold by the influence of the sun.

तस्य भार्या बभूवेष्टा ह्यञ्जनेति परिश्रुता
जनयामास तस्यां वै वायुरात्मजमुत्तमम्

tasya bhāryā babhūveṣṭā hyañjaneti pariśrutā
janayāmāsa tasyāṁ vai vāyurātmajamuttamam
Kesari had a well-known wife by the name of Anjana to whom he was greatly attached. The deity Wind begot on Anjana an excellent son.

शालिशूकसमाभासं प्रासूतेमं तदाञ्जना
फलान्याहर्तुकामा वै निष्क्रान्ता गहने चरा

śāliśūkasamābhāsaṁ prāsūtemaṁ tadāñjanā
phalānyāhartukāmā vai niṣkrāntā gahane carā
Repairing to a dense forest for collecting fruits, the excellent damsel gave birth to Hanuman resembling the tip of a sala tree and went away.

एष मातुर्वियोगाच्च क्षुधया च भृशार्दितः
रुरोद शिशुरत्यर्थं शिशुः शरभराडिव

eṣa māturviyogācca kṣudhayā ca bhṛśārditaḥ
ruroda śiśuratyarthaṁ śiśuḥ śarabharāḍiva
Being distressed with hunger on account of the absence of the mother, Hanuman, just born, cried like Kartikeya, the commander-in-chief of the celestials, in the forest of Saras.

ततोद्यन्तं विवस्वन्तं जपापुष्पोत्करोपमम्
ददृशे फललोभाच्च उत्पपात रविं प्रति

tatodyantaṁ vivasvantaṁ japāpuṣpotkaropamam
dadṛśe phalalobhācca utpapāta raviṁ prati
At this time the sun resembling Japa flowers, having risen, Hanuman, to get a fruit, sprang up.

बालार्काभिमुखो बालो बालार्क इव मूर्तिमान्
ग्रहीतुकामो बालार्कं प्लवतेऽम्बरमध्यगः

bālārkābhimukho bālo bālārka iva mūrtimān
grahītukāmo bālārkaṁ plavate'mbaramadhyagaḥ
Being desirous of holding the newly risen sun, Hanuman, resembling it, began to leap in the middle of the welkin.

एतस्मिन्प्लवमाने तु शिशुभावे हनूमति
देवदानवसिद्धानां विस्मयः सुमहानभूत्

etasminplavamāne tu śiśubhāve hanūmati
devadānavasiddhānāṁ vismayaḥ sumahānabhūt
The child Hanuman having thus ascended the sky, celestials, Danavas and Yaksas surprisingly exclaimed.

नाप्येवं वेगवान्वायुर्गरुडो न मनस्तथा
यथायं वायुपुत्रस्तु क्रमतेऽम्बरमुत्तमम्

nāpyevaṁ vegavānvāyurgaruḍo na manastathā
yathāyaṁ vāyuputrastu kramate'mbaramuttamam
The velocity, with which Marut's son is going, is not possessed even by the Wind, Garuda and mind.

यदि तावच्छिशोरस्य ईदृशौ गतिविक्रमौ
यौवनं बलमासाद्य कथं वेगो भविष्यति

yadi tāvacchiśorasya īdṛśau gativikramau
yauvanaṁ balamāsādya kathaṁ vego bhaviṣyati
If he has got such vehemence in his boyhood what great strength he shall have in his youth.

तमनुप्लवते वायुः प्लवन्तं पुत्रमात्मनः
सूर्यदाहभयाद्रक्षंस्तुषारचयशीतलः

tamanuplavate vāyuḥ plavantaṁ putramātmanaḥ
sūryadāhabhayādrakṣaṁstuṣāracayaśītalaḥ
His own son thus leaping, the wind, becoming cool by the touch of snow, began to follow him proceeding in the sky lest the rays of the sun might scorch him.

बहुयोजनसाहस्रं क्रमत्येष ततोऽम्बरम्
पितुर्बलाच्च बाल्याच्च भास्कराभ्याशमागतः

bahuyojanasāhasraṁ kramatyeṣa tato'mbaram
piturbalācca bālyācca bhāskarābhyāśamāgataḥ
Rising high up in the sky on account of childish freaks and traversed many thousand leagues by the help of his father Hanuman neared the sun.

शिशुरेष त्वदोषज्ञ इति मत्वा दिवाकरः
कार्यं चात्र समायत्तमित्येवं न ददाह सः

śiśureṣa tvadoṣajña iti matvā divākaraḥ
kāryaṁ cātra samāyattamityevaṁ na dadāha saḥ
Considering that he was a mere child and therefore not tarnished by any sin and that a great divine work would be accomplished by him in future the sun did not burn Hanuman.

यमेव दिवसं ह्येष ग्रहीतुं भास्करं प्लुतः
तमेव दिवसं राहुर्जिघृक्षति दिवाकरम्

yameva divasaṁ hyeṣa grahītuṁ bhāskaraṁ plutaḥ
tameva divasaṁ rāhurjighṛkṣati divākaram
At the every day when Hanuman sprang up to hold the sun, Rahu too essayed to possess him.

अनेन च परामृष्टो राम सूर्यरथोपरि
अपक्रान्तस्ततस्त्रस्तो राहुश्चन्द्रार्कमर्दनः

anena ca parāmṛṣṭo rāma sūryarathopari
apakrāntastatastrasto rāhuścandrārkamardanaḥ
Having reached the top of the sun's car Hanuman touched Rahu; so he, the repressor of the moon's rays, accordingly went back on beholding the sun thus possessed.

स इन्द्रभवनं गत्वा सरोषः सिंहिकासुतः
अब्रवीद्भ्रुकुटीं कृत्वा देवं देवगणैर्वृतम्

sa indrabhavanaṁ gatvā saroṣaḥ siṁhikāsutaḥ
abravīdbhrukuṭīṁ kṛtvā devaṁ devagaṇairvṛtam
And repairing to the house of Indra, Sinhika's son, in wrath and with frowns, said to him encircled by the celestials.

बुभुक्षापनयं दत्त्वा चन्द्रार्कौ मम वासव
किमिदं तत्त्वया दत्तमन्यस्य बलवृत्रहन्

bubhukṣāpanayaṁ dattvā candrārkau mama vāsava
kimidaṁ tattvayā dattamanyasya balavṛtrahan
O Vasava! O slayer of Bala and Vrtra-to remove my hunger you did give me both the sun and moon; why you have then given them to another?

अद्याहं पर्वकाले तु जिघृक्षुः सूर्यमागतः
अथान्यो राहुरासाद्य जग्राह सहसा रविम्

adyāhaṁ parvakāle tu jighṛkṣuḥ sūryamāgataḥ
athānyo rāhurāsādya jagrāha sahasā ravim
On account of the Parva I came to devour the sun but another Rahu came and possessed him.

इन्द्रः करीन्द्रमारुह्य राहुं कृत्वा पुरःसरम्
प्रायाद्यत्राभवत्सूर्यः सहानेन हनूमता

indraḥ karīndramāruhya rāhuṁ kṛtvā puraḥsaram
prāyādyatrābhavatsūryaḥ sahānena hanūmatā

Hearing the words of Rahu, the King of the deities, wearing a golden garland, having his understanding bewildered, proceeded, on the back of his elephant-chief Airavata, huge like the summit of the Kailasa hill, with temporal juice always trickling, having four tasks, roaring, and adorned with golden bells, towards Hanuman and the sun with Rahu before him.

अथातिरभसेनागाद्राहुरुत्सृज्य वासवम्
अनेन च स वै दृष्ट आधावञ्शैलकूटवत्

athātirabhasenāgādrāhurutsṛjya vāsavam
anena ca sa vai dṛṣṭa ādhāvañśailakūṭavat
Having left behind Indra, Rahu, quickly went there but fled away on beholding the hugebodied Hanuman resembling a mountain summit.

ततः सूर्यं समुत्सृज्य राहुमेवमवेक्ष्य च
उत्पपात पुनर्व्योम ग्रहीतुं सिंहिकासुतम्

tataḥ sūryaṁ samutsṛjya rāhumevamavekṣya ca
utpapāta punarvyoma grahītuṁ siṁhikāsutam
Thereupon leaving aside the sun and being desirous of holding Rahu, the son of Simhika considering him as a fruit, Hanuman again sprang up into the sky.

उत्सृज्यार्कमिमं राम आधावन्तं प्लवंगमम्
दृष्ट्वा राहुः परावृत्य मुखशेषः पराङ्मुखः

utsṛjyārkamimaṁ rāma ādhāvantaṁ plavaṁgamam
dṛṣṭvā rāhuḥ parāvṛtya mukhaśeṣaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ
Beholding Hanuman approach renouncing the sun, Rahu with his countenance only visible, desisted and went back.

इन्द्रमाशंसमानस्तु त्रातारं सिंहिकासुतः
इन्द्र इन्द्रेति संत्रासान्मुहुर्मुहुरभाषत

indramāśaṁsamānastu trātāraṁ siṁhikāsutaḥ
indra indreti saṁtrāsānmuhurmuhurabhāṣata
And considering Indra as the saviour the son of Simhika, stricken with fear, again and again cried aloud "Indra! Indra!!"

राहोर्विक्रोशमानस्य प्रागेवालक्षितः स्वरः
श्रुत्वेन्द्रोवाच मा भैषीरयमेनं निहन्म्यहम्

rāhorvikrośamānasya prāgevālakṣitaḥ svaraḥ
śrutvendrovāca mā bhaiṣīrayamenaṁ nihanmyaham
Understanding everything by the piteous accents of Rahu Indra said, “No fear, I shall soon slay him.”

ऐरावतं ततो दृष्ट्वा महत्तदिदमित्यपि
फलं तं हस्तिराजानमभिदुद्राव मारुतिः

airāvataṁ tato dṛṣṭvā mahattadidamityapi
phalaṁ taṁ hastirājānamabhidudrāva mārutiḥ
Thereupon beholding the huge-bodied Airavat and considering him as a bigger fruit Maruti ran towards him.

तदास्य धावतो रूपमैरावतजिघृक्षया
मुहूर्तमभवद्घोरमिन्द्राग्न्योरिव भास्वरम्

tadāsya dhāvato rūpamairāvatajighṛkṣayā
muhūrtamabhavadghoramindrāgnyoriva bhāsvaram
Proceeding thus tempestuously when he rose above the head of Indra, Hanuman, looked in a moment dreadful like the fire of dissolution.

एवमाधावमानं तु नातिक्रुद्धः शचीपतिः
हस्तान्तेनातिमुक्तेन कुलिशेनाभ्यताडयत्

evamādhāvamānaṁ tu nātikruddhaḥ śacīpatiḥ
hastāntenātimuktena kuliśenābhyatāḍayat
But not greatly enraged the thousand-eyed lord of Saci, with the thunder bolt in his hand, struck the running Hanuman.

ततो गिरौ पपातैष इन्द्रवज्राभिताडितः
पतमानस्य चैतस्य वामो हनुरभज्यत

tato girau papātaiṣa indravajrābhitāḍitaḥ
patamānasya caitasya vāmo hanurabhajyata
Belaboured by the thunder-bolt of Indra Hanuman fell down on a summit and broke his left jaw.

तस्मिंस्तु पतिते बाले वज्रताडनविह्वले
चुक्रोधेन्द्राय पवनः प्रजानामशिवाय च

tasmiṁstu patite bāle vajratāḍanavihvale
cukrodhendrāya pavanaḥ prajānāmaśivāya ca
He being thus overwhelmed by the stoke of Indra's thunder-bolt, the Wind-god became displeased with the king of celestials and was determined upon bringing about mischief to all created beings.

विण्मूत्राशयमावृत्य प्रजास्वन्तर्गतः प्रभुः
रुरोध सर्वभूतानि यथा वर्षाणि वासवः

viṇmūtrāśayamāvṛtya prajāsvantargataḥ prabhuḥ
rurodha sarvabhūtāni yathā varṣāṇi vāsavaḥ

The all-comprehending wind, not spreading himself, entered into a cave with his son. Like to Vasava distressing all creatures by putting a stop to the showers, the wind too put all animals into unbearable suffering by obstructing all execrations.

वायुप्रकोपाद्भूतानि निरुच्छ्वासानि सर्वतः
संधिभिर्भज्यमानानि काष्ठभूतानि जज्ञिरे

vāyuprakopādbhūtāni nirucchvāsāni sarvataḥ
saṁdhibhirbhajyamānāni kāṣṭhabhūtāni jajñire
On account of the anger of the Wind-god their breath was completely obstructed, and the joints-as if pierced, became hard as wood.

निःस्वधं निर्वषट्कारं निष्क्रियं धर्मवर्जितम्
वायुप्रकोपात्त्रैलोक्यं निरयस्थमिवाबभौ

niḥsvadhaṁ nirvaṣaṭkāraṁ niṣkriyaṁ dharmavarjitam
vāyuprakopāttrailokyaṁ nirayasthamivābabhau
Svadhyaya Vasatkara and all the religious observances of the triple world were put a stop to by the anger of the Wind-god. So the three world appeared as if stricken with sorrow.

ततः प्रजाः सगन्धर्वाः सदेवासुरमानुषाः
प्रजापतिं समाधावन्नसुखार्ताः सुखैषिणः

tataḥ prajāḥ sagandharvāḥ sadevāsuramānuṣāḥ
prajāpatiṁ samādhāvannasukhārtāḥ sukhaiṣiṇaḥ
Thereupon the affixed celestials, Gandharvas, Asuras and men repaired to the Patriarch Brahma with a view to bring about the wellbeing of created beings.

त्वया दत्तोऽयमस्माकमायुषः पवनः पतिः
सोऽस्मान्प्राणेश्वरो भूत्वा कस्मादेषोऽद्य सत्तम

tvayā datto'yamasmākamāyuṣaḥ pavanaḥ patiḥ
so'smānprāṇeśvaro bhūtvā kasmādeṣo'dya sattama

With their bellies swollen for the obstruction of the wind the celestials with folded hands said: "O lord of created beings, you have created four classes of beings and you have given us wind to preserve our lives. But we do not know, why the wind, the lord of our beings, is distressing us, by obstructing our movements like to females confined in an inner apartment.
वायुसंरोधजं दुःखमिदं नो नुद शत्रुहन्
vāyusaṁrodhajaṁ duḥkhamidaṁ no nuda śatruhan
Being thus distressed by the wind we have come to seek your shelter. O you the remover of miseries-do you remove our affictions consequent upon the obstruction of the wind..

एतत्प्रजानां श्रुत्वा तु प्रजानाथः प्रजापतिः
कारणादिति तानुक्त्वा प्रजाः पुनरभाषत

etatprajānāṁ śrutvā tu prajānāthaḥ prajāpatiḥ
kāraṇāditi tānuktvā prajāḥ punarabhāṣata
Hearing those words of the created beings, and saying the reason of that the lord of creation (the Patriarch Brahma) again said.

यस्मिन्वः कारणे वायुश्चुक्रोध च रुरोध च
प्रजाः शृणुध्वं तत्सर्वं श्रोतव्यं चात्मनः क्षमम्

yasminvaḥ kāraṇe vāyuścukrodha ca rurodha ca
prajāḥ śṛṇudhvaṁ tatsarvaṁ śrotavyaṁ cātmanaḥ kṣamam
Hear, O created beings, why the wind, being enraged, has obstructed the course of all beings. All that deserves to be listened and it is right too.

पुत्रस्तस्यामरेशेन इन्द्रेणाद्य निपातितः
राहोर्वचनमाज्ञाय राज्ञा वः कोपितोऽनिलः

putrastasyāmareśena indreṇādya nipātitaḥ
rāhorvacanamājñāya rājñā vaḥ kopito'nilaḥ
Hearing the words of Rahu, Indra, the king of ION 35 RAMAYANAM the celestials, has belaboured the Wind-god's son. It is for this that he has been offended.

अशरीरः शरीरेषु वायुश्चरति पालयन्
शरीरं हि विना वायुं समतां याति रेणुभिः

aśarīraḥ śarīreṣu vāyuścarati pālayan
śarīraṁ hi vinā vāyuṁ samatāṁ yāti reṇubhiḥ
Preserving the bodies, the wind, having no persons, passes through them all. Without wind the body becomes like wood.

अद्यैव च परित्यक्तं वायुना जगदायुषा
अद्यैवेमे निरुच्छ्वासाः काष्ठकुड्योपमाः स्थिताः

adyaiva ca parityaktaṁ vāyunā jagadāyuṣā
adyaiveme nirucchvāsāḥ kāṣṭhakuḍyopamāḥ sthitāḥ

Therefore the wind constitutes the life, the happiness and the whole universe. Renouncing the wind the world cannot attain to happiness. Being cast off by the wind and having their breaths obstructed, behold, the world, today appear like dried wood.

तद्यामस्तत्र यत्रास्ते मारुतो रुक्प्रदो हि वः
मा विनाशं गमिष्याम अप्रसाद्यादितेः सुतम्

tadyāmastatra yatrāste māruto rukprado hi vaḥ
mā vināśaṁ gamiṣyāma aprasādyāditeḥ sutam
Let us therefore go there where the wind, the giver of our afflictions, wait. If we do not please the son of Aditi we shall all meet with destruction.

ततः प्रजाभिः सहितः प्रजापतिः; सदेवगन्धर्वभुजंगगुह्यकः
जगाम तत्रास्यति यत्र मारुतः; सुतं सुरेन्द्राभिहतं प्रगृह्य सः

tataḥ prajābhiḥ sahitaḥ prajāpatiḥ; sadevagandharvabhujaṁgaguhyakaḥ
jagāma tatrāsyati yatra mārutaḥ; sutaṁ surendrābhihataṁ pragṛhya saḥ
Thereupon the Patriarch Brahma, the celestials, Gandharvas, serpents, Guhyakas and other created beings went where the wind was waiting with his own son belaboured by the king of the celestials.

ततोऽर्कवैश्वानरकाञ्चनप्रभं; सुतं तदोत्सङ्गगतं सदागतेः
चतुर्मुखो वीक्ष्य कृपामथाकरो;त्सदेवसिद्धर्षिभुजंगराक्षसः

tato'rkavaiśvānarakāñcanaprabhaṁ; sutaṁ tadotsaṅgagataṁ sadāgateḥ
caturmukho vīkṣya kṛpāmathākaro;tsadevasiddharṣibhujaṁgarākṣasaḥ
Thereupon beholding that boy, on the lap of the Wind-God, resembling gold and Baisvanara, the four-mouthed Brahma, the celestials, Gandharvas, Rsis, Yaksas and Raksasas were all moved with pity.

ततः पितामहं दृष्ट्वा वायुः पुत्रवधार्दितः
शिशुकं तं समादाय उत्तस्थौ धातुरग्रतः

tataḥ pitāmahaṁ dṛṣṭvā vāyuḥ putravadhārditaḥ
śiśukaṁ taṁ samādāya uttasthau dhāturagrataḥ
Seeing Brahma the Vayu troubled with the death of his son, stood in front of the sustainer of the world.

चलत्कुण्डलमौलिस्रक्तपनीयविभूषणः
पादयोर्न्यपतद्वायुस्तिस्रोऽवस्थाय वेधसे

calatkuṇḍalamaulisraktapanīyavibhūṣaṇaḥ
pādayornyapatadvāyustisro'vasthāya vedhase
Thrice the Vayu prostrated before the Brahma with swinging ear-rings, illustrious diadem, garland and ornament of the gold,

तं तु वेदविदाद्यस्तु लम्बाभरणशोभिना
वायुमुत्थाप्य हस्तेन शिशुं तं परिमृष्टवान्

taṁ tu vedavidādyastu lambābharaṇaśobhinā
vāyumutthāpya hastena śiśuṁ taṁ parimṛṣṭavān
The knower of the Vedas lifted up the Vayu with his outstretched and adorned hands and embraced the child.

स्पृष्टमात्रस्ततः सोऽथ सलीलं पद्मजन्मना
जलसिक्तं यथा सस्यं पुनर्जीवितमाप्तवान्

spṛṣṭamātrastataḥ so'tha salīlaṁ padmajanmanā
jalasiktaṁ yathā sasyaṁ punarjīvitamāptavān
With the touch of lotusborn Brahma, the child (Hanuman) came back to life just like the crop irrigated with water.

प्राणवन्तमिमं दृष्ट्वा प्राणो गन्धवहो मुदा
चचार सर्वभूतेषु संनिरुद्धं यथापुरा

prāṇavantamimaṁ dṛṣṭvā prāṇo gandhavaho mudā
cacāra sarvabhūteṣu saṁniruddhaṁ yathāpurā
Seeing the child alive, the Vayu. started blowing happily through all the lokas in the form of vital air.

मरुद्रोगविनिर्मुक्ताः प्रजा वै मुदिताभवन्
शीतवातविनिर्मुक्ताः पद्मिन्य इव साम्बुजाः

marudrogavinirmuktāḥ prajā vai muditābhavan
śītavātavinirmuktāḥ padminya iva sāmbujāḥ
Having released from the confinement of Vayu, all the creatures became happy like lotus flowers when rid of cold winds.

ततस्त्रियुग्मस्त्रिककुत्त्रिधामा त्रिदशार्चितः
उवाच देवता ब्रह्मा मारुतप्रियकाम्यया

tatastriyugmastrikakuttridhāmā tridaśārcitaḥ
uvāca devatā brahmā mārutapriyakāmyayā

Then Brahma keeping the well being of Vayu in his mind spoke to the Gods. Brahma is endowed with three attributive epithets, viz. Triyugma; (three paired) Tridhama (three formed). Tridasarcita (worshipped by three and ten Gods).

भो महेन्द्राग्निवरुणधनेश्वरमहेश्वराः
जानतामपि तत्सर्वं हितं वक्ष्यामि श्रूयताम्

bho mahendrāgnivaruṇadhaneśvaramaheśvarāḥ
jānatāmapi tatsarvaṁ hitaṁ vakṣyāmi śrūyatām
O powerful Indra, Agni, Varuna, Mahesvara and Kubera although you know it well, I will relate it for your well being.

अनेन शिशुना कार्यं कर्तव्यं वो भविष्यति
ददतास्य वरान्सर्वे मारुतस्यास्य तुष्टिदान्

anena śiśunā kāryaṁ kartavyaṁ vo bhaviṣyati
dadatāsya varānsarve mārutasyāsya tuṣṭidān
This child will carry out your intentions, so offer him boons to please the God Vayu.

ततः सहस्रनयनः प्रीतिरक्तः शुभाननः
कुशे शयमयीं मालां समुत्क्षिप्येदमब्रवीत्

tataḥ sahasranayanaḥ prītiraktaḥ śubhānanaḥ
kuśe śayamayīṁ mālāṁ samutkṣipyedamabravīt
Thereupon the thousand eyed, charming Indra setting aside the garland of lotus flowers spoke thus.

मत्करोत्सृष्टवज्रेण हनुरस्य यथा क्षतः
नाम्नैष कपिशार्दूलो भविता हनुमानिति

matkarotsṛṣṭavajreṇa hanurasya yathā kṣataḥ
nāmnaiṣa kapiśārdūlo bhavitā hanumāniti
Since his chin got wounded by the thunderbolt released by me, so this tiger among Mongoloids will be known as Hanunian.

अहमेवास्य दास्यामि परमं वरमुत्तमम्
अतः प्रभृति वज्रस्य ममावध्यो भविष्यति

ahamevāsya dāsyāmi paramaṁ varamuttamam
ataḥ prabhṛti vajrasya mamāvadhyo bhaviṣyati
I will offer him a unique boon. He will not be killed hereafter with the help of my Vajra (or a weapon made of thunderbolt).

मार्ताण्डस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र भगवांस्तिमिरापहः
तेजसोऽस्य मदीयस्य ददामि शतिकां कलाम्

mārtāṇḍastvabravīttatra bhagavāṁstimirāpahaḥ
tejaso'sya madīyasya dadāmi śatikāṁ kalām
The god Martanda, the dispeller of darkness, on that occasion told that I will bestow upon him the hundredth part of my brilliance,

यदा तु शास्त्राण्यध्येतुं शक्तिरस्य भविष्यति
तदास्य शास्त्रं दास्यामि येन वाग्मी भविष्यति

yadā tu śāstrāṇyadhyetuṁ śaktirasya bhaviṣyati
tadāsya śāstraṁ dāsyāmi yena vāgmī bhaviṣyati

When he will be capable of learning Sastras, I will transmit in him the knowledge of all the Sastras, so that he may become a good orater. Now shall be able to vie with him in the knowledge of Sastras.

वरुणश्च वरं प्रादान्नास्य मृत्युर्भविष्यति
वर्षायुतशतेनापि मत्पाशादुदकादपि

varuṇaśca varaṁ prādānnāsya mṛtyurbhaviṣyati
varṣāyutaśatenāpi matpāśādudakādapi
Varuna bestowed upon him the boon that he well not die for hundred ayuta years even from the my noose (Pasa) or waters either.

यमोऽपि दण्डावध्यत्वमरोगत्वं च नित्यशः
दिशतेऽस्य वरं तुष्ट अविषादं च संयुगे

yamo'pi daṇḍāvadhyatvamarogatvaṁ ca nityaśaḥ
diśate'sya varaṁ tuṣṭa aviṣādaṁ ca saṁyuge
Yama granted invulnerability to his Danda and diseases. The Kuber told he will ever remain happy and satisfied even at the time adversary.

गदेयं मामिका नैनं संयुगेषु वधिष्यति
इत्येवं वरदः प्राह तदा ह्येकाक्षिपिङ्गलः

gadeyaṁ māmikā nainaṁ saṁyugeṣu vadhiṣyati
ityevaṁ varadaḥ prāha tadā hyekākṣipiṅgalaḥ
This mace of mine will not cause his death. So was said by Kubera endowed with one brown eye.

मत्तो मदायुधानां च न वध्योऽयं भविष्यति
इत्येवं शंकरेणापि दत्तोऽस्य परमो वरः

matto madāyudhānāṁ ca na vadhyo'yaṁ bhaviṣyati
ityevaṁ śaṁkareṇāpi datto'sya paramo varaḥ
Sankara also bestowed upon him a great boon that this cannot be killed even by my weapons.

सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्योऽयं भविष्यति
दीर्घायुश्च महात्मा च इति ब्रह्माब्रवीद्वचः

sarveṣāṁ brahmadaṇḍānāmavadhyo'yaṁ bhaviṣyati
dīrghāyuśca mahātmā ca iti brahmābravīdvacaḥ
And Brahma bestowed his blessings upon him saying that he will live long and will be invulnerable to all the weapons invented by Brahma.

ततः सुराणां तु वरैर्दृष्ट्वा ह्येनमलंकृतम्
चतुर्मुखस्तुष्टमुखो वायुमाह जगद्गुरुः

tataḥ surāṇāṁ tu varairdṛṣṭvā hyenamalaṁkṛtam
caturmukhastuṣṭamukho vāyumāha jagadguruḥ
Afterwards seeing him equipped with the blessings of Gods. Caturmukha Brahma, the teacher of the whole world told Vayu happily.

अमित्राणां भयकरो मित्राणामभयंकरः
अजेयो भविता तेऽत्र पुत्रो मारुतमारुतिः

amitrāṇāṁ bhayakaro mitrāṇāmabhayaṁkaraḥ
ajeyo bhavitā te'tra putro mārutamārutiḥ
Your son Hanuman, O Marut, will terrorise the foes and safeguard the friends. He will be in conquerable.

रावणोत्सादनार्थानि रामप्रीतिकराणि च
रोमहर्षकराण्येष कर्ता कर्माणि संयुगे

rāvaṇotsādanārthāni rāmaprītikarāṇi ca
romaharṣakarāṇyeṣa kartā karmāṇi saṁyuge
In the war he will kill do such bewildering deeds as will destroy Ravana and please Rama.

एवमुक्त्वा तमामन्त्र्य मारुतं तेऽमरैः सह
यथागतं ययुः सर्वे पितामहपुरोगमाः

evamuktvā tamāmantrya mārutaṁ te'maraiḥ saha
yathāgataṁ yayuḥ sarve pitāmahapurogamāḥ
Having thus said all the Gods followed by Pitamaha Brahma went to the directions they came from with the permission of Vayu.

सोऽपि गन्धवहः पुत्रं प्रगृह्य गृहमानयत्
अञ्जनायास्तमाख्याय वरं दत्तं विनिःसृतः

so'pi gandhavahaḥ putraṁ pragṛhya gṛhamānayat
añjanāyāstamākhyāya varaṁ dattaṁ viniḥsṛtaḥ
The Vayu also brought his son at his house. He went out having told Anjana about it all.

प्राप्य राम वरानेष वरदानबलान्वितः
बलेनात्मनि संस्थेन सोऽपूर्यत यथार्णवः

prāpya rāma varāneṣa varadānabalānvitaḥ
balenātmani saṁsthena so'pūryata yathārṇavaḥ
Having obtained boons Hanuman became highly and powerful and accelerated in himself. He became full like ocean, O' Rama.

बलेनापूर्यमाणो हि एष वानरपुंगवः
आश्रमेषु महर्षीणामपराध्यति निर्भयः

balenāpūryamāṇo hi eṣa vānarapuṁgavaḥ
āśrameṣu maharṣīṇāmaparādhyati nirbhayaḥ
Having become powerful, the best of Mongoloids, started committing offences against Maharsis in their hermitages.

स्रुग्भाण्डानग्निहोत्रं च वल्कलानां च संचयान्
भग्नविच्छिन्नविध्वस्तान्सुशान्तानां करोत्ययम्

srugbhāṇḍānagnihotraṁ ca valkalānāṁ ca saṁcayān
bhagnavicchinnavidhvastānsuśāntānāṁ karotyayam
He broke the sacrificial ladles and vessels and also the heaps of banks belonging to the ascetics.

ततो महर्षयः क्रुद्धा भृग्वङ्गिरसवंशजाः
शेपुरेनं रघुश्रेष्ठ नातिक्रुद्धातिमन्यवः

tato maharṣayaḥ kruddhā bhṛgvaṅgirasavaṁśajāḥ
śepurenaṁ raghuśreṣṭha nātikruddhātimanyavaḥ
Even though prohibited by his father, Hanuman crossed the limits which enraged the Rsis of the lines of Bhtgu and Angira and bestowed curse upon him. O best of the Raghus.

बाधसे यत्समाश्रित्य बलमस्मान्प्लवंगम
तद्दीर्घकालं वेत्तासि नास्माकं शापमोहितः

bādhase yatsamāśritya balamasmānplavaṁgama
taddīrghakālaṁ vettāsi nāsmākaṁ śāpamohitaḥ
That you will be unconscious of the prowess endowed with which you torment us. You will be conscious of your power only after being reminded of it.

ततस्तु हृततेजौजा महर्षिवचनौजसा
एषो श्रमाणि नात्येति मृदुभावगतश्चरन्

tatastu hṛtatejaujā maharṣivacanaujasā
eṣo śramāṇi nātyeti mṛdubhāvagataścaran
Thereupon, having devoid of prowess and glory, he used to wander in the hermitages silently and decently.

अथ ऋक्षरजा नाम वालिसुग्रीवयोः पिता
सर्ववानरराजासीत्तेजसा इव भास्करः

atha ṛkṣarajā nāma vālisugrīvayoḥ pitā
sarvavānararājāsīttejasā iva bhāskaraḥ
There was a king of all Mongoloids named as Rksaraja; the father of Vali and Sugriva. He was as glorious as the Sun.

स तु राज्यं चिरं कृत्वा वानराणां हरीश्वरः
ततस्त्वर्क्षरजा नाम कालधर्मेण संगतः

sa tu rājyaṁ ciraṁ kṛtvā vānarāṇāṁ harīśvaraḥ
tatastvarkṣarajā nāma kāladharmeṇa saṁgataḥ
The Siva having ruled the country of Mongoloids for a long time, offered to Rksaraja with the passage of time.

तस्मिन्नस्तमिते वाली मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रकोविदैः
पित्र्ये पदे कृतो राजा सुग्रीवो वालिनः पदे

tasminnastamite vālī mantribhirmantrakovidaiḥ
pitrye pade kṛto rājā sugrīvo vālinaḥ pade
After the death of Rksaraja, the ministers and the counsellors installed Vali at the place of his father and Sugriva at the place of Vali (the crown prince).

सुग्रीवेण समं त्वस्य अद्वैधं छिद्रवर्जितम्
अहार्यं सख्यमभवदनिलस्य यथाग्निना

sugrīveṇa samaṁ tvasya advaidhaṁ chidravarjitam
ahāryaṁ sakhyamabhavadanilasya yathāgninā
From the childhood onward he developed an unbrokeable friendship with Sugriva like air with the fire.

एष शापवशादेव न वेदबलमात्मनः
वालिसुग्रीवयोर्वैरं यदा राम समुत्थितम्

eṣa śāpavaśādeva na vedabalamātmanaḥ
vālisugrīvayorvairaṁ yadā rāma samutthitam
O Rama! Hanuman could not be conscious of his power due to the curse at the time of altercations between Sugriva and Vali.

न ह्येष राम सुग्रीवो भ्राम्यमाणोऽपि वालिना
वेदयानो न च ह्येष बलमात्मनि मारुतिः

na hyeṣa rāma sugrīvo bhrāmyamāṇo'pi vālinā
vedayāno na ca hyeṣa balamātmani mārutiḥ
In fact, O Rama! wondering Sugriva also did not know about the might of Hanuman.

पराक्रमोत्साहमतिप्रतापैः; सौशील्यमाधुर्यनयानयैश्च
गाम्भीर्यचातुर्यसुवीर्यधैर्यै;र्हनूमतः कोऽप्यधिकोऽस्ति लोके

parākramotsāhamatipratāpaiḥ; sauśīlyamādhuryanayānayaiśca
gāmbhīryacāturyasuvīryadhairyai;rhanūmataḥ ko'pyadhiko'sti loke

Who is there in the world superior to Hanuman in respect of prowess, enthusiasm, intelligence, glory, well behavedness, sweetness, diplomacy or otherwise profundity, shrewdness, virility and patience.

असौ पुरा व्याकरणं ग्रहीष्य;न्सूर्योन्मुखः पृष्ठगमः कपीन्द्रः
उद्यद्गिरेरस्तगिरिं जगाम; ग्रन्थं महद्धारयदप्रमेयः

asau purā vyākaraṇaṁ grahīṣya;nsūryonmukhaḥ pṛṣṭhagamaḥ kapīndraḥ
udyadgirerastagiriṁ jagāma; granthaṁ mahaddhārayadaprameyaḥ
Having curiosity to learn grammar, the best of Mongols of immeasurable power went towards the hill of rising Sun facing Sunward with the view to ask queries and to master the great work.

प्रवीविविक्षोरिव सागरस्य; लोकान्दिधक्षोरिव पावकस्य
लोकक्षयेष्वेव यथान्तकस्य; हनूमतः स्थास्यति कः पुरस्तात्

pravīvivikṣoriva sāgarasya; lokāndidhakṣoriva pāvakasya
lokakṣayeṣveva yathāntakasya; hanūmataḥ sthāsyati kaḥ purastāt

He actually rivals the teacher of gods, i.e. Bshaspati in all the branches of learning and austerities. Who can stand before Hanuman who resembled like ocean likely to engulf the worlds and like fire likely to burn the worlds at the time of decreation of universo.

एषोऽपि चान्ये च महाकपीन्द्राः; सुग्रीवमैन्दद्विविदाः सनीलाः
सतारतारेयनलाः सरम्भा;स्त्वत्कारणाद्राम सुरैर्हि सृष्टाः

eṣo'pi cānye ca mahākapīndrāḥ; sugrīvamaindadvividāḥ sanīlāḥ
satāratāreyanalāḥ sarambhā;stvatkāraṇādrāma surairhi sṛṣṭāḥ
He and other chiefs of Mongols like Sugriva, Mainda, Dvivida, including Nila, Tara, Tareya (son of Tara i.e. Angada), Nala as also Rambha were created by God for the sake of you O' Rama!

तदेतत्कथितं सर्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि
हनूमतो बालभावे कर्मैतत्कथितं मया

tadetatkathitaṁ sarvaṁ yanmāṁ tvaṁ paripṛcchasi
hanūmato bālabhāve karmaitatkathitaṁ mayā
All what was asked by you has been said. The facts of Hanuman performed in childhood has also been related by me.

दृष्टः संभाषितश्चासि राम गच्छमहे वयम्
एवमुक्त्वा गताः सर्वे ऋषयस्ते यथागतम्

dṛṣṭaḥ saṁbhāṣitaścāsi rāma gacchamahe vayam
evamuktvā gatāḥ sarve ṛṣayaste yathāgatam

Thereupon the highly effulgent Agastya said to Rama: "O Rama, we have all seen you and been honoured; now we shall depart.” Saying this, they, being honoured, repaired to their respective habitations.

विमृश्य च ततो रामो वयस्यमकुतोभयम्
प्रतर्दनं काशिपतिं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्

vimṛśya ca tato rāmo vayasyamakutobhayam
pratardanaṁ kāśipatiṁ pariṣvajyedamabravīt
Having bade adieu to his maternal uncle Rama embraced his friend Pratardana, the undaunted king of Kasi and said.

दर्शिता भवता प्रीतिर्दर्शितं सौहृदं परम्
उद्योगश्च कृतो राजन्भरतेन त्वया सह

darśitā bhavatā prītirdarśitaṁ sauhṛdaṁ param
udyogaśca kṛto rājanbharatena tvayā saha
You have displayed your brotherly feelings and delight by making arrangements for my installation in the company of Bharata.

तद्भवानद्य काशेयीं पुरीं वाराणसीं व्रज
रमणीयां त्वया गुप्तां सुप्राकारां सुतोरणाम्

tadbhavānadya kāśeyīṁ purīṁ vārāṇasīṁ vraja
ramaṇīyāṁ tvayā guptāṁ suprākārāṁ sutoraṇām
O king, do you now leave for your city Varanasi, highly picturesque, well-guarded, girt by strong walls on all sides and having welldecorated gateways.

एतावदुक्त्वा उत्थाय काकुत्स्थः परमासनात्
पर्यष्वजत धर्मात्मा निरन्तरमुरोगतम्

etāvaduktvā utthāya kākutsthaḥ paramāsanāt
paryaṣvajata dharmātmā nirantaramurogatam
Saying this, Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha rose up from his seat and embraced him cordially.

विसृज्य तं वयस्यं स स्वागतान्पृथिवीपतीन्
प्रहसन्राघवो वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम्

visṛjya taṁ vayasyaṁ sa svāgatānpṛthivīpatīn
prahasanrāghavo vākyamuvāca madhurākṣaram
Having bade adieu to the king of Kasi, Rama, with a smiling countenance and sweet accents, said to the three hundred assembled kings.

भवतां प्रीतिरव्यग्रा तेजसा परिरक्षिता
धर्मश्च नियतो नित्यं सत्यं च भवतां सदा

bhavatāṁ prītiravyagrā tejasā parirakṣitā
dharmaśca niyato nityaṁ satyaṁ ca bhavatāṁ sadā

Being well protected by your own prowess, you have all displayed your great love for me. By your piety, truthfulness, sagacity and strength, the vicious-souled Ravana has been slain. Forsooth, I am merely the instrument in the destruction of Ravana-he has been slain by your strength.

उद्युक्तानां च सर्वेषां पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम्
कालो ह्यतीतः सुमहान्गमने रोचतां मतिः

udyuktānāṁ ca sarveṣāṁ pārthivānāṁ mahātmanām
kālo hyatītaḥ sumahāngamane rocatāṁ matiḥ

Hearing that Sita, the daughter of Janaka, had been stolen away from the forest the highminded Bharata did bring you all-but fortunately you were not constrained to go through miseries. High-minded as you are, you were all prepared for this work. Long since you have here. I think it better that you should proceed to your respective habitations.

ते प्रयाता महात्मानः पार्थिवाः सर्वतो दिशम्
कम्पयन्तो महीं वीराः स्वपुराणि प्रहृष्टवत्

te prayātā mahātmānaḥ pārthivāḥ sarvato diśam
kampayanto mahīṁ vīrāḥ svapurāṇi prahṛṣṭavat
Having agitated the earth with thousands of elephants and horses the kings proceeded to various quarters.

भरतेन वयं पश्चात्समानीता निरर्थकम्
हता हि राक्षसास्तत्र पार्थिवैः स्युर्न संशयः

bharatena vayaṁ paścātsamānītā nirarthakam
hatā hi rākṣasāstatra pārthivaiḥ syurna saṁśayaḥ

Those kings, proud and powerful, spoke to one another-We did not face Ravana~ the enemy of Rama; Bharata did uselessly invite us after the destruction of Ravana. Had they brought us earlier, we would, forsooth, have slain him,

रामस्य बाहुवीर्येण पालिता लक्ष्मणस्य च
सुखं पारे समुद्रस्य युध्येम विगतज्वराः

rāmasya bāhuvīryeṇa pālitā lakṣmaṇasya ca
sukhaṁ pāre samudrasya yudhyema vigatajvarāḥ
We would have, on the other side of the Ocean, well protected by the prowess of Rama and Laksmana, and freed from all disturbances, fought at pleasure.

एताश्चान्याश्च राजानः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः
कथयन्तः स्वराष्ट्राणि विविशुस्ते महारथाः

etāścānyāśca rājānaḥ kathāstatra sahasraśaḥ
kathayantaḥ svarāṣṭrāṇi viviśuste mahārathāḥ
Being thus delighted, all those assembled princes proceeded to their respective kingdoms, dwelling on these and various other topics.

भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चैव शत्रुघ्नश्च महारथः
आदाय तानि रत्नानि अयोध्यामगमन्पुनः

bharato lakṣmaṇaścaiva śatrughnaśca mahārathaḥ
ādāya tāni ratnāni ayodhyāmagamanpunaḥ

And taking all those jewels, the highly powerful Bharata, Laksmana and satrughna returned to their own city. Having arrived at the picturesque city Ayodhya those foremost of men, made presents of various jewels to Rama.

ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसो रामदत्तानि तान्यथ
शिरोभिर्धारयामासुर्बाहुभिश्च महाबलाः

te sarve hṛṣṭamanaso rāmadattāni tānyatha
śirobhirdhārayāmāsurbāhubhiśca mahābalāḥ
And those highly powerful monkeys and night-rangers wore on their heads and arms those jewels conferred on them by Rama.

पपुश्चैव सुगन्धीनि मधूनि विविधानि च
मांसानि च सुमृष्टानि फलान्यास्वादयन्ति च

papuścaiva sugandhīni madhūni vividhāni ca
māṁsāni ca sumṛṣṭāni phalānyāsvādayanti ca
The monkeys lived there all happily feasting on fragrant honey, well-cooked meat and various fruits and roots.

एवं तेषां निवसतां मासः साग्रो गतस्तदा
मुहूर्तमिव तत्सर्वं रामभक्त्या समर्थयन्

evaṁ teṣāṁ nivasatāṁ māsaḥ sāgro gatastadā
muhūrtamiva tatsarvaṁ rāmabhaktyā samarthayan
In this way they spent more than a month—but it appeared to them as a moment on account of their devotion to Rama.

रेमे रामः स तैः सार्धं वानरैः कामरूपिभिः
राजभिश्च महावीर्यै राक्षसैश्च महाबलैः

reme rāmaḥ sa taiḥ sārdhaṁ vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
rājabhiśca mahāvīryai rākṣasaiśca mahābalaiḥ
He, too also spent his time happily with monkeys assuming shapes at will, the highly powerful Raksasas and the mighty bears.

एवं तेषां ययौ मासो द्वितीयः शैशिरः सुखम्
वानराणां प्रहृष्टानां राक्षसानां च सर्वशः

evaṁ teṣāṁ yayau māso dvitīyaḥ śaiśiraḥ sukham
vānarāṇāṁ prahṛṣṭānāṁ rākṣasānāṁ ca sarvaśaḥ
In this way, the delighted monkeys and Raks asas spent the second winter month. Enjoying delight they thus spent their days happily in the city of Ayodhya working to the welfare of Rama.

तथा स्म तेषां वसतामृक्षवानररक्षसाम्
राघवस्तु महातेजाः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्

tathā sma teṣāṁ vasatāmṛkṣavānararakṣasām
rāghavastu mahātejāḥ sugrīvamidamabravīt
In this wise, the monkeys, bears and Raksasas spent their days in Ayodhya. Thereupon the highly effulgent Rama, the descendant of Raghu said to Sugriva.

गम्यतां सौम्य किष्किन्धां दुराधर्षां सुरासुरैः
पालयस्व सहामात्यै राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्

gamyatāṁ saumya kiṣkindhāṁ durādharṣāṁ surāsuraiḥ
pālayasva sahāmātyai rājyaṁ nihatakaṇṭakam
"O gentle one, proceeding to the city of Kis kindha, hard to be got at by the celestials and Asuras, do you reign there undisturbed with your councillors.

एवमुक्त्वा च सुग्रीवं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः
विभीषणमथोवाच रामो मधुरया गिरा

evamuktvā ca sugrīvaṁ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
vibhīṣaṇamathovāca rāmo madhurayā girā
Having said this and embraced Sugriva again and again Rama addressed Vibhisana with sweet accents.

मा च बुद्धिमधर्मे त्वं कुर्या राजन्कथंचन
बुद्धिमन्तो हि राजानो ध्रुवमश्नन्ति मेदिनीम्

mā ca buddhimadharme tvaṁ kuryā rājankathaṁcana
buddhimanto hi rājāno dhruvamaśnanti medinīm

I know, you are cognisant of piety; the citizens, your councillors and your brother Kubera also love you; do you therefore go and govern Lanka piously, O king; never cherish any vile intention; the honest kings always enjoy the earth.

अहं च नित्यशो राजन्सुग्रीवसहितस्त्वया
स्मर्तव्यः परया प्रीत्या गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः

ahaṁ ca nityaśo rājansugrīvasahitastvayā
smartavyaḥ parayā prītyā gaccha tvaṁ vigatajvaraḥ
And my only request to you, O king, is that you may with love remember me and Sugriva. Do you now proceed, divested of sorrow.

रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः
साधु साध्विति काकुत्स्थं प्रशशंसुः पुनः पुनः

rāmasya bhāṣitaṁ śrutvā ṛkṣavānararākṣasāḥ
sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṁ praśaśaṁsuḥ punaḥ punaḥ

Hearing the words of Rama, the bears, monkeys and Raksasas repeatedly exclaimed glory to Rama and said. 'O Rama, having long arms, your understanding resemble that of the Self-Sprung, your prowess is equally wonderful and your beauty is also par excellence.”

तेषामेवं ब्रुवाणानां वानराणां च रक्षसाम्
हनूमान्प्रणतो भूत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्

teṣāmevaṁ bruvāṇānāṁ vānarāṇāṁ ca rakṣasām
hanūmānpraṇato bhūtvā rāghavaṁ vākyamabravīt

The monkeys and Raksasas having said this, Hanuman bowing, said to Rama "May my loving reverence be always in you, O king; may my devotion to you remain unshaken, O hero; and may my mind be not attached to any other thing. May my life remain in my body as long as the stories of Rama shall be in currency on earth. Let not this prove otherwise.

एवं ब्रुवाणं राजेन्द्रो हनूमन्तमथासनात्
उत्थाय च परिष्वज्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह

evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ rājendro hanūmantamathāsanāt
utthāya ca pariṣvajya vākyametaduvāca ha
After Hanuman had said this, Rama rose up from his throne and having embraced Hanuman affectionately said.

ततोऽस्य हारं चन्द्राभं मुच्य कण्ठात्स राघवः
वैदूर्यतरलं स्नेहादाबबन्धे हनूमति

tato'sya hāraṁ candrābhaṁ mucya kaṇṭhātsa rāghavaḥ
vaidūryataralaṁ snehādābabandhe hanūmati
Having said this, Rama took off from his neck a chain 'set with sapphires brilliant as the rays of the moon and placed it round the neck of Hanuman.

तेनोरसि निबद्धेन हारेण स महाकपिः
रराज हेमशैलेन्द्रश्चन्द्रेणाक्रान्तमस्तकः

tenorasi nibaddhena hāreṇa sa mahākapiḥ
rarāja hemaśailendraścandreṇākrāntamastakaḥ
Like to the mountain Sumeru beautified by the rising of the moon on its summit, Hanuman, the foremost of monkeys, appeared graceful with the chain placed on his breast.

श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतदुत्थायोत्थाय वानराः
प्रणम्य शिरसा पादौ प्रजग्मुस्ते महाबलाः

śrutvā tu rāghavasyaitadutthāyotthāya vānarāḥ
praṇamya śirasā pādau prajagmuste mahābalāḥ
And hearing the words of Raghava, the highly powerful monkeys, one by one, saluted Rama, touching his feet and went away.

सुग्रीवश्चैव रामेण परिष्वक्तो महाभुजः
विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा निरन्तरमुरोगतः

sugrīvaścaiva rāmeṇa pariṣvakto mahābhujaḥ
vibhīṣaṇaśca dharmātmā nirantaramurogataḥ
Both Sugriva and the virtuous-souled Vibhisana embraced Rama and three of them were beside themselves with tears.

सर्वे च ते बाष्पगलाः साश्रुनेत्रा विचेतसः
संमूढा इव दुःखेन त्यजन्ते राघवं तदा

sarve ca te bāṣpagalāḥ sāśrunetrā vicetasaḥ
saṁmūḍhā iva duḥkhena tyajante rāghavaṁ tadā
And other monkeys and Raksasas were all moved with tears and sorrow to take leave of Rama,

विसृज्य च महाबाहुरृक्षवानरराक्षसान्
भ्रातृभिः सहितो रामः प्रमुमोद सुखी सुखम्

visṛjya ca mahābāhurṛkṣavānararākṣasān
bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rāmaḥ pramumoda sukhī sukham
Having bade adieu to bears, monkeys and Raksasas the long-armed Rama began to live happily in the company of his brothers.

अथापराह्णसमये भ्रातृभिः सह राघवः
शुश्राव मधुरां वाणीमन्तरिक्षात्प्रभाषिताम्

athāparāhṇasamaye bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rāghavaḥ
śuśrāva madhurāṁ vāṇīmantarikṣātprabhāṣitām
Thereupon afternoon, Lord Raghava along with his brothers heard from the air the following sweet accents.

सौम्य राम निरीक्षस्व सौम्येन वदनेन माम्
कैलासशिखरात्प्राप्तं विद्धि मां पुष्करं प्रभो

saumya rāma nirīkṣasva saumyena vadanena mām
kailāsaśikharātprāptaṁ viddhi māṁ puṣkaraṁ prabho
O gentle Rama, do you with a delighted countenance behold me. O lord, know me as Puspaka coming from the abode of Kuberu.

निर्जितस्त्वं नरेन्द्रेण राघवेण महात्मना
निहत्य युधि दुर्धर्षं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्

nirjitastvaṁ narendreṇa rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
nihatya yudhi durdharṣaṁ rāvaṇaṁ rākṣasādhipam
O foremost of men, at your command I did go there to carry him. But he said to me. “Having slain the irrepressible Ravana in battle the highsouled Rama, the foremost of men, has conquered you.

ममापि परमा प्रीतिर्हते तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि
रावणे सगणे सौम्य सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवे

mamāpi paramā prītirhate tasmindurātmani
rāvaṇe sagaṇe saumya saputrāmātyabāndhave
I have greatly been delighted on the destruction of the vicious-souled Ravana, with his relatives, sons and friends.

स त्वं रामेण लङ्कायां निर्जितः परमात्मना
वह सौम्य तमेव त्वमहमाज्ञापयामि ते

sa tvaṁ rāmeṇa laṅkāyāṁ nirjitaḥ paramātmanā
vaha saumya tameva tvamahamājñāpayāmi te
O gentle one, the great Rama has conquered you in Lanka. I permit you, therefore to convey him.

एष मे परमः कामो यत्त्वं राघवनन्दनम्
वहेर्लोकस्य संयानं गच्छस्व विगतज्वरः

eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yattvaṁ rāghavanandanam
vaherlokasya saṁyānaṁ gacchasva vigatajvaraḥ
You are the fit conveyance for traversing all regions. But my earnest desire is that you should take Rama, the descendant of Raghu. Do, you therefore go there at pleasure without any sorrow.

तच्छासनमहं ज्ञात्वा धनदस्य महात्मनः
त्वत्सकाशं पुनः प्राप्तः स एवं प्रतिगृह्ण माम्

tacchāsanamahaṁ jñātvā dhanadasya mahātmanaḥ
tvatsakāśaṁ punaḥ prāptaḥ sa evaṁ pratigṛhṇa mām
Hearing this command of the high-souled Kubera I have come to you. Do you fearlessly accept me..

गम्यतां च यथाकाममागच्छेस्त्वं यदा स्मरे
एवमस्त्विति रामेण विसृष्टः पुष्पकः पुनः
अभिप्रेतां दिशं प्रायात्पुष्पकः पुष्पभूषितः

gamyatāṁ ca yathākāmamāgacchestvaṁ yadā smare
evamastviti rāmeṇa visṛṣṭaḥ puṣpakaḥ punaḥ
abhipretāṁ diśaṁ prāyātpuṣpakaḥ puṣpabhūṣitaḥ
Having been adored by Rama and saying ‘so be it' Puspaka L.oceeded towards its wished for direction.

एवमन्तर्हिते तस्मिन्पुष्पके विविधात्मनि
भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम्

evamantarhite tasminpuṣpake vividhātmani
bharataḥ prāñjalirvākyamuvāca raghunandanam
And the holy Puspaka car having thus vanquished, Bharata with folded palms, said to Rama, the delight of Raghu.

अनामयाच्च मर्त्यानां साग्रो मासो गतो ह्ययम्
जीर्णानामपि सत्त्वानां मृत्युर्नायाति राघव

anāmayācca martyānāṁ sāgro māso gato hyayam
jīrṇānāmapi sattvānāṁ mṛtyurnāyāti rāghava

O hero, during your divine administration, we have seen many inhuman creatures and objects speak like men. During all these months since your installation subjects have not suffered from any disease. Even the most aged animals have not met with death. The female, without any risk, have been giving birth to children and all people are plump and delighted.

एता वाचः सुमधुरा भरतेन समीरिताः
श्रुत्वा रामो मुदा युक्तः प्रमुमोद सुखी सुखम्

etā vācaḥ sumadhurā bharatena samīritāḥ
śrutvā rāmo mudā yuktaḥ pramumoda sukhī sukham
Hearing those sweet accents given vent to by Bharata, Rama, the foremost of kings was greatly delighted

तत्र तत्र वनोद्देशे वैदूर्यमणिसंनिभैः
शाद्वलैः परमोपेताः पुष्पितद्रुमसंयुताः

tatra tatra vanoddeśe vaidūryamaṇisaṁnibhaiḥ
śādvalaiḥ paramopetāḥ puṣpitadrumasaṁyutāḥ
And the forest was encompassed by stone walls and in the-irtside were dwelling many a Sardula bird resembling Vaiduryas. All the trees in the forest were filled with flowers.

मांसानि च विचित्राणि फलानि विविधानि च
रामस्याभ्यवहारार्थं किंकरास्तूर्णमाहरन्

māṁsāni ca vicitrāṇi phalāni vividhāni ca
rāmasyābhyavahārārthaṁ kiṁkarāstūrṇamāharan
And in rio time the servants brought for him well-cooked meat and various fruits.

उपनृत्यन्ति राजानं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः
बालाश्च रूपवत्यश्च स्त्रियः पानवशं गताः

upanṛtyanti rājānaṁ nṛtyagītaviśāradāḥ
bālāśca rūpavatyaśca striyaḥ pānavaśaṁ gatāḥ

The intelligent and beautiful females being intoxicated after taking wine, and well-skilled in the art of singing and dancing, began to dance before Rama. The virtuous-souled Rama, the foremost of those who know how to please, satisfied those beautiful damsels adorned with various ornaments.

एवं रामो मुदा युक्तः सीतां सुरुचिराननाम्
रमयामास वैदेहीमहन्यहनि देववत्

evaṁ rāmo mudā yuktaḥ sītāṁ surucirānanām
ramayāmāsa vaidehīmahanyahani devavat
Being greatly delighted the celestial-like Rama pleased everyday Sita resembling a celestial damsel.

पूर्वाह्णे पौरकृत्यानि कृत्वा धर्मेण धर्मवित्
शेषं दिवसभागार्धमन्तःपुरगतोऽभवत्

pūrvāhṇe paurakṛtyāni kṛtvā dharmeṇa dharmavit
śeṣaṁ divasabhāgārdhamantaḥpuragato'bhavat
Once on a morning time, having performed all the religious ceremonies, in the fore part of the day, Rama, to spend the evening, entered the inner apartment.

सीता च देवकार्याणि कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकानि तु
श्वश्रूणामविशेषेण सर्वासां प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता

sītā ca devakāryāṇi kṛtvā paurvāhṇikāni tu
śvaśrūṇāmaviśeṣeṇa sarvāsāṁ prāñjaliḥ sthitā
Sita, too, having performed all religious ceremonies of morning, first in all, attended to the service of her mother-in-law.

ततो राममुपागच्छद्विचित्रबहुभूषणा
त्रिविष्टपे सहस्राक्षमुपविष्टं यथा शची

tato rāmamupāgacchadvicitrabahubhūṣaṇā
triviṣṭape sahasrākṣamupaviṣṭaṁ yathā śacī
Thereupon wearing a beautifully coloured cloth and being adorned with various ornaments Sita appeared before Rama like to saci approaching the king of celestials in heaven.

दृष्ट्वा तु राघवः पत्नीं कल्याणेन समन्विताम्
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्

dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ patnīṁ kalyāṇena samanvitām
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt
And beholding the auspicious signs of pregnancy in his souse Rama attained to excessive delight.

अपत्यलाभो वैदेहि ममायं समुपस्थितः
किमिच्छसि हि तद्ब्रूहि कः कामः क्रियतां तव

apatyalābho vaidehi mamāyaṁ samupasthitaḥ
kimicchasi hi tadbrūhi kaḥ kāmaḥ kriyatāṁ tava
Thereupon he said to the beautiful Sita resembling a celestial damsel:-"0 Vaidehi, signs of pregnancy are manifest in you. What desires of your can we satisfy?"

तथेति च प्रतिज्ञातं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
विस्रब्धा भव वैदेहि श्वो गमिष्यस्यसंशयम्

tatheti ca pratijñātaṁ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
visrabdhā bhava vaidehi śvo gamiṣyasyasaṁśayam
Whereto replied Rama of unwearied actions, saying 'so be it.' Believe me, O Vaidehi, that you shall undoubtedly go there to-morrow.

एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थो मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम्
मध्यकक्षान्तरं रामो निर्जगाम सुहृद्वृतः

evamuktvā tu kākutstho maithilīṁ janakātmajām
madhyakakṣāntaraṁ rāmo nirjagāma suhṛdvṛtaḥ
Having thus addressed Maithili, the daughter of Janaka, Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, then issued out of the inner apartment and entered the middle one filled with his friends.

तत्रोपविष्टं राजानमुपासन्ते विचक्षणाः
कथानां बहुरूपाणां हास्यकाराः समन्ततः

tatropaviṣṭaṁ rājānamupāsante vicakṣaṇāḥ
kathānāṁ bahurūpāṇāṁ hāsyakārāḥ samantataḥ
Rama having taken his seat there, the experienced councillors encircling him began to dwell upon many amusing stories.

एते कथा बहुविधा परिहाससमन्विताः
कथयन्ति स्म संहृष्टा राघवस्य महात्मनः

ete kathā bahuvidhā parihāsasamanvitāḥ
kathayanti sma saṁhṛṣṭā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kasyapa, Mangala, Kula, Surajin, Kaliya, Bhadra Dantavaktra, Sumagadha-all delightedly began to introduce many amusing talks before the high-souled Rama.

मामाश्रितानि कान्याहुः पौरजानपदा जनाः
किं च सीतां समाश्रित्य भरतं किं नु लक्ष्मणम्

māmāśritāni kānyāhuḥ paurajānapadā janāḥ
kiṁ ca sītāṁ samāśritya bharataṁ kiṁ nu lakṣmaṇam

Thereupon Rama incidentally addressed them saying, “O Bhadra, how do the inhabitants of the city and provinces talk about Sita, Bharata, Laksmana, Satrughna and the mother Kaikeyi? The kings, when they deviate from the paths of justice, become objects of censure in the houses of men and even in the forests as well.”

एवमुक्ते तु रामेण भद्रः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्
स्थिताः कथाः शुभा राजन्वर्तन्ते पुरवासिनाम्

evamukte tu rāmeṇa bhadraḥ prāñjalirabravīt
sthitāḥ kathāḥ śubhā rājanvartante puravāsinām

Rama having said this, Bhadra with folded hands replied: "O king, the citizens speak many good things about you; besides they dilate upon many things in their own houses regarding your conquest acquired by the destruction of the Ten-necked demon."

शुभाशुभानि वाक्यानि यान्याहुः पुरवासिनः
श्रुत्वेदानीं शुभं कुर्यां न कुर्यामशुभानि च

śubhāśubhāni vākyāni yānyāhuḥ puravāsinaḥ
śrutvedānīṁ śubhaṁ kuryāṁ na kuryāmaśubhāni ca

Hearing the words of Bhadra, Rama said:“Without hiding anything, do you relate every thing from the beginning vent to by the citizens. Hearing the good and bad opinions of the citizens I shall desist from bad actions and engage in good ones.

कथयस्व च विस्रब्धो निर्भयो विगतज्वरः
कथयन्ते यथा पौरा जना जनपदेषु च

kathayasva ca visrabdho nirbhayo vigatajvaraḥ
kathayante yathā paurā janā janapadeṣu ca
Whatever citizens say the vicious actions of mine in the city, relate to me confidently and fearlessly.

राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भद्रः सुरुचिरं वचः
प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुं प्राञ्जलिः सुसमाहितः

rāghaveṇaivamuktastu bhadraḥ suruciraṁ vacaḥ
pratyuvāca mahābāhuṁ prāñjaliḥ susamāhitaḥ
Hearing the sweet accents of Rama, Bhadra, with a quiescent mind and folded palms, said.

शृणु राजन्यथा पौराः कथयन्ति शुभाशुभम्
चत्वरापणरथ्यासु वनेषूपवनेषु च

śṛṇu rājanyathā paurāḥ kathayanti śubhāśubham
catvarāpaṇarathyāsu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca
Hear, o king, I shall relate to you all those unpleasant things frequently dwelt upon by people in court-yards, markets, public roads, forests and gardens.

दुष्करं कृतवान्रामः समुद्रे सेतुबन्धनम्
अकृतं पूर्वकैः कैश्चिद्देवैरपि सदानवैः

duṣkaraṁ kṛtavānrāmaḥ samudre setubandhanam
akṛtaṁ pūrvakaiḥ kaiściddevairapi sadānavaiḥ
Indeed Rama has accomplished a wonderfully hard work; our ancestors, the celestials, the Danavas none heard of constructing a bridge over the ocean?

रावणश्च दुराधर्षो हतः सबलवाहनः
वानराश्च वशं नीता ऋक्षाश्च सह राक्षसैः

rāvaṇaśca durādharṣo hataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ
vānarāśca vaśaṁ nītā ṛkṣāśca saha rākṣasaiḥ
Rama has slain the irrepressible Ravana with his army and brought over the monkeys, bears and Raksasas to his own side.

हत्वा च रावणं युद्धे सीतामाहृत्य राघवः
अमर्षं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा स्ववेश्म पुनरानयत्

hatvā ca rāvaṇaṁ yuddhe sītāmāhṛtya rāghavaḥ
amarṣaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā svaveśma punarānayat
Having discomfitted Ravana, in the encounter Rama has released Sita, but not being the least enraged on account of her being touched by Ravana he has brought to her his own city.

एवं बहुविधा वाचो वदन्ति पुरवासिनः
नगरेषु च सर्वेषु राजञ्जनपदेषु च

evaṁ bahuvidhā vāco vadanti puravāsinaḥ
nagareṣu ca sarveṣu rājañjanapadeṣu ca
O King, the citizens thus talk of many types in every corner of cities and provinces.

तस्यैतद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा राघवः परमार्तवत्
उवाच सर्वान्सुहृदः कथमेतन्निवेद्यताम्

tasyaitadbhāṣitaṁ śrutvā rāghavaḥ paramārtavat
uvāca sarvānsuhṛdaḥ kathametannivedyatām
Hearings those words of Bhadra, Raghava was greatly sorry and asked his friends “Do the subjects thus talk about me?”

सर्वे तु शिरसा भूमावभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च
प्रत्यूचू राघवं दीनमेवमेतन्न संशयः

sarve tu śirasā bhūmāvabhivādya praṇamya ca
pratyūcū rāghavaṁ dīnamevametanna saṁśayaḥ

Thereupon lowering their heads and saluting him they all said to Raghava, of a depressed mind-“For sooth, the subjects thus talk about.” Thereupon Kakutstha, the slayer of enemies, bearing all those words, dismissed his friends.

विसृज्य तु सुहृद्वर्गं बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य राघवः
समीपे द्वाःस्थमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्

visṛjya tu suhṛdvargaṁ buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ
samīpe dvāḥsthamāsīnamidaṁ vacanamabravīt
Having sent away his friends and determined what to do, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, commanded the warder, who was seated hard by, saying.

शीघ्रमानय सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्
भरतं च महाबाहुं शत्रुघ्नं चापराजितम्

śīghramānaya saumitriṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ śubhalakṣaṇam
bharataṁ ca mahābāhuṁ śatrughnaṁ cāparājitam
Do you bring in no time, Laksmana, a son of Sumitra, gifted with auspicious marks, alongwith great Bharata and the irrepressible Satrughna.

रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः
लक्ष्मणस्य गृहं गत्वा प्रविवेशानिवारितः

rāmasya bhāṣitaṁ śrutvā dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
lakṣmaṇasya gṛhaṁ gatvā praviveśānivāritaḥ
Hearing the words of Rama and placing his folded palms on his head the warder reached house of Laksmana and unobstructed entered therein.

उवाच च तदा वाक्यं वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः
द्रष्टुमिच्छति राजा त्वां गम्यतां तत्र मा चिरम्

uvāca ca tadā vākyaṁ vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
draṣṭumicchati rājā tvāṁ gamyatāṁ tatra mā ciram
And having saluted him, with folded palms he said to the high-souled Laksmana and:-"The King wishes to behold you-do you soon go there.

बाढमित्येव सौमित्रिः श्रुत्वा राघवशासनम्
प्राद्रवद्रथमारुह्य राघवस्य निवेशनम्

bāḍhamityeva saumitriḥ śrutvā rāghavaśāsanam
prādravadrathamāruhya rāghavasya niveśanam
Thereupon being apprised of Raghava's command and saying 'so be it.' Saumitri ascended his car and went speedily towards Rama's abode.

प्रयान्तं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा द्वाःस्थो भरतमन्तिकात्
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति

prayāntaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ dṛṣṭvā dvāḥstho bharatamantikāt
uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṁ rājā tvāṁ draṣṭumicchati
Having beheld Laksmana's departure the warder humbly went to Bharata and having blessed him with folded hands said: “The King wishes to see you."

भरतस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थाद्रामसमीरितम्
उत्पपातासनात्तूर्णं पद्भ्यामेव ततोऽगमत्

bharatastu vacaḥ śrutvā dvāḥsthādrāmasamīritam
utpapātāsanāttūrṇaṁ padbhyāmeva tato'gamat
Hearing of the command of Rama from the warder, the highly powerful Bharata at once got up from his seat and proceeded on foot.

दृष्ट्वा प्रयान्तं भरतं त्वरमाणः कृताञ्जलिः
शत्रुघ्नभवनं गत्वा ततो वाक्यं जगाद ह

dṛṣṭvā prayāntaṁ bharataṁ tvaramāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
śatrughnabhavanaṁ gatvā tato vākyaṁ jagāda ha
Seeing Bharata's departure the warder speedily went to the mansion of Satrughna and with folded hands said.

एह्यागच्छ रघुश्रेष्ठ राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति
गतो हि लक्ष्मणः पूर्वं भरतश्च महायशाः

ehyāgaccha raghuśreṣṭha rājā tvāṁ draṣṭumicchati
gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṁ bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ
"Do you come, O foremost Raghus, the King wish to behold you.” Laksmana and Bharata are also there.

श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य शत्रुघ्नो रामशासनम्
शिरसा वन्द्य धरणीं प्रययौ यत्र राघवः

śrutvā tu vacanaṁ tasya śatrughno rāmaśāsanam
śirasā vandya dharaṇīṁ prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ
Hearing the words of the warder Satrughna lowered his head and rising up speedily proceeded to Rama.

कुमारानागताञ्श्रुत्वा चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः
अवाक्शिरा दीनमना द्वाःस्थं वचनमब्रवीत्

kumārānāgatāñśrutvā cintāvyākulitendriyaḥ
avākśirā dīnamanā dvāḥsthaṁ vacanamabravīt

So long Rama was engaged poorly in anxious meditation with his crown bent downwards. Informed of the princes' arrival he commanded the warder, “Do you soon bring the princes here. My life depends upon them. They are my dearest life.

आज्ञप्तास्तु नरेन्द्रेण कुमाराः शुक्लवाससः
प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा विविशुस्ते समाहिताः

ājñaptāstu narendreṇa kumārāḥ śuklavāsasaḥ
prahvāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā viviśuste samāhitāḥ
Having obtained Rama's command, the princes, clothed in white raiment, entered there, with folded palms and quiescent mind.

ते तु दृष्ट्वा मुखं तस्य सग्रहं शशिनं यथा
संध्यागतमिवादित्यं प्रभया परिवर्जितम्

te tu dṛṣṭvā mukhaṁ tasya sagrahaṁ śaśinaṁ yathā
saṁdhyāgatamivādityaṁ prabhayā parivarjitam
Having entered there they saw that Rama's countenance was shorn of beauty like to the moon possessed by Rahu, the setting sun and the withered lotus and his eyes were full of tears.

ततोऽभिवाद्य त्वरिताः पादौ रामस्य मूर्धभिः
तस्थुः समाहिताः सर्वे रामश्चाश्रूण्यवर्तयत्

tato'bhivādya tvaritāḥ pādau rāmasya mūrdhabhiḥ
tasthuḥ samāhitāḥ sarve rāmaścāśrūṇyavartayat
Then having approached him quickly, and saluted his feet they all anxiously sat there. Rama also wiped off his tears.

तान्परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यामुत्थाप्य च महाभुजः
आसनेष्वाध्वमित्युक्त्वा ततो वाक्यं जगाद ह

tānpariṣvajya bāhubhyāmutthāpya ca mahābhujaḥ
āsaneṣvādhvamityuktvā tato vākyaṁ jagāda ha
Thereupon having embraced them with his arms he raised up the princes and pressed them to take their seats. Then he said.

भवन्तः कृतशास्त्रार्था बुद्धौ च परिनिष्ठिताः
संभूय च मदर्थोऽयमन्वेष्टव्यो नरेश्वराः

bhavantaḥ kṛtaśāstrārthā buddhau ca pariniṣṭhitāḥ
saṁbhūya ca madartho'yamanveṣṭavyo nareśvarāḥ
"You are mine all; you constitute my life; O princes, I am governing the kingdom gained by you; you are all learned, pious and intelligent. Do you follow the duties I point out."

तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां दीनचेतसाम्
उवाच वाक्यं काकुत्स्थो मुखेन परिशुष्यता

teṣāṁ samupaviṣṭānāṁ sarveṣāṁ dīnacetasām
uvāca vākyaṁ kākutstho mukhena pariśuṣyatā
The princes were all waiting with a poorly heart when Rama, with a dried countenance, addressed them, saying.

सर्वे शृणुत भद्रं वो मा कुरुध्वं मनोऽन्यथा
पौराणां मम सीतायां यादृशी वर्तते कथा

sarve śṛṇuta bhadraṁ vo mā kurudhvaṁ mano'nyathā
paurāṇāṁ mama sītāyāṁ yādṛśī vartate kathā
May good betide you-do not act against my desire. Hear, what the citizens have been talking about me and Sita.

पौरापवादः सुमहांस्तथा जनपदस्य च
वर्तते मयि बीभत्सः स मे मर्माणि कृन्तति

paurāpavādaḥ sumahāṁstathā janapadasya ca
vartate mayi bībhatsaḥ sa me marmāṇi kṛntati
The citizens as well as the inhabitants of provinces have been showering censures upon me. I have been pierced to the very vitals by those accusations.

जानासि हि यथा सौम्य दण्डके विजने वने
रावणेन हृता सीता स च विध्वंसितो मया

jānāsi hi yathā saumya daṇḍake vijane vane
rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā sa ca vidhvaṁsito mayā

I have been born in the illustrious family by the high-souled Iksvakus. Sita has been born also in the holy family of the great Janaka; gentle Laksmana, you know how in the solitary forest of Dandaka, Sita was stolen away by Ravana and how have I slain him.

प्रत्यक्षं तव सौमित्रे देवानां हव्यवाहनः
अपापां मैथिलीमाह वायुश्चाकाशगोचरः

pratyakṣaṁ tava saumitre devānāṁ havyavāhanaḥ
apāpāṁ maithilīmāha vāyuścākāśagocaraḥ

To secure my confidence, Sita, in your very presence, entered fire. At that time, O Saumitri, fire, carrying sacrificial oblations and the wind of the sky declared Sita's innocence before the celestials. in the presence of all the Rsis and gods, the Sun and Moon announced the innocence of the daughter of Janaka.

एवं शुद्धसमाचारा देवगन्धर्वसंनिधौ
लङ्काद्वीपे महेन्द्रेण मम हस्ते निवेशिता

evaṁ śuddhasamācārā devagandharvasaṁnidhau
laṅkādvīpe mahendreṇa mama haste niveśitā
Indra, the king of the celestials, himself handed over the chaste Sita to me in the island of Lanka.

अन्तरात्मा च मे वेत्ति सीतां शुद्धां यशस्विनीम्
ततो गृहीत्वा वैदेहीमयोध्यामहमागतः

antarātmā ca me vetti sītāṁ śuddhāṁ yaśasvinīm
tato gṛhītvā vaidehīmayodhyāmahamāgataḥ
My mind know Sita as chaste for ever. So, at that time, I came back to Ayodhya with Sita.

अयं तु मे महान्वादः शोकश्च हृदि वर्तते
पौरापवादः सुमहांस्तथा जनपदस्य च

ayaṁ tu me mahānvādaḥ śokaśca hṛdi vartate
paurāpavādaḥ sumahāṁstathā janapadasya ca
But now a great sorrow consequent upon the censure of the citizens and villagers has pierced my heart.

अकीर्तिर्यस्य गीयेत लोके भूतस्य कस्यचित्
पतत्येवाधमाँल्लोकान्यावच्छब्दः स कीर्त्यते

akīrtiryasya gīyeta loke bhūtasya kasyacit
patatyevādhamā̐llokānyāvacchabdaḥ sa kīrtyate
He, who is notorious on this earth and as long as that notoriety remains current, is classed among the vile.

अकीर्तिर्निन्द्यते दैवैः कीर्तिर्देवेषु पूज्यते
कीर्त्यर्थं च समारम्भः सर्व एव महात्मनाम्

akīrtirnindyate daivaiḥ kīrtirdeveṣu pūjyate
kīrtyarthaṁ ca samārambhaḥ sarva eva mahātmanām
Even the celestials speak ill of bad name whereas fame is adored in all the regions. Therefore the high-souled exert their best to acquire reputations.

अप्यहं जीवितं जह्यां युष्मान्वा पुरुषर्षभाः
अपवादभयाद्भीतः किं पुनर्जनकात्मजाम्

apyahaṁ jīvitaṁ jahyāṁ yuṣmānvā puruṣarṣabhāḥ
apavādabhayādbhītaḥ kiṁ punarjanakātmajām
O foremost of men, what to speak of the daughter of Janaka-I can even renounce my life and yourselves in fear of a bad name.

तस्माद्भवन्तः पश्यन्तु पतितं शोकसागरे
न हि पश्याम्यहं भूयः किंचिद्दुःखमतोऽधिकम्

tasmādbhavantaḥ paśyantu patitaṁ śokasāgare
na hi paśyāmyahaṁ bhūyaḥ kiṁcidduḥkhamato'dhikam
Do you therefore perceive into what great abyss of sorrow and ill-fame I have fallen. Up to this time I have never experienced such a mighty grief.

श्वस्त्वं प्रभाते सौमित्रे सुमन्त्राधिष्ठितं रथम्
आरुह्य सीतामारोप्य विषयान्ते समुत्सृज

śvastvaṁ prabhāte saumitre sumantrādhiṣṭhitaṁ ratham
āruhya sītāmāropya viṣayānte samutsṛja
Do you, O Laksmana, next morning, ascending the car driven by Sumantra, take away Sita to another country.

गङ्गायास्तु परे पारे वाल्मीकेः सुमहात्मनः
आश्रमो दिव्यसंकाशस्तमसातीरमाश्रितः

gaṅgāyāstu pare pāre vālmīkeḥ sumahātmanaḥ
āśramo divyasaṁkāśastamasātīramāśritaḥ
There is a picturesque hermitage of the highsouled Valmiki situate on the Tamasa on the other side of the river Ganga.

तत्रैनां विजने कक्षे विसृज्य रघुनन्दन
शीघ्रमागच्छ सौमित्रे कुरुष्व वचनं मम

tatraināṁ vijane kakṣe visṛjya raghunandana
śīghramāgaccha saumitre kuruṣva vacanaṁ mama
Do you, O delight of Raghus, soon come back, leaving behind Sita in that lonely place. Do you carry out my words. Do you not speak anything regarding Sita's banishment.

मानयन्तु भवन्तो मां यदि मच्छासने स्थिताः
इतोऽद्य नीयतां सीता कुरुष्व वचनं मम

mānayantu bhavanto māṁ yadi macchāsane sthitāḥ
ito'dya nīyatāṁ sītā kuruṣva vacanaṁ mama

For my life and arms, do you not proffer any request to me regarding this. If so, you shall only endanger my well-being and I shall ever regard you as my enemies. If you obey my behest's, do you honour my words now. Do you take away Sita from here.

पूर्वमुक्तोऽहमनया गङ्गातीरे महाश्रमान्
पश्येयमिति तस्याश्च कामः संवर्त्यतामयम्

pūrvamukto'hamanayā gaṅgātīre mahāśramān
paśyeyamiti tasyāśca kāmaḥ saṁvartyatāmayam
Ere this Sita had communicated her intention of beholding the hermitages of ascetics on the banks of the Ganga. Let that desire of hers be now satisfied.

एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थो बाष्पेण पिहितेक्षणः
प्रविवेश स धर्मात्मा भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः

evamuktvā tu kākutstho bāṣpeṇa pihitekṣaṇaḥ
praviveśa sa dharmātmā bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ

While saying this, the eyes of the virtuoussouled Rama were covered with tears. Sighing hard like to an elephant, he, with a heart stricken with grief, departed to his own quarter in the company of his brothers.

ततो रजन्यां व्युष्टायां लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः
सुमन्त्रमब्रवीद्वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता

tato rajanyāṁ vyuṣṭāyāṁ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ
sumantramabravīdvākyaṁ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
The night being over, Laksmana, with a poor heart and dried countenance, addressed Sumantra, saying.

सारथे तुरगाञ्शीघ्रं योजयस्व रथोत्तमे
स्वास्तीर्णं राजभवनात्सीतायाश्चासनं शुभम्

sārathe turagāñśīghraṁ yojayasva rathottame
svāstīrṇaṁ rājabhavanātsītāyāścāsanaṁ śubham

O charioteer, do you soon yoke quick coursing steeds to an excellent chariot, and for Sita place an excellent seat on the car. At the command of the King, I shall take Sita to the hermitage of the ascetics ever engaged in pious actions. Do you soon bring the chariot here.

सुमन्त्रस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः
रथं सुरुचिरप्रख्यं स्वास्तीर्णं सुखशय्यया

sumantrastu tathetyuktvā yuktaṁ paramavājibhiḥ
rathaṁ suruciraprakhyaṁ svāstīrṇaṁ sukhaśayyayā

Obeying the mandate, and bringing a beautiful and holy car drawn by first-rate steeds and having excellent seats, he said to Saumitri, the enhancer of friends' honour “O lord, here is the chariot ready-do you now satisfy your desire.

एवमुक्तः सुमन्त्रेण राजवेश्म स लक्ष्मणः
प्रविश्य सीतामासाद्य व्याजहार नरर्षभः

evamuktaḥ sumantreṇa rājaveśma sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
praviśya sītāmāsādya vyājahāra nararṣabhaḥ
Hearing the words of Sumantra, Laksmana, the foremost of men, approached Sita in the inner apartment and said.

एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे गमनं चाभ्यरोचयत्

evamuktā tu vaidehī lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe gamanaṁ cābhyarocayat
Hearing the words of the high-souled Laksmana, Janaki attained to excessive delight and became anxious to go.

वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च
गृहीत्वा तानि वैदेही गमनायोपचक्रमे

vāsāṁsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca
gṛhītvā tāni vaidehī gamanāyopacakrame
Taking various jewels and costly clothes she said to Laksmana, on the eve of her departure “I shall confer these ornaments, these costly clothes and riches on the female ascetics."

इमानि मुनिपत्नीनां दास्याम्याभरणान्यहम्
सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा रथमारोप्य मैथिलीम्
प्रययौ शीघ्रतुरगो रामस्याज्ञामनुस्मरन्

imāni munipatnīnāṁ dāsyāmyābharaṇānyaham
saumitristu tathetyuktvā rathamāropya maithilīm
prayayau śīghraturago rāmasyājñāmanusmaran
Saying 'we shall do the same' he made Sita ascend the car and remembering Rama's command proceeded, being carried by quickcoursing steeds.

अब्रवीच्च तदा सीता लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्
अशुभानि बहून्यद्य पश्यामि रघुनन्दन

abravīcca tadā sītā lakṣmaṇaṁ lakṣmivardhanam
aśubhāni bahūnyadya paśyāmi raghunandana
Thereupon Sita said to Laksmana, the enhancer of prosperity:-:0 descendant of Raghu, I behold many inauspicious omens. My right eye and body are trembling.

नयनं मे स्फुरत्यद्य गात्रोत्कम्पश्च जायते
हृदयं चैव सौमित्रे अस्वस्थमिव लक्षये

nayanaṁ me sphuratyadya gātrotkampaśca jāyate
hṛdayaṁ caiva saumitre asvasthamiva lakṣaye
My mind is growing depressed. It is stricken with anxiety and I have accordingly grown restless.

औत्सुक्यं परमं चापि अधृतिश्च परा मम
शून्यामिव च पश्यामि पृथिवीं पृथुलोचन

autsukyaṁ paramaṁ cāpi adhṛtiśca parā mama
śūnyāmiva ca paśyāmi pṛthivīṁ pṛthulocana
I behold the earth as void of all happiness. O you fond of brothers— has your brother met with any calamity?

पुरे जनपदे चैव कुशलं प्राणिनामपि
इत्यञ्जलिकृता सीता देवता अभ्ययाचत

pure janapade caiva kuśalaṁ prāṇināmapi
ityañjalikṛtā sītā devatā abhyayācata
Are all my mothers-in-law and subjects well?

ततो वासमुपागम्य गोमतीतीर आश्रमे
प्रभाते पुनरुत्थाय सौमित्रिः सूतमब्रवीत्

tato vāsamupāgamya gomatītīra āśrame
prabhāte punarutthāya saumitriḥ sūtamabravīt

Thereupon having arrived at the hermitage situate on the banks of Gomati Laksmana spent the night there. Thereupon at dawn he rose up and asked the charioteer to get the chariot ready, saying, “Like to the powerful Mahadeva we shall hold the waters of the Bhagirathi on our head.”

सोऽश्वान्विचारयित्वाशु रथे युक्त्वा मनोजवान्
आरोहस्वेति वैदेहीं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्

so'śvānvicārayitvāśu rathe yuktvā manojavān
ārohasveti vaidehīṁ sūtaḥ prāñjalirabravīt
Thereupon Sumantra yoked the horses, gifted with the fleet course of the mind, to the chariot and with folded hands said to Sita “Do you ascend the car."

सा तु सूतस्य वचनादारुरोह रथोत्तमम्
सीता सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सुमन्त्रेण च धीमता

sā tu sūtasya vacanādāruroha rathottamam
sītā saumitriṇā sārdhaṁ sumantreṇa ca dhīmatā

According to the request of the intelligent charioteer, Sita, with Laksmana, ascended that excellent conveyance. In no time the daughter of Janaka, having expansive eyes, arrived at the banks of the Ganga removing all sins.

अथार्धदिवसं गत्वा भागीरथ्या जलाशयम्
निरीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणो दीनः प्ररुरोद महास्वनम्

athārdhadivasaṁ gatvā bhāgīrathyā jalāśayam
nirīkṣya lakṣmaṇo dīnaḥ praruroda mahāsvanam
Reaching the currents of Bhagirathi before noon Laksmana, on beholding her, cried aloud.

सीता तु परमायत्ता दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणमातुरम्
उवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञ किमिदं रुद्यते त्वया

sītā tu paramāyattā dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamāturam
uvāca vākyaṁ dharmajña kimidaṁ rudyate tvayā

Thereupon beholding Laksmana thus distressed, Sita, conversant with piety, waxing are anxious said. “Why you weeping, Laksmana? I have reached the banks of Jahnavi, for which I have so long desired. So this is the time for rejoicing and do not give me pain at this time.

नित्यं त्वं रामपादेषु वर्तसे पुरुषर्षभ
कच्चिद्विनाकृतस्तेन द्विरात्रे शोकमागतः

nityaṁ tvaṁ rāmapādeṣu vartase puruṣarṣabha
kaccidvinākṛtastena dvirātre śokamāgataḥ
O foremost of men, you do spend your days and nights in the company of Rama. You have left him for two days only, are you sorry for this?

ममापि दयितो रामो जीवितेनापि लक्ष्मण
न चाहमेवं शोचामि मैवं त्वं बालिशो भव

mamāpi dayito rāmo jīvitenāpi lakṣmaṇa
