In this wise, the celestials being stricken with anxiety, according to the previous command of Visnu, engaged in celebrating the sacrifice.

ते तु दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षं मोहितं ब्रह्महत्यया
तं पुरस्कृत्य देवेशमश्वमेधं प्रचक्रिरे

te tu dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaṁ mohitaṁ brahmahatyayā
taṁ puraskṛtya deveśamaśvamedhaṁ pracakrire
With Rsis and Rtvikas they fearfully approached Purandra; and beholding him assailed by the sin of Brahmanicide, they with him, at their head, engaged in celebrating a horse-sacrifice.

ते तामूचुस्ततो देवास्तुष्टाः प्रीतिसमन्विताः
चतुर्धा विभजात्मानमात्मनैव दुरासदे

te tāmūcustato devāstuṣṭāḥ prītisamanvitāḥ
caturdhā vibhajātmānamātmanaiva durāsade

After the sacrifice the sin issued out of Indra's person and addressing the high-souled deities said: Do you all ascertain, where I shall go now. There upon highly pleased the deities replied: Do you divide yourself into four portions.

देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनाम्
संनिधौ स्थानमन्यत्र वरयामास दुर्वसा

devānāṁ bhāṣitaṁ śrutvā brahmahatyā mahātmanām
saṁnidhau sthānamanyatra varayāmāsa durvasā

Hearing the words of the high-souled celestials she divided herself into four parts and wishing for a separate habitation said:-By one portion, I shall at my pleasure, live in rivers full of water during rains and shall obstruct people from going there.

प्रत्यूचुस्तां ततो देवा यथा वदसि दुर्वसे
तथा भवतु तत्सर्वं साधयस्व यथेप्सितम्

pratyūcustāṁ tato devā yathā vadasi durvase
tathā bhavatu tatsarvaṁ sādhayasva yathepsitam
Hearing those words the deities said What you have said shall be carried out. Do what you wish.

ततः प्रीत्यान्विता देवाः सहस्राक्षं ववन्दिरे
विज्वरः पूतपाप्मा च वासवः समपद्यत

tataḥ prītyānvitā devāḥ sahasrākṣaṁ vavandire
vijvaraḥ pūtapāpmā ca vāsavaḥ samapadyata
There upon the celestials, delighted, adored their Chief divested of sins and crowned with victory.

प्रशान्तं च जगत्सर्वं सहस्राक्षे प्रतिष्ठते
यज्ञं चाद्भुतसंकाशं तदा शक्रोऽभ्यपूजयत्

praśāntaṁ ca jagatsarvaṁ sahasrākṣe pratiṣṭhate
yajñaṁ cādbhutasaṁkāśaṁ tadā śakro'bhyapūjayat
And Vasava being installed again on the throne, the whole universe was at rest. There upon Indra worshipped Visnu in the shape of that wonderful sacrifice.

ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रभावो रघुनन्दन
यजस्व सुमहाभाग हयमेधेन पार्थिव

īdṛśo hyaśvamedhasya prabhāvo raghunandana
yajasva sumahābhāga hayamedhena pārthiva
O descendant of Raghu, such is the power of a horse-sacrifice. O honourable king, therefore, you may perform this sacrifice.

तच्छ्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः प्रहसन्राघवो वचः

tacchrutvā lakṣmaṇenoktaṁ vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ
pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ prahasanrāghavo vacaḥ
Hearing the words of Laksmana and smiling, the highly effulgent descendant of Raghu, Rama, skilled in the are of speech, replied.

एवमेतन्नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण
वृत्रघातमशेषेण वाजिमेधफलं च यत्

evametannaraśreṣṭha yathā vadasi lakṣmaṇa
vṛtraghātamaśeṣeṇa vājimedhaphalaṁ ca yat
Laksmana, O foremost of men, you have truly related the story of Vstra's destruction and the fruits of horse-sacrifice.

श्रूयते हि पुरा सौम्य कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः
पुत्रो बाह्लीश्वरः श्रीमानिलो नाम सुधार्मिकः

śrūyate hi purā saumya kardamasya prajāpateḥ
putro bāhlīśvaraḥ śrīmānilo nāma sudhārmikaḥ
0gentle one, I have heard, that formerly in the province of Valhika, the graceful king lla, the son of the patriarch Kardama, was highly pious.

स राजा पृथिवीं सर्वां वशे कृत्वा महायशाः
राज्यं चैव नरव्याघ्र पुत्रवत्पर्यपालयत्

sa rājā pṛthivīṁ sarvāṁ vaśe kṛtvā mahāyaśāḥ
rājyaṁ caiva naravyāghra putravatparyapālayat
O foremost of men, having brought the entire earth under his subjects like to his own sons.

सुरैश्च परमोदारैर्दैतेयैश्च महासुरैः
नागराक्षसगन्धर्वैर्यक्षैश्च सुमहात्मभिः

suraiśca paramodārairdaiteyaiśca mahāsuraiḥ
nāgarākṣasagandharvairyakṣaiśca sumahātmabhiḥ

O descendant of Raghu, being terrified, the generous deities, the rich Daityas, the highly powerful Nagas, the irrepressible Raksasas, Gandharvas and Yaksas used to adore him perpetually. The high-souled Ila being enraged, the three worlds used to be convulsed with terror.

स राजा तादृशो ह्यासीद्धर्मे वीर्ये च निष्ठितः
बुद्ध्या च परमोदारो बाह्लीकानां महायशाः

sa rājā tādṛśo hyāsīddharme vīrye ca niṣṭhitaḥ
buddhyā ca paramodāro bāhlīkānāṁ mahāyaśāḥ
And albeit so very powerful the highly illustrious king of Valhika never swerved from the path of morality nor neglected his deities and rather intelligently used to administer all business.

स प्रचक्रे महाबाहुर्मृगयां रुचिरे वने
चैत्रे मनोरमे मासि सभृत्यबलवाहनः

sa pracakre mahābāhurmṛgayāṁ rucire vane
caitre manorame māsi sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ

Once on a time in the picturesque season of spring the mighty-armed Ila, with his army and conveyances, entered into a charming forest, and on the pretext of hunting, slew hundreds and thousands of deer. With slaying deer only the high-souled king was not satisfied.

नानामृगाणामयुतं वध्यमानं महात्मना
यत्र जातो महासेनस्तं देशमुपचक्रमे

nānāmṛgāṇāmayutaṁ vadhyamānaṁ mahātmanā
yatra jāto mahāsenastaṁ deśamupacakrame
He slew millions of diverse other animals. In this way being engaged in hunting the king Ila arrived where Kartikeya was born.

तस्मिंस्तु देवदेवेशः शैलराजसुतां हरः
रमयामास दुर्धर्षैः सर्वैरनुचरैः सह

tasmiṁstu devadeveśaḥ śailarājasutāṁ haraḥ
ramayāmāsa durdharṣaiḥ sarvairanucaraiḥ saha
At that time, in that hilly fountain there was sporting in the company of his followers, the irrepressible god of gods, the three-eyed deity with the daughter of the Chief of mountains.

कृत्वा स्त्रीभूतमात्मानमुमेशो गोपतिध्वजः
देव्याः प्रियचिकीर्षुः स तस्मिन्पर्वतनिर्झरे

kṛtvā strībhūtamātmānamumeśo gopatidhvajaḥ
devyāḥ priyacikīrṣuḥ sa tasminparvatanirjhare
Being desirous of satisfying the goddess Uma, her lord. whose emblem is bull, was sporting under the guise of a female.

ये च तत्र वनोद्देशे सत्त्वाः पुरुषवादिनः
यच्च किंचन तत्सर्वं नारीसंज्ञं बभूव ह

ye ca tatra vanoddeśe sattvāḥ puruṣavādinaḥ
yacca kiṁcana tatsarvaṁ nārīsaṁjñaṁ babhūva ha
In that forest land, all male animals or trees were metamorphosed into the other sex at that time.

ततो देवं महात्मानं शितिकण्ठं कपर्दिनम्
जगाम शरणं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहनः

tato devaṁ mahātmānaṁ śitikaṇṭhaṁ kapardinam
jagāma śaraṇaṁ rājā sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
There with his followers and army the king took shelter or the high-souled and red-throated deity.

ततः प्रहस्य वरदः सह देव्या महायशाः
प्रजापतिसुतं वाक्यमुवाच वरदः स्वयम्

tataḥ prahasya varadaḥ saha devyā mahāyaśāḥ
prajāpatisutaṁ vākyamuvāca varadaḥ svayam
There upon the great god, the conferror of boons, with the goddess, smiling said:

उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ राजर्षे कार्दमेय महाबल
पुरुषत्वमृते सौम्य वरं वरय सुव्रत

uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rājarṣe kārdameya mahābala
puruṣatvamṛte saumya varaṁ varaya suvrata

Rise up, O son of Kardama, O you of great strength, O gentle one, do you beg of me any other boon than that of obtaining your manhood. Being thus disappointed by the great deity, the king Ila, metamorphosed into a female, became greatly sorry and did not pray for any other boon.

ततः शोकेन महता शैलराजसुतां नृपः
प्रणिपत्य महादेवीं सर्वेणैवान्तरात्मना

tataḥ śokena mahatā śailarājasutāṁ nṛpaḥ
praṇipatya mahādevīṁ sarveṇaivāntarātmanā

Being stricken with great sorrow, the king, with whole heart, saluted the daughter of the mountain-chief and said:-0 goddess, you are the protectress of all-you do confer boons on all; seeing you does not become fruitless. Do you therefore have compassion on me.

हृद्गतं तस्य राजर्षेर्विज्ञाय हरसंनिधौ
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं देवी रुद्रस्य संमता

hṛdgataṁ tasya rājarṣervijñāya harasaṁnidhau
pratyuvāca śubhaṁ vākyaṁ devī rudrasya saṁmatā

There upon, cognisant of that king's intention, the goddess, with Hara's consent, said. Half of the boon, that you shall beg of us both, shall be granted by Mahadeva, and the other half shall be granted by me. Do you therefore beg of me the half.

यदि देवि प्रसन्ना मे रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि
मासं स्त्रीत्वमुपासित्वा मासं स्यां पुरुषः पुनः

yadi devi prasannā me rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi
māsaṁ strītvamupāsitvā māsaṁ syāṁ puruṣaḥ punaḥ

Hearing of that excellent and wondrous boon the king became greatly delighted and said:-If you are pleased with me, O goddess, do you confer upon me this boon, that I may be for one month, a female gifted with wonderful beauty in the three worlds and for another month I may be a male.

राजन्पुरुषभूतस्त्वं स्त्रीभावं न स्मरिष्यसि
स्त्रीभूतश्चापरं मासं न स्मरिष्यसि पौरुषम्

rājanpuruṣabhūtastvaṁ strībhāvaṁ na smariṣyasi
strībhūtaścāparaṁ māsaṁ na smariṣyasi pauruṣam

There upon understanding king's desire, the beautiful goddess Parvati, mercifully said: The boon, according to your desire, shall be granted. O king, when you shall attain to the male figure, you shall not remember anything of your female form. And when you shall a assume the charming female figure you shall forget everything of your male state.

एवं स राजा पुरुषो मासं भूत्वाथ कार्दमिः
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी नारी मासमेकमिलाभवत्

evaṁ sa rājā puruṣo māsaṁ bhūtvātha kārdamiḥ
trailokyasundarī nārī māsamekamilābhavat
O Laksmana, by virtue of this boon, the king Ila for one month used to become a man and for the next used to become female, charming in the three worlds under the name of Ila.

तौ रामं प्राञ्जलीभूत्वा तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः
विस्तरं तस्य भावस्य तदा पप्रच्छतुः पुनः

tau rāmaṁ prāñjalībhūtvā tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ
vistaraṁ tasya bhāvasya tadā papracchatuḥ punaḥ
Having heard of the story of the king Ila from Rama, Laksmana and Bharata were greatly surprised. And And with folded hands they, requesting the noble king Rama, for further particulars, said.

कथं स राजा स्त्रीभूतो वर्तयामास दुर्गतिम्
पुरुषो वा यदा भूतः कां वृत्तिं वर्तयत्यसौ

kathaṁ sa rājā strībhūto vartayāmāsa durgatim
puruṣo vā yadā bhūtaḥ kāṁ vṛttiṁ vartayatyasau
How could the king Ila subject himself to those afflictions in the shape of a female? And how did he use to behave himself in his male form?

तयोस्तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितम्
कथयामास काकुत्ष्ठस्तस्य राज्ञो यथा गतम्

tayostadbhāṣitaṁ śrutvā kautūhalasamanvitam
kathayāmāsa kākutṣṭhastasya rājño yathā gatam
Hearing those words begotten of curiosity, Rama engaged in relating the whole story as he had heard before, saying.

तमेव प्रथमं मासं स्त्रीभूत्वा लोकसुन्दरी
ताभिः परिवृता स्त्रीभिर्येऽस्य पूर्वं पदानुगाः

tameva prathamaṁ māsaṁ strībhūtvā lokasundarī
tābhiḥ parivṛtā strībhirye'sya pūrvaṁ padānugāḥ

In the first month, assuming his female form having lotus-eyes and charming the three world, he used to sport in the forest abounding in groves, in the company of his companions metamorphosed into the same form.

वाहनानि च सर्वाणि संत्यक्त्वा वै समन्ततः
पर्वताभोगविवरे तस्मिन्रेमे इला तदा

vāhanāni ca sarvāṇi saṁtyaktvā vai samantataḥ
parvatābhogavivare tasminreme ilā tadā
Having sent away all his conveyances Ila used to sport in the mountain vale.

अथ तस्मिन्वनोद्देशे पर्वतस्याविदूरतः
सरः सुरुचिरप्रख्यं नानापक्षिगणायुतम्

atha tasminvanoddeśe parvatasyāvidūrataḥ
saraḥ suruciraprakhyaṁ nānāpakṣigaṇāyutam
Thus roaming, Ila one day espied Budha, a bundle of rays, resembling the full moon in a picturesque pond filled with birds at some distance from the mountain.

तपन्तं च तपस्तीव्रमम्भोमध्ये दुरासदम्
यशक्सरं कामगमं तारुण्ये पर्यवस्थितम्

tapantaṁ ca tapastīvramambhomadhye durāsadam
yaśaksaraṁ kāmagamaṁ tāruṇye paryavasthitam
Having compassion for all creatures Budha, at that time, was performing, hard, glorious and wished-for austerities within waters.

सा तं जलाशयं सर्वं क्षोभयामास विस्मिता
सह तैः पूर पुरुषैः स्त्रीभूतै रघुनन्दन

sā taṁ jalāśayaṁ sarvaṁ kṣobhayāmāsa vismitā
saha taiḥ pūra puruṣaiḥ strībhūtai raghunandana
O son of Raghu, on beholding him Ila was greatly surprised, and with her female companions began to agitate waters.

इलां निरीक्षमाणः स त्रैलोक्याभ्यधिकां शुभाम्
चिन्तां समभ्यतिक्रामत्का न्वियं देवताधिका

ilāṁ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sa trailokyābhyadhikāṁ śubhām
cintāṁ samabhyatikrāmatkā nviyaṁ devatādhikā

As soon as Budha saw her he was assailed by the arrows of Cupid. Not being able to control himself he grew impatient within waters and thought. This damsel is far more beautiful even than the celestial girls.

न देवीषु न नागीषु नासुरीष्वप्सरःसु च
दृष्टपूर्वा मया काचिद्रूपेणैतेन शोभिता

na devīṣu na nāgīṣu nāsurīṣvapsaraḥsu ca
dṛṣṭapūrvā mayā kācidrūpeṇaitena śobhitā
I have never seen before a like among the celestials, Nagas, Asuras and Apsaras.

सदृशीयं मम भवेद्यदि नान्यपरिग्रहा
इति बुद्धिं समास्थाय जलात्स्थलमुपागमत्

sadṛśīyaṁ mama bhavedyadi nānyaparigrahā
iti buddhiṁ samāsthāya jalātsthalamupāgamat
If she has not been married before then she is my worthy spouse. With this resolution Budha got up from the waters, and repairing to his hermitage, sent for the fair ones. they all saluted him.

स ताः पप्रच्छ धर्मात्म कस्यैषा लोकसुन्दरी
किमर्थमागता चेह सत्यमाख्यात माचिरम्

sa tāḥ papraccha dharmātma kasyaiṣā lokasundarī
kimarthamāgatā ceha satyamākhyāta māciram
Thereupon the virtuous-souled Budha accosted them saying: Whose daughter is this graceful girl among you and for what she has come here? Do not delay-tell me soon.

शुभं तु तस्य तद्वाक्यं मधुरं मधुराक्षरम्
श्रुत्वा तु ताः स्त्रियः सर्वा ऊचुर्मधुरया गिरा

śubhaṁ tu tasya tadvākyaṁ madhuraṁ madhurākṣaram
śrutvā tu tāḥ striyaḥ sarvā ūcurmadhurayā girā
Hearing those sweet words of Budha, the all females also said in sweet accents.

अस्माकमेषा सुश्रोणी प्रभुत्वे वर्तते सदा
अपतिः काननान्तेषु सहास्माभिरटत्यसौ

asmākameṣā suśroṇī prabhutve vartate sadā
apatiḥ kānanānteṣu sahāsmābhiraṭatyasau
This fair damsel is our supreme lady. She has no husband. Journeying she has come here in the forest with us.

तद्वाक्यमव्यक्तपदं तासां स्त्रीणां निशम्य तु
विद्यामावर्तनीं पुण्यामावर्तयत स द्विजः

tadvākyamavyaktapadaṁ tāsāṁ strīṇāṁ niśamya tu
vidyāmāvartanīṁ puṇyāmāvartayata sa dvijaḥ
Hearing those plain words, Budha thought of the learning by which one can perceive everything.

सोऽर्थं विदित्वा निखिलं तस्य राज्ञो यथागतम्
सर्वा एव स्त्रियस्ताश्च बभाषे मुनिपुंगवः

so'rthaṁ viditvā nikhilaṁ tasya rājño yathāgatam
sarvā eva striyastāśca babhāṣe munipuṁgavaḥ
And being informed of all inatters regarding the king Ila, thereby that foremost of sages said to the females.

अत्र किं पुरुषा भद्रा अवसञ्शैलरोधसि
वत्स्यथास्मिन्गिरौ यूयमवकाशो विधीयताम्

atra kiṁ puruṣā bhadrā avasañśailarodhasi
vatsyathāsmingirau yūyamavakāśo vidhīyatām
Do you all live in this mountain being Kimpurusas; do you make your respective habitations here.

मूलपुत्रफलैः सर्वा वर्तयिष्यथ नित्यदा
स्त्रियः किम्पुरुषान्नाम भर्तॄन्समुपलप्स्यथ

mūlaputraphalaiḥ sarvā vartayiṣyatha nityadā
striyaḥ kimpuruṣānnāma bhartṝnsamupalapsyatha
I shall give you always fruits and roots. O you females, you shall have all Kimpurusas as your husbands.

ताः श्रुत्वा सोमपुत्रस्य वाचं किंपुरुषीकृताः
उपासां चक्रिरे शैलं बह्व्यस्ता बहुधा तदा

tāḥ śrutvā somaputrasya vācaṁ kiṁpuruṣīkṛtāḥ
upāsāṁ cakrire śailaṁ bahvyastā bahudhā tadā
According to the words of Budha they lived in that mountains as Kimpurusas. In this wise many Kimpurusa-Budhas were procreated.

श्रुत्वा किंपुरुषोत्पत्तिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तदा
आश्चर्यमिति चाब्रूतामुभौ रामं जनेश्वरम्

śrutvā kiṁpuruṣotpattiṁ lakṣmaṇo bharatastadā
āścaryamiti cābrūtāmubhau rāmaṁ janeśvaram
Having heard of the origin of Kimpurusas, both Bharata and Laksmana said to Rama: This is a wonderful story.

अथ रामः कथामेतां भूय एव महायशाः
कथयामास धर्मात्मा प्रजापतिसुतस्य वै

atha rāmaḥ kathāmetāṁ bhūya eva mahāyaśāḥ
kathayāmāsa dharmātmā prajāpatisutasya vai
Thereupon the highly illustrious Rama, the foremost of the pious, again began with the story of Ila, the son of the patriarch.

सर्वास्ता विद्रुता दृष्ट्वा किंनरीरृषिसत्तमः
उवाच रूपसंपन्नां तां स्त्रियं प्रहसन्निव

sarvāstā vidrutā dṛṣṭvā kiṁnarīrṛṣisattamaḥ
uvāca rūpasaṁpannāṁ tāṁ striyaṁ prahasanniva
Beholding the Kinnaris repairing to a distance, Buddha the foremost of ascetics, smiling said, to the beautiful Ila:

सोमस्याहं सुदयितः सुतः सुरुचिरानने
भजस्व मां वरारोहे भक्त्या स्निग्धेन चक्षुषा

somasyāhaṁ sudayitaḥ sutaḥ surucirānane
bhajasva māṁ varārohe bhaktyā snigdhena cakṣuṣā
O you of a graceful presence, I am the most favourite son of the moon; O fair one, do you, with delight, cast looks upon me.

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शून्ये स्वजनवर्जिता
इला सुरुचिरप्रख्यं प्रत्युवाच महाग्रहम्

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā śūnye svajanavarjitā
ilā suruciraprakhyaṁ pratyuvāca mahāgraham
Hearing the words of the highly effulgent and beautiful Budha in the picturesque forest land divested of men and animals, Ila said.

अहं कामकरी सौम्य तवास्मि वशवर्तिनी
प्रशाधि मां सोमसुत यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु

ahaṁ kāmakarī saumya tavāsmi vaśavartinī
praśādhi māṁ somasuta yathecchasi tathā kuru
O gentle one, I am not subject to any body; I surrender myself to you out of my own accord. O son of Soma, you may command me whatever you wish.

तस्यास्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं श्रुत्वा हर्षसमन्वितः
स वै कामी सह तया रेमे चन्द्रमसः सुतः

tasyāstadadbhutaprakhyaṁ śrutvā harṣasamanvitaḥ
sa vai kāmī saha tayā reme candramasaḥ sutaḥ
Hearing those wondrous words, the son of moon, possessed by lust, began to live with her.

बुधस्य माधवो मासस्तामिलां रुचिराननाम्
गतो रमयतोऽत्यर्थं क्षणवत्तस्य कामिनः

budhasya mādhavo māsastāmilāṁ rucirānanām
gato ramayato'tyarthaṁ kṣaṇavattasya kāminaḥ
And living in the company of Ila, having a graceful countenance, Budha, possessed by desire, spent the entire month of Madhu like a moment.

अथ मासे तु संपूर्णे पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननः
प्रजापतिसुतः श्रीमाञ्शयने प्रत्यबुध्यत

atha māse tu saṁpūrṇe pūrṇendusadṛśānanaḥ
prajāpatisutaḥ śrīmāñśayane pratyabudhyata

There upon after the expiry of a month, the graceful king Ila, son of Soma, engaged from sleep and beholding Budha, the son of Soma, engaged in austerities with uplifted hands in the midst of waters, said.

भगवन्पर्वतं दुर्गं प्रविष्टोऽस्मि सहानुगः
न च पश्यामि तत्सैन्यं क्व नु ते मामका गताः

bhagavanparvataṁ durgaṁ praviṣṭo'smi sahānugaḥ
na ca paśyāmi tatsainyaṁ kva nu te māmakā gatāḥ
'O illustrious Sir, with my followers I entered this dense forest-I do not see them now anywhere. Where have they gone?

तच्छ्रुत्वा तस्य राजर्षेर्नष्टसंज्ञस्य भाषितम्
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं सान्त्वयन्परया गिरा

tacchrutvā tasya rājarṣernaṣṭasaṁjñasya bhāṣitam
pratyuvāca śubhaṁ vākyaṁ sāntvayanparayā girā
Hearing the words of the royal saint, who had lost all recollection, Budha, with sweet words consoled him and said.

अश्मवर्षेण महता भृत्यास्ते विनिपातिताः
त्वं चाश्रमपदे सुप्तो वातवर्षभयार्दितः

aśmavarṣeṇa mahatā bhṛtyāste vinipātitāḥ
tvaṁ cāśramapade supto vātavarṣabhayārditaḥ
All your followers have been destroyed by a downpour of huge rocks; yourself, being afraid of the storm, was also asleep in the hermitage.

समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते निर्भयो विगतज्वरः
फलमूलाशनो वीर वस चेह यथासुखम्

samāśvasihi bhadraṁ te nirbhayo vigatajvaraḥ
phalamūlāśano vīra vasa ceha yathāsukham
You have no fear now. Therefore, O hero, being consoled and renouncing all anxiety do you live here happily living upon fruits and roots.

स राजा तेन वाक्येन प्रत्याश्वस्तो महायशाः
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं दीनो भृत्यजनक्षयात्

sa rājā tena vākyena pratyāśvasto mahāyaśāḥ
pratyuvāca śubhaṁ vākyaṁ dīno bhṛtyajanakṣayāt
Being comforted by those words, the highminded king Ila, stricken with distress in consequence of the destruction of his servants, poorly replied.

त्यक्ष्याम्यहं स्वकं राज्यं नाहं भृत्यैर्विना कृतः
वर्तयेयं क्षणं ब्रह्मन्समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि

tyakṣyāmyahaṁ svakaṁ rājyaṁ nāhaṁ bhṛtyairvinā kṛtaḥ
vartayeyaṁ kṣaṇaṁ brahmansamanujñātumarhasi
O Brahmana, I shall renounce my own kingdom. Separated from my servants, I shall not be able to live even for a moment. Do you give me permission in this.

सुतो धर्मपरो ब्रह्मञ्ज्येष्ठो मम महायशाः
शशबिन्दुरिति ख्यातः स मे राज्यं प्रपत्स्यते

suto dharmaparo brahmañjyeṣṭho mama mahāyaśāḥ
śaśabinduriti khyātaḥ sa me rājyaṁ prapatsyate
O Brahmana, my eldest son, the highly illustrious Sasabindu, the foremost of the pious, shall be the owner of my kingdom.

न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं गत्वा भृत्यदारान्सुखान्वितान्
प्रतिवक्तुं महातेजः किंचिदप्यशुभं वचः

na hi śakṣyāmyahaṁ gatvā bhṛtyadārānsukhānvitān
prativaktuṁ mahātejaḥ kiṁcidapyaśubhaṁ vacaḥ
O Brahmana, renouncing my servants and wives of the country I shall not be able to wait here. Therefore, O highly effulgent one, do you not give me such an unpleasant command of remaining here.

तथा ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे बुधः परममद्भुतम्
सान्त्वपूर्वमथोवाच वासस्त इह रोचताम्

tathā bruvati rājendre budhaḥ paramamadbhutam
sāntvapūrvamathovāca vāsasta iha rocatām

Hearing those wonderful words of the king Ila, Budha consoling him, said:-Do you wait here. Be not aggrieved, O highly powerful son of Kardama. If you do live here for a year, I shall render your well-being.

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बुधस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः
वासाय विदधे बुद्धिं यदुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā budhasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
vāsāya vidadhe buddhiṁ yaduktaṁ brahmavādinā
Hearing the words of Budha, of unwearied actions, the king Ila desired to live there.

मासं स स्त्री तदा भूत्वा रमयत्यनिशं शुभा
मासं पुरुषभावेन धर्मबुद्धिं चकार सः

māsaṁ sa strī tadā bhūtvā ramayatyaniśaṁ śubhā
māsaṁ puruṣabhāvena dharmabuddhiṁ cakāra saḥ
There upon becoming a man for the next month he began to perform ascetic penances.

जातमात्रं तु सुश्रोणी पितुर्हस्ते न्यवेशयत्
बुधस्य समवर्णाभमिलापुत्रं महाबलम्

jātamātraṁ tu suśroṇī piturhaste nyaveśayat
budhasya samavarṇābhamilāputraṁ mahābalam

There upon in the ninth month, Ila, having a beautiful waist, gave birth to a highly effulgent son, under the name of Pururava, born of the lions of Budha, and equally graceful like him. and she handed over the highly powerful son to his father Budha.

बुधोऽपि पुरुषीभूतं समाश्वास्य नराधिपम्
कथाभी रमयामास धर्मयुक्ताभिरात्मवान्

budho'pi puruṣībhūtaṁ samāśvāsya narādhipam
kathābhī ramayāmāsa dharmayuktābhirātmavān
There upon after a year Ila having regained the male form, Budha by means of various words afforded delight to him.

तथोक्तवति रामे तु तस्य जन्म तदद्भुतम्
उवाच लक्ष्मणो भूयो भरतश्च महायशाः

tathoktavati rāme tu tasya janma tadadbhutam
uvāca lakṣmaṇo bhūyo bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ
Rama having thus described the wonderful birth of Pururava, the illustrious Bharata and Laksmana asked him again saying.

सा प्रिया सोमपुत्रस्य संवत्सरमथोषिता
अकरोत्किं नरश्रेष्ठ तत्त्वं शंसितुमर्हसि

sā priyā somaputrasya saṁvatsaramathoṣitā
akarotkiṁ naraśreṣṭha tattvaṁ śaṁsitumarhasi
O foremost of men, tell us what did Ila afterwards do after living in the company of Soma's son for a year.

तयोस्तद्वाक्यमाधुर्यं निशम्य परिपृच्छतोः
रामः पुनरुवाचेमां प्रजापतिसुते कथाम्

tayostadvākyamādhuryaṁ niśamya paripṛcchatoḥ
rāmaḥ punaruvācemāṁ prajāpatisute kathām
Hearing their sweet words Rama again began with the story of Kardama's son and said.

एतान्सर्वान्समानीय वाक्यज्ञस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः
उवाच सर्वान्सुहृदो धैर्येण सुसमाहितः

etānsarvānsamānīya vākyajñastattvadarśinaḥ
uvāca sarvānsuhṛdo dhairyeṇa susamāhitaḥ

In turn, the heroic Ila, having regained his manhood, the highly illustrious and intelligent Budha, well-informed of birth and well-skilled in the are of speech, sent for the highly liberal Samvarta, Bhrgu's son Cyavana, Aristanemi, the foremost of Munis, Durvasa, capable of affording delight, and other friends gifted with patience and said.

अयं राजा महाबाहुः कर्दमस्य इलः सुतः
जानीतैनं यथा भूतं श्रेयो ह्यस्य विधीयताम्

ayaṁ rājā mahābāhuḥ kardamasya ilaḥ sutaḥ
jānītainaṁ yathā bhūtaṁ śreyo hyasya vidhīyatām
You all know well, how this mighty-armed Ila, Kardama's son, attained to this peculiar condition.

तेषां संवदतामेव तमाश्रममुपागमत्
कर्दमः सुमहातेजा द्विजैः सह महात्मभिः

teṣāṁ saṁvadatāmeva tamāśramamupāgamat
kardamaḥ sumahātejā dvijaiḥ saha mahātmabhiḥ
There upon while those high-souled ones were conversing upon this subject, the highly effulgent Kardama arrived at the hermitage.

पुलस्त्यश्च क्रतुश्चैव वषट्कारस्तथैव च
ओंकारश्च महातेजास्तमाश्रममुपागमन्

pulastyaśca kratuścaiva vaṣaṭkārastathaiva ca
oṁkāraśca mahātejāstamāśramamupāgaman
Pulastya, Kratu, Vasatkara and the highly effulgent Omkara came there following him.

ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसः परस्परसमागमे
हितैषिणो बाह्लि पतेः पृथग्वाक्यमथाब्रुवन्

te sarve hṛṣṭamanasaḥ parasparasamāgame
hitaiṣiṇo bāhli pateḥ pṛthagvākyamathābruvan
Being greatly delighted for their arrival they all gave out their individual opinion for bringing about the well-being of the king of Valhika.

कर्दमस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं सुतार्थं परमं हितम्
द्विजाः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यच्छ्रेयः पार्थिवस्य हि

kardamastvabravīdvākyaṁ sutārthaṁ paramaṁ hitam
dvijāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṁ yacchreyaḥ pārthivasya hi
For the welfare of his son, the patriarch Kardama said: Hear, O twice-born ones, how the well-being of the king Ila may be secured.

नान्यं पश्यामि भैषज्यमन्तरेण वृषध्वजम्
नाश्वमेधात्परो यज्ञः प्रियश्चैव महात्मनः

nānyaṁ paśyāmi bhaiṣajyamantareṇa vṛṣadhvajam
nāśvamedhātparo yajñaḥ priyaścaiva mahātmanaḥ
For this decease do not find any other good medicine but Uma's lord. And save Asvamedha there is no other sacrifice more favourite to the high-souled deity.

तस्माद्यजामहे सर्वे पार्थिवार्थे दुरासदम्
कर्दमेनैवमुक्तास्तु सर्व एव द्विजर्षभाः
रोचयन्ति स्म तं यज्ञं रुद्रस्याराधनं प्रति

tasmādyajāmahe sarve pārthivārthe durāsadam
kardamenaivamuktāstu sarva eva dvijarṣabhāḥ
rocayanti sma taṁ yajñaṁ rudrasyārādhanaṁ prati

Let us all therefore celebrate that hard sacrifice on behalf of this king. Thereupon the wors of Kardama, Samvarta's disciple, the royal saint Marutta, the conqueror of enemies, collected all articles for the sacrifice.

ततो यज्ञो महानासीद्बुधाश्रमसमीपतः
रुद्रश्च परमं तोषमाजगाम महायशाः

tato yajño mahānāsīdbudhāśramasamīpataḥ
rudraśca paramaṁ toṣamājagāma mahāyaśāḥ

There upon in the vicinity of Budha's hermitage that mighty sacrifice was celebrated. And by that the Great Rudra lord of Uma, attained to delight and said to the twice-born ones, and others at the end of that sacrifice in the presence of the king Ila.

प्रीतोऽस्मि हयमेधेन भक्त्या च द्विजसत्तमाः
अस्य बाह्लिपतेश्चैव किं करोमि प्रियं शुभम्

prīto'smi hayamedhena bhaktyā ca dvijasattamāḥ
asya bāhlipateścaiva kiṁ karomi priyaṁ śubham
O foremost of twice-born ones, I have been greatly delighted with this sacrifice and your devotion. Tell me now, what I can do for this king of Valhika.

तथा वदति देवेशे द्विजास्ते सुसमाहिताः
प्रसादयन्ति देवेशं यथा स्यात्पुरुषस्त्विला

tathā vadati deveśe dvijāste susamāhitāḥ
prasādayanti deveśaṁ yathā syātpuruṣastvilā
Hearing the words of Mahadeva, the Brahmanas having propitiated him with great devotion, prayed for Ila's manhood.

ततः प्रीतमना रुद्रः पुरुषत्वं ददौ पुनः
इलायै सुमहातेजा दत्त्वा चान्तरधीयत

tataḥ prītamanā rudraḥ puruṣatvaṁ dadau punaḥ
ilāyai sumahātejā dattvā cāntaradhīyata
There upon delighted the highly effulgent Mahadeva, having having conferred upon him manhood, disappeared.

ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रभावः पुरुषर्षभौ
स्त्रीभूतः पौरुषं लेभे यच्चान्यदपि दुर्लभम्

īdṛśo hyaśvamedhasya prabhāvaḥ puruṣarṣabhau
strībhūtaḥ pauruṣaṁ lebhe yaccānyadapi durlabham
O foremost of men, such is the power of the horse-sacrifice, that the king Ila, though converted into a female, regained manhood by virtue thereof.

एतदाख्याय काकुत्स्थो भ्रातृभ्याममितप्रभः
लक्ष्मणं पुनरेवाह धर्मयुक्तमिदं वचः

etadākhyāya kākutstho bhrātṛbhyāmamitaprabhaḥ
lakṣmaṇaṁ punarevāha dharmayuktamidaṁ vacaḥ
Having thus addressed his both brothers, Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha of unmitigated prowess, again said to Laksmana, in words pregnant with morality.

वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ कश्यपम्
द्विजांश्च सर्वप्रवरानश्वमेधपुरस्कृतान्

vasiṣṭhaṁ vāmadevaṁ ca jābālimatha kaśyapam
dvijāṁśca sarvapravarānaśvamedhapuraskṛtān

O Laksmana, having invited Vasistha, the foremost of twice-born ones, conversant with all the rites of Asvamedha, Vamadeva, Jabali, and Kasyapa and consulted with them duly I shall set free a horse gifted with all marks.

तद्वाक्यं राघवेणोक्तं श्रुत्वा त्वरितविक्रमः
द्विजान्सर्वान्समाहूय दर्शयामास राघवम्

tadvākyaṁ rāghaveṇoktaṁ śrutvā tvaritavikramaḥ
dvijānsarvānsamāhūya darśayāmāsa rāghavam
Hearing the words of Rama, Laksmana, of unmitigated prowess, invited all those Brahmanas and approached Rama.

ते दृष्ट्वा देवसंकाशं कृतपादाभिवन्दनम्
राघवं सुदुराधर्षमाशीर्भिः समपूजयन्

te dṛṣṭvā devasaṁkāśaṁ kṛtapādābhivandanam
rāghavaṁ sudurādharṣamāśīrbhiḥ samapūjayan
Seeing them, Rama saluted them touching their feet. And the Brahmanas too, beholding the irrepressible celestial, like Raghava, welcomed him with blessings.

प्राञ्जलिस्तु ततो भूत्वा राघवो द्विजसत्तमान्
उवाच धर्मसंयुक्तमश्वमेधाश्रितं वचः

prāñjalistu tato bhūtvā rāghavo dvijasattamān
uvāca dharmasaṁyuktamaśvamedhāśritaṁ vacaḥ
The.. upon Rama, with folded hands, asked of those leading twice-born ones, questions regarding the Asvamedha sacrifice.

स तेषां द्विजमुख्यानां वाक्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्
अश्वमेधाश्रितं श्रुत्वा भृशं प्रीतोऽभवत्तदा

sa teṣāṁ dvijamukhyānāṁ vākyamadbhutadarśanam
aśvamedhāśritaṁ śrutvā bhṛśaṁ prīto'bhavattadā
And being informed from the Brahmanas of many unheard of virtues of Asvamedha, Rama was greatly delighted.

विज्ञाय तु मतं तेषां रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
प्रेषयस्व महाबाहो सुग्रीवाय महात्मने

vijñāya tu mataṁ teṣāṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
preṣayasva mahābāho sugrīvāya mahātmane

And according to their desire he said to Laksmana:— you having long arms, do you soon send an emissary to the high-souled Sugriva, communicating to him 'Do you come here to enjoy festivities in the company of all those highly powerful monkeys and hears under you; may good betide you.

विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिः कामगैर्बहुभिर्वृतः
अश्वमेधं महाबाहुः प्राप्नोतु लघुविक्रमः

vibhīṣaṇaśca rakṣobhiḥ kāmagairbahubhirvṛtaḥ
aśvamedhaṁ mahābāhuḥ prāpnotu laghuvikramaḥ
See that Vibhisana of unequalled prowess, the king of Raksasas, encircled by his followers coursing at will, may be present at the horse sacrifice.

राजानश्च नरव्याघ्र ये मे प्रियचिकीर्षवः
सानुगाः क्षिप्रमायान्तु यज्ञभूमिमनुत्तमाम्

rājānaśca naravyāghra ye me priyacikīrṣavaḥ
sānugāḥ kṣipramāyāntu yajñabhūmimanuttamām
Let the great kings, wishing my welfare with their followers be present at the sacrifice.

देशान्तरगता ये च द्विजा धर्मपरायणाः
निमन्त्रयस्व तान्सर्वानश्वमेधाय लक्ष्मण

deśāntaragatā ye ca dvijā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
nimantrayasva tānsarvānaśvamedhāya lakṣmaṇa
O Laksmana, do you also invite carefully, for witnessing the ceremony, other pious foreign kings who are friendly to me.

ऋषयश्च महाबाहो आहूयन्तां तपोधनाः
देशान्तरगता ये च सदाराश्च महर्षयः

ṛṣayaśca mahābāho āhūyantāṁ tapodhanāḥ
deśāntaragatā ye ca sadārāśca maharṣayaḥ

O you having long arms, do you also invite the Rsis, having asceticism for their wealth and other pious Brahmanas living in various provinces with their wives. Do you also invite actors and songsters. Do you order that a spacious, sacrificial ground may be made on the banks of the river Gomati in the Naimisa forest, O you having long arms, that part of the country is best suited and holy.

सुवर्णकोट्यो बहुला हिरण्यस्य शतोत्तराः
अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे महामतिः

suvarṇakoṭyo bahulā hiraṇyasya śatottarāḥ
agrato bharataḥ kṛtvā gacchatvagre mahāmatiḥ

O you having long arms, let Bharata go before with a million of beasts carrying rice, sessamun seed, Kindney bean, Chickpea, pulse, Masha (a sort of Kindney bean) salt, oil, clarified butter and a hundred koti of silver and golden coins.

अन्तरापणवीथ्यश्च सर्वांश्च नटनर्तकान्
नैगमान्बालवृद्धांश्च द्विजांश्च सुसमाहितान्

antarāpaṇavīthyaśca sarvāṁśca naṭanartakān
naigamānbālavṛddhāṁśca dvijāṁśca susamāhitān
Let merchants, to set up shops on the way, actors, dancers, cooks, and many youthful females follow Bharata.

यज्ञवाटं महाबाहुर्दृष्ट्वा परममद्भुतम्
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे श्रीमानिति च सोऽब्रवीत्

yajñavāṭaṁ mahābāhurdṛṣṭvā paramamadbhutam
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe śrīmāniti ca so'bravīt

Having speedily despatched before all articles of sacrifice, Bharata's elder brother Rama set free a black horse, gifted with all marks and worthy of the sacrifice and placed Laksmana with Rtvik in charge of it. There upon the mighty-armed Kakuthstha, in the company of his soldiers, proceeded to the Naimina forest and beholding the wonderful sacrificial ground attained to an excess of delight and said:-It has become highly charming.

नैमिषे वसतस्तस्य सर्व एव नराधिपाः
आजग्मुः सर्वराष्ट्रेभ्यस्तान्रामः प्रत्यपूजयत्

naimiṣe vasatastasya sarva eva narādhipāḥ
ājagmuḥ sarvarāṣṭrebhyastānrāmaḥ pratyapūjayat
While he remained in the Naimisa forest, all the kings sent him presents and Rama also made returns.

उपकार्यान्महार्हांश्च पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम्
सानुगानां नरश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश महाद्युतिः

upakāryānmahārhāṁśca pārthivānāṁ mahātmanām
sānugānāṁ naraśreṣṭho vyādideśa mahādyutiḥ

Vibhisana, in the company of many Raksasas, with a collected mind, began to serve the Rsis, having asceticism for their wealth. And the highly powerful Rama, the foremost of men, set aside valuable houses for the accommodation of the high-souled kings.

अन्नपानानि वस्त्राणि सानुगानां महात्मनाम्
भरतः संददावाशु शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा

annapānāni vastrāṇi sānugānāṁ mahātmanām
bharataḥ saṁdadāvāśu śatrughnasahitastadā
According to the command of Rama, Bharata, with Satrughna, made arrangements for highly valuable quarters, food, drink and clothes.

वानराश्च महात्मानः सुग्रीवसहितास्तदा
विप्राणां प्रणताः सर्वे चक्रिरे परिवेषणम्

vānarāśca mahātmānaḥ sugrīvasahitāstadā
viprāṇāṁ praṇatāḥ sarve cakrire pariveṣaṇam
And the highly powerful monkeys with Sugriva and Brahmanas engaged in the work of distribution.

विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिः स्रग्विभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः
ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां किंकरः पर्युपस्थितः

vibhīṣaṇaśca rakṣobhiḥ sragvibhirbahubhirvṛtaḥ
ṛṣīṇāmugratapasāṁ kiṁkaraḥ paryupasthitaḥ
And Vibhisana, surrounded by various Raksasas and females, engaged in the service of the high-souled Rsis intent on hard penances.

न कश्चिन्मलिनस्तत्र दीनो वाप्यथ वा कृशः
तस्मिन्यज्ञवरे राज्ञो हृष्टपुष्टजनावृते

na kaścinmalinastatra dīno vāpyatha vā kṛśaḥ
tasminyajñavare rājño hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛte

Indeed before words came out from the lips of the beggars, monkeys and Raksasas satisfied them with gifts. And all the ascetics living for ever and having asceticism for wealth that were present there, could not think of any other sacrifice, accompanied by so profuse presents, they had seen before.

सर्वत्र वानरास्तस्थुः सर्वत्रैव च राक्षसाः
वासो धनानि कामिभ्यः पूर्णहस्ता ददुर्भृशम्

sarvatra vānarāstasthuḥ sarvatraiva ca rākṣasāḥ
vāso dhanāni kāmibhyaḥ pūrṇahastā dadurbhṛśam
Being present everywhere the Raksasas and Vanaras gave away enough of riches and clothes even to them who did not want.

ईदृशो राजसिंहस्य यज्ञः सर्वगुणान्वितः
संवत्सरमथो साग्रं वर्तते न च हीयते

īdṛśo rājasiṁhasya yajñaḥ sarvaguṇānvitaḥ
saṁvatsaramatho sāgraṁ vartate na ca hīyate
And though this sacrifice, gifted with all marks, of Rama, a lion among kings, continued for a year still his accumulated treasure was not exhausted, but rather was increased.

वर्तमाने तथाभूते यज्ञे परमकेऽद्भुते
सशिष्य आजगामाशु वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुंगवः

vartamāne tathābhūte yajñe paramake'dbhute
saśiṣya ājagāmāśu vālmīkirmunipuṁgavaḥ
That sacrifice, the like of which was never seen before, having been undertaken the illustrious ascetic Valmiki, with his disciples, came there.

स दृष्ट्वा दिव्यसंकाशं यज्ञमद्भुतदर्शनम्
एकान्ते ऋषिवाटानां चकार उटजाञ्शुभान्

sa dṛṣṭvā divyasaṁkāśaṁ yajñamadbhutadarśanam
ekānte ṛṣivāṭānāṁ cakāra uṭajāñśubhān
And beholding this wonderful sacrifice resembling that of the celestials, his followers, the Rsis, made charming cottages in a solitary corner and at no distance.

ऋषिवाटेषु पुण्येषु ब्राह्मणावसथेषु च
रथ्यासु राजमार्गेषु पार्थिवानां गृहेषु च

ṛṣivāṭeṣu puṇyeṣu brāhmaṇāvasatheṣu ca
rathyāsu rājamārgeṣu pārthivānāṁ gṛheṣu ca

There upon Valmiki said to his disciples, Lava and Kuca Do you carefully and delightedly sing the whole of Ramayana in the highly holy hermitages, of the Rsis, in the homes where perpetual fire is kept up by the Brahmanas, in streets and palaces, at the gate of Rama's house, in the sacrificial arena and before all Rtvik.

इमानि च फलान्यत्र स्वादूनि विविधानि च
जातानि पर्वताग्रेषु आस्वाद्यास्वाद्य गीयताम्

imāni ca phalānyatra svādūni vividhāni ca
jātāni parvatāgreṣu āsvādyāsvādya gīyatām
And eating all those sweet fruits that are on the summit of the mountain near our hermitage, do you engage in chanting the sweet Ramayana.

न यास्यथः श्रमं वत्सौ भक्षयित्वा फलानि वै
मूलानि च सुमृष्टानि नगरात्परिहास्यथ

na yāsyathaḥ śramaṁ vatsau bhakṣayitvā phalāni vai
mūlāni ca sumṛṣṭāni nagarātparihāsyatha
If your begin singing after taking all those sweet fruits you shall not experience exhaustion in singing nor you shall forget measure.

यदि शब्दापयेद्रामः श्रवणाय महीपतिः
ऋषीणामुपविष्टानां ततो गेयं प्रवर्तताम्

yadi śabdāpayedrāmaḥ śravaṇāya mahīpatiḥ
ṛṣīṇāmupaviṣṭānāṁ tato geyaṁ pravartatām
If Rama, the lord of earth, invites you to sing the Ramayana, you may fearlessly sing it there in due notes and measures before the assembled ascetics.

दिवसे विंशतिः सर्गा गेया वै परया मुदा
प्रमाणैर्बहुभिस्तत्र यथोद्दिष्टं मया पुरा

divase viṁśatiḥ sargā geyā vai parayā mudā
pramāṇairbahubhistatra yathoddiṣṭaṁ mayā purā
During the day do you sing, in your sweet voice, twenty sections out of many I have laid in the Ramayana consisting of many slokas.

लोभश्चापि न कर्तव्यः स्वल्पोऽपि धनकाङ्क्षया
किं धनेनाश्रमस्थानां फलमूलोपभोगिनाम्

lobhaścāpi na kartavyaḥ svalpo'pi dhanakāṅkṣayā
kiṁ dhanenāśramasthānāṁ phalamūlopabhoginām
Do not cherish the least longing for riches. Of what avail is wealth to ascetics living perpetually on fruits and roots?

यदि पृच्छेत्स काकुत्स्थो युवां कस्येति दारकौ
वाल्मीकेरथ शिष्यौ हि ब्रूतामेवं नराधिपम्

yadi pṛcchetsa kākutstho yuvāṁ kasyeti dārakau
vālmīkeratha śiṣyau hi brūtāmevaṁ narādhipam
If Rama asks you about your father you may say, We are both disciples of the high souled Valmiki.

इमास्तन्त्रीः सुमधुराः स्थानं वा पूर्वदर्शितम्
मूर्छयित्वा सुमधुरं गायेतां विगतज्वरौ

imāstantrīḥ sumadhurāḥ sthānaṁ vā pūrvadarśitam
mūrchayitvā sumadhuraṁ gāyetāṁ vigatajvarau
O Kusa and Lava, in your proper mood do you sing the sweet song with charming Murchana accompanied by the sweet notes of Vina.

आदिप्रभृति गेयं स्यान्न चावज्ञाय पार्थिवम्
पिता हि सर्वभूतानां राजा भवति धर्मतः

ādiprabhṛti geyaṁ syānna cāvajñāya pārthivam
pitā hi sarvabhūtānāṁ rājā bhavati dharmataḥ
Before you begin with the song, without disregarding the king, do you bow to him reverentially. Morally the king is the father of all.

तद्युवां हृष्टमनसौ श्वः प्रभाते समाधिना
गायेतां मधुरं गेयं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम्

tadyuvāṁ hṛṣṭamanasau śvaḥ prabhāte samādhinā
gāyetāṁ madhuraṁ geyaṁ tantrīlayasamanvitam
Do you therefore both, delightedly and with a collected mind, early in the morning, sing the theme in a sweet voice and accompanied by the music of the stringed instrument.

इति संदिश्य बहुशो मुनिः प्राचेतसस्तदा
वाल्मीकिः परमोदारस्तूष्णीमासीन्महायशाः

iti saṁdiśya bahuśo muniḥ prācetasastadā
vālmīkiḥ paramodārastūṣṇīmāsīnmahāyaśāḥ
Having in this wise given counsels, the highly generous and great ascetic Valmiki, son of Praceta, became silent.

तामद्भुतां तौ हृदये कुमारौ; निवेश्य वाणीमृषिभाषितां शुभाम्
समुत्सुकौ तौ सुखमूषतुर्निशां; यथाश्विनौ भार्गवनीतिसंस्कृतौ

tāmadbhutāṁ tau hṛdaye kumārau; niveśya vāṇīmṛṣibhāṣitāṁ śubhām
samutsukau tau sukhamūṣaturniśāṁ; yathāśvinau bhārgavanītisaṁskṛtau
Like to the two Asvins following the moral precepts of Sukra, the two princes, placing those wonderful counsels of Valmiki in their minds, spent the night with a heart stricken with curiosity.

तौ रजन्यां प्रभातायां स्नातौ हुतहुताशनौ
यथोक्तमृषिणा पूर्वं तत्र तत्राभ्यगायताम्

tau rajanyāṁ prabhātāyāṁ snātau hutahutāśanau
yathoktamṛṣiṇā pūrvaṁ tatra tatrābhyagāyatām
There upon the night being over, having bathed and performed the Homa; both Lava and Kusa, in consonance with Rsi's command, began the song.

प्रमाणैर्बहुभिर्बद्धां तन्त्रीलयसमन्विताम्
बालाभ्यां राघवः श्रुत्वा कौतूहलपरोऽभवत्

pramāṇairbahubhirbaddhāṁ tantrīlayasamanvitām
bālābhyāṁ rāghavaḥ śrutvā kautūhalaparo'bhavat

That song was composed by the first preceptor (Valmiki) never heard of before, consisting of sounds originating from six places, containing all metres, many proofs and set in accompaniment with the music of a stringed instrument. Hearing such a song from the boys Rama was stricken with curiosity.

जटिलौ यदि न स्यातां न वल्कलधरौ यदि
विशेषं नाधिगच्छामो गायतो राघवस्य च

jaṭilau yadi na syātāṁ na valkaladharau yadi
viśeṣaṁ nādhigacchāmo gāyato rāghavasya ca

And they all attentively said to one anotherBoth of them take after Rama, like to a bubble resembling the one it rises from. There would not have been perceived the least difference between them and Rama had they not been clothed in dark and used clotted hair. The citizens and villagers speaking thus with one another Kusa and Lava chanted twenty sections beginning from the first, pointed out by Narada.

ततोऽपराह्णसमये राघवः समभाषत
श्रुत्वा विंशतिसर्गांस्तान्भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलः

tato'parāhṇasamaye rāghavaḥ samabhāṣata
śrutvā viṁśatisargāṁstānbharataṁ bhrātṛvatsalaḥ

Having heard up to twentieth section, Rama, fond of his brother, said to Laksmana in the afternoon, O Kakutstha, do you soon confer upon these two high-souled ones eighteen thousand gold coins and all other-things they wish for.

तस्य चैवागमं रामः काव्यस्य श्रोतुमुत्सुकः
पप्रच्छ तौ महातेजास्तावुभौ मुनिदारकौ

tasya caivāgamaṁ rāmaḥ kāvyasya śrotumutsukaḥ
papraccha tau mahātejāstāvubhau munidārakau

Hearing those words of them, Rama and the audience were greatly worked up with curiosity and surprise. There upon being anxious to learn of the origin of the poem, the highly effulgent Rama asked the two Muni boys, saying. What is the proof of the story of this poem?

किंप्रमाणमिदं काव्यं का प्रतिष्ठा महात्मनः
कर्ता काव्यस्य महतः को वासौ मुनिपुंगवः

kiṁpramāṇamidaṁ kāvyaṁ kā pratiṣṭhā mahātmanaḥ
kartā kāvyasya mahataḥ ko vāsau munipuṁgavaḥ
How great is his fame who has composed it? What leading ascetic is the author of this great poem?

पृच्छन्तं राघवं वाक्यमूचतुर्मुनिदारकौ
वाल्मीकिर्भगवान्कर्ता संप्राप्तो यज्ञसंनिधिम्
येनेदं चरितं तुभ्यमशेषं संप्रदर्शितम्

pṛcchantaṁ rāghavaṁ vākyamūcaturmunidārakau
vālmīkirbhagavānkartā saṁprāpto yajñasaṁnidhim
yenedaṁ caritaṁ tubhyamaśeṣaṁ saṁpradarśitam
Rama having thus asked them those two Muni boys said: The illustrious Valmiki is the author of this poem. He has described in this poem your endless story. He has of late come to your sacrifice.

यदि बुद्धिः कृता राजञ्श्रवणाय महारथ
कर्मान्तरे क्षणी हूतस्तच्छृणुष्व सहानुजः

yadi buddhiḥ kṛtā rājañśravaṇāya mahāratha
karmāntare kṣaṇī hūtastacchṛṇuṣva sahānujaḥ
O mighty car-warrior, o king, if you do wish to hear the whole of it, do you, at your leisure, hear it delightedly in the company of your younger brother.

बाढमित्यब्रवीद्रामस्तौ चानुज्ञाप्य राघवम्
प्रहृष्टौ जग्मतुर्वासं यत्रासौ मुनिपुंगवः

bāḍhamityabravīdrāmastau cānujñāpya rāghavam
prahṛṣṭau jagmaturvāsaṁ yatrāsau munipuṁgavaḥ
Saying 'so it shall be' Rama bade them adieu and they too, delighted, repaired to where Valmiki, the foremost of Munis was.

रामोऽपि मुनिभिः सार्धं पार्थिवैश्च महात्मभिः
श्रुत्वा तद्गीतमाधुर्यं कर्मशालामुपागमत्

rāmo'pi munibhiḥ sārdhaṁ pārthivaiśca mahātmabhiḥ
śrutvā tadgītamādhuryaṁ karmaśālāmupāgamat
There upon having heard that charming song in the company of ascetics and kings the highminded Rama repaired to the place of business.

रामो बहून्यहान्येव तद्गीतं परमाद्भुतम्
शुश्राव मुनिभिः सार्धं राजभिः सह वानरैः

rāmo bahūnyahānyeva tadgītaṁ paramādbhutam
śuśrāva munibhiḥ sārdhaṁ rājabhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
Rama heard that highly sacred theme for many long days in the company of ascetics, kings and Vanaras.

तस्मिन्गीते तु विज्ञाय सीतापुत्रौ कुशीलवौ
तस्याः परिषदो मध्ये रामो वचनमब्रवीत्

tasmingīte tu vijñāya sītāputrau kuśīlavau
tasyāḥ pariṣado madhye rāmo vacanamabravīt

And understanding from the story that Kusa and Lava were Janaki's sons, Rama mentioning her name said before the assembly:-Send a good emissary to the illustrious Valmiki and let him communicate to the ascetics that if Janaki is sinless and has lead a pure life in the forest; let her give proof of purity by the great ascetic's permission.

छन्दं मुनेस्तु विज्ञाय सीतायाश्च मनोगतम्
प्रत्ययं दातुकामायास्ततः शंसत मे लघु

chandaṁ munestu vijñāya sītāyāśca manogatam
pratyayaṁ dātukāmāyāstataḥ śaṁsata me laghu
Let the emissaries learn well the intention of the ascetic in this and if Sita is at heart willing to bring in proofs.

श्वः प्रभाते तु शपथं मैथिली जनकात्मजा
करोतु परिषन्मध्ये शोधनार्थं ममेह च

śvaḥ prabhāte tu śapathaṁ maithilī janakātmajā
karotu pariṣanmadhye śodhanārthaṁ mameha ca
To uphold her as well as mine purity, let Maithili, the daughter of Janaka, swear before the assembly in the morning of the next day.

ते प्रणम्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तममितप्रभम्
ऊचुस्ते रामवाक्यानि मृदूनि मधुराणि च

te praṇamya mahātmānaṁ jvalantamamitaprabham
ūcuste rāmavākyāni mṛdūni madhurāṇi ca

Hearing the words of Rania, messengers went to Valmiki and saluting the high-souled (ascetic) burning in his effulgence and of incomparable lustre, communicated to him, in sweet words all what Rama had said.

तेषां तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामस्य च मनोगतम्
विज्ञाय सुमहातेजा मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्

teṣāṁ tadbhāṣitaṁ śrutvā rāmasya ca manogatam
vijñāya sumahātejā munirvākyamathābravīt
Hearing the words of the messengers and understanding Rama's intention the ascetic said.

एवं भवतु भद्रं वो यथा तुष्यति राघवः
तथा करिष्यते सीता दैवतं हि पतिः स्त्रियाः

evaṁ bhavatu bhadraṁ vo yathā tuṣyati rāghavaḥ
tathā kariṣyate sītā daivataṁ hi patiḥ striyāḥ
What Rama has said shall be satisfied. May good betide you. Husband is the greatest god for women. So SIta shall carry out his behests.

तथोक्ता मुनिना सर्वे रामदूता महौजसः
प्रत्येत्य राघवं सर्वे मुनिवाक्यं बभाषिरे

tathoktā muninā sarve rāmadūtā mahaujasaḥ
pratyetya rāghavaṁ sarve munivākyaṁ babhāṣire
The great ascetic having said this, the highly powerful emissaries, approaching Rama, communicated to him what the Muni had said.

ततः प्रहृष्टः काकुत्स्थः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं महात्मनः
ऋषींस्तत्र समेतांश्च राज्ञश्चैवाभ्यभाषत

tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ kākutsthaḥ śrutvā vākyaṁ mahātmanaḥ
ṛṣīṁstatra sametāṁśca rājñaścaivābhyabhāṣata
Hearing the words of the high-souled Valmiki, Rama was greatly delighted. Having addressed the assembled Rsis and kings he said.

भगवन्तः सशिष्या वै सानुगाश्च नराधिपाः
पश्यन्तु सीताशपथं यश्चैवान्योऽभिकाङ्क्षते

bhagavantaḥ saśiṣyā vai sānugāśca narādhipāḥ
paśyantu sītāśapathaṁ yaścaivānyo'bhikāṅkṣate
The Rsis with their disciples, and the kings with their followers and all others willing shall see Sita swear here.

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः
सर्वेषामृषिमुख्यानां साधुवादो महानभूत्

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
sarveṣāmṛṣimukhyānāṁ sādhuvādo mahānabhūt
Hearing the words of the high-souled Rama, all the high-souled Rsis began to speak of him in high terms and said.

राजानश्च महात्मानः प्रशंसन्ति स्म राघवम्
उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ त्वय्येव भुवि नान्यतः

rājānaśca mahātmānaḥ praśaṁsanti sma rāghavam
upapannaṁ naraśreṣṭha tvayyeva bhuvi nānyataḥ
O foremost of men, such an action becomes you not any one else.

एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा श्वोभूत इति राघवः
विसर्जयामास तदा सर्वांस्ताञ्शत्रुसूदनः

evaṁ viniścayaṁ kṛtvā śvobhūta iti rāghavaḥ
visarjayāmāsa tadā sarvāṁstāñśatrusūdanaḥ
There upon having settled that Sita would swear next day, Rama, the slayer of enemies, dismissed them all.

तथा समागतं सर्वमश्वभूतमिवाचलम्
श्रुत्वा मुनिवरस्तूर्णं ससीतः समुपागमत्

tathā samāgataṁ sarvamaśvabhūtamivācalam
śrutvā munivarastūrṇaṁ sasītaḥ samupāgamat

Besides thousands and thousands of Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, sadras and Brahmanas of firm tenancies, also hailed there from various parts to witness Sita's trial. Having arrived there they all sat down motionless like mountains. There upon, Valmiki, the foremost of ascetics, speedily came there accompanied by Sita.

तां दृष्ट्वा श्रीमिवायान्तीं ब्रह्माणमनुगामिनीम्
वाल्मीकेः पृष्ठतः सीतां साधुकारो महानभूत्

tāṁ dṛṣṭvā śrīmivāyāntīṁ brahmāṇamanugāminīm
vālmīkeḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sītāṁ sādhukāro mahānabhūt

With her face downwards, folded palms, eyes full of tears and meditating upon Rama in her mind, Sita, following the Rsis, came before the assembly. There arose a great uproar of eulogy from the assembly when they saw Sita following Valmiki like to the Sruti following Brahma.

ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वेषामेवमाबभौ
दुःखजेन विशालेन शोकेनाकुलितात्मनाम्

tato halahalāśabdaḥ sarveṣāmevamābabhau
duḥkhajena viśālena śokenākulitātmanām
There upon members, stricken with sorrow, made a tumultuous sound. Among the visitors some praised Rama, some praised $ita and others eulogised both of them.

ततो मध्यं जनौघानां प्रविश्य मुनिपुंगवः
सीतासहायो वाल्मीकिरिति होवाच राघवम्

tato madhyaṁ janaughānāṁ praviśya munipuṁgavaḥ
sītāsahāyo vālmīkiriti hovāca rāghavam

There upon having entered that huge assemblage in company of Sita, the great ascetic Valmiki addressed Rama, saying: O son of Dasaratha, in fear of calumny, you did renounce her near my hermitage, albeit Sita is pure and follows the ways of morality.

लोकापवादभीतस्य तव राम महाव्रत
प्रत्ययं दास्यते सीता तामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि

lokāpavādabhītasya tava rāma mahāvrata
pratyayaṁ dāsyate sītā tāmanujñātumarhasi

O Rama of firm vows, you are afraid of the censure of the people. Sita has becoming willing to give testimony (of her purity) for removing the calumny of the public; do you mercifully give her permission in this.

इमौ च जानकीपुत्रावुभौ च यमजातकौ
सुतौ तवैव दुर्धर्षौ सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते

imau ca jānakīputrāvubhau ca yamajātakau
sutau tavaiva durdharṣau satyametadbravīmi te

I tell you the truth, O Rama, that these irrepressible twin brothers are your sons, O descendant of Raghu. I am the tenth son of Praceta, so, far from speaking untruth it does not even spring up in my mind. I therefore know the truth that these twins are your sons.

बहुवर्षसहस्राणि तपश्चर्या मया कृता
तस्याः फलमुपाश्नीयामपापा मैथिली यथा

bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi tapaścaryā mayā kṛtā
tasyāḥ phalamupāśnīyāmapāpā maithilī yathā

I have performed austere penances for many thousand years; I now swear before you, that if this Maithili is found touched by any sin I shall not reap the fruit of my ascetic observances extending over many thousand years.

अहं पञ्चसु भूतेषु मनःषष्ठेषु राघव
विचिन्त्य सीतां शुद्धेति न्यगृह्णां वननिर्झरे

ahaṁ pañcasu bhūteṣu manaḥṣaṣṭheṣu rāghava
vicintya sītāṁ śuddheti nyagṛhṇāṁ vananirjhare
O descendant of Raghu, finding Sita pure in mind and five elements of body I took her near the spring in the forest.

इयं शुद्धसमाचारा अपापा पतिदेवता
लोकापवादभीतस्य दास्यति प्रत्ययं तव

iyaṁ śuddhasamācārā apāpā patidevatā
lokāpavādabhītasya dāsyati pratyayaṁ tava
Besides this Sita, of pure ways, divested of sins and ever considering her husband as deity, shall give testimony this day.

वाल्मीकिनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः प्रत्यभाषत
प्राञ्जलिर्जगतो मध्ये दृष्ट्वा तां देववर्णिनीम्

vālmīkinaivamuktastu rāghavaḥ pratyabhāṣata
prāñjalirjagato madhye dṛṣṭvā tāṁ devavarṇinīm
After the great Rsis Valmiki had said this, Rama, on beholding the daughter of Janaka resembling a celestial, in the midst of the assembly, with folded hands, said.

एवमेतन्महाभाग यथा वदसि धर्मवित्
प्रत्ययो हि मम ब्रह्मंस्तव वाक्यैरकल्मषैः

evametanmahābhāga yathā vadasi dharmavit
pratyayo hi mama brahmaṁstava vākyairakalmaṣaiḥ

O great one, you are conversant with piety. By your words shorn of sin, I have been convinced that Janaki is of pure ways. Still, O Brahmana, what you have commanded shall be carried out; let Sita produce testimony of the purity of her character.

प्रत्ययो हि पुरा दत्तो वैदेह्या सुरसंनिधौ
सेयं लोकभयाद्ब्रह्मन्नपापेत्यभिजानता
परित्यक्ता मया सीता तद्भवान्क्षन्तुमर्हति

pratyayo hi purā datto vaidehyā surasaṁnidhau
seyaṁ lokabhayādbrahmannapāpetyabhijānatā
parityaktā mayā sītā tadbhavānkṣantumarhati
O Brahmana, vilification of the people is very powerful. Although I know that Janaki has not been touched by any sin still I have renounced her. Do you therefore forgive me.

जानामि चेमौ पुत्रौ मे यमजातौ कुशीलवौ
शुद्धायां जगतो मध्ये मैथिल्यां प्रीतिरस्तु मे

jānāmi cemau putrau me yamajātau kuśīlavau
śuddhāyāṁ jagato madhye maithilyāṁ prītirastu me
I know that these twin brothers Kusa and Lava are my sons. Yet if Janaki gives evidence of her own purity before the assembly I shall be greatly satisfied.

अभिप्रायं तु विज्ञाय रामस्य सुरसत्तमाः
पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य सर्व एव समागताः

abhiprāyaṁ tu vijñāya rāmasya surasattamāḥ
pitāmahaṁ puraskṛtya sarva eva samāgatāḥ
Being apprised of Rama's intention as to Sita's trial the celestials all came there on the occasion.

आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा विश्वेदेवा मरुद्गणाः
अश्विनावृषिगन्धर्वा अप्सराणां गणास्तथा
साध्याश्च देवाः सर्वे ते सर्वे च परमर्षयः

ādityā vasavo rudrā viśvedevā marudgaṇāḥ
aśvināvṛṣigandharvā apsarāṇāṁ gaṇāstathā
sādhyāśca devāḥ sarve te sarve ca paramarṣayaḥ
The Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Visvadeva, Maruts, Sadhyas, Siddhas, Nagas, and Rsis placing Brahma before them, all came there.

तदद्भुतमिवाचिन्त्यं निरीक्षन्ते समाहिताः
मानवाः सर्वराष्ट्रेभ्यः पूर्वं कृतयुगे यथा

tadadbhutamivācintyaṁ nirīkṣante samāhitāḥ
mānavāḥ sarvarāṣṭrebhyaḥ pūrvaṁ kṛtayuge yathā

As soon as those words were uttered, sweet, fragrant, cold air, the witness of virtue and vice, blowing mildly, excited the joy of the assembly. People, hailing from various countries, with all attention began to witness this wondrous and unthought of event. In the golden age only the celestial wind used to blow, and it now blew even in the Treta Yuga and forsooth it was a matter of exceeding surprise.

सर्वान्समागतान्दृष्ट्वा सीता काषायवासिनी
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमधोदृष्टिरवाङ्मुखी

sarvānsamāgatāndṛṣṭvā sītā kāṣāyavāsinī
abravītprāñjalirvākyamadhodṛṣṭiravāṅmukhī
There upon beholding all people assembled there, Janaka's daughter, wearing a red cloth, with her face and looks downwards and folded palms said.

यथाहं राघवादन्यं मनसापि न चिन्तये
तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति

yathāhaṁ rāghavādanyaṁ manasāpi na cintaye
tathā me mādhavī devī vivaraṁ dātumarhati
I have never thought of any other person in my mind but Rama; by the strength of this virtue let the goddess Vasundhara give me room.

तथा शपन्त्यां वैदेह्यां प्रादुरासीत्तदद्भुतम्
भूतलादुत्थितं दिव्यं सिंहासनमनुत्तमम्

tathā śapantyāṁ vaidehyāṁ prādurāsīttadadbhutam
bhūtalādutthitaṁ divyaṁ siṁhāsanamanuttamam
As soon as Sita swore in this wise a wonderful incident took place. From inside the earth a celestial and excellent throne rose up.

ध्रियमाणं शिरोभिस्तन्नागैरमितविक्रमैः
दिव्यं दिव्येन वपुषा सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्

dhriyamāṇaṁ śirobhistannāgairamitavikramaiḥ
divyaṁ divyena vapuṣā sarvaratnavibhūṣitam
It was carried on head by the Nagas of unmitigated prowess, having celestial persons and adorned with celestial jewels and ornaments.

तस्मिंस्तु धरणी देवी बाहुभ्यां गृह्य मैथिलीम्
स्वागतेनाभिनन्द्यैनामासने चोपवेषयत्

tasmiṁstu dharaṇī devī bāhubhyāṁ gṛhya maithilīm
svāgatenābhinandyaināmāsane copaveṣayat
Having stretched out her arms and taken Maithili, the goddess earth welcomed her and placed her on the throne.

तामासनगतां दृष्ट्वा प्रविशन्तीं रसातलम्
पुष्पवृष्टिरविच्छिन्ना दिव्या सीतामवाकिरत्

tāmāsanagatāṁ dṛṣṭvā praviśantīṁ rasātalam
puṣpavṛṣṭiravicchinnā divyā sītāmavākirat
And while seated on the throne she was entering the earth, she was covered with the continued showers of celestial flowers.

साधुकारश्च सुमहान्देवानां सहसोत्थितः
साधु साध्विति वै सीते यस्यास्ते शीलमीदृशम्

sādhukāraśca sumahāndevānāṁ sahasotthitaḥ
sādhu sādhviti vai sīte yasyāste śīlamīdṛśam

Eulogising her at that time, the celestials said: Oh! highly praiseworthy is your conduct, O Sita. Being present in the welkin and beholding Sita enter into the Earth, the celestials again and again eulogised her in various words.

यज्ञवाटगताश्चापि मुनयः सर्व एव ते
राजानश्च नरव्याघ्रा विस्मयान्नोपरेमिरे

yajñavāṭagatāścāpi munayaḥ sarva eva te
rājānaśca naravyāghrā vismayānnoparemire
The Rsis, kings and other leading men present in the sacrificial arena repeatedly expressed their surprise.

अन्तरिक्षे च भूमौ च सर्वे स्थावरजङ्गमाः
दानवाश्च महाकायाः पाताले पन्नगाधिपाः

antarikṣe ca bhūmau ca sarve sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ
dānavāśca mahākāyāḥ pātāle pannagādhipāḥ
Beholding Sita's censure thus removed all animals, animate or inanimate, either on earth or in the sky, were greatly delighted.

केचिद्विनेदुः संहृष्टाः केचिद्ध्यानपरायणाः
केचिद्रामं निरीक्षन्ते केचित्सीतामचेतनाः

kecidvineduḥ saṁhṛṣṭāḥ keciddhyānaparāyaṇāḥ
kecidrāmaṁ nirīkṣante kecitsītāmacetanāḥ
Some cried aloud in joy, some remained silent, and some motionless espied Rama or Sita.

सीताप्रवेशनं दृष्ट्वा तेषामासीत्समागमः
तं मुहूर्तमिवात्यर्थं सर्वं संमोहितं जगत्

sītāpraveśanaṁ dṛṣṭvā teṣāmāsītsamāgamaḥ
taṁ muhūrtamivātyarthaṁ sarvaṁ saṁmohitaṁ jagat

In this wise beholding Sita's entrance into the Earth the ascetics were greatly delighted. They all attaining to the same state of mind, the whole universe, for a moment, was possessed with the state of equality.

तदावसाने यज्ञस्य रामः परमदुर्मनाः
अपश्यमानो वैदेहीं मेने शून्यमिदं जगत्
शोकेन परमायत्तो न शान्तिं मनसागमत्

tadāvasāne yajñasya rāmaḥ paramadurmanāḥ
apaśyamāno vaidehīṁ mene śūnyamidaṁ jagat
śokena paramāyatto na śāntiṁ manasāgamat
In Janaki's absence the whuic orld appeared to him as blank. Now being overwhelmed with grief he lost all mental peace.

ततो विसृज्य तान्सर्वान्रामो राजीवलोचनः
हृदि कृत्वा तदा सीतामयोध्यां प्रविवेश सः

tato visṛjya tānsarvānrāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
hṛdi kṛtvā tadā sītāmayodhyāṁ praviveśa saḥ
Having conferred various gifts upon the kings, Raksasas, monkeys and leading Brahmanas, Rama sent them away and meditating upon Sita's absence entered Ayodhya.

न सीतायाः परां भार्यां वव्रे स रघुनन्दनः
यज्ञे यज्ञे च पत्न्यर्थं जानकी काञ्चनी भवत्

na sītāyāḥ parāṁ bhāryāṁ vavre sa raghunandanaḥ
yajñe yajñe ca patnyarthaṁ jānakī kāñcanī bhavat
And from the time of Sita's entering into Patala he did not take any other spouse. And having made a golden image of Sita he engage in the performance of various sacrifices.

अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां गोसवैश्च महाधनैः
ईजे क्रतुभिरन्यैश्च स श्रीमानाप्तदक्षिणैः

agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṁ gosavaiśca mahādhanaiḥ
īje kratubhiranyaiśca sa śrīmānāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
In this wise for thousand years he celebrated many Horse-sacrifices, many Vajapeyas with profuse gold, Agnistomas, Atiratras, numberless Gomedhas and various other sacrifices.

एवं स कालः सुमहान्राज्यस्थस्य महात्मनः
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य व्यतीयाद्राघवस्य तु

evaṁ sa kālaḥ sumahānrājyasthasya mahātmanaḥ
dharme prayatamānasya vyatīyādrāghavasya tu
Rama being engaged in governing the kingdom and performing many pious rites long time passed away.

ऋक्षवानररक्षांसि स्थिता रामस्य शासने
अनुरज्यन्ति राजानो अहन्यहनि राघवम्

ṛkṣavānararakṣāṁsi sthitā rāmasya śāsane
anurajyanti rājāno ahanyahani rāghavam
And being under his subjection, bears monkeys, Raksasa and kings always afforded delight to him.

काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः सुभिक्षं विमला दिशः
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णं पुरं जनपदस्तथा

kāle varṣati parjanyaḥ subhikṣaṁ vimalā diśaḥ
hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇaṁ puraṁ janapadastathā
On account of showers in proper time there was enough of food in his kingdom. The quarters were pure and delightful. The citizens and villagers were happy and healthy.

नाकाले म्रियते कश्चिन्न व्याधिः प्राणिनां तदा
नाधर्मश्चाभवत्कश्चिद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति

nākāle mriyate kaścinna vyādhiḥ prāṇināṁ tadā
nādharmaścābhavatkaścidrāme rājyaṁ praśāsati
None met with premature death. In fact, in his regime all calamities were removed.

अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राममाता यशस्विनी
पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृता कालधर्ममुपागमत्

atha dīrghasya kālasya rāmamātā yaśasvinī
putrapautraiḥ parivṛtā kāladharmamupāgamat
There upon after many years, the illustrious, Kausalya, Rama's mother, surrounded by her sons and grand-sons, breathed her last.

अन्वियाय सुमित्रापि कैकेयी च यशस्विनी
धर्मं कृत्वा बहुविधं त्रिदिवे पर्यवस्थिता

anviyāya sumitrāpi kaikeyī ca yaśasvinī
dharmaṁ kṛtvā bahuvidhaṁ tridive paryavasthitā

Performing many pious observances Kaikayi followed her and obtained peace in the land of immortals. Those noble ladies, being united with the king Dasaratha, in heaven, were greatly delighted and obtained all virtues.

तासां रामो महादानं काले काले प्रयच्छति
मातॄणामविशेषेण ब्राह्मणेषु तपस्विषु

tāsāṁ rāmo mahādānaṁ kāle kāle prayacchati
mātṝṇāmaviśeṣeṇa brāhmaṇeṣu tapasviṣu

Besides, having worshipped the deities and manes on the occasion of his father's Sradha ceremony the high-souled Rama distributed many jewels and engaged in the performance of a very difficult sacrifice.

कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य युधाजित्केकयो नृपः
स्वगुरुं प्रेषयामास राघवाय महात्मने

kasyacittvatha kālasya yudhājitkekayo nṛpaḥ
svaguruṁ preṣayāmāsa rāghavāya mahātmane

Once on a time Yudhajit, the king of Kekaya, sent to the high-souled Rama, Gargya— son of his own preceptor Angiras-a Brahmana saint of unmitigated prowess; and with him he sent, as tokens of affections, gifts of ten thousand horses, numberless blankets various jewels, diverse clothes and well washed coverlets.

प्रत्युद्गम्य च काकुत्स्थः क्रोशमात्रं सहानुगः
गार्ग्यं संपूजयामास धनं तत्प्रतिगृह्य च

pratyudgamya ca kākutsthaḥ krośamātraṁ sahānugaḥ
gārgyaṁ saṁpūjayāmāsa dhanaṁ tatpratigṛhya ca

Hearing of the arrival of the great saint Gargya with above valuable presents sent by his maternal uncle Yudhajit, the intelligent Rama, with his brothers, proceeded about a Krosa to receive him and adored him particularly likely to the lord of celestials honouring Bihaspati.

किमाह मातुलो वाक्यं यदर्थं भगवानिह
प्राप्तो वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठ साक्षादिव बृहस्पतिः

kimāha mātulo vākyaṁ yadarthaṁ bhagavāniha
prāpto vākyavidāṁ śreṣṭha sākṣādiva bṛhaspatiḥ

Having thus welcomed that foremost of Rsis and accepted the valuable presents sent by his maternal uncle he asked the ascetic about his welfare in every thing. There upon the great Rsis being seated, he said. You are the foremost of those skilled in the are of speech like the very preceptor of the celestials. Since your own self has here My uncle must have commissioned you with a very important message.

मातुलस्ते महाबाहो वाक्यमाह नरर्षभ
युधाजित्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं श्रूयतां यदि रोचते

mātulaste mahābāho vākyamāha nararṣabha
yudhājitprītisaṁyuktaṁ śrūyatāṁ yadi rocate

Hearing those words of Rama the great saint communicated to him the object of his coming, saying. O you having long arms, if you do like, hear what loving words your maternal uncle Yudhajit, the foremost of men, has said.

तं च रक्षन्ति गन्धर्वाः सायुधा युद्धकोविदाः
शैलूषस्य सुता वीरास्तिस्रः कोट्यो महाबलाः

taṁ ca rakṣanti gandharvāḥ sāyudhā yuddhakovidāḥ
śailūṣasya sutā vīrāstisraḥ koṭyo mahābalāḥ

The Gandharvas, holding weapons and expert in warfare, guard that beautiful province abounding in fruits and roots on the banks of the come river Sindhu. O hero, those Gandharvas are highly powerful and three kotis in number.

तान्विनिर्जित्य काकुत्स्थ गन्धर्वविषयं शुभम्
निवेशय महाबाहो द्वे पुरे सुसमाहितः

tānvinirjitya kākutstha gandharvaviṣayaṁ śubham
niveśaya mahābāho dve pure susamāhitaḥ

Having hoisted your flag of victory and conquered that highly picturesque city of Gandharvas do you include that kingdom within your well-established territories. None can enter there. O you having long arms, I do not request you for any harm of you. Let that highly charming country be liked by you.

तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवः प्रीतो महर्षेर्मातुलस्य च
उवाच बाढमित्येवं भरतं चान्ववैक्षत

tacchrutvā rāghavaḥ prīto maharṣermātulasya ca
uvāca bāḍhamityevaṁ bharataṁ cānvavaikṣata
Hearing the words of the maternal uncle communicated by the great saint, Rama, with delight, said.

निवेश्य ते पुरवरे आत्माजौ संनिवेश्य च
आगमिष्यति मे भूयः सकाशमतिधार्मिकः

niveśya te puravare ātmājau saṁniveśya ca
āgamiṣyati me bhūyaḥ sakāśamatidhārmikaḥ
Having established two kingdoms and installed his two sons there Bharata, the foremost of the pious, shall come back to me.

ब्रह्मर्षिमेवमुक्त्वा तु भरतं सबलानुगम्
आज्ञापयामास तदा कुमारौ चाभ्यषेचयत्

brahmarṣimevamuktvā tu bharataṁ sabalānugam
ājñāpayāmāsa tadā kumārau cābhyaṣecayat
Having thus said to the Brahmarsi, Rama commanded Bharata and welcomed the two princes.

नक्षत्रेण च सौम्येन पुरस्कृत्याङ्गिरः सुतम्
भरतः सह सैन्येन कुमाराभ्यां च निर्ययौ

nakṣatreṇa ca saumyena puraskṛtyāṅgiraḥ sutam
bharataḥ saha sainyena kumārābhyāṁ ca niryayau
There upon under the auspices of favourable stars, having placed Gargya, son of Aigiras before them, Bharata with the princes and army issued out of the city of Ayodhya.

सा सेना शक्रयुक्तेव नरगान्निर्ययावथ
राघवानुगता दूरं दुराधर्षा सुरासुरैः

sā senā śakrayukteva naragānniryayāvatha
rāghavānugatā dūraṁ durādharṣā surāsuraiḥ
Rama's army unconquerable even by the celestials went out from the city like a celestial host under the command of Indra.

मांसाशीनि च सत्त्वानि रक्षांसि सुमहान्ति च
अनुजग्मुश्च भरतं रुधिरस्य पिपासया

māṁsāśīni ca sattvāni rakṣāṁsi sumahānti ca
anujagmuśca bharataṁ rudhirasya pipāsayā
Animals, living upon flesh and huge-bodied Raksasas longing for blood and many terrible and dreadful carnivorous creatures followed Bharata wishing the flesh of Gandharvas.

भूतग्रामाश्च बहवो मांसभक्षाः सुदारुणाः
गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि भोक्तुकामाः सहस्रशः

bhūtagrāmāśca bahavo māṁsabhakṣāḥ sudāruṇāḥ
gandharvaputramāṁsāni bhoktukāmāḥ sahasraśaḥ
Animals, living upon flesh and huge-bodied Raksasas longing for blood and many terrible and dreadful carnivorous creatures followed Bharata wishing the flesh of Gandharvas.

सिंहव्याघ्रसृगालानां खेचराणां च पक्षिणाम्
बहूनि वै सहस्राणि सेनाया ययुरग्रतः

siṁhavyāghrasṛgālānāṁ khecarāṇāṁ ca pakṣiṇām
bahūni vai sahasrāṇi senāyā yayuragrataḥ
Besides many thousand birds, moving in the sky, lions, tigers and boars went before the army.

अध्यर्धमासमुषिता पथि सेना निरामया
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा केकयं समुपागमत्

adhyardhamāsamuṣitā pathi senā nirāmayā
hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā kekayaṁ samupāgamat
The army, consisting of delighted and healthy subjects spending half a month in the way, arrived at the Kekaya kingdom in good health. commanded Bharata and welcomed the two princes.

श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः
युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत्

śrutvā senāpatiṁ prāptaṁ bharataṁ kekayādhipaḥ
yudhājidgārgyasahitaṁ parāṁ prītimupāgamat
Hearing of the arrival of the Bharata with the army Gargya and Yudhajit, the king of Kekayas, were greatly delighted.

स निर्ययौ जनौघेन महता केकयाधिपः
त्वरमाणोऽभिचक्राम गन्धर्वान्देवरूपिणः

sa niryayau janaughena mahatā kekayādhipaḥ
tvaramāṇo'bhicakrāma gandharvāndevarūpiṇaḥ
He, the king of Kekaya, with a huge army they speedily went out for conquering the Gandharvas.

भरतश्च युधाजिच्च समेतौ लघुविक्रमौ
गन्धर्वनगरं प्राप्तौ सबलौ सपदानुगौ

bharataśca yudhājicca sametau laghuvikramau
gandharvanagaraṁ prāptau sabalau sapadānugau
There upon the highly powerful and lightarmed Bharata and Yudhajit, with the soldiers and followers, arrived at the city of Gandharvas.

श्रुत्वा तु भरतं प्राप्तं गन्धर्वास्ते समागताः
योद्धुकामा महावीर्या विनदन्तः समन्ततः

śrutvā tu bharataṁ prāptaṁ gandharvāste samāgatāḥ
yoddhukāmā mahāvīryā vinadantaḥ samantataḥ
Having heard of the coming of Bharata the highly powerful Gandharvas gathered round and sent up leonine roars.

ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्
सप्तरात्रं महाभीमं न चान्यतरयोर्जयः

tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṁ tumulaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
saptarātraṁ mahābhīmaṁ na cānyatarayorjayaḥ
There upon began the battle capable of making down erect and continued for a week. On neither side there was victory or defeat.

ततो रामानुजः क्रुद्धः कालस्यास्त्रं सुदारुणम्
संवर्तं नाम भरतो गन्धर्वेष्वभ्ययोजयत्

tato rāmānujaḥ kruddhaḥ kālasyāstraṁ sudāruṇam
saṁvartaṁ nāma bharato gandharveṣvabhyayojayat
There upon enraged Bharata, Rama's younger brother, discharged a dreadful arrow named Samvarata resembling the fire of dissolution against Gandharvas.

ते बद्धाः कालपाशेन संवर्तेन विदारिताः
क्षणेनाभिहतास्तिस्रस्तत्र कोट्यो महात्मना

te baddhāḥ kālapāśena saṁvartena vidāritāḥ
kṣaṇenābhihatāstisrastatra koṭyo mahātmanā
Having bound them all with the noose of death and sundered them with Sangharata, Bharata despatched all the Gandharvas to the abode of death.

तं घातं घोरसंकाशं न स्मरन्ति दिवौकसः
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तादृशानां महात्मनाम्

taṁ ghātaṁ ghorasaṁkāśaṁ na smaranti divaukasaḥ
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tādṛśānāṁ mahātmanām

Even the celestials could not recollect if such a dreadful encounter had happened before. In a moment the huge Gandharva host was slain. After the destruction of the Gandharvas, Kaikeyi's son Bharata set up two excellent and prosperous cities in the province of Gandharva.

धनरत्नौघसंपूर्णो काननैरुपशोभिते
अन्योन्यसंघर्षकृते स्पर्धया गुणविस्तरे

dhanaratnaughasaṁpūrṇo kānanairupaśobhite
anyonyasaṁgharṣakṛte spardhayā guṇavistare
Both the cities were filled with profuse riches and jewels and covered with various gardens. As for many ornaments both of them as if vied with one another.

उभे सुरुचिरप्रख्ये व्यवहारैरकल्मषैः
उद्यानयानौघवृते सुविभक्तान्तरापणे

ubhe suruciraprakhye vyavahārairakalmaṣaiḥ
udyānayānaughavṛte suvibhaktāntarāpaṇe

By just purchases and sales, and by the conduct of the people the cities grew highly charming. Both of them were filled with gardens and conveyances. Rows of shops were well arranged by the streets in both the cities.

उभे पुरवरे रम्ये विस्तरैरुपशोभिते
गृहमुख्यैः सुरुचिरैर्विमानैः समवर्णिभिः

ubhe puravare ramye vistarairupaśobhite
gṛhamukhyaiḥ surucirairvimānaiḥ samavarṇibhiḥ
Both of them were adorned with many excellent fancy articles, picturesque houses, charming palaces and many beautiful and high Tala, Tamala, Tilaka and Vakula trees.

शोभिते शोभनीयैश्च देवायतनविस्तरैः
निवेश्य पञ्चभिर्वर्षैर्भरतो राघवानुजः
पुनरायान्महाबाहुरयोध्यां कैकयीसुतः

śobhite śobhanīyaiśca devāyatanavistaraiḥ
niveśya pañcabhirvarṣairbharato rāghavānujaḥ
punarāyānmahābāhurayodhyāṁ kaikayīsutaḥ
Having reared up those two cities within five years, Rama's younger brother, the mighty armed Bharata, son of Kaikeyl, returned to Ayodhya.?

सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवापरम्
राघवं भरतः श्रीमान्ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः

so'bhivādya mahātmānaṁ sākṣāddharmamivāparam
rāghavaṁ bharataḥ śrīmānbrahmāṇamiva vāsavaḥ

Like to Vasava saluting Brahma he adored the high-souled Raghava the very personation of virtue and communicated to him duly the destruction of the Gandharvas and the establishment of the two cities. And hearing the words of Bharata, Rama attained to an excess of delight. are

तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षमापेदे राघवो भ्रातृभिः सह
वाक्यं चाद्भुतसंकाशं भ्रातॄन्प्रोवाच राघवः

tacchrutvā harṣamāpede rāghavo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
vākyaṁ cādbhutasaṁkāśaṁ bhrātṝnprovāca rāghavaḥ
Hearing the wonderful words of Bharata both Rama and Laksmana were greatly delighted. And then Rama said to Laksmana.

इमौ कुमारौ सौमित्रे तव धर्मविशारदौ
अङ्गदश्चन्द्रकेतुश्च राज्यार्हौ दृढधन्विनौ

imau kumārau saumitre tava dharmaviśāradau
aṅgadaścandraketuśca rājyārhau dṛḍhadhanvinau
O Saumitri, your two sons, Angada and Candraketu well-versed in religions, perfectly qualified in governing the kingdom and highly powerful.

इमौ राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यामि देशः साधु विधीयताम्
रमणीयो ह्यसंबाधो रमेतां यत्र धन्विनौ

imau rājye'bhiṣekṣyāmi deśaḥ sādhu vidhīyatām
ramaṇīyo hyasaṁbādho rametāṁ yatra dhanvinau
I shall therefore install them on throne. O gentle man, do you find out such country where those two skilful archers may unobstructed roam about.

न राज्ञां यत्र पीदा स्यान्नाश्रमाणां विनाशनम्
स देशो दृश्यतां सौम्य नापराध्यामहे यथा

na rājñāṁ yatra pīdā syānnāśramāṇāṁ vināśanam
sa deśo dṛśyatāṁ saumya nāparādhyāmahe yathā
And where if a kingdom is established it might:not disturb the peace of hermitage and happiness of other kings.

तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह
अयं कारापथो देशः सुरमण्यो निरामयः

tathoktavati rāme tu bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha
ayaṁ kārāpatho deśaḥ suramaṇyo nirāmayaḥ
Rama, having finished his speech Bharata replied:-The country of Karupatha is highly picturesque and freed from all thorns.

निवेश्यतां तत्र पुरमङ्गदस्य महात्मनः
चन्द्रकेतोश्च रुचिरं चन्द्रकान्तं निरामयम्

niveśyatāṁ tatra puramaṅgadasya mahātmanaḥ
candraketośca ruciraṁ candrakāntaṁ nirāmayam
Let the city for high souled Angada be established there. And let the beautiful and healthy country of Candradkanta be the kingdom of Candraketu.

तद्वाक्यं भरतेनोक्तं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः
तं च कृत्वा वशे देशमङ्गदस्य न्यवेशयत्

tadvākyaṁ bharatenoktaṁ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ
taṁ ca kṛtvā vaśe deśamaṅgadasya nyaveśayat
Rama approved of the words of Bharata and having brought the country of Karupatha under his subjection gave it to Angada.

अङ्गदीया पुरी रम्या अङ्गदस्य निवेशिता
रमणीया सुगुप्ता च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा

aṅgadīyā purī ramyā aṅgadasya niveśitā
ramaṇīyā suguptā ca rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
He reared a beautiful and well-protected city for Angada.

चन्द्रकेतोस्तु मल्लस्य मल्लभूम्यां निवेशिता
चन्द्रकान्तेति विख्याता दिव्या स्वर्गपुरी यथा

candraketostu mallasya mallabhūmyāṁ niveśitā
candrakānteti vikhyātā divyā svargapurī yathā
And in the country of Malaya he reared a city for Candraketu, named Candrakanta highly picturesque and like to the city of celestials.

लक्ष्मणस्त्वङ्गदीयायां संवत्सरमथोषितः
पुत्रे स्थिते दुराधर्षे अयोध्यां पुनरागमत्

lakṣmaṇastvaṅgadīyāyāṁ saṁvatsaramathoṣitaḥ
putre sthite durādharṣe ayodhyāṁ punarāgamat
Having spent a year in Angada's city and finding his son well established in the kingdom Laksmana returned to Ayodhya.

भरतोऽपि तथैवोष्य संवत्सरमथाधिकम्
अयोध्यां पुनरागम्य रामपादावुपागमत्

bharato'pi tathaivoṣya saṁvatsaramathādhikam
ayodhyāṁ punarāgamya rāmapādāvupāgamat
And Bharata, according to his desire, having spent more than a year in the city of Candrakanta, came back to Ayodhya and saluted Rama's feet.

उभौ सौमित्रिभरतौ रामपादावनुव्रतौ
कालं गतमपि स्नेहान्न जज्ञातेऽतिधार्मिकौ

ubhau saumitribharatau rāmapādāvanuvratau
kālaṁ gatamapi snehānna jajñāte'tidhārmikau

The pious Laksmana and Bharata— both the brothers, were greatly attached to Rama; and though the spent their days in another place they did not experience any pain in consequence of separation from their sons.

एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तेषां ययुस्तदा
धर्मे प्रयतमानानां पौरकार्येषु नित्यदा

evaṁ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa teṣāṁ yayustadā
dharme prayatamānānāṁ paurakāryeṣu nityadā
Observing all virtues in this way, Rama, the foremost of the pious, Bharata and Laksmana governed the subjects for ten thousand years.

विहृत्य कालं परिपूर्णमानसाः; श्रिया वृता धर्मपथे परे स्थिताः
त्रयः समिद्धा इव दीप्ततेजसा; हुताग्नयः साधु महाध्वरे त्रयः

vihṛtya kālaṁ paripūrṇamānasāḥ; śriyā vṛtā dharmapathe pare sthitāḥ
trayaḥ samiddhā iva dīptatejasā; hutāgnayaḥ sādhu mahādhvare trayaḥ

Having spent their days in the city of Ayodhya, the very city of virtue, the three brothers, appearing graceful like the burning fire receiving oblations in a great sacrifice, attained to joy in the fullness of time.

कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य रामे धर्मपथे स्थिते
कालस्तापसरूपेण राजद्वारमुपागमत्

kasyacittvatha kālasya rāme dharmapathe sthite
kālastāpasarūpeṇa rājadvāramupāgamat
In this wise the virtuous Rama having spent some time Kala, assuming the shape of an ascetic, arrived at the palace gate.

दूतो ह्यतिबलस्याहं महर्षेरमितौजसः
रामं दिदृक्षुरायातः कार्येण हि महाबल

dūto hyatibalasyāhaṁ maharṣeramitaujasaḥ
rāmaṁ didṛkṣurāyātaḥ kāryeṇa hi mahābala
I am the messenger of the great saint Atibala of incomparable effulgence. O you of great strength, for a particular business, I have come here to sec Rama.

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिस्त्वरयान्वितः
न्यवेदयत रामाय तापसस्य विवक्षितम्

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā saumitristvarayānvitaḥ
nyavedayata rāmāya tāpasasya vivakṣitam
Hearing the words of the great saint, Saumitri speedily went to Raghava and communicated to him the arrival of the ascetic, saying.

जयस्व राजन्धर्मेण उभौ लोकौ महाद्युते
दूतस्त्वां द्रष्टुमायातस्तपस्वी भास्करप्रभः

jayasva rājandharmeṇa ubhau lokau mahādyute
dūtastvāṁ draṣṭumāyātastapasvī bhāskaraprabhaḥ
O you of great effulgence, observing the royal duties, may you acquire victory in both the worlds; one ambassador radiant like the sun by virtue of his asceticism, has come here to visit you.

तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं श्रुत्वा राम उवाच ह
प्रवेश्यतां मुनिस्तात महौजास्तस्य वाक्यधृक्

tadvākyaṁ lakṣmaṇenoktaṁ śrutvā rāma uvāca ha
praveśyatāṁ munistāta mahaujāstasya vākyadhṛk
Hearing the words of Laksmana, Rama said: “Do you speedily bring here the highly effulgent ascetic bringing in a message."

सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रावेशयत तं मुनिम्
ज्वलन्तमिव तेजोभिः प्रदहन्तमिवांशुभिः

saumitristu tathetyuktvā prāveśayata taṁ munim
jvalantamiva tejobhiḥ pradahantamivāṁśubhiḥ
There upon saying so be it, Saumitri conducted, the effulgent ascetic to Rama's house.

सोऽभिगम्य रघुश्रेष्ठं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा
ऋषिर्मधुरया वाचा वर्धस्वेत्याह राघवम्

so'bhigamya raghuśreṣṭhaṁ dīpyamānaṁ svatejasā
ṛṣirmadhurayā vācā vardhasvetyāha rāghavam
And having approached Rama the foremost? of Raghus, the ascetic, burning in his own energy, said to him, in sweet accents:-0 great king may prosperity crown you.

तस्मै रामो महातेजाः पूजामर्घ्यपुरोगमाम्
ददौ कुशलमव्यग्रं प्रष्टुं चैवोपचक्रमे

tasmai rāmo mahātejāḥ pūjāmarghyapurogamām
dadau kuśalamavyagraṁ praṣṭuṁ caivopacakrame
And having welcomed him with water and Argya, the highly effulgent Rama asked him about his well-being.

पृष्टश्च कुशलं तेन रामेण वदतां वरः
आसने काञ्चने दिव्ये निषसाद महायशाः

pṛṣṭaśca kuśalaṁ tena rāmeṇa vadatāṁ varaḥ
āsane kāñcane divye niṣasāda mahāyaśāḥ
Being asked by Rama as to his welfare, that foremost of ascetics, skilled in the are of speech, sat on a golden seat.

तमुवाच ततो रामः स्वागतं ते महामुने
प्रापयस्व च वाक्यानि यतो दूतस्त्वमागतः

tamuvāca tato rāmaḥ svāgataṁ te mahāmune
prāpayasva ca vākyāni yato dūtastvamāgataḥ
There upon welcoming him Rama said:-Do you communicate to me his words by whom you have been sent.

चोदितो राजसिंहेन मुनिर्वाक्यमुदीरयत्
द्वन्द्वमेतत्प्रवक्तव्यं न च चक्षुर्हतं वचः

codito rājasiṁhena munirvākyamudīrayat
dvandvametatpravaktavyaṁ na ca cakṣurhataṁ vacaḥ
Being thus addressed by Rama, a lion among kings, the ascetic said:-If do you wish to bring about the well-being of the celestials, my earnest desire is that we may talk over it in a solitary place.

यः शृणोति निरीक्षेद्वा स वध्यस्तव राघव
भवेद्वै मुनिमुख्यस्य वचनं यद्यवेक्षसे

yaḥ śṛṇoti nirīkṣedvā sa vadhyastava rāghava
bhavedvai munimukhyasya vacanaṁ yadyavekṣase
And if you have any regard for the words of that foremost of ascetics, do you so order that whoever shall hear or see us, when we shall converse in a solitary place, shall be slain by you.

तथेति च प्रतिज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
द्वारि तिष्ठ महाबाहो प्रतिहारं विसर्जय

tatheti ca pratijñāya rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
dvāri tiṣṭha mahābāho pratihāraṁ visarjaya
There upon Rama promised that it should be done and said to Laksmana:-O you having long arms, sending away the warder do you wait at the gate.

स मे वध्यः खलु भवेत्कथां द्वन्द्वसमीरिताम्
ऋषेर्मम च सौमित्रे पश्येद्वा शृणुयाच्च यः

sa me vadhyaḥ khalu bhavetkathāṁ dvandvasamīritām
ṛṣermama ca saumitre paśyedvā śṛṇuyācca yaḥ
When I shall talk with this ascetic in this solitary room whoever, shall hear or see us, shall be slain by me.

ततो निक्षिप्य काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणं द्वारसंग्रहे
तमुवाच मुनिं वाक्यं कथयस्वेति राघवः

tato nikṣipya kākutstho lakṣmaṇaṁ dvārasaṁgrahe
tamuvāca muniṁ vākyaṁ kathayasveti rāghavaḥ

Having thus piaced Laksmana at the gate Rama said to that Rsis:-O great saint, tell me what he has communicated to you. O Muni, what is your intention and by what high-souled Rsis you have been sent here. Tell me all this without any fear, I have become anxious to hear it.

शृणु राम महाबाहो यदर्थमहमाहतः
पितामहेन देवेन प्रेषितोऽस्मि महाबल

śṛṇu rāma mahābāho yadarthamahamāhataḥ
pitāmahena devena preṣito'smi mahābala
There upon the great saint said:-Hear, O king, O you gifted with great energy, for what I have come here. O you of great strength, the great Patriarch has sent me to you.

तवाहं पूर्वके भावे पुत्रः परपुरंजय
मायासंभावितो वीर कालः सर्वसमाहरः

tavāhaṁ pūrvake bhāve putraḥ parapuraṁjaya
māyāsaṁbhāvito vīra kālaḥ sarvasamāharaḥ
O hero, I am your son. You did, in your pristine birth, beget me on Maya-I am Kala, the destroyer of all.

पितामहश्च भगवानाह लोकपतिः प्रभुः
समयस्ते महाबाहो स्वर्लोकान्परिरक्षितुम्

pitāmahaśca bhagavānāha lokapatiḥ prabhuḥ
samayaste mahābāho svarlokānparirakṣitum
